detail.source:
# An ad-hoc type whose `url` is scoped to a cyclic pair (open <-> review, as building <-> review
# is on a brief) and whose `submit`/`bounce` transitions require nothing - so `open` has no
# stage-required content and any edge there can only be a stage-entry one.
def _stage_entry_page_type() -> PageType:
    return PageType(
        tag="xtest-stage-entry", name="Stage entry fixture",
        description="ad-hoc stage-entry-edge fixture",
        sections=(
            SectionSpec("summary", "Summary", (_prose("body", description="the summary instruction"),)),
            SectionSpec("release", "Release", (_scalar("url", description="the release url"),)),
        ),
        commands=(
            set_prose_cmd("summary"),
            set_scalar_cmd("release", field="url", legal_in=("open", "review")),
            transition_cmd("begin", "draft -> open", requires=(("summary", "body"),)),
            transition_cmd("submit", "open -> review"),
            transition_cmd("bounce", "review -> open"),
            add_link_cmd(), set_title_cmd(),
        ),
        fsm=FSMSpec(name="XStageEntry", initial="draft", states=("draft", "open", "review")),
    )


def _stage_entry_page(page_type: PageType, status: str) -> Page:
    return Page(id="xtest-stage-entry:1", type="xtest-stage-entry", title="X", status=status,
                sections=initial_sections(page_type))


def test_field_setter_edges_surface_a_stage_entry_setter_no_transition_requires():
    """A setter scoped by legal_in enters `do` where its scope opens, even though no transition
    legal there requires its field - and even though the status has no stage-required content at
    all, which used to make the function return early."""
    entry = _stage_entry_page_type()
    edges = {e["command"]: e for e in field_setter_edges(_stage_entry_page(entry, "open"), entry)}
    assert "setUrl" in edges
    url = edges["setUrl"]
    assert url["kind"] == "field" and url["section"] == "release" and url["field"] == "url"
    # Identical in shape to a stage-required edge - the instruction is inline and no key marks it out.
    assert url["instruction"] == "the release url"
    assert set(url) == {"pageId", "pageType", "kind", "section", "field", "instruction",
                        "command", "statusRevisionToken"}


def test_field_setter_edges_stage_entry_is_the_nearest_status_of_a_cyclic_scope():
    """open <-> review is a cycle, so the scope opens at whichever the page reaches first. The
    edge shows in `open` and not in `review`, so the nudge fires once rather than in every status
    the setter stays legal in."""
    entry = _stage_entry_page_type()
    assert "setUrl" in {e["command"] for e in field_setter_edges(_stage_entry_page(entry, "open"), entry)}
    assert "setUrl" not in {e["command"] for e in field_setter_edges(_stage_entry_page(entry, "review"), entry)}
    # And nowhere its legal_in does not name at all.
    assert "setUrl" not in {e["command"] for e in field_setter_edges(_stage_entry_page(entry, "draft"), entry)}


def test_field_setter_edges_stage_entry_respects_the_parent_gate():
    """A wholly parent-gated stage offers nothing at all, stage-entry edges included. test-child's
    draft-scoped adds (addCheck, addNote, addDecisions) are stage-entry edges no transition
    requires, so without the gate a pinned child would advertise its whole authoring surface the
    moment it is created - the exact leak the parent guard exists to prevent."""
    child = new_child(make_counter())                      # test-child in `draft`
    open_commands = {e["command"] for e in field_setter_edges(child, CHILD)}
    assert {"addCheck", "addNote", "addDecisions"} <= open_commands
    assert field_setter_edges(child, CHILD, {"markReady"}) == []

detail.source:
allowed = fsm.allowed_events(page_type.fsm, page.status)
    stage_events = allowed - set(blocked_events)
    required = {
        section_field
        for command in page_type.commands
        if _is_status_transition(command) and command.event in stage_events
        for section_field in command.requires
    }
    # A stage whose every legal event is parent-blocked is not this page's work yet, so it offers
    # nothing - the same reasoning that leaves `required` empty there, stated directly because a
    # stage-entry edge has no transition to be dropped from the topology.
    entry_open = not allowed or bool(stage_events)
    legal = legal_commands(page, page_type)
    # PageType's post-init rejects a type declaring two setters for one field, so the first
    # legal one found is the only one there is.
    setters: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
    for command in page_type.commands:
        section, field = command.section, command.field
        if section is None or field is None:      # transitions / addLink / setTitle target no field
            continue
        if not legal.get(command.name) or not is_field_setter(command):
            continue
        stage_entry = (entry_open and command.legal_in is not None
                       and page.status in stage_entry_statuses(page_type.fsm, command.legal_in))
        if (section, field) in required or stage_entry:
            setters.setdefault((section, field), command.name)
    return [_field_setter_edge(page, page_type, section, field, command_name)
            for (section, field), command_name in setters.items()]

Keep what it already says about the stage-required rule and about blocked_events, and add that a setter scoped by legal_in also enters where that scope opens, that the two sets are deduplicated by (section, field), and that a wholly parent-gated stage suppresses the stage-entry half. Keep the existing note that a legal_in of None means the setter is surfaced only when its field is stage-required, since that is unchanged and is what keeps setSummary from reappearing everywhere.

Run uv run pytest tests/test_commands.py --testmon and watch the three new tests pass with the existing field-setter-edge tests still green - in particular test_field_setter_edges_are_stage_and_legal_in_scoped, which asserts an empty list in the sealed status, and test_field_setter_edges_drop_blocked_events, which asserts an empty list for a gated child. Then commit.

Add one store-level test for the effectful shell in tests/test_store.py, placed with the other next_actions tests after test_next_actions_child_guard_does_not_withhold_field_setters around line 656. store.next_actions already calls field_setter_edges once per page and extends the do list with the result, so this asserts wiring rather than logic: the new edges reach a real rollup carrying the page's own revision token, and are indistinguishable in shape from the stage-required ones.

def test_next_actions_do_includes_stage_entry_field_setters(store):
    """A setter scoped by legal_in reaches the rollup where its scope opens, even though no
    transition requires its field. test-child's addCheck is draft-scoped and markReady requires
    only steps.items, so addCheck can only be here as a stage-entry edge - and it appears only
    once the parent has unlocked the child's stage."""
    workspace = store.create_workspace("demo")
    result = store.create_page(workspace.id, "test-lifecycle", "F")
    parent, child = result.page, _child(result, "test-child")
    _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [
        {"command": "setSummary", "args": {"text": "x"}},
        {"command": "beginPlanning"},
    ])
    do = store.next_actions(workspace.id, parent.id)["do"]
    child_edges = {edge["command"]: edge for edge in do if edge["pageId"] == child.id}
    assert "addCheck" in child_edges
    add_check = child_edges["addCheck"]
    assert add_check["kind"] == "field"
    assert add_check["section"] == "checks" and add_check["field"] == "items"
    assert add_check["instruction"]
    assert add_check["statusRevisionToken"] == store.get_page(workspace.id, child.id).status_revision_token
    # No key tells a stage-entry edge apart from the stage-required addStep beside it.
    assert set(add_check) == set(child_edges["addStep"])

Expect everything to pass unchanged. The only fixture whose rollup grows is test-child in draft, which gains addCheck, addNote and addDecision beside the addStep it already emitted; the existing assertions on it use membership rather than equality, so they should hold. If a test in tests/test_server.py or tests/test_web.py snapshots a whole do list for a page carrying a legal_in-scoped setter, widen that expectation to include the new edges rather than narrowing the feature - the edges are the point of the change. Do not touch tests that fail for an unrelated reason; raise those instead.
Then confirm the production surface is the ten edges the spec names, with a throwaway script run from the repo root. This is a check, not a file to keep - delete it once it has printed.

# scratch check: write to a temp file and run with `uv run python <file>`
from src.pagetypes._registry import REGISTRY
from src.pagetypes.core.specs import TRANSITION, COMPOUND
from src.pagetypes.core.commands import is_field_setter
from src.commands import stage_entry_statuses
from src import fsm as fsmmod

for tag, page_type in sorted(REGISTRY.items()):
    for status in page_type.fsm.states:
        allowed = fsmmod.allowed_events(page_type.fsm, status)
        required = {sf for c in page_type.commands
                    if c.kind in (TRANSITION, COMPOUND) and c.event in allowed
                    for sf in c.requires}
        for c in page_type.commands:
            if c.kind in (TRANSITION, COMPOUND) and c.event is not None:
                continue
            if not is_field_setter(c) or c.legal_in is None or status not in c.legal_in:
                continue
            if (c.section, c.field) in required:
                continue
            if status in stage_entry_statuses(page_type.fsm, c.legal_in):
                print(f"{tag:20s} {status:12s} {c.name}")

inlines: Ten lines and no others, none of them in a terminal status. If the output differs, the rule is wrong rather than the expectation - stop and raise it rather than adjusting the list.

items.text: Pure: a single-status scope always qualifies. Call stage_entry_statuses on an ad-hoc FSMSpec draft->open->review->done with a bounce edge review->open, passing legal_in ('review',). Expect exactly {'review'} - the trivial setPullRequestUrl case, qualifying despite `open` transitioning into it, because `open` is outside the scope. Test: test_stage_entry_statuses_single_status_scope_always_qualifies.

Pure: only edges between scoped statuses disqualify. Same ad-hoc FSM, legal_in ('review','done'). Expect {'review'} - `done` is entered from `review`, which is inside the scope, so it is dropped; `review` is entered only from `open`, outside it, so it stays. This is the bug-report setPullRequestUrl shape and is the case that would wrongly return both statuses if the rule read incoming edges globally. Test: test_stage_entry_statuses_ignore_edges_from_outside_the_scope.

Pure: a cyclic scope falls back to nearest-to-initial. Same ad-hoc FSM, legal_in ('open','review'), where open->review and review->open are both inside the scope. Expect {'open'}: draft->open is one edge and draft->open->review is two. This is the recordCommit shape; without the fallback the expected value would be the empty set. Test: test_stage_entry_statuses_fall_back_to_nearest_initial_when_the_scope_is_cyclic.

Pure: the fallback keeps every status tied at the shortest distance. Build an FSMSpec with draft->a, draft->b, a->b and b->a, and pass legal_in ('a','b'). Expect {'a','b'} - both are one edge from draft, and a tie is not broken arbitrarily. Test: test_stage_entry_statuses_fallback_keeps_every_status_at_the_shortest_distance.

Pure: total over degenerate input. An empty legal_in returns the empty set. A cyclic scope no path from the initial status reaches - an FSMSpec whose only edges are x->y and y->x, with initial 'draft' - also returns the empty set rather than picking an arbitrary status or raising. A legal_in naming a status the FSM does not declare neither raises nor disturbs the real entry statuses: it is carried in the result (an unknown name has no incoming edge, so the within-set rule keeps it) and is simply never equal to a page's actual status, which is the specced contract. Nothing in this case raises. Tests: test_stage_entry_statuses_empty_scope_and_unreachable_scope_yield_nothing and test_stage_entry_statuses_tolerate_a_status_the_fsm_does_not_declare.

Pure, against the real page types: stage_entry_statuses on the production FSMs read via get_page_type (no page is created, which test mode forbids for production types). feature-brief with ('review',) gives {'review'}; feature-brief with ('building','review','shipped') gives {'building'}; bug-report with ('review','done') gives {'review'}; bug-report with ('open','review','done','closed') gives {'open'}; decision-record with ('authoring','accepted') gives {'authoring'}. These are the exact legal_in tuples setPullRequestUrl, recordCommit and setSupersededBy declare, so this is what proves the ten-edge production surface rather than only the ad-hoc FSMs. Test: test_stage_entry_statuses_on_the_production_lifecycles.

Edges: a stage-entry setter is surfaced where no transition requires its field. Build an ad-hoc page type whose release.url scalar is legal_in ('open','review') and whose submit/bounce transitions require nothing, put a page in 'open', and call field_setter_edges. Expect setUrl present with kind 'field', section 'release', field 'url' and the FieldSpec description carried as instruction. This is the case the current early return on an empty required set makes impossible, so it fails before the change. Test: test_field_setter_edges_surface_a_stage_entry_setter_no_transition_requires.

Edges: the edge shape carries no discriminator. On the same ad-hoc page in 'open', assert the setUrl edge's key set is exactly {pageId, pageType, kind, section, field, instruction, command, statusRevisionToken} - identical to a stage-required edge, with nothing marking it optional. A new key added by mistake fails here. Test: test_field_setter_edges_surface_a_stage_entry_setter_no_transition_requires.

Edges: the nudge fires once across a cyclic scope. Same ad-hoc page type, legal_in ('open','review'). In 'open' setUrl is present; in 'review' it is absent even though the command is still legal there; in 'draft' it is absent because the scope does not name it. The middle assertion is the whole point of the feature and would fail under a plain 'legal_in contains the status' rule. Test: test_field_setter_edges_stage_entry_is_the_nearest_status_of_a_cyclic_scope.

Edges: a wholly parent-gated stage offers nothing, stage-entry edges included. Take a test-child page in 'draft' (markReady is its only legal event and is parent-guarded). With no blocked events, addCheck, addNote and addDecisions are all present - draft-scoped setters no transition requires, so they can only be stage-entry edges. Note the blocks field's add is addDecisions, plural: addDecision is the remove command's singular and would fail the assertion. With blocked_events {'markReady'}, field_setter_edges returns the empty list. Without the entry_open gate the second assertion fails, which is the leak this case exists to catch. Test: test_field_setter_edges_stage_entry_respects_the_parent_gate.

Edges, regression: the existing stage-required behaviour is unchanged. The pre-existing tests must still pass untouched - field_setter_edges on the ad-hoc seal fixture returns [] in 'sealed'; setSummary (legal_in None) shows in test-lifecycle 'draft' but not in 'planning'; a blocked markReady silences a test-child; an unrelated blocked event leaves the edges intact; and every edge still carries its instruction under 'instruction' and no 'description' key. Tests: test_field_setter_edges_are_stage_and_legal_in_scoped, test_field_setter_edges_drop_legal_in_none_noise, test_field_setter_edges_drop_blocked_events, test_field_setter_edges_group_blocks_and_carry_instructions, test_field_setter_edges_use_the_instruction_key_not_description.

Edges, regression: excluded command kinds stay excluded. test-flow's reorderCommit names the terminal 'closed' in its legal_in and so is legal there, but a reorder is not a field setter and must not appear in do. Confirmed by the existing test_next_actions_terminal_state_has_no_field_setters, which drives a test-flow page to 'closed' and asserts the rollup carries no kind='field' edge at all while the reopen transition still shows. Test: test_next_actions_terminal_state_has_no_field_setters.

Store: the new edges reach a real nextActions rollup. Create a test-lifecycle page with its pinned test-child, drive the parent to 'planning' so the child's stage unlocks, and read next_actions on the parent subtree. The child's addCheck edge is present with kind 'field', section 'checks', field 'items', a non-empty instruction, and a statusRevisionToken equal to the child page's own - not the parent's. Its key set matches the stage-required addStep edge beside it exactly. Test: test_next_actions_do_includes_stage_entry_field_setters.

Store, regression: a parent-gated child still says nothing. The existing test_next_actions_withholds_child_field_setters_until_parent_unlocks asserts that while the parent is 'draft' the child contributes zero kind='field' edges to the rollup, and that its blocked reason names the parent rather than steps.items. This is the assertion the stage-entry rule would break if the parent gate were omitted, so it must pass unchanged rather than be widened.

Whole suite and types. uv run pytest passes with no test removed or weakened, and uv run basedpyright reports no new errors. The only expected movement is that a test-child in draft now emits more field edges than before; any assertion that breaks on that must be widened to include the new edges, never narrowed by restricting the feature. A failure anywhere else is a real regression and is raised rather than accommodated.

Production surface. With the change in place, enumerate every registered page type and status, filtering to is_field_setter commands whose legal_in names the status, whose (section, field) is not already required by a transition legal there, and where the status is in stage_entry_statuses. Expect exactly ten lines: feature-brief planReview addFinding, feature-brief building recordCommit, feature-brief review setPullRequestUrl, epic planReview addFinding, bug-report open recordCommit, bug-report review setPullRequestUrl, simple-change open recordCommit, simple-change review setPullRequestUrl, decision-record authoring setSupersededBy, implementation-plan draft addDataModels. None is in a terminal status. More or fewer lines means the rule is wrong. Run as a throwaway script, not a kept test - the pure production-FSM assertions above are what the suite keeps.

overview.body:
This spec covers one pure function and one call site: how `commands.field_setter_edges` decides which field-setter commands enter the `do` list of a `nextActions` / `next` payload. Today a setter enters `do` only when its (section, field) is required content for a transition legal from the current status. This adds a second, independent reason to enter: the command is scoped by `legal_in` and the page sits in one of the statuses where that scope first opens. The two sets are unioned and deduplicated by (section, field).

Out of scope: the shape of a `do` edge (unchanged - no new key), the transition / blocked / humanGates / attention lists (untouched), the store, the server tools, guidance, and any change to which commands are LEGAL. This feature only changes what is SURFACED; `legal_commands` decides what may be run, exactly as before, and every new edge is intersected with it.

The derivation stays generic: it reads `legal_in` and the derived FSM transition table only, so a new page type is handled with no change here.

body.text: Behaviour

A field-setter command scoped by legal_in becomes a do edge in the statuses where its scope first opens - its stage-entry statuses. The edge is emitted whenever the page sits in such a status and the command is legal there, whether or not its field already holds content, and whether or not any transition requires that field. A command with legal_in None keeps today's behaviour exactly: it has no scope to enter, so it is surfaced only when its field is stage-required.

The stage-required rule is unchanged and continues to hold on its own. The new rule only ever adds edges; no edge emitted today stops being emitted, with the single exception described under Parent gating, which withholds the new edges in the same circumstance that already withholds the old ones.
Stage-entry statuses (pure)

A new pure helper in src/commands.py, derived from the page type's FSM alone. The FSM transition table is itself derived - each transition command contributes one (event, source, dest, agency) per entry in its own legal_in - so incoming edges are read straight off fsm.transitions.

Primary rule, within-set: a status in legal_in qualifies when no OTHER status listed in that same legal_in transitions into it. Edges arriving from statuses outside the scope are ignored, which is what makes a single-status legal_in always qualify.

Fallback, nearest-to-initial: when the primary rule leaves nothing - the scoped statuses form a cycle, as building and review do - the qualifying statuses are those at the shortest BFS distance from the FSM's initial status, measured over the same transition table. Statuses unreachable from the initial status are not candidates; if no scoped status is reachable, the command has no stage-entry status and stays silent. Ties at the same distance all qualify.
field_setter_edges: the union

The existing signature and return shape are unchanged: field_setter_edges(page, page_type, blocked_events=()) returns a list of edge dicts built by _field_setter_edge, keyed internally by (section, field) so a field is one edge naming one command. The function gains a second membership test in its loop and loses its early return.

The early return on an empty required set has to go: a feature-brief in review has no stage-required content at all - neither requestChanges nor ship declares requires - yet review is exactly where setPullRequestUrl must appear. With the early return removed, an empty required set simply contributes no members to the union.

Note the reordering: the is_field_setter and legality tests move ahead of the membership tests, because both branches need them. This is behaviour-preserving for the stage-required branch - the same two conditions gate it today, only later in the loop.

A transition command is never a candidate: transitions carry no section or field, so the first continue drops them before legal_in is ever consulted. That is what keeps a transition command's legal_in - which means source statuses, not a content lock - out of this derivation entirely.
Parent gating

blocked_events already withholds stage-required content: the store passes the events barred by a failing ParentStateGuard, and their requires are dropped from the union because nothing authored on this page can clear them. A stage-entry edge is tied to no transition, so it needs the condition stated directly: the new edges are withheld when the current stage is wholly parent-gated, meaning every event legal from the current status is blocked.

That is the entry_open flag above. A status with no outgoing events at all - a dead-end terminal status - is not gated by anything and keeps its stage-entry edges, subject as always to legal_commands, which locks authoring in a terminal status unless the command names that status in its own legal_in. A status where only some events are parent-blocked is not wholly gated and keeps its edges too.

This is what preserves the pinned-child behaviour: a test-child in draft whose feature-brief-equivalent parent has not reached the unlocking stage has markReady as its only legal event, so a blocked markReady leaves the stage closed and addStep, addCheck, addNote and addDecision all stay silent - as they must, since draft-scoped setters would otherwise leak the whole authoring surface the parent gate exists to withhold.
Edge shape and the store

A stage-entry edge is emitted by the existing _field_setter_edge and is byte-for-byte the same shape as a stage-required one: pageId, pageType, kind set to field, section, field, instruction taken from the FieldSpec description, command, and statusRevisionToken. No new key and no new kind, so nextActions, createPage and mutatePageBatch need no change, and no consumer of `next` needs to learn anything.

store.next_actions is unchanged: it already calls field_setter_edges once per page with that page's parent-blocked events and extends do with the result. The effectful side gains nothing; the whole rule lives in the pure module.
The resulting surface

Computed over every registered page type and status, deduplicated against what is already emitted. Ten edges in total, none in a terminal status. Everything else that carries a legal_in is either already surfaced as stage-required content or is a kind is_field_setter excludes.

body.source:
page type            status      command             rule
-------------------  ----------  ------------------  --------
feature-brief        planReview  addFinding          within-set
feature-brief        building    recordCommit        fallback
feature-brief        review      setPullRequestUrl   within-set
epic                 planReview  addFinding          within-set
bug-report           open        recordCommit        fallback
bug-report           review      setPullRequestUrl   within-set
simple-change        open        recordCommit        fallback
simple-change        review      setPullRequestUrl   within-set
decision-record      authoring   setSupersededBy     fallback
implementation-plan  draft       addDataModels       within-set

body.text: The test fixtures gain edges too, which is where the suite will move: a test-child in draft newly surfaces addCheck, addNote and addDecision beside the addStep it already emits, because only steps.items is stage-required there. Existing assertions that pin an exact edge set for those pages have to be widened rather than worked around.
Error paths

There are none to add. stage_entry_statuses is total over any FSMSpec and any legal_in tuple: an empty legal_in yields an empty set, a scope whose statuses are all unreachable yields an empty set, and a status named in legal_in but absent from the FSM's states simply never matches page.status. It raises nothing and reads no page content, so it cannot fail on a malformed page. Every edge it proposes is still gated by legal_commands, so a command that is not actually runnable can never be surfaced.

The one performance note: stage_entry_statuses is called per candidate command per page, and each call walks the transition table. The tables are tuples of at most a few dozen entries and next_actions already walks every command of every page in the subtree, so the added work is proportional and small. No caching is specced - a cache keyed on an FSMSpec would be a second mechanism to explain for no measurable gain at this size.

"First available" means within-set: a status in a command's legal_in qualifies when no OTHER status in that same legal_in transitions into it. Rejected: reading it globally over the whole FSM, which is the literal wording but selects zero statuses on all eleven registered page types - only an FSM's initial status could ever qualify, and every type that scopes content by legal_in also carries a reopen-style edge back into it (ready to draft, closed to open). The within-set reading is what makes the trivial case work: setPullRequestUrl is legal_in review alone, and building transitions into review from outside the scope, which the rule ignores.

A cyclic scope falls back to the legal_in statuses nearest the FSM's initial status by BFS distance. Rejected: accepting silence, which is a shorter rule but loses recordCommit entirely - building and review transition into each other via submitForReview and requestChanges, so neither is unentered, and the one command whose stage guidance says "record each commit as you make it" would never be surfaced. The fallback costs a BFS over a table of at most a few dozen edges and recovers recordCommit in building, recordCommit in open on bug-report and simple-change, and setSupersededBy in authoring. Ties at equal distance all qualify; statuses unreachable from the initial status are not candidates.

A stage-entry edge is emitted in exactly the shape of a stage-required one - no discriminating key, no new kind. Rejected: adding a required true/false flag, which would keep the payload honest about which edges are preconditions but adds a key every consumer and every doc has to account for. The accepted cost is that `do` no longer means strictly "author this to advance": it now means "what is worth doing in this status". That widening is documented on the Self-direction architecture page rather than encoded in the payload.

Eligibility reuses is_field_setter unchanged - SET_SCALAR, SET_PROSE, ADD_ELEMENT and a page-level ADD_BLOCK. Rejected: including element transitions (markStepDone, markCasePassed and the dispatch marks), which is arguably the real building-stage work but has no (section, field) instruction shape to carry and reverses a stated invariant; and the literal reading, every command carrying a legal_in, which would add removeStep, reorderStep, reorderStepDetail, reorderDataModel, removeFinding, markCommitStale and escalateQuestion, turning `do` into the describeMutations list.

A stage-entry edge is unconditional while the page sits in the status - it does not disappear once its field holds content. Rejected: suppressing a populated field, which would make `do` shrink as work is done but makes the derivation a function of page content rather than of page type and status alone. The existing stage-required edges are already emitted regardless of whether their field is populated, and stage guidance is likewise present on every write in a status, so unconditional is the consistent choice.

Stage-entry edges are withheld when every event legal from the current status is parent-blocked - a wholly gated stage. Rejected: routing legal_in through blocked_events, which does not apply because a stage-entry edge is tied to no transition and so has nothing to subtract; and omitting the gate, which would let a pinned child emit its whole draft-scoped authoring surface the moment it is created, defeating the parent-gated stage exposure invariant and breaking two existing tests. A partially gated stage keeps its edges, because some other transition is still this page's to drive.

inlines.text: The record for the user-facing
that GitHub visitors land on. The file itself lives at the repository root; this page holds why it is shaped the way it is, so a later revision does not have to re-derive the argument.
Audience and angle

Written for someone who has never seen pasta and is deciding in thirty seconds whether it solves a problem they have. Not for a contributor: the internals appear only where they are the product. The pitch is deliberately narrow - the FSM hands the agent the instruction for the stage it is actually in, so a written-out process (TDD, reproduce-before-you-fix, spec-then-plan) arrives at the moment it applies instead of being read once at the top of a session and competing with every token after it.
Structure

items.text: Tagline, one-paragraph what-it-is, and the Flying Spaghetti Monster naming aside.
The problem with putting your process in a prompt: names the concrete failure modes (fixing a symptom without reproducing, planning against unread code, marking a test passed that never ran).
The loop: the
payload, and a table of the four buckets with who acts on each.
Quick start, with the copy-the-skill subsection under it. Placed here on purpose: a reader who has just seen the loop can run it before being asked to read a lifecycle.
A process, written out: the feature-brief lifecycle as a plain-text status chain with no event names, the
guidance quoted verbatim, the hot-reload note, and the Model view screenshot closing the section.
Gates that actually hold, in prose.
Page types, in prose. Write your own process, development, licence.

inlines.text: Decisions

items.text: Lead with the bug-report Page screenshot; the Model screenshot closes A process, written out, where it lands beside the bug-report discussion it illustrates. The two images carry different arguments and are not interchangeable.
Both images are

tags with a hardcoded width, not markdown syntax, so they render at a chosen size rather than filling the column. The files are 830 pixels wide and displayed at 550, so browsers downscale them and they stay sharp on high-DPI screens.
Quote the real
stage guidance rather than paraphrase it. The prose is the product; summarising it would sell it short.

The lifecycle is plain text in a fenced block, not a rendered diagram, and it names statuses only. A mermaid state diagram was written first and dropped: the text form carries what each stage is FOR alongside the chain, which the diagram could not, and it depends on no renderer. FSM event names were then dropped from it as well, and from the prose around it, because the statuses carry the meaning and the command names are jargon here.

Prose beats formatting almost everywhere here. The gates section, the page types and the customisation seams were each first written as a bulleted list with bold lead-ins and backticked terms, and each read as heavier than the idea it carries: three formatting signals doing one job. Exactly ONE table survives, the four
buckets, because it is genuinely comparative across the same columns; its third column is headed who and reads agent or you.
Shell fences are tagged
, not

. The bash highlighter colours these lines badly and there is nothing in them a reader needs syntax colour to parse. The JSON blocks keep their tags, since those highlight correctly and are real JSON.

The skill-copy step is ONE command copying the one skill, with no global-install variant, and it ends on a bold instruction to ask the agent to cook a feature, a simple change, a bug report or some documentation. An MCP server the agent can use is not one it will use; this is the step that makes the workflow start in pasta. The command uses
because
is GNU coreutils only and fails on BSD cp, and the source has no trailing slash because BSD cp would then copy the directory's contents rather than the directory.
Link to the just project before listing the recipes. The commands mean nothing to a reader who does not already have the tool.
Name the licence rather than only linking it: AGPL-3.0, with the text at
. Someone weighing a network-served server wants the copyleft terms up front, not one click away.
The toc page type is left out of the page-types section entirely. It is plumbing rather than something a reader chooses, and the name is jargon on a page aimed at someone who has never seen the tool.
The pinned children (spec, implementation plan, testing plan) are mentioned once, under the feature brief that creates them, rather than as a standalone paragraph.

Say that hot reload makes the workflow itself editable against a running session. That is what makes writing your own process practical rather than theoretical, and it is the natural close to the lifecycle section.

Say plainly that marking things done still requires honesty from the agent, and that the value is that the claims are separate, recorded and gated. Overclaiming enforcement would be the easiest way to lose a reader who tries it.
No em dashes in the file.
One non-documentation change rides in the same commit: the justfile's parallel
recipe drops
, leaving
plus
. The standalone
recipe is kept. This is what let the README document
again, having earlier had to document
because
pulled in a tool a reader would not have.

inlines.text: Screenshots
Two PNGs committed under
(a bug-report Page view) and
(the Model view for bug-report in

, showing the state diagram, the transitions legal from there, and the authoring commands). Both were resized to 75 percent, 830x968, after the first draft, and are rendered at width 550. The resize made the files LARGER (roughly 183KB to 450KB and 179KB to 371KB) because the resample re-encoded without the originals' optimisation; running them through a PNG optimiser is outstanding if the weight ever matters.

feature-brief:mumfpmtz-f10791.title: Archived pages are only deleted when scheduled for deletion

summary.body:
Archiving a page should mean "out of the way", not "queued for destruction". Today the hourly cleanup sweep treats every archived page as expiring, so an archive worth keeping indefinitely cannot exist. Deletion becomes an explicit second decision: a page carries a delete-scheduled state of its own, and an archived page is only ever deleted when it also carries that flag. Archived pages that are not scheduled live in the archive forever.

The outcome: (1) `Page` gains a persisted `delete_scheduled` boolean; (2) the sweep's archived arm narrows from "hidden" to "hidden AND delete_scheduled", while the separate unfiled-orphan arm is left untouched; (3) the page view gains a button beside Archive/Unarchive that toggles the state, and scheduling also archives the page so the two can never disagree; (4) an HTTP route backs that button, mirroring the existing archive routes. No new MCP tools and no new page-type commands - the archive path stays as it is.

Grounding settled the open question in the first draft of this summary: the existing five-day `expires_at` grace period and its backup-before-prune transaction stay exactly as they are. Scheduling makes a page a candidate, the next sweep stamps it, and the sweep after the expiry deletes it - so this feature changes which pages are candidates and adds nothing that deletes.

items.name: src/cleanup.py
items.text: PURE + EFFECTFUL, split cleanly. Pure: reachability() (L73) walks down root_page_ids/child_ids sorting every page into findable/hidden/unfiled; classify() (L132) turns a Workspace + now into a Sweep{stamp, clear, prune}. The line this feature changes is L141: `targets = reach.hidden | reach.unfiled` - the set of pages that get stamped and eventually pruned. Effectful: run_once() calls store, _loop/start_scheduler/stop_scheduler own an asyncio task, and the module reads PASTA_CLEANUP and the clock. expiry_for() and delete_subtree() are pure and unaffected.

items.name: src/model.py - Page dataclass (L16)
items.text: PURE. Holds `archived: bool = False` (L26) and `expires_at: str | None = None` (L29), whose comment states it is written and cleared only by the sweep. Page.copy() (L34) enumerates every field explicitly, so a new field that is not added there is silently dropped on every command-path copy. This is where the new delete-scheduled field belongs.

items.name: src/serialize.py - page_to_dict (L14) / page_from_dict (L30)
items.text: PURE. A near-identity mapping that defines the on-disk shape; page_from_dict reads each optional field with a .get default (e.g. `archived=data.get("archived", False)`), which is how existing workspace files that predate a field keep loading. A new persisted field needs a line in each direction plus that legacy default.

items.name: src/store.py - _set_page_archived (L670), archive_page/unarchive_page (L689/L692)
items.text: EFFECTFUL: takes _transaction_lock_for(workspace_id), loads the workspace from disk, mutates, _touch_and_save. _set_page_archived rejects a pinned auto-created child (archive the parent instead) and cascades the flag onto the target's own pinned children, so parent and pinned children never disagree. A new delete-scheduled setter has to follow exactly this shape, including the pinned-child rules, or the two flags can drift apart on pinned children.

items.name: src/store.py - cleanup_workspace (L631)
items.text: EFFECTFUL: the one transaction that applies a sweep - load, classify, write_backup only when something will be pruned, then clear stamps, write stamps, delete_subtree each prune root, _touch_and_save, all inside one transaction lock. It applies whatever classify() decided and contains no policy of its own, so narrowing the delete rule needs no change here.

items.name: src/server.py - route_page (L178) and route_archive_page/route_unarchive_page (L215/L224)
items.text: EFFECTFUL (HTTP + store + websocket). route_page builds the template context and already passes `archived: page.archived` explicitly to drive the Archive button; a second button needs its own context key the same way. The two archive routes are the exact pattern the new route must mirror: POST, _guard_http(), one STORE call, `await ws_reloader.refresh()`, return PlainTextResponse(status_code=202). Note the comment above them claims a 303 redirect while the code returns 202 - do not copy the comment's claim.

The new button goes in this row beside the archive form, and the inline script at L28-35 attaches a scroll-to-top handler by element id to each form - a new form needs the same treatment or it must be left out of that script deliberately.

items.text: TEST (pure). test_page_expires_at_round_trips (L61) and test_page_expires_at_defaults_to_none_for_legacy_files assert the persisted shape of the sweep's field through _sample_page (L12); a new persisted field needs the same round-trip and legacy-default pair.

Python floor is `requires-python = ">=3.14"` (pyproject.toml L6). Test runner is pytest (dev group `pytest>=9.1.1`, `pytest-testmon>=2.2.0`), and CLAUDE.md states: "Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing." testpaths = ["tests"], pythonpath = ["."].

Type checking is basedpyright with `typeCheckingMode = "recommended"` over `include = ["src/**/*"]` (pyproject.toml [tool.pyright]), with only reportAny and reportExplicitAny disabled. Existing code satisfies it by annotating every signature and discarding unused returns with `_ = ...` (e.g. `_ = task.cancel()` in cleanup.py L245); new code must match.
CLAUDE.md naming rule, copied verbatim: "Use the word \"create\" instead of \"mint\" when creating something." Applies to any new identifier, comment or UI copy this feature adds.

Invariant that must survive, from the Scheduled workspace cleanup architecture page: "A page is never deleted without a durable backup of the workspace it came from" - the backup is written before any mutation in the same locked pass, and an OSError there abandons the pass. This feature must not create a deletion path that bypasses cleanup_workspace.

Invariant that must survive, from the same page and enforced by classify(): `expires_at` is written and cleared ONLY by the sweep - no page-type command and no web route may set it. A page already carrying an expiry is never re-stamped (or the deadline moves every hour and nothing expires), and a page that stops being a target has its stamp cleared.

The sweep is pure-then-effectful by design, stated in the cleanup.py module docstring: "Classification is pure, so it unit-tests with no filesystem; the store owns the transaction. This module never imports store - the dependency runs store -> cleanup." The new delete rule therefore belongs in classify(), not in store.cleanup_workspace, and cleanup.py must not gain a store import.

Direct contradiction with an invariant recorded on the Archiving architecture page (architecture:mrtqsu5j-4643c4): "Archiving a page is reversible for a bounded grace period, not indefinitely: once the stamped expiry passes, the page and its whole subtree are permanently deleted." That invariant is exactly what this feature reverses - archiving becomes indefinitely reversible. The invariant has to give, and its stated failure mode ("violated the other, workspaces resume growing without bound") is the cost the user is knowingly accepting.

The Scheduled workspace cleanup page (architecture:msrxuvy1-990b09) states its Purpose as deleting pages "archived and forgotten" and its Details say "Two things are called an orphan here, and both are cleaned" - the archived-and-hidden arm and the unfiled arm. Narrowing only the first arm leaves the page half-true; the Purpose and Details prose has to give while the backup/grace machinery it describes stays exactly as it is.

Existing tests encode the rule being changed and will fail: tests/test_cleanup.py test_classify_stamps_hidden_and_unfiled_only (L101) asserts an archived page with no other state is stamped, and test_classify_never_restamps_an_existing_expiry (L107) and test_classify_prunes_only_maximal_subtree_roots (L117) both build their fixtures from a bare archived page. These are the specification of the old behaviour, so they must be updated deliberately as part of the change rather than discovered as breakage.

Prior art that partly solves the ask and must not be duplicated: `Page.expires_at` plus the stamp/clear/prune machinery already provides a delay between the decision and the deletion, and store.cleanup_workspace already provides the backup-then-prune transaction. This feature needs a new decision flag, not a new deletion path - a second mechanism that deletes pages would bypass the backup invariant.

store._set_page_archived (L670) refuses to run on a pinned auto-created child and cascades `archived` onto the target's pinned children. A delete-scheduled flag that does not follow the same two rules would let a pinned child end up scheduled while its parent is not, or vice versa - a disagreement the archive flag deliberately cannot have.

Stale comment already in the tree at src/server.py L211-214: it says the archive routes "303-redirect back to the page (GET) so a reload/back-button doesn't re-POST", but both routes return PlainTextResponse(status_code=202) and the page.html forms are driven by a client-side handler. Raising it rather than fixing it in passing; the new route should copy the code's actual 202 behaviour, not the comment's claim.

Found during the build, not during grounding: seven existing tests used archiving as the way to make a page a deletion candidate, and the plan named only two of them. tests/test_cleanup.py test_run_once_sweeps_every_workspace, and in tests/test_store.py test_cleanup_stamps_an_archived_page_but_does_not_delete_it, test_cleanup_prunes_only_after_the_expiry_passes, test_cleanup_writes_a_backup_before_pruning, test_cleanup_clears_the_stamp_when_a_page_is_unarchived, test_cleanup_prunes_an_archived_parent_with_its_shadowed_children and test_cleanup_aborts_without_deleting_when_the_backup_cannot_be_written. Each now schedules the page instead of only archiving it, so it goes on testing the machinery it was written for rather than passing vacuously; the two whose names stated the old rule were renamed to say scheduled.

architecture:mrtqsu5j-4643c4 "Archiving" - goes stale in several places: the Summary sentence "Page archiving is reversible for a five-day grace period, after which the cleanup sweep deletes the page"; the Purpose paragraph making archiving "the signal that a page is a candidate for removal"; the Usage paragraph "Archiving a page now also starts a deletion clock ... To keep a page indefinitely, unarchive it"; the Data model paragraph on which flags exist; the Details section "Grace period and the deletion clock"; and the invariant "Archiving a page is reversible for a bounded grace period, not indefinitely".

architecture:msrxuvy1-990b09 "Scheduled workspace cleanup" - goes stale in: the Summary ("stamps a uniform expiry on pages that can no longer be found"); the Purpose paragraph on reclaiming space from pages "archived and forgotten"; the Data model paragraph describing Page.expires_at as the only persisted field the sweep owns and as "orthogonal to both `archived` and FSM status"; and the Details opening "Two things are called an orphan here, and both are cleaned". The Code references list also needs the new field's home.

scripts/validate_workspace.py module docstring (L22-25) tells the reader that pages filed nowhere are orphans which "The server's hourly cleanup sweep treats as prunable after a 5-day grace period". This stays true only if the unfiled-orphan arm of the sweep is left alone; if that arm changes, this docstring changes with it.

No user-facing doc goes stale: README.md and docsite/ do not mention the deletion clock, and the only other hits for the grace period are the vendored docs/python-statemachine/*.md, which are unrelated. The generated page-type docs are unaffected because this feature adds no page-type command.

architecture:mrtqsu5j-4643c4 "Archiving" - its Code references list names the symbol `src/store.py; symbol: _set_page_archived`, which the build renames to `_set_page_archive_state` when it generalises the setter to carry both flags. The reference needs repointing at ship, alongside the prose changes recorded above.

The sweep deletes on two arms, not one: pages that are archived (or hidden beneath an archived ancestor), and pages that are filed nowhere at all - the unfiled orphans a structural bug leaves behind, which the offline validator also reports. The ask names only the archived arm. Does the unfiled-orphan arm keep deleting on its own after a grace period, or does the new delete-scheduled flag become the single condition under which anything is ever deleted?
items.answer: The unfiled-orphan arm is left exactly as it is; only the archived arm narrows. The ask is about the archive - "some pages should be allowed to live forever in the archive" - and an unfiled orphan is not in the archive, it is a page a structural bug lost. Nobody can schedule it for deletion from the tree, because the tree cannot show it, so making the flag the sole condition would turn that arm into an unbounded leak and would also falsify the validator docstring that tells a reader orphans are reclaimed. Consequence accepted and worth stating: a page that is archived AND also unfiled is still deleted after its grace period without being scheduled, because it qualifies on the orphan arm. That state only arises from a structural bug, not from archiving.

items.text: Once a page is both archived and scheduled for deletion, is it deleted at the next hourly sweep, or does the existing five-day `expires_at` grace period still run first so the decision stays undoable for five days?
items.answer: The five-day grace period still runs. Scheduling makes a page a deletion candidate; the next sweep stamps `expires_at` five days out at 12:00 UTC exactly as archiving does today, and the sweep after that instant deletes it behind a workspace backup. Deleting at the next sweep would put a permanent deletion one mis-click away and would discard the safety property the component was built around - "nothing is deleted at the moment a human archives something, only five days later". Keeping the delay also means no new deletion path exists: the flag only changes which pages become candidates, and every deletion still goes through the same backup-then-prune transaction.

items.text: Scheduling deletion also applies Archived, per the ask. What is the inverse - does unarchiving a scheduled page also cancel its deletion schedule, or does the page stay armed so that re-archiving it later resumes the deletion?
items.answer: Unarchiving clears the deletion schedule, so scheduled implies archived in both directions. The alternative - a page left armed while visible - creates exactly the surprise this feature exists to remove: a page that looks live, sits in the tree, and carries a countdown nobody can see. It would also contradict the mental model the archive already teaches, where unarchiving is the way to rescue a page. Clearing on unarchive keeps the two flags from ever disagreeing and makes the visible state honest: anything findable in the tree is not scheduled for deletion.

items.text: Should a descendant hidden beneath a page scheduled for deletion be stamped with its own expiry, as it is today, or should only the scheduled page itself be stamped and the descendants removed with it when its subtree is pruned?
items.answer: Only the scheduled page itself is stamped. A hidden descendant is no longer a stamping target, and it is removed when its scheduled ancestor's subtree is pruned by delete_subtree, which already takes every descendant and unlinks the root. This keeps the flag meaning one thing - a deliberate human decision - rather than something that appears to spread down a subtree, and it removes the need for the `covered` maximal-root filter to reconcile parent and child stamps on this arm. No behaviour is lost: the subtree still goes as one unit, which is what the existing invariant on descendants promises.

findings.issue: Blocking, in the store-test step and the sweep-transaction step: both wrote `page = store.create_page(workspace.id, "test-fields", "p")` and then used page.id. Store.create_page returns a create RESULT carrying .page and .children, not a Page, so every one of those tests would fail with an AttributeError on a result object before it ever reached the behaviour under test - and an implementer would read that failure as a bug in the feature. Applied: both steps rewritten to take the page off the result with .page, matching the idiom the surrounding tests in tests/test_store.py and tests/test_web.py already use.

Blocking, against the plan's own standard that a step is read alone and out of order: three steps carried placeholder ellipses deferring to a neighbouring test - `...   # build parent + pinned child exactly as the cascade test above does` and `workspace, page, part = ...   # same three lines of setup as test_page_view_shows_archive_button`. That is the 'same as step N' pattern the steps field explicitly forbids, and it leaves an implementer guessing at the pinned-child fixture in particular. Applied: every placeholder replaced with the real setup lines, plus the two API facts they depend on stated in the step - that create_page returns a result, and that the test-lifecycle page type is the one declaring a pinned test-child.

Blocking, a pre-existing test the plan failed to name: tests/test_store.py test_cleanup_prunes_an_archived_parent_with_its_shadowed_children builds a bare archived parent and expects it pruned. Under the new rule an archived parent nobody scheduled is never pruned, so that test fails and the plan gave no instruction for it - the implementer would meet it as unexplained breakage mid-build. Applied: the sweep-transaction step now names it alongside test_cleanup_stamps_an_archived_page_but_does_not_delete_it and says to schedule the parent in both.

Should-fix: the web-test step deferred a decision into the build - 'Check while writing it whether the page view renders an archived page without that parameter; if it does, drop the parameter'. A plan that asks the implementer to decide something is a plan that has not finished deciding. Settled during this review by reading the route: route_page resolves the page through Store.get_page, which does not filter on archived (only tree and search apply the subtree rule), so the view renders a scheduled-and-archived page normally. Applied: the step now fetches without any query string and states why.

Should-fix, a gap in the recorded documentation impact rather than in the steps: the build renames the private store method _set_page_archived to _set_page_archive_state, and the Archiving architecture page lists that exact symbol in its Code references. Nothing in the brief recorded it, so the rename would have been missed when the pages are reconciled at ship. Applied: a documentation item added naming the code reference to repoint.

# Schedule/cancel a page's deletion from its web view. There is no MCP equivalent, like the
# status override below: scheduling is a decision a person makes in the browser. Scheduling
# also archives, so a page queued for deletion is never left in a live view.
@app.post("/ws:{workspaceIdPart}/page/{pageId}/schedule-delete", response_class=PlainTextResponse)
async def route_schedule_page_deletion(workspaceIdPart: str, pageId: str):
    with _guard_http():
        workspace_id = f"ws:{workspaceIdPart}"
        STORE.schedule_page_deletion(workspace_id, pageId)
        await ws_reloader.refresh()
        return PlainTextResponse(status_code=202)


@app.post("/ws:{workspaceIdPart}/page/{pageId}/unschedule-delete", response_class=PlainTextResponse)

overview.body:
This spec covers one change to the cleanup subsystem and the thin web surface over it: a page gains a persisted `delete_scheduled` flag, and the sweep's archived arm narrows from "every page hidden behind the archive" to "hidden AND scheduled for deletion". An archived page that nobody scheduled is never stamped and never deleted, so it lives in the archive indefinitely.

It also covers the controls that set the flag: a store method pair, two HTTP POST routes mirroring the existing archive routes, and one button in the page view beside Archive/Unarchive. Scheduling a page also archives it, and unarchiving a page cancels its schedule, so the two flags can never disagree in a way a reader would have to reason about.

Deliberately out of scope: no new MCP tool and no new page-type command - the MCP archive path is unchanged, and `delete_scheduled` is set only through the store and the web routes. The deletion machinery itself is untouched: the five-day `expires_at` grace period, the backup-before-prune transaction and the subtree prune all stay exactly as they are, and this feature adds no code that deletes a page. The separate unfiled-orphan arm of the sweep is also untouched. No data migration is written; the first sweep after deployment clears the stale expiries by itself, which the design section explains.

body.text: The two flags and the four states

A page carries two independent booleans. `archived` keeps its current meaning exactly: hidden from tree, search and render, and not mutable until unarchived. `delete_scheduled` is new and means only one thing - a person has decided this page may be destroyed. Neither flag deletes anything on its own; the sweep reads both.

body.source:
archived  delete_scheduled   what it means                        what the sweep does
--------  ----------------   ---------------------------------    ----------------------------------
false     false              a live page                          nothing; clears any stale expiry
true      false              archived, kept indefinitely          nothing; clears any stale expiry
true      true               archived and scheduled for deletion  stamps expires_at, then prunes it
false     true               unreachable by construction          nothing; clears any stale expiry

body.text: The fourth row cannot be reached through any control this spec adds: scheduling sets `archived` at the same time, and unarchiving clears `delete_scheduled`. It is nevertheless defined rather than forbidden, because a hand-edited workspace file could produce it and the sweep must not delete a page a user can see. The rule that makes it safe is that the sweep tests hidden-ness itself rather than trusting the flag.
Data model (pure)

One new field on `Page` in src/model.py, placed after `expires_at` so the sweep's fields sit together, and added to `Page.copy()` - which enumerates fields explicitly, so an omission there would silently drop the flag on every command-path copy.

body.source:
@dataclass
class Page:
    ...
    # UTC ISO-8601 instant after which the cleanup sweep deletes this page, or None.
    # Written and cleared only by the sweep, never by a page-type command.
    expires_at: str | None = None
    # A deliberate decision that this page may be destroyed. The sweep deletes a page
    # only when this is set and the page is also out of sight; archiving alone keeps a
    # page indefinitely.
    delete_scheduled: bool = False

    def copy(self) -> "Page":
        return Page(
            ...
            expires_at=self.expires_at,
            delete_scheduled=self.delete_scheduled,
            status_revision_token=self.status_revision_token,
        )

body.text: The rule (pure) - src/cleanup.py

The whole behavioural change is the target set in `classify`. Today it is `reach.hidden | reach.unfiled`; it becomes the scheduled subset of hidden, unioned with the unfiled orphans as before. Everything downstream of that line - the never-re-stamp rule, the clear rule, the expiry comparison, the maximal-root `covered` filter - is correct as written and is not touched.

body.source:
def classify(workspace: Workspace, now: datetime) -> Sweep:
    reach = reachability(workspace)
    # Out of sight is no longer enough: an archived page is a deletion candidate only
    # once someone schedules it. Pages filed nowhere remain candidates on their own,
    # because nobody can reach one to schedule it.
    scheduled = {page_id for page_id in reach.hidden
                 if workspace.pages[page_id].delete_scheduled}
    targets = scheduled | reach.unfiled
    ...

body.text: Three consequences follow from that one line, and none needs further code. A descendant hidden under a scheduled page is not itself a target, so it is never stamped; it is removed when its ancestor's subtree is pruned by `delete_subtree`, which already takes every descendant. An archived page that is not scheduled is not a target, so `clear` drops any expiry it carries. And a scheduled page that becomes findable again - unarchived by hand in the file - is not in `reach.hidden`, so it too is cleared rather than deleted.

The module docstring's second paragraph currently says an expiry is stamped on "archived pages, the pages hidden underneath them, and pages filed nowhere", which the new rule falsifies. It is updated to name the scheduled-and-hidden arm and the unfiled arm.
Migration: there is none, by design

Pages already carrying an `expires_at` from the old rule are archived but not scheduled, so under the new rule they stop being targets. The `clear` arm of the very first sweep after deployment therefore drops every one of those stamps, and the pages stay in the archive. No migration script runs, nothing is rewritten ahead of time, and a page whose expiry had already elapsed is rescued as long as that sweep runs before the one that would have pruned it. This is a required behaviour, not an incidental one, and the testing plan covers it.
Store (effectful) - src/store.py

`_set_page_archived` becomes `_set_page_archive_state`, taking each flag as an optional keyword where None means leave it as it was. This keeps one copy of the two pinned-child rules - refuse to act on a pinned auto-created child, and cascade every flag onto the target's own pinned children - so the archive flag and the schedule flag can never drift apart on a pinned child. The transaction shape is unchanged: one `_transaction_lock_for`, load, mutate, `_touch_and_save`, return the page.
The IllegalCommandError message is left exactly as it reads today. It states the rule that matters - act on the parent instead - and existing callers and tests assert on it.
Four public methods sit on top, each one line, and each carrying the policy at its own call site rather than hiding it in the shared helper.
`cleanup_workspace` is not touched. It applies whatever `classify` decided and holds no policy of its own, so the backup-before-prune guarantee is inherited unchanged.
HTTP routes (effectful) - src/server.py

Two POST routes, placed directly after the existing archive routes and copying their shape exactly: guard, one store call, fire the live-reload refresh, return 202. They exist because a browser cannot call MCP; there is deliberately no MCP equivalent, matching the status-override route.

body.source:
@app.post("/ws:{workspaceIdPart}/page/{pageId}/schedule-delete", response_class=PlainTextResponse)
async def route_schedule_page_deletion(workspaceIdPart: str, pageId: str):
    with _guard_http():
        workspace_id = f"ws:{workspaceIdPart}"
        STORE.schedule_page_deletion(workspace_id, pageId)
        await ws_reloader.refresh()
        return PlainTextResponse(status_code=202)


@app.post("/ws:{workspaceIdPart}/page/{pageId}/unschedule-delete", response_class=PlainTextResponse)
async def route_unschedule_page_deletion(workspaceIdPart: str, pageId: str):
    with _guard_http():
        workspace_id = f"ws:{workspaceIdPart}"
        STORE.unschedule_page_deletion(workspace_id, pageId)
        await ws_reloader.refresh()
        return PlainTextResponse(status_code=202)

body.text: Error paths are the ones the guard already provides and no others: an unknown page id raises NotFoundError and a pinned auto-created child raises IllegalCommandError, both surfaced by `_guard_http` exactly as the archive routes surface them. The new routes return 202 like the code beside them, not the 303 the stale comment above those routes describes.
`route_page` passes one more context key, next to the `archived` key that already drives the Archive button.
