# Drives the Set to delete / Cancel delete button beside it.
"delete_scheduled": page.delete_scheduled,

body.text: Page view - src/templates/page.html

One form in the `#page-actions` row, immediately after the archive form and before the status dropdown, built the same way: the action and the label both switch on the context flag. The button reads `Set to delete` when the page is not scheduled and `Cancel delete` when it is.

body.source:
<form id="delete-schedule-form" method="post"
      action="/{{ workspace_id }}/page/{{ page_id }}/{% if delete_scheduled %}unschedule-delete{% else %}schedule-delete{% endif %}">
    <button type="submit">{% if delete_scheduled %}Cancel delete{% else %}Set to delete{% endif %}</button>
</form>

body.text: The inline script at the bottom of the template attaches a scroll-to-top handler to each form by id; the new form gets the same handler, so all three controls behave identically on submit.

Nothing else in the UI changes. The page view does not display `expires_at` today and does not start to; the button label is the whole of the feedback, because the button reading `Cancel delete` is what tells a reader the page is scheduled.

The unfiled-orphan arm of the sweep is left exactly as it is; only the archived arm narrows to require the new flag. Rejected: making `delete_scheduled` the single condition for any deletion. That reading is defensible from the literal ask, but an unfiled orphan is not in the archive - it is a page a structural bug lost - and it cannot be scheduled from the tree because the tree cannot show it. Making the flag the sole condition would turn that arm into an unbounded leak with no control able to drain it, and would falsify the validator docstring that tells a reader orphans are reclaimed after a grace period. Accepted consequence, recorded so it is not a surprise: a page that is archived and ALSO unfiled is still deleted after its grace period without being scheduled, because it qualifies on the orphan arm. That state arises only from a structural bug, never from archiving a page.

The existing five-day `expires_at` grace period runs after scheduling, unchanged. Scheduling makes a page a candidate, the next hourly sweep stamps it with an expiry at 12:00 UTC five days out, and the sweep after that instant prunes it behind a full workspace backup. Rejected: deleting at the next sweep once the flag is set. That would put a permanent deletion one mis-click away and discard the property the component was built around - nothing is destroyed at the moment a human decides, only days later, and only if the decision still stands. Keeping the delay also means this feature adds no code that deletes: it only changes which pages become candidates, so the backup-before-prune guarantee is inherited rather than re-implemented.

Unarchiving clears `delete_scheduled`, so scheduled implies archived in both directions; cancelling a deletion, by contrast, leaves the page archived, because staying in the archive is the point of the feature. Rejected: leaving a page armed while it is visible. That produces exactly the surprise this feature exists to remove - a page that sits in the tree looking live while carrying a countdown nobody can see - and it contradicts the model the archive already teaches, where unarchiving is the way to rescue a page. Clearing on unarchive makes the visible state honest: anything findable in the tree is not scheduled for deletion.

Only the scheduled page itself is stamped. A descendant hidden beneath it is no longer a stamping target and is removed when the scheduled ancestor's subtree is pruned, which `delete_subtree` already does in full. Rejected: stamping descendants as the current code does. That would make the flag look as though it spreads down a subtree when it is meant to record one person's decision about one page, and it would leave expiries scattered across pages nobody scheduled. Nothing is lost: the subtree still goes as one unit, which is what the existing invariant about descendants promises, and the `covered` maximal-root filter still earns its place for nested scheduled pages and for unfiled orphan subtrees.

summary.body:
Insert a `done` state into the feature-brief lifecycle between `review` and the human `ship` gate, mirroring the shape `simple-change` and `bug-report` already have: an agent `markDone` edge out of review, `ship` moving to hang off done, and `requestChanges` gaining done as a second source. Today a brief goes straight from review to a human gate, so there is no state that says "the agent is finished and this is waiting on a person", and the three activities the brief's own review guidance defers - integrating the work, recording the final shas, reconciling the docs it declared stale - are described as happening at `ship`, on the far side of an edge the agent cannot cross.

Alongside that, `done` gets a stage-guidance text on all three page types, and the feature-brief's merge-process workspace guidance moves from `review` to `done`, so all three hand over this workspace's merge process at the same point - and stop doing it at a status whose own guidance says not to merge yet.

The outcome: reaching `done` on any of the three types tells the agent exactly what remains before a person can close or ship it, including how this workspace integrates finished work.

items.name: src/pagetypes/feature.py - _FEATURE_BRIEF
items.text: Pure declaration data. Holds the feature-brief PageType: its sections, its commands (including `transition_cmd("requestChanges", "review -> building")` and `transition_cmd("ship", "review -> shipped (human gate)", agency="human", guards=(...))` at lines 271-279), its `workspace_guidance` tuple (line 192-195, MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD currently declared for `("review",)`), and its FSMSpec (lines 285-298) with states `draft, grounding, spec, planning, planReview, building, review, shipped, abandoned`, `terminal_states=("shipped", "abandoned")` and six `status_guidance` pairs. The FSM transition table is NOT authored here - `PageType.__post_init__` derives it from the commands, so a new edge is added by adding/altering a command, not by editing the FSM.

items.name: src/pagetypes/feature.py - _COMMIT_LOG_STATES and the two ParentStateGuards
items.text: Pure declaration data in the same module. `_COMMIT_LOG_STATES = ("building", "review", "shipped")` (line 83) is the `legal_in` for recordCommit / markCommitStale. `_FEATURE_IN_SPEC_OR_LATER` (line 307-311) and `_FEATURE_IN_PLANNING_OR_LATER` (line 313-317) list `required_statuses=("spec"|"planning", "planning", "planReview", "building", "review", "shipped")` - these gate the pinned feature-spec's `markSealed` and the two plans' `markReady` on the brief's status. A status inserted between `review` and `shipped` that is missing from these tuples silently locks the pinned children while the brief sits in it.

items.name: src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py
items.text: Pure prose constants, imports nothing at all so it stays a leaf. Holds every production status-guidance text. Relevant constants: `FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW` (feature-brief's own take on `review`, whose closing paragraph says rebasing, recording commits and reconciling stale docs all happen 'at ship') and the bare `REVIEW` shared by simple-change and bug-report (whose closing paragraph says rebasing happens 'at close' and the commit 'is recorded by close itself'). Neither the bare `REVIEW` pair nor anything else declares a text for the `done` status: `done` has no stage guidance on any page type today.

items.name: src/pagetypes/simple_change.py - _SIMPLE_CHANGE
items.text: Pure declaration data. The shape being mirrored: states `("draft", "open", "review", "done", "closed")`, `markDone` review -> done (agent), `requestChanges` legal_in `("review", "done")` -> open (either), `close` / `closeWithoutCommit` done -> closed as human `transition_on_add_cmd` compounds, `reopen` closed -> open. `setPullRequestUrl` is legal_in `("review", "done")` and `_COMMIT_LOG_STATES = ("open", "review", "done", "closed")`. Its `workspace_guidance` already declares MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD for `("done",)`; its `status_guidance` covers only draft, open and review. Declares no `terminal_states`.

items.name: src/pagetypes/bug_report.py - _BUG_REPORT
items.text: Pure declaration data, the same five-state shape as simple-change: same states, same markDone / requestChanges / close / closeWithoutCommit / reopen edges, `setPullRequestUrl` legal_in `("review", "done")`, `_COMMIT_LOG_STATES = ("open", "review", "done", "closed")`, MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD already declared for `("done",)`, and `status_guidance` covering only draft, open and review.

items.name: src/store.py - workspace_guidance() and Store.next_actions()
items.text: `workspace_guidance(page_type, status, config)` (line 75-86) is pure: for each WorkspaceGuidanceSpec whose `guidance_for` contains the status it emits `guidance_<field>` = label + stored text, skipping absent/empty text. `Store.next_actions` (lines 491-502) performs I/O and, for a focused page, adds `guidance` = PAGE_STATUS_GUIDANCE + the status's stage text when one is declared, then merges in the workspace_guidance keys. The two are independent: workspace guidance already emits at a status with no stage guidance. Neither needs changing - both are already driven entirely off the declarations.

items.name: src/fsm.py - build_machine()
items.text: Pure. Builds one python-statemachine class per FSMSpec and infers `final=True` for any state that is not the source of a transition, which is what satisfies the library's trap-state validation. A new `done` state that is the source of outgoing edges is therefore non-final and needs no extra declaration; `terminal_states` on the FSMSpec is a separate, authoring-lock concept and is unrelated to this inference.

items.name: src/pagetypes/epic.py - _EPIC
items.text: Pure declaration data. Read to check the blast radius: the epic root has its own `review -> shipped (human gate)` edge guarded by `ChildStateGuard("feature-brief", ("shipped",), "every child feature-brief must be shipped")` (lines 204-208), and `_EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER` lists `required_statuses=("decomposition", "planReview", "executing", "review", "shipped")` - the epic's own statuses, not the brief's. Inserting `done` into the feature-brief leaves both intact, because briefs still reach `shipped`.

items.name: scripts/feature_brief_probe.py
items.text: Effectful: a manual end-to-end probe that drives a real feature-brief over MCP against a running server, printing the do/blocked/humanGates/attention rollup at each stage. Its docstring states 'The run STOPS at `review`: `ship` is a human gate and the probe never crosses one', and step 14 is `record("14. REVIEW (ship is a human gate - stopping here)", brief)`. Run manually via `just brief-probe`; it is not part of the test suite or CI.

items.name: tests/test_pagetypes.py and tests/test_fsm.py - the production invariants
items.text: Effectful only in that they read the registry. The suite runs in test mode (tests/conftest.py calls `set_test_mode(True)` at import), so production page types are off-limits and behavioural tests run against the `test-*` fixtures in src/testtypes.py. A handful of generic invariants still cover production, either by naming the types from their own modules (`test_every_production_guidance_text_comes_from_the_stage_guidance_module`, which requires every production guidance text to be a constant of `_stage_guidance`) or via the `production_mode` fixture (`test_validate_registry_passes_over_the_production_registry`, `test_production_status_evaluation_matches_the_declared_transition_table`).
CLAUDE.md, verbatim: 'Use the word "create" instead of "mint" when creating something.' and 'Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing.'

Workspace testingTool guidance, verbatim: 'Use `uv run pytest --testmon` to initialize the red/green test cache, then run it again every time to verify tests with changes made.' A --testmon run reporting the affected tests passing is treated as equivalent to the full suite; the suite must not be re-run without --testmon to 'make sure'.
pyproject.toml: `requires-python = ">=3.14"`. Dependencies relevant here: `fastmcp>=3.4.4`, `python-statemachine` (the FSM notes in src/fsm.py are verified against 3.2.0).

tests/conftest.py puts the whole run in test mode: production page types do not resolve, are not listed, and a page of one cannot be created - any attempt raises ProductionTypeInTestError. A test that needs them must ask for the `production_mode` fixture. So no behavioural test can drive a real feature-brief page through its statuses.

tests/test_pagetypes.py::test_every_production_guidance_text_comes_from_the_stage_guidance_module - every text a production page type declares as status_guidance must be a module-level constant of `src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py`. An inline guidance string fails the suite.

`_stage_guidance.py` module docstring, verbatim: 'A constant is named for its status. A bare name is the only text for that status anywhere; a name carrying a page-type prefix is one type's own take on a status name that several types claim.' The existing REVIEW / FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW pair is the worked example of that rule.

`validate_workspace_guidance` (src/pagetypes/core/validation.py, folded into the load-time raise) rejects a `guidance_for` status that is not a real status of the declaring type, and rejects a field several types declare carrying a different description or label in any of them. Both are checked at registry load, so a mistake fails the server's cold start rather than surfacing at runtime.

A page-status edge is declared exactly once, on its command: `PageType.__post_init__` derives `FSMSpec.transitions` from the commands and `legal_in` overrides the source parsed from a transition_cmd's description. An FSMSpec author writes only the status set - writing a transition table there would be overwritten and is not how an edge is added.

src/pagetypes/feature.py declares MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD for `("review",)` while `FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW` in _stage_guidance.py tells the agent, in the same status, that 'rebasing onto main happens at ship, not before'. The workspace's configured mergeProcess text ('Create a github PR for the user to review.') is therefore handed over at exactly the status whose own guidance defers merging. Something has to give: either the review text stops deferring, or the merge guidance moves off `review`.

`FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW` names `ship` as the place three activities happen - 'rebasing onto main happens at ship, not before; recording commits happens after ship, once the shas are final; and reconciling the documentation pages the brief named as going stale also happens at ship'. `ship` is a human edge, so today those three are described as happening on the far side of a gate the agent cannot cross. A `done` state between review and ship is where they actually belong, so that paragraph collides with the new state and must be re-pointed rather than left.

`_COMMIT_LOG_STATES = ("building", "review", "shipped")` in src/pagetypes/feature.py is the legal_in for recordCommit and markCommitStale. A new `done` status absent from it would make the brief's own commit log unwritable in the one status where the final shas exist - the opposite of what simple-change and bug-report do, where `done` is in their `_COMMIT_LOG_STATES`.

`_FEATURE_IN_SPEC_OR_LATER` and `_FEATURE_IN_PLANNING_OR_LATER` enumerate the brief statuses at which the pinned children unlock, and both stop at `review, shipped`. A `done` status missing from them would re-lock the feature-spec's markSealed and both plans' markReady while the brief sits in `done` - a silent regression with no error message, only an edge that disappears from `next`.

src/pagetypes/epic.py keeps its own `review -> shipped` human gate with no `done` in between, so after this change the two root types stop having the same end-of-life shape. The user asked only for the feature-brief, so this is raised rather than fixed: the epic's ship guard reads child briefs' `shipped` status, which still exists, so nothing breaks.

scripts/feature_brief_probe.py documents and implements 'The run STOPS at `review`: `ship` is a human gate and the probe never crosses one'. With `markDone` added, `review` is no longer the last agent edge, so the probe would stop one step short of the end of the agent's reach while still claiming to walk the whole of it.

pasta architecture page 'Page types & FSM implementation' (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2), Details section, the 'Guidance: per status, and per workspace' paragraph: 'architecture and decision-record declare it for authoring, the feature-brief for its six working statuses, and simple-change and bug-report for draft, open and review; every other status takes the absent path'. The counts and the status lists both change.
README.md lines 82-99: the `draft -> ... -> review -> <- human gate -> shipped` ASCII lifecycle diagram for the feature-brief, which shows the human gate hanging directly off `review`.
pasta document page 'GitHub README (user-facing)' (document:mtiodadq-2fb6a6) - the page that mirrors README.md, including the feature-brief lifecycle diagram section it describes verbatim.

scripts/feature_brief_probe.py module docstring, the line 'The run STOPS at `review`: `ship` is a human gate and the probe never crosses one.' - stale as soon as `markDone` exists, whether or not the probe itself is extended.
Should the feature-brief's mergeProcess workspace guidance MOVE from `review` to `done`, or be shown at both? Showing it at `review` contradicts that status's own text, which defers merging.
items.answer: Move it to `done` only. Emitting it at `review` contradicts that status's own text, which defers merging; leaving it there and adding done would have the server contradict itself in a single response. Recorded in the spec's decisions.

items.text: Should `done` carry one shared stage-guidance constant across all three page types, or a bare DONE for simple-change and bug-report plus a FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE of its own - mirroring the existing REVIEW / FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW pair? The three differ in what remains at `done`: the brief records its own commits and reconciles stale docs, while the other two have their commit recorded by the human `close` compound itself.
items.answer: Two constants, mirroring REVIEW / FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW: a bare `DONE` shared by simple-change and bug-report, and a `FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE` of its own. The brief records its own commits and reconciles stale docs at done; on the other two the human `close` compound records the commit itself, so one shared text could not be true for both. Recorded in the spec's decisions.

items.text: Should `abandon` become legal from `done` on the feature-brief? It is currently legal in draft through review, and simple-change and bug-report offer no abandon at all to mirror.
items.answer: No. `abandon` keeps its legal_in of draft through review. The two types being mirrored offer no abandon at all, and a human who wants to drop the work at done has `requestChanges` into building, where abandon is already legal. Recorded in the spec's decisions.

items.text: Should scripts/feature_brief_probe.py be extended one step to drive `review -> done` and stop there, or left at `review` with only its docstring corrected?
items.answer: Extend it one step to `markDone` and stop at `done`. The probe's job is to print the rollup at every stage the agent can reach; left at review it would never print the rollup at done, which is the stage this feature adds and where the merge-process guidance now appears. Recorded in the spec's decisions.

items.text: Do all three activities the review guidance defers - integrating the work, recording the final shas, and reconciling the documentation pages the brief named as going stale - move to the new `done` state, or only integration?
items.answer: Only integration moves to `done`. Recording the final commits and reconciling the stale documentation pages stay after `ship`: the human gate is what authorizes them, and a `done` state that reconciles documentation before a person has signed off has the agent updating the wiki on the strength of its own review - which is exactly the gate the state was supposed to be standing in front of. Settled by the user while the brief was in review; the first build had moved all three and is being corrected.

items.text: What exactly does the `done` stage tell the agent to do? The phrase "integrate the work" is ambiguous about whether the work is merged at that point.
items.answer: `done` means the work is DONE - finished and verified - and explicitly not merged, not closed and not shipped. The text has to say that outright, because "integrate the work" reads as permission to merge. Beyond stating it, the status carries exactly two pieces of work, both conditional: update the recorded commit shas if any moved, and follow the workspace's merge-process guidance if there is one. If neither applies there is nothing to do at `done` at all, and that is a correct and expected outcome rather than a sign something was missed. Settled by the user during the build.

findings.issue: Implementation-plan step 5 (insert the done status into the feature-brief lifecycle): the expected output pinned under its verification command listed four lines, but the command filters events markDone, requestChanges, ship AND abandon with source in review or done - and abandon keeps review as a source, so it prints a fifth line, 'abandon review -> abandoned human'. An implementer comparing real output against the pinned output would read a correct edit as a failure and could revert it. Applied by editing the step: the fifth line is now in the expected output, plus a paragraph saying that a SIXTH line 'abandon done -> abandoned human' would mean done was wrongly added to abandon's legal_in - which turns the extra line from a trap into the check that the spec's 'abandon is unchanged' decision actually held.

DONE = """
done - the work is written, verified and done. It is not merged, not closed and not
signed off: this status says the agent has nothing left to build, and it says nothing
more than that. There is one thing to do here, and only if it applies:

- Follow the merge process guidance beside this text, if this workspace configured
  one, and leave the pull request url on the page if that produces one. With no merge
  process configured there is nothing to do at all, which is the expected outcome and
  not a sign something was missed.

Nothing is built here and no commit is recorded: close records it. Closing is a human
edge, and closing is where the work is actually merged - drive up to that gate and
stop. If anything turns up outstanding, use requestChanges to go back to open rather
than leave a known gap at the gate.
"""

FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE = """
done - the build is verified and the work is done. It is not merged, not shipped and
not signed off: this status says the agent has nothing left to build, and it says
nothing more than that. There are two things to do here, and each only if it applies:

- Update the recorded commits if their shas moved, flagging as stale any sha that has
  left history. If none moved, there is nothing to do.
- Follow the merge process guidance beside this text, if this workspace configured
  one, and leave the pull request url on the page if that produces one. If there is no
  merge process, there is nothing to do.

With neither applying there is nothing to do at done at all, which is the expected
outcome and not a sign something was missed. Recording the final commits waits until
after ship, once the shas are final, and reconciling the documentation pages the brief
named as going stale waits for ship too: the sign-off is what authorizes both, and
doing either here would cross the gate rather than drive up to it. Shipping is a human
edge: drive up to it and stop. If anything turns up outstanding, use requestChanges to
go back to building rather than leave a known gap for the ship gate to find.
"""

# 1. the import block at the top of the file, adding one name alphabetically:
from ._stage_guidance import (
    BUILDING,
    FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE,
    FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW,
    GROUNDING,
    PLANNING,
    PLAN_REVIEW,
    SPEC,
)

# 2. the three transition commands. requestChanges and ship are edited in place;
#    markDone is new and goes immediately before requestChanges.
#
# FROM:
        transition_cmd("requestChanges", "review -> building", agency="either"),
        transition_cmd("ship", "review -> shipped (human gate)", agency="human", guards=(
            ChildStateGuard("implementation-plan", ("done", "skipped"),
                            "every implementation-plan step must be done or skipped",
                            section="steps", field="items"),
            ChildStateGuard("testing-plan", ("passed", "skipped"),
                            "every testing-plan case must be passed or skipped",
                            section="cases", field="items"),
        )),
#
# TO:
        transition_cmd("markDone", "review -> done"),
        transition_cmd("requestChanges", "review or done -> building",
                       legal_in=("review", "done"), agency="either"),
        transition_cmd("ship", "done -> shipped (human gate)", agency="human", guards=(
            ChildStateGuard("implementation-plan", ("done", "skipped"),
                            "every implementation-plan step must be done or skipped",
                            section="steps", field="items"),
            ChildStateGuard("testing-plan", ("passed", "skipped"),
                            "every testing-plan case must be passed or skipped",
                            section="cases", field="items"),
        )),

# 3. and 4. the FSMSpec at the bottom of the _FEATURE_BRIEF declaration: one status
#    inserted between review and shipped, one guidance pair appended.
    fsm=FSMSpec(
        name="FeatureBrief",
        initial="draft",
        states=("draft", "grounding", "spec", "planning", "planReview", "building", "review",
                "done", "shipped", "abandoned"),
        terminal_states=("shipped", "abandoned"),
        status_guidance=(
            ("grounding", GROUNDING),
            ("spec", SPEC),
            ("planning", PLANNING),
            ("planReview", PLAN_REVIEW),
            ("building", BUILDING),
            ("review", FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW),
            ("done", FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE),
        ),
    ),

items.text: Note on how this plan is verified, read this first. The suite runs in test mode (tests/conftest.py calls set_test_mode(True) at import), so the production page types do not resolve, are not listed, and a page of one cannot be created - any attempt raises ProductionTypeInTestError. No test can therefore drive a real feature-brief page through its statuses, and the project deliberately does not pin production declarations with tests (the architecture page records one such test being written and then removed as overzealous). So the cases below split three ways: existing generic invariants in the suite that cover production and must stay green; direct assertions over the pure functions, run as one-off commands against the production declarations; and one manual end-to-end probe run. Every one of them can come out false.

The production registry still validates. Setup: the change is applied. Action: run `uv run pytest tests/test_pagetypes.py -k production --testmon`. Expected: test_validate_registry_passes_over_the_production_registry, test_declaration_errors_is_none_for_the_production_registry and test_production_types_are_exactly_the_registered_ones all pass. This is the case that would fail if a status_guidance pair named a status the feature-brief does not have, or if the mergeProcess guidance_for named an unknown status - validate_fsm_spec and validate_workspace_guidance are both folded into that raise.

Both new guidance texts live in the stage-guidance module rather than inline. Setup: the change is applied. Action: run `uv run pytest tests/test_pagetypes.py::test_every_production_guidance_text_comes_from_the_stage_guidance_module --testmon`. Expected: it passes, having found DONE and FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE among the module's constants. It fails if either text was written inline in a page-type module.

Every production status machine still builds and agrees with its declared table. Setup: the change is applied. Action: run `uv run pytest tests/test_fsm.py --testmon`. Expected: test_every_production_page_type_holds_its_machine and test_production_status_evaluation_matches_the_declared_transition_table both pass. The second one is what exercises the three changed feature-brief edges through the real python-statemachine class rather than through the declaration; it fails if the derived table and the built machine disagree, and the build itself fails on a trap state or an unreachable status.

The docs still generate for every production type. Setup: the change is applied. Action: run `uv run pytest tests/test_docsgen.py --testmon`. Expected: test_page_machine_qualname_resolves_for_every_production_type passes, so the FeatureBriefMachine still resolves through src/statecharts.py with its new status set and a doc page can be rendered for the new state.

done is reachable from review and is the only source of ship. Setup: the change is applied. Action: run the command below, which asks the built machine directly rather than reading the declaration. Expected output, exactly: `review: ['abandon', 'markDone', 'requestChanges']` then `done: ['requestChanges', 'ship']`. It fails if markDone was not added, if ship still hangs off review, or if abandon leaked into done.

Action: run the command below. Expected output, exactly: `True True True True True`. The five checks are, in order: the review text's first clause now points at done; the review text still defers reconciling the stale documentation pages to ship; the review text still defers recording commits to ship; the done text says both of those wait for ship; and the done text states outright that the work is not merged and not shipped. DONE (ship is a human gate - stopping here)'; the rollup printed under it lists ship as a human gate and markDone is gone from do; and the guidance printed for the page at done carries both the PAGE STATUS GUIDANCE done text and the MERGE PROCESS GUIDANCE line. The probe then archives the brief. It fails if the walk stops at 14, or if the done rollup shows the pinned children's finalize edges blocked on a parent-state reason.

Nothing else in the suite regressed. Setup: the change is applied and the testmon cache initialized with one `uv run pytest --testmon` run. Action: run `uv run pytest --testmon` again. Expected: no failures. The deselected tests are deselected because testmon established the change cannot reach them, so this run stands in for the full suite and must not be re-run without --testmon. overview.body:
This spec covers one subsystem: the page-type declarations under src/pagetypes/. It inserts a done status into the feature-brief lifecycle between review and the human ship gate, mirroring the shape simple-change and bug-report already have, gives done a stage-guidance text on all three page types, and moves the feature-brief's merge-process workspace guidance from review onto done so that every one of the three types hands over the workspace merge process at the same point.

Everything here is declaration data plus prose. No engine code changes: the FSM table is derived from the commands, the guidance emission in store.workspace_guidance and Store.next_actions is already driven entirely off the declarations, and fsm.build_machine already infers finality from the derived transitions. The one non-declaration edit is to scripts/feature_brief_probe.py, a manual probe whose stated stopping point becomes wrong.

Deliberately out of scope: the epic page type, which keeps its own review to shipped human gate; the abandon edge, which stays legal in draft through review only; and reconciling README.md and the two pasta pages the brief listed as going stale, which happens once the implementation has landed rather than as part of it.

body.text: The feature-brief lifecycle after the change

One status is inserted. review stops being the source of the human ship edge and becomes the source of an agent markDone edge; done becomes the source of ship. requestChanges gains done as a second source, exactly as it has on simple-change and bug-report, so a gap found at done sends the work back to building rather than through the gate. No status is removed or renamed, and shipped and abandoned stay terminal.

body.source:
draft -> grounding -> spec -> planning -> planReview -> building -> review -> done -> shipped
                                                            ^                  |        |
                                                            |                  |        (human)
                                                            +--- requestChanges +

markDone        review -> done            agent
requestChanges  review | done -> building  either
ship            done -> shipped            human   (keeps both ChildStateGuards)
abandon         draft..review -> abandoned human   (unchanged: done is NOT a source)

body.text: Where the merge-process guidance is emitted

All three page types end up declaring MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD for the single status done. simple-change and bug-report already do; the feature-brief moves from review to done. Nothing in the emission path changes: store.workspace_guidance is a pure function of the page type, the status and the workspace config, and it already emits a guidance_ key at a status whether or not that status also carries stage guidance.

body.source:
# src/pagetypes/feature.py, in _FEATURE_BRIEF.workspace_guidance
WorkspaceGuidanceSpec(MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD, ("done",), MERGE_PROCESS_DESC, MERGE_PROCESS_LABEL),
# TESTING_TOOL_FIELD ("building",) and GROUNDING_TOOL_FIELD ("grounding",) are unchanged.

# src/pagetypes/simple_change.py and src/pagetypes/bug_report.py: already ("done",), unchanged.

body.text: Stage guidance for done: two constants, mirroring REVIEW and FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW

done means different work on the two sides, so it gets the same two-constant treatment the review status already has: a bare DONE shared by simple-change and bug-report, and a FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE that is the brief's own. What differs is the gate each one stands in front of and what that gate authorizes. On simple-change and bug-report the human close command records the commit itself, so nothing is left for the agent to record. On the feature-brief the human ship gate is what authorizes recording the final shas and reconciling the documentation the brief declared stale, so neither is due at done and the text has to say so rather than leave the agent to assume. Both constants live in src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py, which is what the production-guidance invariant in tests/test_pagetypes.py requires.

body.source:
# src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py, in the "simple-change and bug-report, shared"
# section, immediately after REVIEW.

DONE = """
done - the work is written, verified and done. It is not merged, not closed and not
signed off: this status says the agent has nothing left to build, and it says nothing
more than that. There is one thing to do here, and only if it applies:

- Follow the merge process guidance beside this text, if this workspace configured
  one, and leave the pull request url on the page if that produces one. With no merge
  process configured there is nothing to do at all, which is the expected outcome and
  not a sign something was missed.

Nothing is built here and no commit is recorded: close records it. Closing is a human
edge, and closing is where the work is actually merged - drive up to that gate and
stop. If anything turns up outstanding, use requestChanges to go back to open rather
than leave a known gap at the gate.
"""

# src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py, in the feature-brief section, immediately after
# FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW.

FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE = """
done - the build is verified and the work is done. It is not merged, not shipped and
not signed off: this status says the agent has nothing left to build, and it says
nothing more than that. There are two things to do here, and each only if it applies:

- Update the recorded commits if their shas moved, flagging as stale any sha that has
  left history. If none moved, there is nothing to do.
- Follow the merge process guidance beside this text, if this workspace configured
  one, and leave the pull request url on the page if that produces one. If there is no
  merge process, there is nothing to do.

With neither applying there is nothing to do at done at all, which is the expected
outcome and not a sign something was missed. Recording the final commits waits until
after ship, once the shas are final, and reconciling the documentation pages the brief
named as going stale waits for ship too: the sign-off is what authorizes both, and
doing either here would cross the gate rather than drive up to it. Shipping is a human
edge: drive up to it and stop. If anything turns up outstanding, use requestChanges to
go back to building rather than leave a known gap for the ship gate to find.
"""

body.text: FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW is re-pointed at done

Only one of the three activities the review text defers actually moves, and it is renamed on the way. Review stops saying "rebasing onto main happens at ship" and says instead that following the merge process happens at done - which is what the agent can legitimately do before a person has signed anything off, because the merge process is what prepares the gate rather than crosses it. Recording the final shas and reconciling the stale documentation pages do not move at all: the human ship gate is what authorizes them, so an agent doing either at done would be acting on the strength of its own review instead of a person's, which is the gate this state was meant to stand in front of. Three passages of the constant change and nothing else in it is touched: the opening sentence, the first clause of the closing paragraph, and its last line.

body.source:

# the opening sentence, FROM:

body.text: src/pagetypes/feature.py: the declaration edits

Seven edits, all of them data. The FSM transition table is not written here; it is derived from the commands by PageType post-init, so the three edges are changed by editing their transition_cmd calls and the FSMSpec carries only the status set and the guidance pairs.

body.source:
# 1. the import, adding the new constant alphabetically among the existing ones
from ._stage_guidance import (
    BUILDING,
    FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE,
    FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW,
    GROUNDING,
    PLANNING,
    PLAN_REVIEW,
    SPEC,
)

# 2. the commit log opens at done, where the final shas exist
_COMMIT_LOG_STATES = ("building", "review", "done", "shipped")

# 3. workspace guidance: merge process moves off review
WorkspaceGuidanceSpec(MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD, ("done",), MERGE_PROCESS_DESC, MERGE_PROCESS_LABEL),

# 4. the pull request url stays writable at done, as on the other two types
set_scalar_cmd("pull_request", "url", name="setPullRequestUrl", label="pull request url",
               legal_in=("review", "done")),

# 5. the three edges
transition_cmd("markDone", "review -> done"),
transition_cmd("requestChanges", "review or done -> building",
               legal_in=("review", "done"), agency="either"),
transition_cmd("ship", "done -> shipped (human gate)", agency="human", guards=(
    ChildStateGuard("implementation-plan", ("done", "skipped"),
                    "every implementation-plan step must be done or skipped",
                    section="steps", field="items"),
    ChildStateGuard("testing-plan", ("passed", "skipped"),
                    "every testing-plan case must be passed or skipped",
                    section="cases", field="items"),
)),

# 6. the FSM: one status inserted, one guidance pair appended
fsm=FSMSpec(
    name="FeatureBrief",
    initial="draft",
    states=("draft", "grounding", "spec", "planning", "planReview", "building", "review",
            "done", "shipped", "abandoned"),
    terminal_states=("shipped", "abandoned"),
    status_guidance=(
        ("grounding", GROUNDING),
        ("spec", SPEC),
        ("planning", PLANNING),
        ("planReview", PLAN_REVIEW),
        ("building", BUILDING),
        ("review", FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW),
        ("done", FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE),
    ),
),

# 7. the two ParentStateGuards admit the new status, so the pinned children stay unlocked
_FEATURE_IN_SPEC_OR_LATER = ParentStateGuard(
    parent_type="feature-brief",
    required_statuses=("spec", "planning", "planReview", "building", "review", "done", "shipped"),
    message="the feature-brief must be in spec or later",
)

_FEATURE_IN_PLANNING_OR_LATER = ParentStateGuard(
    parent_type="feature-brief",
    required_statuses=("planning", "planReview", "building", "review", "done", "shipped"),
    message="the feature-brief must be in planning or later",
)

The probe exists to show which instructions the server hands an agent at which stage, and it stops where the agent's reach ends. markDone extends that reach by one, so the probe follows it and stops at done, which is where the human ship gate now sits. Three edits: the lifecycle line and the stopping-point line in the module docstring, and one more mutate plus record after step 14.

body.text: What the change cannot get wrong silently, and what it can

Three of the edits fail loudly if missed. A guidance pair naming a status the type does not have is rejected by validate_fsm_spec in the load-time raise. A workspace-guidance guidance_for naming an unknown status is rejected by validate_workspace_guidance in the same raise. An inline guidance string instead of a _stage_guidance constant fails the production-guidance invariant in tests/test_pagetypes.py. A malformed edge set fails python-statemachine's connectivity and trap-state checks when the machine is built, which the aggregated validator reports.

Two can go wrong quietly, and are the reason they are called out here rather than left to the diff. Forgetting done in either ParentStateGuard re-locks the pinned feature-spec and the two plans while the brief sits in done: no error, just markSealed and markReady disappearing from next with a parent-state reason. Forgetting done in _COMMIT_LOG_STATES makes recordCommit illegal in the one status whose own guidance tells the agent to record commits: that one surfaces as an IllegalCommandError only when an agent tries it.

Move it. The feature-brief declares MERGE_PROCESS_FIELD for ("done",) only, so all three page types hand over the workspace merge process at the same point. Showing it at both was rejected: the review text tells the agent in so many words that merging is not part of that status, so emitting the merge process there is the server contradicting itself in a single response, and leaving the contradiction in place would undercut the new state's whole reason to exist. Leaving it on review alone was rejected for the same reason plus a second one: done would then be the only status in the flow with no instruction of any kind.

Two constants: a bare DONE for simple-change and bug-report, and FEATURE_BRIEF_DONE for the brief, exactly mirroring the existing REVIEW and FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW pair and the naming rule in the _stage_guidance module docstring. One shared constant was rejected because the two sides genuinely differ at this status: the brief records its own commits and reconciles the documentation it declared stale, while on the other two the human close compound records the commit itself, so a single text would have to either tell the brief's agent nothing about its commit log or tell the other two to record a commit that close will record for them. Three separate prefixed constants were rejected as duplication: simple-change and bug-report already share their REVIEW text and have identical resolution shapes, so nothing distinguishes their done.

No. abandon keeps its explicit legal_in of draft, grounding, spec, planning, planReview, building, review. A brief in done has verified work behind it, and the two types being mirrored offer no abandon at all, so there is no shape to copy. A human who does want to drop the work at that point has requestChanges into building, where abandon is already legal, so nothing is unreachable; adding the source would be an edge the ask did not call for.

Extend it by one step, to markDone, and stop at done. The probe's stated job is to walk the lifecycle to the end of the agent's reach and print the rollup at each stage; markDone moves that end, so a probe left at review would stop one stage short of the thing this feature adds, and the rollup at done - which is where the merge process guidance now appears - would never be printed by the tool built to print it. Correcting only the docstring was rejected as leaving the probe accurate about itself but useless for the change it is meant to exercise.

Only integration moves to done. Recording the final commits and reconciling the documentation pages the brief declared stale both stay after ship. Moving all three was the first build's mistake and it broke the thing the state was added to protect: the ship gate is what authorizes touching the wiki and writing the final shas, so an agent doing either at done reconciles documentation on the strength of its own review, with no person having signed anything off. What legitimately belongs at done is the work that PREPARES the gate rather than crosses it - integrating per the workspace merge process, which in this workspace means opening a pull request for a person to review, and flagging any recorded commit whose sha that integration invalidated. Rejected: moving all three (breaks the gate, as above). Rejected: moving none of them, which would leave done with no work of its own and the merge-process guidance arriving at a status that has nothing to do with it.

The done text states outright that the work is done and is NOT merged, closed or shipped, and then carries exactly two conditional pieces of work: update the recorded commit shas if any moved, and follow the workspace merge-process guidance if there is one. If neither applies, there is nothing to do at done, and the text says so explicitly so that an agent finding nothing to do does not go looking for work to invent. Rejected: the phrase "integrate the work", which reads as permission to merge and leaves the agent to guess how far integration goes - the whole point of the state is that the work has stopped short of merging. Rejected: naming the concrete merge steps (rebase, push, open a pull request) in the stage text, because those belong to the workspace's own mergeProcess guidance, which is emitted beside this text and is the one place that knows them; the stage text points at it rather than duplicating and contradicting it.

summary.body: Make the pasta MCP's request surface self-describing so an authoring agent never has to guess. Four outcomes: (1) the `instructions` text carries each request tool's JSON `name` and `input_schema` so agents stop guessing parameter names; (2) the `instructions` text describes workspace-guidance setup, naming the settable fields without detailing each one; (3) `describePageType` requires a page type and fails when none is given, rather than treating it as optional; (4) a separate tool enumerates all page types (replacing describePageType's list mode) and, since every page type is already named in the instructions, that tool does not itself need advertising. The result is agents that author correctly on the first call because instructions plus introspection are complete, instead of inferring parameter names or leaning on describePageType's list mode.

overview.body: Make the pasta MCP request surface self-describing, entirely within the MCP tool shell (src/server.py) plus one new pure module (src/instructions.py). Four changes: (1) instructions() gains a projected section listing each request tool's JSON name and input_schema so agents stop guessing argument names; (2) instructions() also gains a short section naming the settable workspace-guidance fields; (3) describePageType requires a `type` and no longer lists types when it is omitted; (4) a new listPageTypes tool takes over enumeration. Deliberately unchanged: the page-type registry, the store, the renderer, and the pure describe_page_type projection. The docsite generator and the architecture/README pages are not edited here - documentation is reconciled at ship.

body.text: Scope and touched files

Changes are confined to the MCP shell and one new pure module. src/server.py: the instructions() and describePageType() tools change, and a listPageTypes() tool is added. src/instructions.py (new, pure): holds the prose and assembles the projected sections. tests/test_server.py: new integration tests. No changes to src/describe.py, the registry, the store, or the renderer.
Task 2 - describePageType requires a type

Make `type` a required parameter and drop the None-listing branch. FastMCP rejects a missing required argument at the schema boundary, so no manual None check remains; an unknown type keeps the existing ToolError naming the registered types. The tool description loses its 'Omit type to list types' sentence.
Task 3 - listPageTypes tool

A new read tool returning exactly the shape the removed None-branch returned, so the enumerate-all-page-types capability is preserved. It is excluded from the instructions schema listing (Task 1) because the page types are already named in the instructions prose, but it stays a normal tool visible in tools/list.
Tasks 1 & 4 - self-describing instructions

instructions() stops returning a static literal. A new pure module src/instructions.py holds the static prose (moved verbatim from the current tool) and assembles two projected sections: the request tools' JSON name/input_schema, and the settable workspace-guidance field names. instructions() becomes a thin shell that gathers the live inputs and calls the pure renderer, so the text cannot drift from the tools and registry it describes.

body.source:
# src/instructions.py  (pure - no I/O)
HIDDEN_FROM_SCHEMAS = frozenset({"instructions", "listPageTypes"})

_PROSE = """<the existing instructions prose, moved here verbatim>"""

def render_tool_schemas(tools: list[tuple[str, dict]]) -> str:
    """A '## Request tool schemas' section: a fenced json block of
    [{"name", "input_schema"}] for every tool NOT in HIDDEN_FROM_SCHEMAS,
    sorted by name for deterministic output."""

def render_guidance_fields(fields: list[str]) -> str:
    """A '## Workspace guidance setup' section naming setWorkspaceGuidance and
    listing the field names only (no per-field descriptions)."""

def render_instructions(tools: list[tuple[str, dict]],
                        guidance_fields: list[str]) -> str:
    """_PROSE + guidance-fields section + tool-schemas section."""

# src/server.py  (shell)
from .instructions import render_instructions
from .pagetypes._registry import workspace_guidance_fields  # added import

@mcp.tool
async def instructions() -> str:
    """Retrieve instructions for pasta MCP."""
    tools = [(t.name, t.to_mcp_tool().inputSchema) for t in mcp.list_tools()]
    return render_instructions(tools, sorted(workspace_guidance_fields()))

body.text: Assembly order: prose, then the workspace-guidance section, then the schema section. render_tool_schemas filters HIDDEN_FROM_SCHEMAS and sorts by name so output is deterministic and test-stable; each entry is {"name": <tool>, "input_schema": <inputSchema>} serialized with json.dumps(indent=2) inside a fenced json block. mcp.list_tools() is synchronous in fastmcp 3.4.4 and to_mcp_tool().inputSchema is the exact client-visible schema. The tool set is independent of test mode, whereas workspace_guidance_fields() follows the registry in play (fixtures under test mode, production fields on a live server).
Pure / effect split and error paths

Pure: everything in src/instructions.py - functions of their inputs alone, no I/O, unit-testable with synthetic tool lists and field names. Effectful shell: the three server.py tools; instructions() reads the live tool list and the registry, describePageType/listPageTypes read the registry. Error paths: a describePageType call missing `type` is rejected by FastMCP argument validation and surfaces as a tool error; an unknown type raises the existing ToolError naming registered types; listPageTypes and instructions add no new error paths. The render_* functions are total - a zero-arg tool renders an empty properties object, and an empty guidance-field list renders a short 'none configured' line.
Scope refinement - named tools only (during build)

Per a user request during the build, the request-schema section lists only the tools the instructions text already names, not the whole registered surface. render_tool_schemas takes a second argument named_text and includes a tool only when its backticked reference (a `name` or `name(` occurrence) appears in that text. This replaces the HIDDEN_FROM_SCHEMAS constant shown above: the prose is now the single source of truth for which tools appear, and it already omits instructions and listPageTypes, so no hidden-list is needed. render_instructions builds named_text as the prose plus the workspace-guidance section, then passes it to render_tool_schemas - so a tool named only in the guidance section (setWorkspaceGuidance) is included too. With the current prose the listed set is attention, createPage, describeMutations, describePageType, listWorkspaces, mutatePageBatch, nextActions, search, setWorkspaceGuidance and tree.

Chosen: generate the schema section dynamically from mcp.list_tools() at call time, formatted by a pure renderer. Rejected: hardcoding the JSON in the instructions string - it would drift from the real tool signatures the moment any tool's arguments change, which is the exact failure this feature removes. A call-time projection is the same anti-drift guarantee pasta's page-type docsgen already relies on.

Chosen: list every registered tool except `instructions` (a zero-arg, self-referential bootstrap) and `listPageTypes` (the ask says it need not be advertised), via HIDDEN_FROM_SCHEMAS. Rejected: a hand-curated subset - it would itself drift and leave whatever was omitted back in the guessing regime this feature removes.

Chosen: name the tool listPageTypes in camelCase. Rejected: 'ListPageTypes' (PascalCase, as the ask wrote it informally) - every existing tool is camelCase (listWorkspaces, describePageType, describeMutations, ...), so matching the convention keeps the surface consistent.

Chosen: a short 'Workspace guidance setup' section that names setWorkspaceGuidance and lists only the settable field names, generated from workspace_guidance_fields(). Rejected: including each field's description - the ask explicitly says no detailed descriptions, and per-field descriptions remain available via describePageType's workspaceGuidance.

Chosen: list only the tools the instructions prose already names - a tool qualifies when its backticked reference (`name` or `name(`) appears in the text above the schema section. Rejected: listing every registered tool minus a HIDDEN_FROM_SCHEMAS set, which dumps the whole surface (archiving, reparent, link, rename, ...) the instructions never discuss. Making the prose the source of truth also removes the need for a hidden-list, since the prose already omits instructions and listPageTypes. This supersedes the earlier decision on question mumkd11p (all-minus-hidden).

summary.body: Today the review-status guidance (FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW for feature-briefs, and the shared REVIEW for simple-change and bug-report) asks the agent to verify implementation, test runs, regressions, purity and comments, but says nothing about tests that only guard code the change removed, and its comment-review bullet does not cover wordy explanations of well-known technology concepts. Add one bullet to both review texts telling the agent to remove tests that have now run and passed but are conditioned on removed parts of the code - for example asserting that a removed field no longer exists - and extend the comment-review bullet in both to say wordy explanations of well-known technology concepts should be removed.

motivation.body: Requested by the user: "Add extra item to review state: Remove tests that have now executed but that are conditioned on removed parts of code, such as asserts that a field doesn't exist. This is a simple change to edit the texts." and, as a follow-up, "Also add the review comment instructions: remove wordy explanations of well known technology concepts". Red-green work on removals produces tests that assert absence; once the removal is verified they only pin a past implementation and add noise to the suite. Comments explaining well-known concepts add verbosity without informing the reader.

criteria.text: FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW contains a bullet telling the agent to remove tests that have run but are conditioned on removed code, with the example of asserting a field does not exist.
The shared REVIEW text (simple-change and bug-report) contains the same bullet.
No other status guidance text changes, and the existing review bullets stay as they were.
The full test suite passes, including any generated page-type documentation checks.
The comment-review bullet in both FEATURE_BRIEF_REVIEW and REVIEW says wordy explanations of well-known technology concepts should be removed.

summary.body: Stage 1 of a staged pyright cleanup. The most impactful fix is the command declaration: one `CommandSpec` dataclass carries a `kind` string plus a dozen optional per-kind fields, so every consumer passes `str | None` where `str` is needed (16 of the 24 pyright errors) and guards `is None` everywhere. Replace it with one frozen dataclass per command kind, inheriting from shared group bases, and declare `type CommandSpec = ...` over them (built from an `AuthoringCommand` subset of the non-transition kinds), so a command's fields are exactly the ones its kind uses and pyright narrows by isinstance/match. A compound keeps its generic steps, and each step is applied as a command in its own right - argument validation, legality and store prechecks - with a page-status transition no longer allowed as a step. Also disable `reportPrivateUsage` in the pyright config (71 warnings, accepted for now). Behaviour and the describe JSON contract are otherwise unchanged. Later stages (JSON data model Any, describe payload TypedDicts, hmr dev tooling, lint noise) are recorded but not done here.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/commands.py
items.text: Pure. Declares the single frozen `CommandSpec` dataclass (kind: str plus 12 optional/defaulted per-kind fields: section, field, event, dest, element_map, element_const, element_field, steps, requires, legal_in, ref_check, guards, parent_guards, plus an unused `generated`) and every command factory (set_prose_cmd, set_scalar_cmd, list_cmds, element_cmds, set_element_field_cmd, blocks_cmds, element_blocks_cmds, transition_cmd, transition_on_add_cmd, add_link_cmd, set_title_cmd) and is_field_setter. 3 explicit Any (element_const value, element_cmds marks extra-args, set_element_field_cmd const). The declaration being replaced.

items.name: src/commands.py
items.text: Pure write path. `_apply` dispatches on `command.kind` across 14 kinds; helpers _add_element, _apply_element_writes, _entry_context, _target_entries, _entry_id, _find_element, _element_transition, _add_block, _remove_by_id read section/field/event/element_field off the generic spec. Source of 16 of the 24 pyright errors (str | None passed where str is required, commands.py:340-517). Also unmet_requirements / _is_status_transition / field_setter_edges read requires/event/section/field over every command.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/pagetype.py
items.text: Pure. PageType.__post_init__ `_resolve_block_vocabularies` does `dataclasses.replace(command, args=...)` on every command and `_resolved_arg` reads section/field/element_field/kind; `_status_transitions` derives the FSM table from kind/event/dest/legal_in/agency with `is not None` guards; get_pagetype_command returns `CommandSpec | None`.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/validation.py
items.text: Pure. validate_pagetype_field_setters, validate_pagetype_setter_descriptions and validate_pagetype_block_args read section/field/element_field/kind with `is None` checks over every command.

items.name: src/describe.py
items.text: Pure projection. `_command_summary` emits name/kind/description/section/field/event/agency/legalIn/requires/args for every command - this JSON shape is the public describePageType/describeMutations MCP contract and the docsgen input, so it must stay byte-identical (null where a kind has no such field).

items.name: src/store.py
items.text: Effects (file storage). next_actions loop reads kind/event/agency (store.py:451-461); _check_ref reads ref_check; _child_guard_failure / _parent_guard_failure read guards / parent_guards for any command; _check_link reads kind == ADD_LINK; _check_block_refs / _check_inline_refs read args only.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/specs.py
items.text: Pure. The kind string constants (SET_SCALAR ... SET_TITLE, plain `str` assignments) used as the `kind` discriminator and emitted in describe output.

items.name: pyproject.toml [tool.pyright]
items.text: Config: typeCheckingMode = "recommended", reportAny = false, reportExplicitAny = false, include = ["src/**/*"]. reportPrivateUsage is on via recommended (71 warnings) - to be disabled here. Tests are not type-checked.

items.name: tests/test_pagetypes.py, tests/test_fsm.py
items.text: Tests construct raw `CommandSpec(name, KIND, ...)` positionally (test_pagetypes.py:338, 369, 935, 938, 993, 1003, 1010, 1019) and read section/field/event/dest/element_field/requires off commands gated by kind checks (test_pagetypes.py:148-322, 838, 952). test_fsm.py imports CommandSpec as an annotation only.
requires-python = ">=3.14" (pyproject.toml) - the PEP 695 `type X = ...` statement is available.

Type checker is basedpyright>=1.39.9 (dev group), run as `uv run basedpyright`; config `typeCheckingMode = "recommended"`, `include = ["src/**/*"]`. Baseline measured 2026-10-02: 24 errors, 306 warnings; with reportAny/reportExplicitAny on: 368 errors (197 reportAny, 147 reportExplicitAny).

Tests run with pytest (`uv run pytest --testmon`, CLAUDE.md: 'Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing'). Production page types are off-limits in tests (test-registry swap); tests use src.testtypes fixtures.

The describePageType / describeMutations command summary JSON (name, kind, description, section, field, event, agency, legalIn, requires, args) is a public MCP contract and must not change; kind strings stay as declared in core/specs.py.

core/ layering is acyclic: specs -> args -> fields -> commands -> pagetype -> validation, each module importing only upward; spec dataclasses stay frozen values comparing by content (architecture page 'Page types & FSM implementation').
CLAUDE.md copy rule: use the word "create" instead of "mint".

User preference (2026-10-15): no additional apply functions. Command application stays split between the existing apply_command (name lookup, page copy, section backfill) and _apply (argument validation, legality check, dispatch); validation moves into _apply rather than into a new function, so a compound's steps get it by recursing into _apply.
CommandSpec.generated (core/commands.py:87) is declared but never set or read anywhere in src or tests - dead field. The new per-kind declarations must decide whether to carry it; proposal: drop it.

COMPOUND carries `steps: tuple[CommandSpec, ...]` whose inner TRANSITION step has an event but no dest/legal_in, and whose inner ADD_ELEMENT has no args - the only reason `dest`/`event` must be optional on a transition. Only transition_on_add_cmd creates compounds. A typed union forces this to give: either keep dest optional on transitions, or make the compound hold its add step as a typed field and fire its own event.

A `type CommandSpec = ...` alias cannot be used with isinstance(); no src code does isinstance(x, CommandSpec) today (grep confirmed), but every consumer that branches on `command.kind` and then reads per-kind fields must switch to isinstance / match on the concrete classes for pyright to narrow (plain-str kind constants do not narrow a union).

Not in this stage: the other 8 errors live in dev tooling (_hmr_debug.py: 5 reportAttributeAccessIssue on sys/loop monkeypatch attrs; hmr_server.py:89 Unknown|None passed to __exit__, :194/:195 Optional member access). hmr_server.py:194-195 may be a real None-deref and is raised for stage 2 rather than fixed in passing.

architecture 'Page types & FSM implementation' (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2): Data model paragraph ('A command declares the kind of mutation it performs, its argument specs ... an optional FSM event and destination status (dest, for transitions) ... an optional element_field') and the details 'A status edge is declared once, on its command' (CommandSpec.dest, _status_transitions with `event` set) and 'The command factories' ('No page-type declaration constructs a raw CommandSpec') must describe the per-kind dataclass union (CommandSpec built from the AuthoringCommand subset plus TransitionCommand and CompoundCommand) instead of one CommandSpec with optional fields, and a compound's steps as authoring commands only - a page-status transition is rejected as a step.

architecture 'Authoring & mutation' (architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4): wherever it describes apply_command validating and dispatching a command, the store's per-command prechecks, or the COMPOUND steps tuple - argument validation and the legality check now run at the start of _apply (apply_command keeps lookup, copy and backfill), so each compound step is validated, legality-checked and applied like a top-level command, and mutatePageBatch runs all five prechecks (ref, block ref, inline ref, guards, link) in one loop over the command and each compound step. To be checked and reconciled at ship.

Impact ranking - which stage goes first? Evaluation (with Any reporting on): (1) CommandSpec optional fields -> per-kind dataclass union: fixes 16/24 errors, removes every `str | None` section/field/event/dest leak in commands.py, pagetype.py, validation.py, describe.py, store.py, and 3 explicit Any in core/commands.py; also disable reportPrivateUsage (-71 warnings). (2) Page/args JSON data model (`dict[str, Any]` sections, `args: dict[str, Any]`): the bulk of reportAny/reportExplicitAny (commands.py 35 explicit, store.py 27, render.py 36 reportAny, serialize.py 21) - needs a JSON value type / TypedDicts, large. (3) describe / next-actions payloads as TypedDicts (describe.py, server.py 19 explicit Any). (4) Dev tooling hmr_server.py/_hmr_debug.py: 114 warnings + 8 errors, mostly Unknown from untyped hmr/reactivity libs - low product impact. (5) Lint-only noise: unused imports/call results/implicit concat/missing param types (~70). Proposal: this feature = stage 1 only.
items.answer: Stage 1 = the CommandSpec union plus disabling reportPrivateUsage. It removes the majority of real errors (16/24) with a contained, behaviour-preserving refactor that the user has already designed, while stage 2 (JSON data model Any) is far larger and needs its own design. Stages 2-5 are left for later features in the order listed.

items.text: How does a COMPOUND hold its inner steps once commands are typed per kind - keep a `steps` tuple of CommandSpec (forcing an optional dest on transitions), or give CompoundCommand a typed `add: AddElementCommand` and have it fire its own event?
items.answer: CompoundCommand gets a typed `add: AddElementCommand` field and fires its own `event`; the `steps` tuple goes. Only transition_on_add_cmd creates compounds and they are always exactly add-then-transition, so dest and event become required on every status transition.

items.text: Does the `kind` string survive on the new classes (it is emitted in describe output and compared in tests), and as what?
items.answer: Yes - each concrete class declares `kind: ClassVar[str]` set to its existing constant from core/specs.py. It is not a dataclass field (no constructor arg, not in equality); describe keeps emitting it unchanged. Code that needs per-kind fields narrows with isinstance/match on the class, not on kind.

items.text: Is the never-read `CommandSpec.generated` field carried onto the new base class, or dropped?
items.answer: Dropped - it is never set or read, and re-declaring the base is the natural point to stop carrying it.

items.text: Union spelling: the user wrote `type CommandSpec = Union[...]`; the codebase otherwise writes `X | Y`. Which spelling?
items.answer: `type CommandSpec = Union[...]` exactly as the user wrote it; the alias is the one place it appears, and the user specified it.

items.text: Build finding: with typeCheckingMode=recommended, basedpyright reports `typing.Union` as reportDeprecated ('use "|" instead'), so the decided `type CommandSpec = Union[...]` spelling adds 2 new warnings in a feature whose purpose is to remove them. Keep Union or switch to the `|` spelling?
items.answer: Switched to `type CommandSpec = (A | B | ...)`. It is the same PEP 695 alias over the same 14-member union the user asked for; only the spelling differs, and that spelling is what keeps the touched file free of new warnings. Flagged to the user in the final report so they can revert to Union if they want the literal form.

items.text: Compound shape, revisited by the user at the ship gate: should CompoundCommand keep a generic `steps` tuple and run each step through the same apply_command pipeline as a top-level command (argument validation, legality, apply), instead of holding a typed `add: AddElementCommand`?
items.answer: Yes - user decision, 2026-10-15, superseding the earlier answer that gave CompoundCommand a typed `add`. That answer tightened the compound into add-then-transition only, which the user considers a gap rather than intended behaviour. CompoundCommand keeps a generic `steps` tuple; each step runs through the apply_command pipeline minus the name lookup (a step is not a registered command): its own argument validation against the args it declares, its own legality check, then apply. Each step receives only the args it declares. After the steps the compound fires its own event. The one accepted behaviour change: a page-status transition (TransitionCommand or CompoundCommand) is not allowed as a step.

items.text: How is 'no page-status transition as a step' enforced? Python typing has no union subtraction (no TypeScript-style Exclude<CommandSpec, Transition>). Options: (a) runtime check only - CompoundCommand.__post_init__ raises ValueError when a step is a StatusTransitionCommand, steps typed tuple[CommandSpec, ...]; (b) split the existing union into two named layers - `type AuthoringCommand = <the 12 non-transition classes>` and `type CommandSpec = AuthoringCommand | TransitionCommand | CompoundCommand` - and type steps as tuple[AuthoringCommand, ...], so pyright rejects a transition step; no class is listed twice, so this adds no second list to maintain, and _apply can take `AuthoringCommand | TransitionCommand`; (c) both. No CI workflow runs basedpyright, so only the runtime check is enforced by the test suite. Proposal: (c).
items.answer: (c) both - user decision, 2026-10-15. The union is declared in two layers: `type AuthoringCommand = <the 12 non-transition classes>` and `type CommandSpec = AuthoringCommand | TransitionCommand | CompoundCommand`, and CompoundCommand.steps is typed tuple[AuthoringCommand, ...]. CompoundCommand.__post_init__ also raises ValueError when a step is a StatusTransitionCommand, because no CI runs basedpyright and the runtime check is what the test suite enforces. A basedpyright probe of this exact shape (forward-referenced alias in the steps annotation, isinstance check in __post_init__, recursion over steps in a match) reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.

items.text: Should the store's per-command prechecks also run on compound steps? In mutatePageBatch, _check_ref (an add's ref_check) and _check_link (addLink) run only on the top-level command, and apply_command does not run them, so a step carrying a ref_check, or an addLink step, would skip them. _check_block_refs and _check_inline_refs already cover step args, because a compound's args are its steps' args. Options: (a) run _check_ref and _check_link for each step with that step's args - full parity with a top-level command; (b) leave it - no current step carries a ref_check or is an addLink - and record it as a known limitation. Proposal: (a).
items.answer: (a) - user decision, 2026-10-15. In mutatePageBatch, when the looked-up command is a CompoundCommand, the store also runs _check_ref and _check_link on each step with that step's own args, before apply_command runs, so a step gets the same cross-page prechecks as a top-level command. _check_block_refs and _check_inline_refs are not repeated per step: a compound's args are its steps' args, so the compound-level call already covers them.

items.text: Should the store run all five per-command prechecks (_check_ref, _check_block_refs, _check_inline_refs, _check_guards, _check_link) on each compound step, in one loop over the command and its steps, rather than only _check_ref and _check_link per step?
items.answer: Yes - user decision, 2026-10-15, superseding the answer to mv9ki951-5d1c7b. mutatePageBatch runs all five prechecks in one loop over the looked-up command with its args, followed for a CompoundCommand by each step with commands.step_args(step, args). The earlier selective version left out the block/inline ref checks only as redundant (a compound's args are its steps' args) and _check_guards only because it cannot fail for a non-transition; neither is a reason against running them, and one uniform loop is simpler and stays correct if a compound's args ever differ from its steps'.

findings.issue: Testing case 'Compound behaviour unchanged' cited tests vaguely ('the existing tests ... in test_store.py / test_commands.py'), so a reviewer could not tell which run proves it. Applied: the case now names test_commands.py::test_compound_close_records_commit_and_transitions, ::test_compound_close_illegal_from_draft and test_server.py::test_flow_close_flow.

Steps 4-10 change the CommandSpec declaration and its consumers in sequence, so the full suite is red between step 4 and step 11; this is inherent to replacing a type every module imports. Each step carries a narrower verification (import succeeds, or the touched module's test file passes) and step 11 restores the full green run before the single refactor commit. No edit needed.

Spec coverage checked: classes/alias (step 4), factories and is_field_setter (step 4), _apply match + assert_never and helper narrowing (step 8), pagetype resolution + derived FSM table (step 5), validators with unchanged messages (step 6), describe contract (step 9 + snapshot in steps 1/12), store narrowing only (step 10), reportPrivateUsage (step 2), test updates (step 11). No step outside the spec; no documentation step. Step 8's TypeIs return annotation is the mechanism that lets callers of _is_status_transition narrow, consistent with the spec.

Revision review: steps 12 and 19 and the full-regression case compared a passed-test count from a --testmon run, but testmon reports only the tests it selected, so the count could not prove that nothing was deleted or skipped. Applied: both steps now take the count from 'uv run pytest --collect-only -q' (baseline N, then N + 3) and use the testmon run only for pass/fail; the regression case says the same.

Revision review: done steps 3, 4 and 7 (and the original data-model wording) still show the typed CompoundCommand.add they built. They record what was built before the revision; steps 13, 14 and 16 replace that code and say so, and the data-model block now shows steps. No edit.

Revision review, spec coverage: two-layer alias, steps field and __post_init__ (step 14); transition_on_add_cmd building an add step that declares add_args (14); _is_legal extraction, _check_legal by command, step_args, validation moved into _apply and the compound's recursion (16); per-step _check_ref/_check_link in the store (18); error paths - transition step ValueError (13), step legality (15), step link precheck (17); describe contract and type-check (12, 19). No step outside the spec, no new apply function, no documentation step, and pure steps 13-16 come before effect steps 17-18. Every new case can fail: each names the defect that would make it fail.

Precheck-loop review, spec coverage: the single loop over the command and its steps running all five prechecks (step 20) is the only design change, and step 21 re-verifies regression, collected count and type-check. The refactor has no new failing test by design: it preserves behaviour, and tests/test_store.py::test_compound_step_gets_the_link_precheck would fail if steps dropped out of the loop. No step outside the spec, no documentation step, and the change stays on the effects side with step_args kept pure.

Prune review: the one new step deletes only this PR's tests that assert removed fields are absent (two hasattr assertions and the kind-constructor TypeError test), as the user asked and the review guidance on tests conditioned on removed code directs. The surviving behaviour - ref_check threaded onto the add, kind equal to each class constant - stays covered by test_list_cmds_threads_ref_check_onto_the_add_only, test_factories_build_the_class_of_their_kind and the describe snapshot. def test_factories_build_the_class_of_their_kind():
    add, remove, reorder = list_cmds("items")

    assert type(remove) is RemoveElementCommand and type(reorder) is ReorderElementCommand

def test_compound_holds_its_add_as_a_typed_field():

    assert (compound.event, compound.dest, compound.legal_in) == ("close", "closed", ("open",))
    assert type(compound.add) is AddElementCommand
    assert (compound.add.section, compound.add.field) == ("resolution", "commits")
