Carried by existing tests that must pass unmodified: tests/test_commands.py::test_compound_close_records_commit_and_transitions, tests/test_commands.py::test_compound_close_illegal_from_draft, tests/test_server.py::test_flow_close_flow.

describe contract byte-identical: a JSON snapshot of describe output for every production page type taken before the revision diffs empty against the snapshot taken after it (run as a script, not a test, since production types are off-limits in tests).

The store prechecks a compound step through the single precheck loop (effects, error path): with an ad-hoc page type registered through a patched registered_pagetypes, a mutatePageBatch running a compound whose step is addLink, with toId 'test-flow:missing', raises NotFoundError, and the stored page afterwards has no links and status 'open'. Test: tests/test_store.py::test_compound_step_gets_the_link_precheck. The existing top-level precheck tests in tests/test_store.py (test_add_link_command_enforces_link_rules_and_is_atomic and the ref / inline-ref precheck tests) still pass through the same loop.

Type-check outcome: uv run basedpyright reports 8 errors, all in src/_hmr_debug.py and src/hmr_server.py (none in src/commands.py, src/store.py or src/pagetypes/core/commands.py), zero reportPrivateUsage, and 234 warnings (the revision baseline).

Full regression after pruning: uv run pytest --testmon -q reports no failures, and uv run pytest --collect-only -q collects 775 tests (773 baseline plus the 3 compound tests, minus test_kind_is_a_class_constant_not_a_constructor_argument; the two pruned assertions sit inside tests that remain). The count comes from --collect-only because a --testmon run reports only the tests it selected.

overview.body: Covers the command declaration layer (src/pagetypes/core/commands.py) and its consumers (src/commands.py, core/pagetype.py, core/validation.py, src/describe.py, src/store.py, tests): the single CommandSpec dataclass with a kind string and optional per-kind fields becomes one frozen dataclass per command kind under a small set of group bases, joined by a two-layer alias - `type AuthoringCommand = ...` over the 12 non-transition classes and `type CommandSpec = AuthoringCommand | TransitionCommand | CompoundCommand`. A compound keeps a generic `steps` tuple of authoring commands; each step is applied through _apply with its own argument validation and legality check (validation moves from apply_command into _apply), and the store runs every per-command precheck on the compound and on each of its steps in one loop. Also disables reportPrivateUsage in [tool.pyright]. Behaviour, page-type declarations (which only call the factories), stored data and the describe JSON contract are unchanged, except that a page-status transition is no longer accepted as a compound step. Deliberately left out: the JSON data model Any (`dict[str, Any]` sections and args), describe/next payload TypedDicts, hmr dev tooling errors, and lint-only warnings - those are later stages.

body.text: Class hierarchy (core/commands.py, pure)

All classes are @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) so a subclass may add required fields after a defaulted base. kind is a ClassVar[str] set to the existing constant from core/specs.py on each concrete class. Group bases are public because consumers narrow on them; only the 14 concrete classes appear in the union, declared in two layers so the authoring subset has a name without any class being listed twice (Python typing has no union subtraction).

body.source:
@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class BaseCommand:
    kind: ClassVar[str]
    name: str
    description: str = ""
    args: tuple[ArgSpec, ...] = ()
    legal_in: tuple[str, ...] | None = None
    agency: str = "agent"

class FieldCommand(BaseCommand):            # section: str; field: str  (both required)
class SetScalarCommand(FieldCommand):       # kind = SET_SCALAR
class SetProseCommand(FieldCommand):        # kind = SET_PROSE
class AddElementCommand(FieldCommand):      # kind = ADD_ELEMENT; element_map: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (); ref_check: RefCheck | None = None
class RemoveElementCommand(FieldCommand):   # kind = REMOVE_ELEMENT
class ReorderElementCommand(FieldCommand):  # kind = REORDER_ELEMENT
class ElementWriteCommand(FieldCommand):    # element_map: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (); element_const: tuple[tuple[str, bool], ...] = ()
class SetElementFieldCommand(ElementWriteCommand):   # kind = SET_ELEMENT_FIELD
class ElementTransitionCommand(ElementWriteCommand): # kind = ELEMENT_TRANSITION; event: str
class BlockCommand(FieldCommand):           # element_field: str | None = None  (None = the section's own blocks field)
class AddBlockCommand(BlockCommand):        # kind = ADD_BLOCK
class RemoveBlockCommand(BlockCommand):     # kind = REMOVE_BLOCK
class ReorderBlockCommand(BlockCommand):    # kind = REORDER_BLOCK
class StatusTransitionCommand(BaseCommand): # event: str; dest: str; requires: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (); guards: tuple[ChildStateGuard, ...] = (); parent_guards: tuple[ParentStateGuard, ...] = ()
class TransitionCommand(StatusTransitionCommand):    # kind = TRANSITION
class AddLinkCommand(BaseCommand):          # kind = ADD_LINK
class SetTitleCommand(BaseCommand):         # kind = SET_TITLE

@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class CompoundCommand(StatusTransitionCommand):
    kind: ClassVar[str] = COMPOUND
    steps: tuple[AuthoringCommand, ...]     # required; applied in order, then the compound fires its event

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        for step in self.steps:
            if isinstance(step, StatusTransitionCommand):
                raise ValueError(f"CompoundCommand({self.name!r}): step {step.name!r} is a status "
                                 f"transition - a compound fires only its own event")

type AuthoringCommand = (SetScalarCommand | SetProseCommand | AddElementCommand | RemoveElementCommand
                         | ReorderElementCommand | SetElementFieldCommand | ElementTransitionCommand
                         | AddBlockCommand | RemoveBlockCommand | ReorderBlockCommand
                         | AddLinkCommand | SetTitleCommand)
type CommandSpec = AuthoringCommand | TransitionCommand | CompoundCommand

body.text: The field generated is removed; steps moves from the shared declaration onto CompoundCommand alone, typed tuple[AuthoringCommand, ...]. element_const narrows from Any to bool (every declaration stamps a True flag). element_cmds marks are typed tuple[tuple[str, str, str, tuple[ArgSpec, ...]] | tuple[str, str, str], ...] instead of carrying Any.
Factories (core/commands.py, pure)

Every factory keeps its exact signature and return annotation (CommandSpec / tuple[CommandSpec, ...]) and builds the matching concrete class with keyword arguments: set_prose_cmd -> SetProseCommand, set_scalar_cmd -> SetScalarCommand, list_cmds -> AddElementCommand / RemoveElementCommand / ReorderElementCommand, element_cmds -> ElementTransitionCommand, set_element_field_cmd -> SetElementFieldCommand, blocks_cmds and element_blocks_cmds -> AddBlockCommand / RemoveBlockCommand / ReorderBlockCommand, transition_cmd -> TransitionCommand, add_link_cmd -> AddLinkCommand, set_title_cmd -> SetTitleCommand. transition_on_add_cmd returns CompoundCommand(name, description, event, dest, legal_in, agency, args=add_args, requires, guards, parent_guards, steps=(AddElementCommand(name=f"_{name}Add", section=section, field=field, args=add_args, element_map=_same_named(add_args)),)) - the add step declares the args it consumes, because it now validates them itself. is_field_setter becomes: an AddBlockCommand is a setter iff element_field is None; otherwise isinstance(command, (SetScalarCommand, SetProseCommand, AddElementCommand)).
Write path (src/commands.py, pure)

apply_command keeps the name lookup, the page copy and the section backfill, then calls _apply on the working copy. _apply now begins with _validate_args(command, args) and _check_legal(page, page_type, command) - moved out of apply_command, so no new apply function is added - and then dispatches with `match command:` on the concrete classes, ending in `case _: assert_never(command)`. Branch bodies are unchanged except the compound: for each step it recurses into _apply with step_args(step, args), so a step gets exactly a top-level command's argument validation, legality check and dispatch, on the same working copy; it keeps the last non-None created id and extends created_ids in step order, as before, then fires its own event. The checks now run after the copy and backfill; the backfill only adds empty defaults ('' / [] / None) that _is_populated treats as unset, so legality and every error message are unchanged. _check_legal can no longer look a command up by name (a step is not registered on the page type), so the per-command predicate inside legal_commands is extracted as _is_legal and both use it. The previous trailing ValidationError('Unsupported command kind') is replaced by the assert_never arm.

_is_status_transition(command) becomes isinstance(command, StatusTransitionCommand); _topology_ok and field_setter_edges use it to narrow before reading event / requires. unmet_requirements returns [] for a command that is not a StatusTransitionCommand. field_setter_edges skips commands that are not FieldCommand instead of checking section/field for None.

Helpers take the narrowest group they need: _add_element takes AddElementCommand; _apply_element_writes, _find_element and _set_element_field take ElementWriteCommand; _element_transition takes ElementTransitionCommand; _add_block takes AddBlockCommand; _entry_context, _target_entries, _entry_id, _place_entry, _reorder_entry and _remove_by_id take FieldCommand and read the element field through one new private helper `_element_field(command: FieldCommand) -> str | None` (command.element_field for a BlockCommand, else None). _reject_dangling_preceding and _block_array_arg keep CommandSpec/BaseCommand since they read only name/args.
Declaration setup and validation (core/pagetype.py, core/validation.py, pure)

_resolved_arg returns arg unchanged when the command is not a FieldCommand; the element field is command.element_field for a BlockCommand, arg.name for an AddElementCommand, else None. _status_transitions iterates StatusTransitionCommand instances only and drops the `event/dest is not None` guards. dataclasses.replace(command, args=...) is unchanged (it preserves the concrete class). The three validators replace `section is None or field is None` with `not isinstance(command, FieldCommand)`, keep every message text, and compute element_field the same way as _resolved_arg. validate_pagetype_setter_descriptions narrows with isinstance(command, (SetScalarCommand, SetProseCommand, AddElementCommand)).
Projection and store (src/describe.py pure; src/store.py effects)

_command_summary keeps every key and value: section/field come from a FieldCommand else None; event from a StatusTransitionCommand or ElementTransitionCommand else None; requires from a StatusTransitionCommand else []; legalIn is suppressed for StatusTransitionCommand exactly as for TRANSITION/COMPOUND today. In the store, the next_actions loop skips non-StatusTransitionCommand; _check_ref acts only on an AddElementCommand with a ref_check; _child_guard_failure and _parent_guard_failure return None for a command that is not a StatusTransitionCommand; _check_link tests isinstance(command, AddLinkCommand). In mutatePageBatch the five prechecks - _check_ref, _check_block_refs, _check_inline_refs, _check_guards and _check_link - run in one loop, before apply_command, over the looked-up command with its args followed, for a CompoundCommand, by each step with commands.step_args(step, args). A step therefore gets every cross-page precheck a top-level command gets. For today's compounds the block and inline ref checks repeat over the same args and _check_guards cannot fail for a step; both are accepted for one uniform loop. No rule moves into the store: which args a step sees is decided by the pure step_args.
Config and error paths

pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] gains reportPrivateUsage = false. Expected basedpyright result: the 16 commands.py reportArgumentType errors gone (24 -> 8 errors, the 8 left all in hmr dev tooling), the 71 reportPrivateUsage warnings gone, and no new diagnostics in the touched files. Existing error paths are unchanged: unknown command, bad args, illegal command, missing element, stale read and dangling refs raise the same errors with the same messages; an unsupported kind is no longer representable. New error paths: constructing a CompoundCommand with a status-transition step raises ValueError (at module import for a page type); a step that fails its own argument validation or legality raises the same ValidationError / IllegalCommandError a top-level command would, naming the step; a step that fails any store precheck (ref, block ref, inline ref or link) aborts the batch exactly as a top-level command does. A ref the compound's own args already carry fails first on the compound, with the message naming the compound.
Tests

Raw positional CommandSpec(...) constructions in tests/test_pagetypes.py become keyword constructions of the concrete class. The 'targets no field' validator test (test_pagetypes.py:1010) constructs a non-field command carrying a block array (AddLinkCommand) since an AddBlockCommand without a field is no longer representable. Structural tests that read per-kind fields keep their kind gates (kind is still on every class) or switch to isinstance where a gate is missing. Compound tests: transition_on_add_cmd builds a CompoundCommand whose single step is an AddElementCommand carrying add_args and the same-named element_map; constructing a CompoundCommand with a TransitionCommand step raises ValueError; through apply_command, an ad-hoc page type whose compound step has a legal_in excluding the current status raises IllegalCommandError naming the step; through the store's mutatePageBatch, an ad-hoc page type (registered by monkeypatching registered_pagetypes) whose compound has an addLink step rejects a link to a missing page and writes nothing. The existing compound behaviour tests (test_commands.py::test_compound_close_records_commit_and_transitions, ::test_compound_close_illegal_from_draft, test_server.py::test_flow_close_flow) pass unchanged.

Stage 1 is the CommandSpec union plus disabling reportPrivateUsage. Rejected: starting with the JSON data model Any (largest count but needs its own design of a JSON value type and touches every module) and the hmr dev tooling (most Unknown warnings but low product impact, mostly from untyped third-party libs). The union removes 16 of 24 real errors with a contained, behaviour-preserving change the user already designed.

kind stays as a ClassVar[str] on each concrete class, set from the existing constants. Rejected: removing kind (breaks the describe contract and the docs), and a Literal-typed dataclass field (would be a constructor arg that could disagree with the class). Narrowing is done by isinstance/match on classes.
generated is dropped. Rejected: carrying a field nothing sets or reads onto a freshly declared base.

The alias is spelled with `|`, not typing.Union: in recommended mode basedpyright reports Union as reportDeprecated, which would add warnings in a feature that exists to remove them. Supersedes the decision for muqmi6d3-56ac05 (Union exactly as the user wrote it); it is the same PEP 695 alias over the same members. Rejected: keeping Union and suppressing reportDeprecated for that line.

CompoundCommand keeps a generic steps tuple, and each step is applied through _apply - its own argument validation, legality check and dispatch - with only the args it declares; the compound then fires its own event. Supersedes the decision for muqmi6cx-3e868e (a typed `add: AddElementCommand`), which the user rejected at the ship gate: it narrowed compounds to add-then-transition, a gap rather than intended behaviour, and its inner add never received a command's checks. Validation moves from apply_command into _apply instead of into a new function (user preference), so recursion gives a step exactly what a top-level command gets; apply_command keeps lookup, copy and backfill. Rejected: (1) the typed add field - fixes the shape to one add; (2) splitting apply_command into a lookup and a new apply-by-spec function - the user prefers the existing two-function split; (3) steps naming registered commands - closeWithoutCommit maps different args from recordCommit, and test-flow's commits field has no standalone add. Accepted behaviour change: a page-status transition is not allowed as a step, since the compound owns the one edge it fires.

Both static and runtime enforcement. Steps are typed tuple[AuthoringCommand, ...] over a two-layer union (`type AuthoringCommand = <12 classes>`, `type CommandSpec = AuthoringCommand | TransitionCommand | CompoundCommand`), and CompoundCommand.__post_init__ raises ValueError for a StatusTransitionCommand step. Python typing has no union subtraction; building the full union from the authoring layer names the subset without listing any class twice. The runtime check stays because no CI runs basedpyright. A basedpyright probe of this shape reported 0 errors and 0 warnings. Rejected: runtime check only (pyright could not reject a transition step); alias only (the test suite would not enforce it).

The store runs all five prechecks (_check_ref, _check_block_refs, _check_inline_refs, _check_guards, _check_link) in one loop over the command with its args and, for a compound, each step with step_args(step, args). Supersedes the decision for mv9ki951-5d1c7b, which ran only _check_ref and _check_link per step because the block and inline checks were redundant (a compound's args are its steps' args) and guards cannot apply to a non-transition step. Neither is a reason against running them: the repeated ref checks read the same args at negligible cost, _check_guards returns without failing for a non-transition, and the uniform loop is simpler to read and stays correct if a compound's args ever differ from its steps'. Rejected: the selective per-step checks - correct for today's factory, but special-cased.

feature-brief:mv9mjxa6-7152e9.title: Pyright stage 2: type the HMR dev tooling (0 errors)

summary.body: Stage 2 of the staged pyright cleanup. basedpyright on main reports 8 errors and 234 warnings; all 8 errors and 107 of the warnings are in the HMR dev tooling (src/_hmr_debug.py, src/hmr_server.py, src/hmr_live_refresh.py). None of the errors is a real defect - they are idempotency attributes monkeypatched onto sys and the event loop behind type-ignore comments this checker does not honour, a wrong upstream annotation on hmr's ErrorFilter.__exit__, and a narrowing pyright cannot follow - and nearly all the warnings are our own unannotated parameters, not the untyped hmr library. Type those three files so basedpyright reports 0 errors, without changing any behaviour: annotate parameters, make the idempotency attribute access type-clean, restate the one narrowing pyright can follow, and suppress only the upstream annotation. (The CLI still exits 1 while warnings remain, because recommended mode sets failOnWarnings.) Out of scope, recorded for later stages: the product-code untyped-JSON narrowing (stage 3) and lint-only rules including those inside the HMR files (stage 4).

items.name: src/_hmr_debug.py
items.text: Effects (installs sys.excepthook / sys.unraisablehook wrappers and an asyncio loop exception handler; appends to hmr_debug.log). Imported for its side effect at the end of server.py (server.py:626), so it re-executes on every hot reload; it keeps the ORIGINAL hooks on attributes it sets on `sys` (_hmr_dbg_excepthook_orig, _hmr_dbg_unraisable_orig) and marks the loop (_hmr_dbg_installed) so re-execution wraps only once. Holds 5 of the 8 errors (reportAttributeAccessIssue at :38, :39, :51, :52, :85 - exactly those idempotency attributes; their `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comments are inert, see constraints) and 54 warnings, nearly all from unannotated hook parameters: _fmt(exc_type, exc_value, tb), _excepthook(...), _unraisablehook(args), _loop_handler(loop, context), plus 2 reportUnusedCallResult (f.write, _loop_orig(...)). Not a real defect - the errors are the deliberate monkeypatch.

items.name: src/hmr_server.py
items.text: Effects (uvicorn server, file watcher, reactive module reload, MCP mount swap). 3 errors + 50 warnings. :89 reportArgumentType - _LoggingErrorFilter.__exit__ forwards exc_value (None on a clean exit) to ErrorFilter.__exit__, which the hmr library annotates `exc_value: BaseException` while its own body starts `if exc_value is None: return` - a wrong upstream annotation, not a bug here. :194/:195 reportOptionalMemberAccess - mcp_reload_effect narrows the nonlocal stop_event/finish_event through the aliased bool `is_reload`; pyright does not narrow captured, reassigned variables through an alias. Not a real None-deref: both are assigned together at :199 and nothing awaits between the check and the use. Warnings: unannotated params on __exit__, capture_init(*args, **kwargs), _run_with_session_capture(*args, **kwargs), Reloader.on_changes(files), reloader_lifespan(_app), fastapi_dispatch(scope, receive, send) (~40 of the 50); 3 reportMissingTypeStubs (reactivity), 2 reportImplicitOverride, 1 reportUnannotatedClassAttribute (Reloader.error_filter), 5 reportUnusedCallResult, 1 implicit string concat.

items.name: src/hmr_live_refresh.py
items.text: Effects (holds live browser WebSockets; deliberately excluded from the reload set). 3 warnings, all from the unannotated local `dead = []` in ReloaderConnectionManager.refresh.

items.name: tests/test_hmr_server.py
items.text: The only automated coverage of the HMR tooling: 5 tests pin _LoggingErrorFilter - a swallowed reload error reaches the uvicorn.error logger at ERROR with an [HMR] prefix, names the error, states the consequence, is still swallowed (not re-raised), and a clean exit logs nothing. Its docstring states the reload machinery itself is exercised by hand against the running dev server, not in the suite.

items.name: hmr 0.7.6.3 (reactivity.hmr.core, third-party)
items.text: No stubs or py.typed, but pyright reads its source. Signatures our overrides must match: ErrorFilter.__init__(*exclude_filenames: str) setting self.exclude_filenames = set(...); ErrorFilter.__exit__(self, exc_type: type[BaseException], exc_value: BaseException, traceback: TracebackType) whose body handles exc_value None and returns None or True; BaseReloader.on_changes(self, files: set[Path]); BaseReloader.__init__ assigns self.error_filter = ErrorFilter(...).

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/validation.py, src/render.py, src/store.py, src/commands.py (untyped-JSON narrowing cluster)
items.text: ~60 warnings with one root cause: JSON values typed Any (model.Page.sections is dict[str, dict[str, Any]]; the grammar validators take `run: Any`, `value: Any`, `entry: Any`) narrowed by isinstance(x, dict) / isinstance(x, list), which basedpyright turns into dict[Unknown, Unknown] / list[Unknown], so every loop variable, .get() and set() built from them is Unknown. validation.py (pure, 26: _validate_run, validate_inline_content, validate_block, collect_ref_ids, _block_ref_ids), render.py (pure, ~25: render_blocks list marker lambda, _field_content(value) unannotated, _block_inline_text, page_text), store.py (effects, 6: _resolve_ref candidates, _check_block_refs entry), commands.py (pure, 2: _is_filled len over a narrowed union, _target_blocks return list[Unknown]). These are real type holes in the input-validation and render paths, but closing them needs a recursive JSON value type - a design of its own.

items.name: src/server.py, src/docsgen.py (unannotated locals and callbacks)
items.text: server.py (effects, 21 warnings): 8 from the unannotated `call_next` parameter of the two @app.middleware('http') functions (refuse_invalid_declarations, add_no_cache_headers) and _RefuseInvalidDeclarations.on_call_tool; the rest are lint-only (5 unused Page results from store calls, call-in-default, implicit override, implicit concat, unused `markdown` param, and the intentional side-effect `from . import _hmr_debug` at :626 flagged unused). docsgen.py (pure, 11): 9 from the unannotated `notes = []` in _field_line/_command_line, 2 unused params.

items.name: Lint-only rules across src (~50 warnings)
items.text: reportUnusedImport 13 (9 in src/pagetypes/core/commands.py: replace, ValidationError, FieldSpec, SectionSpec, BLOCKS, LIST, PROSE, AutoChildSpec, FSMSpec - none imported from that module anywhere, already unused before stage 1; ValidationError in core/args.py, core/pagetype.py, core/specs.py; the intentional server.py side-effect import), reportUnusedFunction 8 (false positives: _scalar/_prose/_list/_blocks in core/fields.py and _same_named/_paragraph_text/_heading_text in core/args.py are the page-type declaration DSL imported across modules; only core/args.py::_object has no caller), reportUnusedCallResult 14, reportImplicitStringConcatenation 10, reportUnusedParameter 3, reportImplicitOverride 3 (2 of them in hmr_server.py).

items.name: pyproject.toml [tool.pyright]
items.text: Config: typeCheckingMode = "recommended", reportAny = false, reportExplicitAny = false, reportPrivateUsage = false, include = ["src/**/*"]. Tests are not type-checked. Any rule-level decision (e.g. for the lint-only rules or missing stubs) lands here.

Type checker: basedpyright (dev dependency `basedpyright>=1.39.9`, installed 1.39.9), run as `uv run basedpyright`; pyproject [tool.pyright]: typeCheckingMode = "recommended", reportAny = false, reportExplicitAny = false, reportPrivateUsage = false, include = ["src/**/*"]. Baseline measured 2026-10-15 on main 5a1cef3: 41 files, 8 errors, 234 warnings (exit 1).

In basedpyright's `recommended` (and `all`) ruleset enableTypeIgnoreComments is false (read from the bundled ruleset in basedpyright/dist/pyright.js), so `# type: ignore[...]` comments suppress nothing; only `# pyright: ignore[ruleName]` does. Existing precedent for the latter: src/fsm.py:55 and :58.
requires-python = ">=3.14"; runtime dependency `hmr>=0.7.6.3` (installed 0.7.6.3, ships no stubs or py.typed).

Behaviour-preserving: the HMR machinery has no automated coverage beyond tests/test_hmr_server.py (the _LoggingErrorFilter tests), and its docstring says the reload path is exercised by hand. Changes to hmr_server.py / _hmr_debug.py must therefore be annotation-only or locally provably equivalent; nothing that alters the order of hook installation, the idempotency across re-execution, or the reload/mount sequence.

Tests run with `uv run pytest --testmon` (CLAUDE.md: 'Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing'). No CI workflow exists (.github/workflows absent), so basedpyright is only enforced by running it by hand.
CLAUDE.md copy rule: use the word "create" instead of "mint".

The stage 1 brief (feature-brief:muqmbslm-a61298) ranked the HMR tooling last-but-one as 'mostly Unknown from untyped hmr/reactivity libs - low product impact'. Grounding contradicts the cause: of the 107 HMR warnings (plus 8 errors) only 3 are reportMissingTypeStubs; the rest come from our own unannotated parameters and our own monkeypatching, so the HMR files are cheap to clean, not blocked on a third-party library. (Earlier text on this page saying 112 HMR warnings is a miscount; 107 is the measured figure.)

hmr's ErrorFilter.__exit__ declares exc_value: BaseException (and exc_type / traceback non-optional) while being called with None on every clean exit. Our _LoggingErrorFilter override cannot fix the upstream annotation; it either returns early on None before calling super (equivalent - the base returns None in that case) or suppresses the one argument error with a targeted pyright ignore.

_hmr_debug.py's 5 errors sit on the attributes that make it idempotent across hot-reload re-execution (originals kept on `sys`, a marker on the loop). They must not be 'fixed' by dropping that state; the fix has to keep the same attributes with type-clean access (getattr/setattr) or a targeted pyright ignore.

Dead code surfaced by the warnings, to raise rather than delete in passing: 9 unused imports in src/pagetypes/core/commands.py (unused since before stage 1), unused ValidationError imports in core/args.py, core/pagetype.py, core/specs.py, and core/args.py::_object (no caller in src or tests). The other 7 reportUnusedFunction hits are false positives on the underscore-named declaration DSL, which renaming would only churn.

architecture 'Web UI, HMR & live reload' (architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5), detail 'Where a failed reload is reported': describes _LoggingErrorFilter restating a swallowed failure and the traceback reaching sys.excepthook, which tees it to hmr_debug.log. Typing the HMR files preserves that behaviour, so no text is expected to go stale; re-check at ship only if the _hmr_debug idempotency mechanism or the filter's clean-exit path is restructured. No other page describes the touched code at the type level.

Scope cut - which cluster does stage 2 take? Measured 2026-10-15 on main 5a1cef3: 8 errors / 234 warnings. Clusters: (A) HMR dev tooling - all 8 errors plus ~100 of its 112 warnings, nearly all unannotated parameters in our own code (_hmr_debug.py, hmr_server.py, hmr_live_refresh.py); behaviour-preserving, basedpyright exits 0 afterwards (~234 -> ~133 warnings). (B) Untyped-JSON narrowing in product code - ~60 warnings in validation.py / render.py / store.py / commands.py from Any narrowed by isinstance(dict/list); real type holes in input validation and rendering, but needs a recursive JSON value type and touches the pure core. (C) Lint-only noise - ~50 (13 unused imports incl. 9 dead in core/commands.py, 8 false-positive unused DSL functions, 14 unused call results, 10 implicit string concats) - mostly a config-policy call. Proposal: stage 2 = (A); (B) becomes stage 3 with its own JSON-type design; (C) stage 4.
items.answer: (A) HMR tooling - user decision, 2026-10-15. Stage 2 fixes all 8 errors and the type-related warnings in src/_hmr_debug.py, src/hmr_server.py and src/hmr_live_refresh.py, behaviour-preserving, so basedpyright exits 0. The product-code untyped-JSON narrowing cluster (B) becomes stage 3 with its own JSON value type design; the lint-only cluster (C) becomes stage 4. """Regression tests for the HMR reload-error capture (src._hmr_debug).

The module re-executes on every hot reload, so it keeps the hooks it wraps on `sys` and must
capture them only once - otherwise each reload would wrap the previous wrapper.
"""

import importlib
import sys

import src._hmr_debug as hmr_debug


def test_reexecuting_the_module_keeps_the_original_hooks():
    excepthook_orig = getattr(sys, "_hmr_dbg_excepthook_orig")
    unraisable_orig = getattr(sys, "_hmr_dbg_unraisable_orig")

    reloaded = importlib.reload(hmr_debug)

    assert getattr(sys, "_hmr_dbg_excepthook_orig") is excepthook_orig
    assert getattr(sys, "_hmr_dbg_unraisable_orig") is unraisable_orig
    assert reloaded._excepthook_orig is excepthook_orig
    assert reloaded._unraisable_orig is unraisable_orig
    assert sys.excepthook is reloaded._excepthook
    assert sys.unraisablehook is reloaded._unraisablehook

# expect: 1 passed

overview.body: Types the HMR dev tooling - src/_hmr_debug.py, src/hmr_server.py and src/hmr_live_refresh.py - so basedpyright reports no errors and none of the type-related warnings in those files: annotate every flagged parameter, mark the two overrides, annotate the one class attribute and the one empty list, make the idempotency attributes on sys and the event loop type-clean through setattr/getattr, narrow the reload teardown with a condition pyright can follow, and suppress exactly one argument error caused by hmr's wrong ErrorFilter.__exit__ annotation. body.text: Annotation rule

Annotate parameters only; return types stay as they are (inferred where unannotated today). Every new annotation is the type the caller actually passes, taken from typeshed or the library that calls it. No new type aliases, no new modules, no behaviour change. All three files are effects-only dev tooling; there is no pure logic to separate out.
src/_hmr_debug.py
Add imports `from types import TracebackType` and `from typing import Any`. Parameter annotations:

These match what the hooks are installed into: sys.excepthook (type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType | None), sys.unraisablehook (UnraisableHookArgs) and AbstractEventLoop.set_exception_handler (AbstractEventLoop, dict[str, Any]). The `exc` annotation is what keeps type(exc) and exc.__traceback__ known.
Idempotency attributes: same names, same guards, same order; only the write and the read change form.

feature-brief:mv9o1p19-8501da.title: Pyright stage 3: type the JSON page data in product code

summary.body: Stage 3 of the staged pyright cleanup (after stage 2, feature-brief:mv9mjxa6-7152e9, which typed the HMR dev tooling). Page content and MCP command arguments are untyped JSON: wherever product code checks such a value with isinstance(x, dict) / isinstance(x, list), the value is typed Any, so basedpyright narrows it to dict[Unknown, Unknown] / list[Unknown] and then checks nothing done with it. Measured 2026-10-15 on main dd341ee (0 errors, 138 warnings), 84 warnings are type-related and sit in six product files: the inline-run and block grammar (validation.py 27), Markdown rendering and the search projection (render.py 29), the store's cross-page reference prechecks (store.py 6), the command layer (commands.py 2), and unannotated callbacks and locals - the HTTP and tool-call middlewares (server.py 11) and docsgen's note lists (docsgen.py 9). The outcome wanted: a JSON value type at the points that inspect a value of unchecked shape, so those paths are actually type-checked; all 84 warnings gone (138 -> 53, every remainder a lint-only rule); behaviour and the MCP/describe contracts unchanged for every value the grammar admits. One behaviour change is deliberate: typing the block-reference precheck exposes that a number or boolean block-array argument crashes it with a raw TypeError before validation runs, and that input now gets the existing "must be of type 'array'" ValidationError. Lint-only rules and checker configuration are not part of this stage (stage 4).

Latent defect the typing exposes, colliding with the 'behaviour unchanged' outcome: Store._check_block_refs (src/store.py:1019) iterates `args.get(arg.name) or []` over raw, not-yet-validated command args, so a block-array argument that is a number or boolean raises a bare TypeError out of the precheck instead of reaching the grammar validation. Argument 'blocks' must be of type 'array', got str/dict." It breaks the Project Overview invariant 'Every expected (non-bug) failure is a PastaError subclass ... Violated, a domain failure reaches the client as an unhandled server crash'. Under a JSON value type pyright reports exactly this ('int is not iterable', the same diagnostic probe 1 raised at the identical pattern elsewhere), so typing it honestly means fixing it - a deliberate behaviour change for malformed input only.

items.answer: (a) At the inspection points only. A value of unchecked shape that the code inspects with isinstance is typed JSONValue (validation.py's grammar functions and collect_ref_ids, store._check_block_refs, commands._is_populated / _validate_args, and render's search projection page_text / _block_inline_text / _runs_text); code that trusts stored content keeps its dict[str, Any] / list[Any] declarations, and the few Unknowns there are annotated with that same stored shape (render._field_content value: Any, store._resolve_ref candidates and commands._target_entries blocks as list[dict[str, Any]]). Probe 2 (2026-10-15): 0 errors, 53 warnings, all lint-only, and the 776 tests pass. (b) rejected: probe 1 showed model-wide typing adds 19 errors at 7 sites on trusted stored-data paths outside this stage and removes none of the 84 warnings.

items.text: Does stage 3 fix the Store._check_block_refs TypeError on a number/boolean block-array argument (so the caller gets the existing "Argument 'blocks' must be of type 'array'" ValidationError), given the summary asks for unchanged behaviour?
items.answer: Yes, as the one deliberate behaviour change. Under a JSON value type pyright reports the `or []` iteration as 'int is not iterable', so typing it honestly means guarding it: the precheck walks the argument only when it is an array, and a number or boolean falls through to _validate_args, which already rejects it with "Argument 'blocks' must be of type 'array', got int." That restores the Project Overview invariant that every expected failure is a PastaError. A regression test pins it. Keeping the crash would need a suppression or cast whose only purpose is to preserve a bug.

items.text: The search projection walks content of any shape. Typed with a JSON value, iterating a field or block key that is not an array must be guarded (skip it) rather than iterated as before. On data the grammar admits the result is identical; on content it would reject, the old code iterated a string's characters or a dict's keys (adding them to the search text) and raised on a number. Is skipping a non-array acceptable for that path?
items.answer: Yes. The search projection is only ever handed stored content, and every write passes the grammar, which requires those keys to be arrays; on that content the walk visits exactly the same entries (an absent or None key still gives none, as `or []` did). Only content the grammar rejects differs - a non-array is skipped rather than iterated character by character or key by key into the search text, or raising on a number - and none can be stored through the API.

items.text: Build finding: the plan's per-step test runs were path-limited (`uv run pytest tests/test_pagetypes.py --testmon`) or bare (`uv run pytest --testmon`). After the render.py change the bare run reported 'no tests ran in 0.05s', yet `--testmon tests/test_render.py` then selected and ran 26 affected tests; after that path-limited run, `--testmon tests/` again ran nothing, although the store's search tests also reach render.py. Are the step runs real evidence?
items.answer: Not on their own, so the evidence was rebuilt with full runs. The testmon database had been seeded while grounding, by probe-2 runs against code that was then reverted and re-applied, and a path-limited `--testmon <file>` run records the changed source file's new checksum, so a later suite-wide run no longer treats that file's other dependents as affected. Remedy used: `uv run pytest --testmon-noselect tests/` (runs everything and rewrites the database) after step 4 - 776 passed - and after step 6 - 779 passed; steps 7 and 8 then ran suite-wide `--testmon tests/` (31 and 7 affected tests passed); case 7's refusal tests were also run by name with -p no:testmon (7 passed). Lesson for this workspace: after reverting or probing code, refresh testmon with --testmon-noselect, and never limit a testmon run to one file mid-change.

No step outside the spec and no documentation step. No edit.

Only case 3 can go red first; cases 4-7 pass before and after by design, because the feature preserves behaviour on admitted content. They still fail if the retyping changes an accept/reject decision, a message, a search hit or a refusal, which is what they are there to catch; cases 1 and 2 fail on any surviving or new diagnostic. No edit.

Step 2's intermediate count for src/commands.py (5 warnings: the 3 baseline ones plus 2 new unknown-argument warnings in _validate_args) is derived from probe 2 rather than measured in exactly that intermediate state; step 3's '0 errors, 1 warning' is the binding check for that file. No edit.

overview.body: Types the JSON page data in product code so basedpyright reports none of the 84 type-related warnings in src/pagetypes/core/validation.py, src/render.py, src/store.py, src/commands.py, src/server.py and src/docsgen.py. One recursive alias, JSONValue, is added to src/model.py and used exactly where a value of unchecked shape is inspected with isinstance - the inline-run and block grammar, the inline-ref collector, the store's block-ref precheck, the command layer's argument check, and the search projection - so narrowing yields typed values pyright can check. Code that trusts stored content keeps its existing dict[str, Any] / list[Any] declarations, with the few remaining Unknowns annotated in that same stored shape. The middlewares' call_next parameters get their upstream types, on_call_tool gets @override, and docsgen's note lists get list[str]. Behaviour is unchanged for every value the grammar admits; the one deliberate change is that a number or boolean block-array argument now gets the existing "must be of type 'array'" ValidationError instead of crashing the block-ref precheck with a TypeError, pinned by one regression test. Deliberately left out: Page.sections / Page.links stay typed Any; the lint-only rules (stage 4); pyproject.toml; and the two other raw-error crashes found while grounding, filed as bug-report:mv9olw3x-58f199 (unhashable ref argument) and bug-report:mv9olx3l-fba0e6 (non-object batch entry or args).

body.text: Where the JSON type applies

One rule decides every edit. A value whose shape has not been checked, and which the code inspects with isinstance, is typed JSONValue: narrowing then yields dict[str, JSONValue] / list[JSONValue] instead of dict[Unknown, Unknown] / list[Unknown], and pyright checks each case the value can take. Code that trusts stored content the grammar already admitted keeps the dict[str, Any] / list[Any] declarations it has, and where such a read leaves an Unknown it is annotated with that same stored shape. Page.sections and Page.links keep their Any value type. No suppression comments, no casts, no new module, no pyproject.toml change. Every touched function keeps its name and parameter names. What changes is: parameter and local annotations; the return annotations the three middleware callbacks gain (-> Response, -> ToolResult) with @override on on_call_tool; one new private helper (_as_list); and the restated lines shown below - from_runs' generator, _check_block_refs' loop, and the search projection's array walks.
src/model.py (pure)

Add the alias after the imports, above `@dataclass class Page`. model imports nothing from src, so the page-type core can import it (validation.py already imports the leaves ...errors and ...fsm) without a cycle.

body.text: Regression test

One new test in tests/test_store.py, placed after test_a_ref_checked_block_created_with_its_element_is_checked, parametrized over 5, True and 1.5 as the `blocks` argument of the test-child page's addDecisions, using the existing _mutate and _child helpers on a test-lifecycle page. It expects ValidationError matching "must be of type 'array'" and asserts the child's decisions body is still []. Before the store change it fails (a TypeError escapes); after it passes. No other test changes: the rest of the work is checked by the type checker and the unchanged suite.
Expected outcome

`uv run basedpyright` reports 0 errors, 53 warnings (baseline 0 / 138). Gone: all 84 type-related warnings in the six files plus the reportImplicitOverride on on_call_tool. Left: exactly the lint-only set stage 4 owns - reportUnusedCallResult 14, reportUnusedImport 13, reportImplicitStringConcatenation 10, reportUnusedFunction 8, reportMissingTypeStubs 4, reportUnusedParameter 3, reportCallInDefaultInitializer 1. No other rule fires anywhere. The CLI still exits 1 (failOnWarnings, stage 4); `uv run basedpyright --level error` exits 0. The full pytest suite passes: the 776 existing tests unchanged plus the 3 new parametrized cases. Probe 2 (2026-10-15) applied this design and measured exactly 0 errors / 53 warnings with all 776 existing tests passing.

The JSON type goes only where a value of unchecked shape is inspected with isinstance - the grammar validators and collect_ref_ids, store._check_block_refs, commands._is_populated / _validate_args, and render's search projection - while code that trusts stored content keeps dict[str, Any] / list[Any] and gets stored-shape annotations for its few Unknowns. Rejected: typing Page.sections model-wide (probe 1: +19 errors at 7 sites on trusted stored-data paths outside this stage - commands.py:462/507/527, render.py:469, render_html.py:258, store.py:398/992/1077 - while removing none of the 84 warnings), and casts after each isinstance (they silence the Unknowns without checking anything, the opposite of the outcome asked for). Probe 2 measured the chosen design at 0 errors / 53 warnings, all lint-only, with the suite green.

Fix the _check_block_refs crash in this stage, as its one deliberate behaviour change, with a regression test. Typing the precheck honestly makes pyright report the `or []` iteration as 'int is not iterable'; guarding it lets a number or boolean fall through to _validate_args, which already rejects it with "Argument 'blocks' must be of type 'array', got int." - restoring the Project Overview invariant that every expected failure is a PastaError. Rejected: keeping the crash behind a suppression or cast, whose only purpose would be to preserve a bug. The two crashes typing does not force (an unhashable ref argument in _resolve_ref, a non-object batch entry or args at store.py:581) are left to bug-report:mv9olw3x-58f199 and bug-report:mv9olx3l-fba0e6.

The search projection skips a non-array where it used to iterate one. It is only ever handed stored content, every write passes the grammar that requires those keys to be arrays, and on that content the walk is identical (absent or None still gives no entries). Rejected: preserving the old iteration of strings and dicts for content the grammar rejects - it fed characters and key names into the search text and raised on a number, and it cannot be typed without a cast. The trusted renderers are not changed this way: they keep their stored-shape Any declarations.

feature-brief:mv9o1p77-457515.title: Pyright stage 4: lint-only rules and the warnings gate

summary.body: Stage 4, the last stage of the staged pyright cleanup. Once stages 2 and 3 have removed the real type holes, what remains is lint-style noise: unused imports (including dead ones in the page-type core), ignored call results, implicit string concatenation, unused-function reports that misfire on the underscore-named page-type declaration helpers, unused parameters, and missing type stubs for the hmr library - including the few of these left in the HMR files on purpose by stage 2. Today the checker also fails on any warning (the recommended ruleset's failOnWarnings), so basedpyright cannot be used as a pass/fail gate until the warning count reaches zero or that policy changes. The outcome wanted: one deliberate, project-wide decision per rule - fix the code, or turn the rule off - so that `uv run basedpyright` passes cleanly and can be relied on as a gate. Dead code it surfaces is raised and confirmed rather than deleted in passing.

items.name: pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] and the `just types` gate
items.text: Config, where every rule-off decision lands. Verbatim today: typeCheckingMode = "recommended", reportAny = false, reportExplicitAny = false, reportPrivateUsage = false, include = ["src/**/*"]. The recommended ruleset sets failOnWarnings = true and enableTypeIgnoreComments = false (recorded in stage 2 from basedpyright's bundled ruleset). The gate is justfile `types:` -> `uv run basedpyright` (justfile:25-26), listed in README.md's task table as `just types       # basedpyright`. No CI workflow exists (.github/workflows absent).

Also core/commands.py:434 has one implicit string concatenation (a factory's description).

Type checker: basedpyright 1.39.9 (`basedpyright>=1.39.9` dev dependency), run as `uv run basedpyright` / `just types`. Baseline measured 2026-10-15 on main 7432990: 41 files, 0 errors, 53 warnings, exit 1. Per rule: reportUnusedCallResult 14, reportUnusedImport 13, reportImplicitStringConcatenation 10, reportUnusedFunction 8, reportMissingTypeStubs 4, reportUnusedParameter 3, reportCallInDefaultInitializer 1.

In the recommended ruleset failOnWarnings = true (the CLI exits 1 on any warning) and enableTypeIgnoreComments = false (`# type: ignore` is inert; only `# pyright: ignore[ruleName]` suppresses). Existing `# pyright: ignore[...]` precedents: src/fsm.py:55, src/fsm.py:58, src/hmr_server.py:95. No ruff or flake8 is configured, so the one `# noqa` in src (server.py:635) suppresses nothing.

Measured rule behaviour (probes 2026-10-15, reverted): reportImplicitStringConcatenation allows implicit concatenation wrapped in its own parentheses - fsm.py:92 with the message wrapped as LookupError((...)) reports 0 warnings - and that parenthesized form is already the prevailing style in src, which is why only 10 sites are flagged. A module-level `__all__` naming an underscore helper makes reportUnusedFunction treat it as used. src already uses the `_ = expr` discard idiom 10 times (cleanup.py:167, :224, :249, :266; rwlock.py:34, :55; server.py:132, :134; store.py:157, :1122).

Behaviour-preserving: every MCP tool, web route, describe payload and error message stays as it is; tests (805, `uv run pytest --testmon`) pass unchanged. Edits keep LF line endings (Edit tool, not Path.write_text). CLAUDE.md copy rule: use 'create' instead of 'mint'. The brief's own rule: dead code the warnings surface is raised and confirmed, never deleted in passing.

Dead code surfaced by the warnings, to be confirmed before removal: (1) the 12 unused imports in the page-type core (no re-export, AST-verified); (2) core/args.py:77 _object, an arg helper with no caller anywhere; (3) docsgen._diagram_block's `tag` and `state` parameters, passed by its one caller and never read; (4) server.route_tree's `markdown` query parameter, never read - removing it changes no behaviour, since FastAPI ignores unknown query parameters and route_page keeps its own.

hmr_server.py:233 schedules `asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(ws_reloader.refresh())` without keeping a reference to the task. The asyncio documentation warns that the event loop holds only weak references to tasks, so an unreferenced task can be garbage-collected before it finishes. Assigning it to `_` would silence reportUnusedCallResult without addressing that. The :207 create_task is on a TaskGroup, which holds its tasks, so it is fine. This sits in the HMR dev tooling (behaviour-sensitive, no automated coverage of the reload path).

reportUnusedFunction misfires on the declaration DSL: 7 of its 8 hits are underscore-named helpers used across the package, and the 8th (_object) is real dead code. Turning the rule off removes the false positives but also stops it catching the next dead helper; renaming the DSL without underscores would churn every page-type module; declaring `__all__` in args.py and fields.py keeps the rule live but introduces a convention src does not use yet.

reportMissingTypeStubs cannot be fixed in this codebase: hmr 0.7.6.3 ships its `reactivity` package with no stubs and no py.typed, and basedpyright already reads its source for types (stage 2 typed against it). Only rule-off, per-import `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingTypeStubs]`, or writing local stubs are available. reportCallInDefaultInitializer flags FastAPI's own `Form(...)` default idiom; FastAPI's documented alternative is `Annotated[str, Form()]`.

No pasta architecture page or ADR documents the type-checker configuration (search for 'basedpyright' finds only the stage briefs), so none goes stale.

items.text: reportUnusedFunction misfires on 7 underscore-named declaration helpers used across modules (and correctly finds _object). bug-report:mv9olw3x-58f199.title: A list or object ref argument crashes the cross-page ref check with an unhashable TypeError

report.component: Store cross-page ref prechecks - src/store.py Store._resolve_ref, reached through Store._check_ref (a list add's ref_check) and Store._check_block_refs (a block kind's ref_check); see architecture 'Authoring & mutation'
report.platform: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, Python 3.14.6 via uv, pytest suite in test mode (test-* fixture page types)

summary.body: A command whose ref-checked argument (e.g. questionId) is a JSON array or object makes mutatePageBatch raise a raw TypeError ('cannot use 'list' as a set element (unhashable type: 'list')') out of the store's cross-page ref precheck instead of a ValidationError.

steps.text: Start from a checkout at dd341ee. Add a throwaway test file under tests/ (the test-* fixture page types are registered only in test mode, which tests/conftest.py switches on) that imports Store from src.store and the helpers _child and _mutate from tests.test_store.

In the test: store = Store(tmp_path); workspace = store.create_workspace('demo'); result = store.create_page(workspace.id, 'test-lifecycle', 'Dark mode'); child = _child(result, 'test-child'). The test-child page declares addNote with ref_check=RefCheck(arg='questionId', scope='parent', section='questions', field='items') and a decision block kind carrying the same ref check (src/testtypes.py:395-438).

Call _mutate(store, workspace.id, child.id, [{'command': 'addNote', 'args': {'questionId': ['x'], 'text': 't'}}]) (the helper stamps the current statusRevisionToken). Repeat with 'questionId': {'a': 1}, and with [{'command': 'addDecisions', 'args': {'blocks': [{'kind': 'decision', 'questionId': ['x'], 'text': 't'}]}}]. Run it with `uv run pytest <file> -q -s -p no:testmon` and catch/print the exception type.

expected.body: Each call is rejected with a ValidationError (a PastaError) naming the bad argument, and nothing is written. Grounding: the Project Overview invariant (architecture:mrteq39m-de7a49) 'Every expected (non-bug) failure is a PastaError subclass ... Violated, a domain failure reaches the client as an unhandled server crash instead of an actionable message'. The same precheck already does this for other wrong types: an integer questionId is rejected with the ValidationError "... does not reference an existing element in the parent page's questions.items - the commit is aborted.", and an argument of the wrong JSON type is otherwise rejected by commands._validate_args ("Argument '<name>' must be of type 'string', got <type>.").

observed.body: Every time, a raw TypeError escapes mutate_page_batch (not a PastaError, so the MCP layer's PastaError-to-ToolError translation does not apply): addNote questionId=['x'] -> "TypeError: cannot use 'list' as a set element (unhashable type: 'list')"; addNote questionId={'a': 1} -> "TypeError: cannot use 'dict' as a set element (unhashable type: 'dict')"; addDecisions with a decision block questionId=['x'] -> "TypeError: cannot use 'list' as a set element (unhashable type: 'list')". It arises in Store._resolve_ref (src/store.py:992, `if ref_value not in {element.get('id') for element in candidates}`), which runs before argument validation (store.py:595-600 precede apply_command at :602). Production page types with a ref check (feature-spec's question-linked decision blocks) go through the same function; reproduced on the test fixtures only. Found while grounding feature-brief:mv9o1p19-8501da (pyright stage 3), which does not fix it because basedpyright does not report it.

bug-report:mv9olx3l-fba0e6.title: A non-object batch entry or args value crashes mutatePageBatch with a raw ValueError / TypeError / AttributeError

report.component: Batch envelope parsing in Store.mutate_page_batch (src/store.py:579-582) behind the mutatePageBatch MCP tool; see architecture 'Authoring & mutation'
report.platform: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, Python 3.14.6 via uv; reproduced through the pasta MCP server's mutatePageBatch tool and through the pytest suite in test mode

summary.body: A mutatePageBatch command whose `args` is not a JSON object (an array, string or number), or a batch entry that is not an object, fails with a raw ValueError, TypeError or AttributeError (e.g. 'dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 6; 2 is required') instead of a ValidationError naming the malformed command.

steps.text: Through MCP: on any live page, call mutatePageBatch(workspaceId, pageId, commands=[{"command": "beginGrounding", "args": ["<the page's statusRevisionToken>"]}]) - args given as an array instead of an object.

Through the store, from a checkout at dd341ee in a throwaway test under tests/ (test mode registers the test-* fixtures): store = Store(tmp_path); workspace = store.create_workspace('demo'); page = store.create_page(workspace.id, 'test-fields', 'A').page.

Call store.mutate_page_batch(workspace.id, page.id, [entry]) once for each entry: {'command': 'setTitle', 'args': ['abc123']}, {'command': 'setTitle', 'args': 'abc'}, {'command': 'setTitle', 'args': 5}, and the bare string 'setTitle'. Run with `uv run pytest <file> -q -s -p no:testmon`, catching and printing each exception's type and message.

expected.body: Each malformed command is rejected with a ValidationError (a PastaError), reported like every other batch failure as "Batch aborted at command <index> ('<command>'): ...", and nothing is written. Grounding: the Project Overview invariant (architecture:mrteq39m-de7a49) 'Every expected (non-bug) failure is a PastaError subclass ... Violated, a domain failure reaches the client as an unhandled server crash instead of an actionable message', and the 'Authoring & mutation' data model (architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4): 'Each command in a mutatePageBatch is {command, args}, and args carries the page's current statusRevisionToken as its first entry' - a malformed shape is a caller error, and the batch-abort message is how every other caller error in a batch is reported.

observed.body: Every time. Through MCP (2026-10-15, args as an array): "Error calling tool 'mutatePageBatch': dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 6; 2 is required". Through the store: args ['abc123'] -> "ValueError: dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 6; 2 is required"; args 'abc' -> "ValueError: dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required"; args 5 -> "TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable"; entry 'setTitle' -> "AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'". None of these is a PastaError, and none carries the batch index or command name. The errors come from `command = entry.get('command')` and `args = dict(entry.get('args') or {})` at src/store.py:580-581, which run outside the try block that wraps PastaErrors with the batch-abort message. The non-object entry case is only reachable by calling the store directly (the MCP tool schema types each command as an object); the args cases reach MCP clients. Found while grounding feature-brief:mv9o1p19-8501da (pyright stage 3), which does not fix it: basedpyright does not report it because the batch is typed list[dict[str, Any]].

report.component: Block grammar - src/pagetypes/core/validation.py validate_block, reached from commands._validate_args for every block-array argument; see architecture 'Page types & FSM implementation' (Blocks: the run grammar, the vocabularies, and element blocks)

summary.body: A block whose plain-text argument (e.g. a decision block's `text`) holds a number, array or object is accepted and stored as-is, although the command's argument schema declares that argument a string.

steps.text: Start from a checkout at 8656b9f. Add a throwaway test file under tests/ (test mode registers the test-* fixtures) importing Store from src.store and _child, _mutate from tests.test_store.

feature-brief:mvfc3sbi-d512cc.title: Pink colour theme for the web UI (light and dark)

summary.body: Recolour the human-facing web UI (workspace index, tree view, page view and error page) so it reads as pink in both the Light and the Dark theme, replacing the stock water.css blue-and-grey palette. Light mode becomes a pale-pink page with deep-pink links and accents; dark mode stays dark but turns plum-tinted with bright-pink accents. It is done purely in src/static/styles.css by redefining water.css's colour custom properties per theme, with every text colour kept at WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) against the backgrounds it sits on. Nothing else changes: no route, template, renderer or MCP output, and the Sphinx docs shown in the Model overlay keep their own theme.

items.name: src/static/styles.css
items.text: The water.css overrides sheet, linked from _base.html after the water.css theme sheet so its rules win. It already carries a 'Theme color additions' block that redefines custom properties under body.light and body.dark (--text-error, --text-on-error), and the .pasta-page structured-render rules that take every colour from a water.css custom property. This is where a pink palette goes: redefining water.css's own colour properties under body.light / body.dark recolours every surface (index, tree, page view, nav, error page) at once. Pure presentation, no effects; served by the /static StaticFiles mount in src/server.py.

items.name: src/static/water.css/light.min.css and dark.min.css (vendored)
items.text: The vendored water.css theme sheets. Each defines its whole palette as custom properties on :root (--background-body, --background, --background-alt, --selection, --text-main, --text-bright, --text-muted, --links, --focus, --border, --code, --button-base, --button-hover, --scrollbar-thumb, --scrollbar-thumb-hover, --form-placeholder, --form-text, --variable, --highlight) and styles body, links, buttons, inputs, tables and code from them. Read only: the change overrides these properties rather than editing the vendored files. Pure presentation.

items.name: src/templates/_base.html and src/templates/_theme.js
items.text: _base.html preloads both water.css sheets, links the JS-selected sheet (#js-stylesheet) and then /static/styles.css, and renders <body class="... light"> hidden until _theme.js runs. _theme.js reads the light/dark choice from localStorage, points #js-stylesheet at /static/water.css/<theme>.min.css and sets the body class to light or dark, then unhides the body. This is why body.light / body.dark is the hook the palette keys off; the change reads these but should not need to modify them. Effects: browser DOM and localStorage only.

items.name: src/templates/_nav.html
items.text: The page-view shell (extended only by page.html). Its <style> block holds the sidebar/main layout and the Page | Model toggle, and is the only place in the web UI with literal colours: #8886 for the #main divider and the toggle button borders, #8883 for the pressed toggle background, and #fff behind the #model-view iframe. The translucent greys sit over whatever background is underneath, so they still read on a pink tint; the #fff is the Sphinx doc iframe's backdrop. Pure presentation.

items.name: tests/test_web.py
items.text: FastAPI TestClient tests over the web routes (index, tree, page view, Model toggle, archive/delete/status forms, reloader socket, no-cache headers, the declaration-error refusal). No test covers the static CSS; it is the regression check that the HTML routes are unaffected, and where a test that the stylesheet is served with the pink palette would go. Performs effects through the test client against a temp store.

Architecture invariant (Web UI, HMR & live reload): 'All structured-render styling is scoped under the pasta-page class and takes every colour from a water.css custom property. Violated, a literal colour reads correctly in only one theme'. The palette must therefore be set as custom-property values per theme (body.light / body.dark), never as literal colours on element rules.

Architecture invariant: 'The web UI is strictly read-only' and 'renderPage returns the Markdown one byte-for-byte'. This change is CSS only: no route, template context, renderer or MCP output changes.

Both themes must keep working: the Light / Dark toggle in _base.html stays, and each theme must stay legible (body text, muted text, links and code readable on their backgrounds). Inferred from the existing two-sheet design rather than a written rule.
The vendored water.css files under src/static/water.css/ are not edited; overrides live in src/static/styles.css (its header comment reads '/* Water.css overrides. */'). Inferred from that layout.
CLAUDE.md: 'Use the word "create" instead of "mint" when creating something.' and 'Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing.'

src/static/styles.css 'Theme color additions' already redefines --text-error (#b00020 light, #cf6679 dark) under body.light / body.dark. The pink palette joins that same block rather than adding a competing one, and the error red has to stay distinguishable from the pink accents (error.html colours #title with var(--text-error)).

water.css sets html { scrollbar-color: var(--scrollbar-thumb) var(--background-body) }. The theme class lives on <body>, so variables redefined under body.light / body.dark do not reach the html element: the page scrollbar keeps the stock water.css colours unless the override also targets html (for example :root:has(body.light)). Small, but it is the one surface the body-scoped pattern misses.

src/templates/_nav.html: the Model overlay iframe shows the Sphinx docsite (/sphinx/page-types/<type>-<status>.html, built into docsite/_build/html) on a literal #fff backdrop. The Sphinx docs carry their own theme and will not turn pink; recolouring them is a separate docsite change and out of scope unless asked.

Web UI, HMR & live reload (architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5), Details paragraph 'Where the styling lives, and the two ways to break it': add that the UI's palette is a pink theme set by redefining the water.css colour custom properties under body.light and body.dark in src/static/styles.css, so new styling should keep taking colours from those properties.
How much of the UI turns pink: only the accents (links, focus ring, selection, buttons) or the surfaces too (page background, panels, borders)?
items.answer: Surfaces and accents both. The ask is to make the UI pink, which reads as the whole UI looking pink, not a pink link colour on a white page. The page background, panels (--background, --background-alt), borders, buttons, selection, focus ring, links, code and text tints all move to pink hues, with text kept at AA contrast.

items.text: What does Dark mode become: a dark pink-tinted (plum) theme with pink accents, the same light pink theme, or the stock dark theme left as it is?
items.answer: A dark plum-tinted theme with bright-pink accents. Dark mode has to stay dark or the toggle stops meaning anything, and leaving it stock would make half the UI not pink.

items.text: Is pink a replacement for the existing palette in both themes, or a third selectable theme (Light / Dark / Pink) in the theme toggle?
items.answer: A replacement in both themes. The Light / Dark toggle stays exactly as it is; a third Pink theme would need template and _theme.js changes and is configurability nobody asked for.

items.text: Does the Sphinx page-type documentation shown in the page view's Model overlay (/sphinx, built into docsite/_build/html) also turn pink?
items.answer: No. The Sphinx docsite is a separately built site with its own theme and is only framed by the page view; recolouring it is a docsite change outside this web-UI subsystem.

findings.issue: Step 1 adds a fourth private helper, _rgb, that the spec's interface list does not name. It is the hex parser shared by _contrast_ratio and _hue (two uses, not an abstraction over one) and carries the spec's '#rrggbb only' error path, so it stays; no plan edit.

The automated cases check the stylesheet's palette values, not the rendered page in a browser (for example that :root:has(> body.dark) recolours the scrollbar and follows the toggle). The preview tool is only run when the user asks, so the visual check falls to the human at the ship gate; it should be called out in the hand-back rather than added as a step.

overview.body: This spec recolours the web UI's water.css palette to pink in both the Light and the Dark theme by adding one block of custom-property overrides to src/static/styles.css. It covers which properties are redefined, the exact values, where the block is scoped and why, and the legibility rule every text colour must meet. It deliberately leaves out the theme toggle and _theme.js (unchanged: still Light / Dark), every template including the literal greys and the #fff iframe backdrop in _nav.html, the vendored water.css files, all Python (routes, renderers, the MCP Markdown output), and the Sphinx docsite shown in the Model overlay.

body.text: Where the palette lives

A new block is added to src/static/styles.css directly after the existing 'Theme color additions' block (which stays exactly as it is). It redefines water.css's colour custom properties under two selectors, :root:has(> body.light) and :root:has(> body.dark). The theme class already sits on <body> (the served HTML hard-codes class 'light' and _theme.js swaps it), so these selectors follow the toggle with no script change. They sit on the root rather than on body because water.css draws the page scrollbar from the html element (html { scrollbar-color: var(--scrollbar-thumb) var(--background-body) }), and a property redefined on body never reaches html. Their specificity (0,2,1) beats water.css's :root (0,1,0) whatever order the sheets load in. Every element rule keeps taking its colour from a custom property, so the structured-render invariant holds and the nav, index, tree, page and error views all recolour together. :has() is already used in this sheet (li:has(> button)).
The block

Properties not listed keep their water.css values on purpose: --animation-duration and --select-arrow are not palette colours; --scrollbar-thumb-hover (light) and --scrollbar-thumb (dark) are already var(--button-hover), so they follow the new button colour; --variable and --highlight colour <var> and <mark>, which this UI does not render. The existing --text-error / --text-on-error definitions under body.light and body.dark are unchanged and still apply, since they are redefined on body after the root values are inherited.
Legibility rule

For each theme, after merging the root palette block with the body.<theme> theme-additions block: every foreground in --text-main, --text-bright, --text-muted, --links, --code and --text-error has a WCAG 2.x contrast ratio of at least 4.5 against each of --background-body, --background and --background-alt; and --form-text has at least 4.5 against --button-base and --button-hover. The ratio is (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) over sRGB relative luminance of 6-digit hex colours, L1 the lighter. The values above meet it with the narrowest pairs at light --links on --background 4.73 and dark --text-error on --background-body 4.58. Placeholder text (--form-placeholder) is outside the rule, as in stock water.css (light 3.48 here, against stock 2.6).
Pink rule

For each theme, --background-body and --links each have an HSL hue in the closed range 300 to 350 degrees and a non-zero saturation. This is what makes the palette pink rather than merely changed; stock water.css fails it (white has no hue, #0076d1 sits near 206 degrees). The values above sit at 322 to 336 degrees.
Pure logic and effects

The product change holds no logic: it is static CSS served unchanged by the existing /static StaticFiles mount. The two rules are checked in tests/test_web.py by pure module-level helpers over the stylesheet text, and the only effect is fetching /static/styles.css through the existing client fixture.

Error paths: a property the rules need that a theme does not define makes the test fail with a KeyError naming it, which is the red state before the block exists. The helpers only accept '#rrggbb' values; every colour the rules read is written in that form.

Decision: recolour surfaces and accents together - backgrounds, panels, borders, buttons, selection, focus, links, code and text tints. Rejected: accents only (links, focus, buttons), because a white page with pink links does not read as a pink UI, which is the ask. Rejected: saturated pink backgrounds, because body text could not keep AA contrast on them; the surfaces are pale pink in light mode and plum in dark mode instead.

Decision: Dark mode becomes a dark plum-tinted theme with bright-pink links and code. Rejected: using the light pink theme in dark mode, because the Dark toggle would then do nothing. Rejected: leaving the stock dark theme, because anyone on Dark would see no pink at all.

Decision: pink replaces the palette inside the existing Light and Dark themes; the toggle, _base.html and _theme.js are untouched. Rejected: a third Pink option in the toggle, because it needs template and script changes plus a third water.css base choice, which is configurability the ask did not request.

Decision: the Sphinx docsite in the Model overlay keeps its own theme. Rejected: restyling the docsite, because it is a separately built site (docsite/_build/html) with its own theme configuration, so it is a different subsystem; it can follow as its own change if wanted.

feature-brief:mvht9ej2-e568f1.title: Page-top links to pinned children and the parent page

summary.body: Make it one click to move between a feature and its companion pages from the top of a page in the web UI. Every page that has a parent - pinned or not - opens its top links strip with a "Parent 🔗" link, so the companion pages lead back to their brief. The strip keeps its section, References and Child pages anchors, and on a page with pinned children it then lists one link per pinned child - labelled with the child's title plus the same 🔗 mark and going straight to that child page, one level deep. So a feature-brief's strip ends Child pages, Implementation plan 🔗, Testing plan 🔗, Spec 🔗. Web view only: the renderPage Markdown is unchanged. (Revised after the user's review of PR #45: parent first with the new label, Child pages anchor always kept, link mark on page links.)

items.name: src/render_html.py: _contents_html
items.text: PURE. Builds the page-top links strip (`<nav class="page-contents" aria-label="Sections">`): one `#section-<key>` anchor per declared section with an element-count badge, then fixed `References` and `Child pages` anchors (L271-272). The only place the "Child pages" top link is emitted, so this is the change site. Signature today is `_contents_html(page_type, page)` - no RefContext.

items.name: src/render_html.py: render_page_html
items.text: PURE. Sole caller of _contents_html (L315). Already receives `page`, `page_type` and `ref_context`. A toc returns before the strip is built (L304-305), so a toc has no top links at all. The bottom `#section-children` Child pages section (L311-313) is what the current top link points at and stays as is.

items.name: src/render_html.py: _page_link / _children_html / _escape
items.text: PURE. Prior art for links on the HTML path: href is `/{workspace_id}/page/{page_id}` plus `?archived=true` when `ref_context.show_archived`, every author leaf (titles included) goes through `_escape` (html.escape). _children_html iterates `page.child_ids` in stored order. Read for conventions; not changed.

items.name: src/render.py: RefContext / build_ref_context
items.text: PURE. RefContext carries workspace_id plus per-page-id titles, types, statuses, archived_ids and show_archived for every page in the workspace - enough to name pinned children, test their type, and build the parent href with no I/O. Built once per render by build_ref_context (L345). Read only.

items.name: src/pagetypes/_registry.py: is_auto_child_type
items.text: PURE. `is_auto_child_type(parent_type, child_type)` (L151) is the one definition of a pinned child: the parent's PageType lists the child's type in `auto_children` (AutoChildSpec, src/pagetypes/core/specs.py:199). Store._is_pinned_child (src/store.py:768) wraps it with a Workspace lookup. render.py already imports from _registry, so render_html can import it without a cycle. Read only.

items.name: src/model.py: Page
items.text: PURE dataclass. `parent_id: str | None` and ordered `child_ids: list[str]` are all the tree data the strip needs; there is no pinned flag on Page. Read only.

items.text: EFFECTFUL (loads the workspace file under the shared read lock). Builds the RefContext with escape_plain_text=True and calls render_page_html; reached from server.route_page. Unchanged by this feature - the whole change stays inside the pure renderer.

Two-renderer invariant (Web UI and Reads & navigation pages): the Markdown that renderPage returns must not change by a byte. This feature is HTML-path only; src/render.py's render_page and _render_child_pages stay untouched.
HTML-path escaping invariant: every author-provided leaf placed into the document (page titles included) is escaped with `_escape` (html.escape, quote=True).
Web UI is strictly read-only, and structured-render styling stays scoped under `.pasta-page` with colours only from water.css custom properties.

_contents_html (src/render_html.py:272) emits the `Child pages` anchor unconditionally on every non-toc page. Replacing it outright on any page with pinned children would also drop the top-of-page route to that page's NON-pinned children - the case is an epic, whose Agent plan is pinned (src/pagetypes/epic.py:223) while its feature-brief children are not. What has to give is settled as a question.

_contents_html takes no RefContext, so the pinned children's titles and types and the workspace id needed for page hrefs are out of its reach. Its signature has to gain `ref_context` (its only caller, render_page_html, already holds one).

Store._is_pinned_child (src/store.py:768) already answers "is this pinned" but needs a Workspace and lives on the effectful Store. The renderer must not call it; it should reuse the pure is_auto_child_type with the child type from RefContext.types, so there stays one definition of pinned.

A direct render with no RefContext (several existing tests call render_page_html(page, type) bare) has no titles, types or workspace id, so it cannot name pinned children or build a parent href. Needs a defined fallback.

def _pinned_child_ids(page_type: PageType, page: Page, ref_context: RefContext) -> list[str]:

def _contents_html(page_type: PageType, page: Page, ref_context: RefContext | None) -> str: """A strip of links to every section, each carrying its element count when it has one, so a page of long lists can be navigated without scrolling it. Pinned children are linked by title, standing in for the Child pages anchor once every child is pinned.""" links: list[str] = [] for section in page_type.sections: count = _section_count(section, page) badge = f'{count}' if count else "" links.append(f'' + f"{_escape(section.name)}{badge}") links.append('References') pinned: list[str] = [] if ref_context is not None: pinned = _pinned_child_ids(page_type, page, ref_context) links += [f'' + f"{_escape(ref_context.titles[child_id])}" for child_id in pinned] if not pinned or len(pinned) < len(page.child_ids): links.append('Child pages') return f'
{"".join(links)}
