feature-brief:mw89g5m4-805cc7.title: Footer links to the active repository remote with an AGPL source-code note

summary.body: Replace the web UI footer's copyright credit (`© Copyright 2026 by Dennis S`) with a link to the source repository of the running server, plus a one-sentence note that AGPL software must be offered to its users as source code. The server reads the link from its own git checkout: the current branch's remote, else `origin`, turned into a browsable https URL with any credentials stripped. Pasta is AGPL-3.0 and served over a network, so every running instance, forks included, should point its users at its source without anyone hand-editing a URL. When no browsable remote can be resolved, the footer shows the note alone.

items.name: src/templates/_base.html
items.text:
The page shell that index.html, tree.html, page.html and error.html all extend. Its `
` holds `{% block footer %}` (lines 31-36), currently an `
` and the line `© Copyright 2026 by Dennis S.` This is where the source link and AGPL note go. Presentation only, no effects.

items.name: src/templates/error.html
items.text: Overrides `{% block footer %}` with an empty block (lines 19-20), so the 500 page from `http_exception_handler` and the 503 declaration refusal from `refuse_invalid_declarations` render no footer. Presentation only.

items.name: src/server.py
items.text: Creates the single module-scope `templates = Jinja2Templates(directory="src/templates")` (line 78) that every TemplateResponse renders through: route_index, route_tree, route_page, refuse_invalid_declarations and http_exception_handler. The module body re-executes on a cold start and on every HMR reload, so a value computed at module scope is recomputed on each reload and not per request. Effectful shell (store, HTTP).

items.name: git CLI over the server's checkout
items.text: Confirmed on git 2.56.0: `git ls-remote --get-url` prints the current branch's upstream remote URL, falling back to `origin`, without contacting the network. Here it prints `git@github.com:dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev.git` in the main checkout and in a worktree. It exits 128 with `fatal: No remote configured to list refs from.` outside a repository and in a repository with no remote. It returns an HTTPS remote's embedded credentials verbatim (`https://user:secret@example.com/a/b.git`). Effect: subprocess and filesystem.

items.name: tests/test_web.py
items.text: The `client` fixture repoints `server.STORE` at a per-test Store and wraps `server.app` in a fastapi TestClient. The footer assertions on the rendered index, tree and page views belong here. Test-only.
requires-python = ">=3.14" (pyproject.toml).
No new runtime dependency to read git: shell out to the git CLI with the stdlib `subprocess`. (Inferred preference; pyproject.toml `dependencies` declares no git library and nothing requires one.)
The web UI is strictly read-only (invariant on 'Web UI, HMR & live reload'): the footer is a projection of the server's own checkout, with no new route, lock or stored state.

src.server must be imported only through the reloader's import finder, and a module it imports is reloadable and must not be imported at hmr_server module scope (invariants on 'Web UI, HMR & live reload'). A new module imported from src/server.py satisfies this.

A remote URL can carry credentials, and git returns them verbatim (confirmed: `https://user:secret@example.com/a/b.git`). The footer is served to every visitor, so userinfo must never reach the rendered page. (Inferred requirement, not declared anywhere.)
The licence is AGPL-3.0: README.md '## License' reads `[AGPL-3.0](LICENSE)`.
CLAUDE.md: use the word "create" instead of "mint"; run pytest with --testmon.

Any styling added takes its colours from water.css custom properties, never literals, because a literal colour reads correctly in one theme only (scoped-styling invariant on 'Web UI, HMR & live reload').

The ask says to remove a 'Made by Dennis S' credit, but no such text exists. The footer reads `© Copyright 2026 by Dennis S.` (src/templates/_base.html:34). That is the only credit in the footer, so it is the line being removed, and removing it drops the only copyright notice from the UI.

This checkout has two remotes. main tracks `origin` = `git@github.com:dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev.git` (the dev repository). `upstream` = `https://github.com/dsschneidermann/pasta` is the public one. Reading the active remote literally links the dev repository, and if that is private, the AGPL source offer points at a repository the server's users cannot open.
src/templates/error.html empties the footer block, so the 500 page and the 503 refusal page would not carry the source link unless that override changes.

src/server.py resolves templates, static files and data relative to the process cwd (`src/templates`, `.pasta-data`). The git read should target the checkout that holds the server's code, so it should run against that directory rather than the cwd, which could belong to a different repository.

water.css styles a `footer` element (src/static/water.css/water.css:1609-1667), but _base.html uses `<div id="footer">`, so none of those rules apply today. Recorded only; not to be changed in passing.

architecture 'Web UI, HMR & live reload' (architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5): its Usage and Details say nothing about the page shell's footer. Add how the footer's source link is resolved (from the git remote of the server's own checkout, re-read on every execution of src/server.py, with credentials stripped), and add the new module and _base.html footer to Code references.

Which remote should the footer link to: the current branch's upstream remote falling back to `origin` (what `git ls-remote --get-url` returns; here the dev repository `dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev` over SSH), or always the remote named `upstream` (here the public `dsschneidermann/pasta`)?
items.answer: The user chose the current branch's remote: whatever `git ls-remote --get-url` returns, which is the branch's tracked remote, else `origin`. In this checkout that is dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev. The user accepted that it may be the dev repository.

items.text: What exactly does the footer say: the link text (the repository's host/path, or a fixed label such as 'Source code') and the wording of the AGPL note?
items.answer: The user chose 'repo path + note': `Source: host/path · AGPL software must be offered to its users as source code.` The link text is the browsable URL without its scheme.

items.text: Is the 'Made by Dennis S' credit the footer's `© Copyright 2026 by Dennis S` line, and is that whole line removed with nothing replacing it?
items.answer: Yes. It is the only credit in the footer, and the user said it can go. The whole `© Copyright 2026 by Dennis S` line is replaced by the source line, and no copyright line is added back.

items.text: What does the footer show when no browsable remote URL can be resolved: git missing, the server not in a checkout, no remote configured, or a remote URL in a form that has no web page (a local path, file://)?
items.answer: The AGPL note alone, without the 'Source:' link. The footer never shows a guessed or fallback URL, and a failed git read never fails the page.

items.text: How does a remote URL become the link's href: which URL forms are accepted, and what is stripped (credentials, ports, the `.git` suffix)?
items.answer: Three forms are accepted: scp-like `user@host:path`, `ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path` and `http(s)://[userinfo@]host[:port]/path`. SSH forms become `https://host/path` with the SSH port dropped. HTTP(S) keeps its scheme and port. Userinfo and one trailing `.git` / `/` are always stripped. Anything else (local paths, file://, git://, empty) gives no link.

items.text: Should the 500 page and the 503 declaration refusal, which render error.html with an empty footer block, also carry the source link and note?
items.answer: No. error.html keeps its empty footer override. Those are developer-facing failure pages, the ask did not include them, and changing them is not needed to put the link on every page users browse.

items.text: When, and from which directory, is the remote read: per request or once per execution of src/server.py, and in the process cwd or the directory holding the server's code?
items.answer: Once per execution of src/server.py (a cold start, and again on every HMR reload), never per request. git runs in the directory holding the server's source, not the process cwd.

items.text: During review, the user asked for the long `templates.env.globals` assignment in src/server.py to be split, with the result held in a module global `source_link`, and for the pure mapper to be renamed. What do the names become?
items.answer: Per the user: the pure mapper in src/source_link.py is now `to_source_link(remote_url: str | None) -> SourceLink | None`, with its rules unchanged. src/server.py binds a module global `source_link = to_source_link(read_remote_url(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))` and then sets `templates.env.globals["source_link"] = source_link`. The template still reads `source_link`. This supersedes the function name in the sealed spec's design; the behaviour is unchanged.

items.text: After done, the user asked for the footer's source link to be grey with no underline, like a similar existing style. Which style does it follow?
items.answer: It follows the element ordinal link in src/static/styles.css (`.pasta-page .element-index` / `a.element-index`): colour `var(--text-muted)`, `text-decoration: none`, and `var(--links)` on hover. The footer link gets `#footer a` / `#footer a:hover` rules in src/static/styles.css. The id selector also outranks water.css's `a:hover` underline, so the link is never underlined. Both colours are water.css custom properties, so both themes follow. This supersedes the sealed spec's 'No styling is added'.

items.text: After done, the user asked for the footer to be two lines, broken manually with a br. How are the source link and the note laid out?
items.answer:
Line one is `Source: host/path`, ended by a manual `
` in place of the `·` separator. Line two is the AGPL note. The `
` sits inside the `{% if source_link %}` block, so the note-only footer (no resolvable remote) stays a single line with no stray break. This supersedes the sealed spec's one-line footer markup.

items.text: How closely should the footer tests pin the rendered markup?
items.answer:
Loosely, per the user: asserting the exact footer markup and the presence or absence of the
is overzealous. The footer tests check only that the link's href and the AGPL note appear, and that 'Source:' is absent without a link. The two-line layout is left to the template, unpinned.

items.text: In the PR 55 review, the user commented on the footer tests' `NOTE` constant and on the stylesheet test. How do the tests check the note, and does the stylesheet test stay?
items.answer: Per the user's review: the `NOTE` constant is removed, and both footer tests assert the literal 'AGPL' instead of the note's full wording. `test_footer_link_is_muted_without_an_underline` is removed, and so is its testing-plan case. The `#footer a` rules in src/static/styles.css are unchanged and now untested. Done in b9d2bb8 (implementation-plan step 6).

In a test run both are the same checkout, so that test cannot tell them apart and the claim overstated what it verifies. Applied: the case was reworded to state what it does prove (the global is published from the reader and mapper, and fails with KeyError until wired) and that the directory choice rests on step 3's code.

The spec's TimeoutExpired path in read_remote_url has no case. Covering it needs a test double or a git that hangs, which the testing guidance steers away from for a one-line except clause, so it is left to code reading in review. All other failure paths (no git or missing directory via OSError, no checkout, no remote) run the real git.

overview.body: This spec covers the web UI footer in the shared page shell (src/templates/_base.html). The copyright credit is replaced with `Source: <link> · AGPL software must be offered to its users as source code.` The link is the browsable https form of the git remote of the checkout the server runs from: the current branch's remote, else `origin`. A new module, src/source_link.py, holds a pure URL mapper and a thin git reader. src/server.py reads the remote once each time it executes and publishes the result as one Jinja global, so no route changes. Out of scope: the error.html footer (it stays empty), the MCP surface, the README and LICENSE files, any configuration or environment override for the URL, and styling for the footer.

body.text: Pure side: remote URL to source link
src/source_link.py holds the rules as one pure function of its argument, with no I/O. It returns None whenever the remote has no web page, and never raises.

Rules, applied to remote_url.strip(): None or empty gives None. A string starting with `http://` or `https://` is parsed with urllib.parse.urlsplit and keeps its scheme and port. A string starting with `ssh://` is parsed the same way and becomes `https`, with its port dropped. A string matching the scp-like form `^(?:[^@/:]+@)?([^@/:]{2,}):(.+)$` becomes `https` with group 1 as the host and group 2 as the path. The host must be at least two characters, so a Windows drive path such as `C:/Repos/pasta` or `C:\Repos\pasta` is not taken for a host. Any other string gives None: local paths, `file://`, `git://`, a bare remote name such as `origin`.

For the URL forms: urlsplit's `hostname` is the host, and userinfo (`user:secret@`), query and fragment are always dropped. Reading `.port` can raise ValueError for a non-numeric port, which gives None. A missing hostname, or a hostname containing `:` (an IPv6 literal), also gives None. The path is normalised in this order: strip leading and trailing `/`, remove one trailing `.git`, then strip trailing `/` again. An empty path gives None, because a bare host is not a repository page. The result is `href = f"{scheme}://{host}{':' + str(port) if port kept else ''}/{path}"` and `text = href.partition('://')[2]`.

body.source:
git@github.com:dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev.git -> https://github.com/dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev
https://github.com/dsschneidermann/pasta         -> https://github.com/dsschneidermann/pasta
https://user:secret@example.com/a/b.git          -> https://example.com/a/b
ssh://git@example.com:2222/a/b.git               -> https://example.com/a/b
http://example.com:8080/a/b/                     -> http://example.com:8080/a/b
https://example.com/                             -> None
/srv/git/pasta.git | C:/Repos/pasta | file:///srv/pasta.git | git://example.com/a/b | origin | "" | None -> None

body.text: Effect side: reading the remote
In the same module, a thin reader runs git and returns its trimmed stdout. It holds no rules about URL shapes.

`git ls-remote --get-url` with no remote argument prints the current branch's remote URL, falling back to `origin`, without contacting the network. Each failure ends in None and never in an exception: git not installed (OSError), repo_dir missing (OSError), not a checkout or no remote configured (exit 128), or a hang (TimeoutExpired).
Wiring in src/server.py

Directly after `templates = Jinja2Templates(directory="src/templates")`, the module publishes the link as a Jinja global. That reaches every template that extends _base.html without touching any route's context. It runs on each execution of the module, so on a cold start and again on every HMR reload, and never per request. git runs in the directory holding the server's source rather than the process cwd.

body.source:
from pathlib import Path
from .source_link import read_remote_url, source_link

templates = Jinja2Templates(directory="src/templates")
templates.env.globals["source_link"] = source_link(read_remote_url(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

body.text: Footer markup in src/templates/_base.html

The copyright line is replaced. The `<hr />` and the `#footer` div stay. Jinja autoescaping escapes both the href and the text. error.html keeps its empty `{% block footer %}` override unchanged. No styling is added.

body.source:
{% block footer %}
{% if source_link %}Source: {{ source_link.text }} · {% endif %}AGPL software must be offered to its users as source code. {% endblock %}

body.text: States

There are two footer states. With a resolved link, it shows `Source: text · ` and then the note. Without one, it shows the note alone. A git failure is never surfaced as an error and never blocks the server from starting or reloading.

Link the current branch's remote, else `origin`, as returned by `git ls-remote --get-url` (user's choice). Rejected: always the remote named `upstream`. It would show the public repository in this checkout, but in a fork it points at the original project instead of the fork's modified source, which defeats the AGPL purpose. The user accepted that this checkout links the dev repository.

The footer reads `Source: <host/path link> · AGPL software must be offered to its users as source code.` (user's choice). Rejected: a fixed 'Source code' label, which hides where the link goes, and a single compact parenthesised line. Showing host/path lets a reader see which repository they are being offered.

Remove the whole `© Copyright 2026 by Dennis S` line, with nothing in its place. It is the only credit in the footer, so it is what the ask's 'Made by Dennis S' refers to. Rejected: keeping a copyright line beside the source link, which the user explicitly said could go.

Without a resolvable browsable remote, the footer shows the AGPL note alone, and the git read fails silently to None. Rejected: a hardcoded fallback URL, which would point forks and unrelated checkouts at the wrong source and is configuration nobody asked for. Also rejected: hiding the whole footer, which would drop the licence note exactly where no link can be offered.

Accept the scp-like, `ssh://` and `http(s)://` forms. SSH forms become `https://host/path` with the SSH port dropped, because the SSH port says nothing about the web port. HTTP(S) keeps its scheme and port. Userinfo is always stripped, because git returns embedded credentials verbatim and the footer is public. One `.git` suffix and surrounding slashes are trimmed. Everything else gives no link. Rejected: rewriting `git://` or `file://` to https, since neither reliably has a web page, and passing unknown forms through unchanged, which could put a local path or a non-http scheme into an href.

Leave error.html's empty footer override as it is. The 500 and 503 pages are developer-facing failure pages outside the ask. Rejected: removing the override, which changes pages nobody asked about for no user-facing gain.

Read the remote once per execution of src/server.py, which is a cold start plus every HMR reload, and publish it as a Jinja global. git runs in the directory holding the server's source. Rejected: per request, which adds a subprocess to every page view for a value that practically never changes. Also rejected: the process cwd, which can belong to a different repository than the code being served.

feature-brief:mw8ax3bp-627909.title: Bottom nav link after Child Pages and a floating Top button in the web UI

summary.body: Make long pages in the web UI quicker to move around. Two additions: (1) the page-top links strip of a page view (the `page-contents` nav whose in-page anchors end with "Child pages") gains a "Bottom" anchor right after "Child pages" that jumps to the end of the page, ahead of the pinned-child 🔗 links; (2) every web UI view gets a floating "Top" control with an up-arrow, fixed to the bottom-right corner of the viewport, that jumps back to the top of the page. Both are navigation only: no new routes, no state, no change to the MCP renderPage Markdown.

items.name: src/render_html.py: _contents_html
items.text: PURE. Builds the page-top links strip (`<nav class="page-contents" aria-label="Sections">`) of the structured HTML page body from PageType + Page + RefContext. Order today: optional `Parent 🔗` link, one `#section-<key>` anchor per declared section (with a count badge), `#section-references` "References", `#section-children` "Child pages" (always present), then each pinned child linked by title with the 🔗 mark (only when a RefContext is given). This IS the "nav" the ask means by "after Child Pages". Called only from render_page_html, which skips the strip entirely for a toc page. The MCP renderPage Markdown path (src/render.py) has no strip and must stay untouched.

items.name: src/templates/_base.html
items.text: PRESENTATION (Jinja shell, no I/O of its own). The shared page shell every web view extends - index.html, tree.html, error.html directly and page.html via _nav.html. It holds the theme toggle, `<div id="content">`, and `<div id="footer">` with the Source link + AGPL note as the last element of the body. error.html overrides only the footer *block* to empty, so the `#footer` div itself exists on every view. This is where a floating Top button belongs for it to appear across the whole web UI, and `#footer` is the natural target for a Bottom link.

items.name: src/static/styles.css
items.text: STATIC ASSET. Water.css overrides loaded by _base.html on every view. Holds the shell-level overrides (body.page width, disabled controls, theme colour additions) and the `.pasta-page`-scoped structured-render styling. A fixed-position Top button's styling goes here as its own id-scoped rule, with every colour taken from a water.css custom property.

items.name: src/templates/page.html, src/templates/_nav.html (read, not changed)
items.text: PRESENTATION. page.html renders the body, then `<hr />` and the `#page-actions` row (Archive / Set to delete / State Apply forms) - so on a page view the footer sits below those actions, and jumping to `#footer` brings the actions into view too. _nav.html is the page-view-only layout (sidebar, Page|Model toggle with its inline <style> block). Neither needs to change for this feature.

Pins the strip's exact tail with endswith: test_contents_strip_links_pinned_children_after_the_child_pages_anchor (References, Child pages, then pinned 🔗 links), test_contents_strip_names_only_the_pinned_children, test_contents_strip_without_a_context_keeps_todays_links (References, Child pages, `</nav>`), and test_contents_strip_keeps_the_child_pages_anchor_without_pinned_children. Architecture invariant (Web UI, HMR & live reload): "There are two renderers over the same page and the caller picks: renderPage returns the Markdown one byte-for-byte, while the web page body is built as structured HTML." The Bottom link goes in src/render_html.py only; src/render.py and the renderPage MCP output must not change.

Architecture invariant: "All structured-render styling is scoped under the pasta-page class and takes every colour from a water.css custom property." The Top button lives in the shell outside `.pasta-page`, so it gets its own id-scoped rule, but still takes every colour from a custom property that both src/static/water.css/light.min.css and dark.min.css define (confirmed present in both: --background, --background-alt, --border, --links, --text-main, --text-muted, --button-base, --button-hover, --focus).

The web UI uses only inline vanilla JS included into templates (_reloader.js, _theme.js, _view_toggle.js) and the locally served water.css - no frontend libraries or external assets (inferred from the templates, not a declared rule). The new controls add no routes and change no state.

Strip order: the pinned-children 🔗 links currently follow "Child pages" directly. Placing Bottom right after "Child pages" (the literal ask) puts it between the in-page anchors and the 🔗 page links, which keeps every scroll-this-page anchor together ahead of the open-another-page links. Prior art for scroll-to-top: page.html's archive / delete-schedule / status forms each call window.scrollTo(0, 0) on submit. That is form-submission behaviour, not a reusable control, so it neither conflicts with nor provides the Top button; leave it as is.

Where in the strip does Bottom go: directly after "Child pages" (before the pinned-child 🔗 links), or as the very last entry after them?
items.answer: Directly after "Child pages", before the pinned-child 🔗 links. It is the literal ask, and it keeps every anchor that scrolls this page together, with the 🔗 entries that open another page still last.

items.text: What does Bottom jump to: the shell's `#footer` (the true end of the page, below the page-actions row), or a new end-of-article anchor emitted by the body renderer (just after the Child pages section)?
items.answer: The shell's `#footer`. That div is on every view (error.html only empties its block) and is the last thing on the page, so the jump also shows the page-actions row. An anchor emitted by the renderer would stop above that row.

items.text: Is the floating Top control always visible, or hidden until the reader has scrolled down (which needs a scroll listener in JS)?
items.answer: Always visible. It needs only HTML and CSS, with no scroll listener. Hide-until-scrolled can be added later if the always-visible button gets in the way.

items.text: Which views carry the Top control: every view via the _base.html shell (index, tree, page, error), or the page view only via _nav.html?
items.answer: Every view, via the _base.html shell. The ask says "the web UI", and the workspace tree and index grow long too.

items.text: Is Top a plain fragment link (`<a href="#top">`, no JS, adds `#top` to the URL like the strip's own anchors) or a `<button>` that calls window.scrollTo with JS (no URL change)?
items.answer: A plain fragment link, `<a id="to-top" href="#top">`. With no element whose id is `top` (confirmed: rendered ids are always `section-*` / `element-*`), the HTML spec scrolls a `#top` fragment to the top of the document. That needs no JS and behaves like the strip's own anchors, including Back.

overview.body: This spec adds two ways to move around the web UI. (1) A "Bottom" anchor in the page-top links strip that the structured page body draws (src/render_html.py `_contents_html`). (2) A floating "↑ Top" link in the template shell every view shares (src/templates/_base.html, styled in src/static/styles.css). It leaves out: the MCP renderPage Markdown (src/render.py), which has no strip and stays byte-for-byte the same; the Markdown-rendered nav sidebar; any JavaScript, scroll-aware showing/hiding or smooth scrolling; and any new route, template variable or state.

body.text: Bottom anchor in the contents strip (pure)

`_contents_html(page_type: PageType, page: Page, ref_context: RefContext | None) -> str` keeps its signature and stays a pure function of its arguments. One entry is appended right after the Child pages anchor and before the pinned-child links: `Bottom`, a fixed string with nothing to escape, no count badge and no 🔗 mark (it scrolls this page; it opens no other page). The strip's order becomes: [Parent 🔗] · one anchor per declared section · References · Child pages · Bottom · [pinned children 🔗]. Bottom appears whenever the strip appears, with or without a RefContext. A toc page renders no strip (render_page_html returns early), so it gets no Bottom anchor.

body.text: src/static/styles.css gets one id-scoped block, placed after the "Theme color additions" block and before the structured-page-render block. Every colour is a water.css custom property that both light.min.css and dark.min.css define, so the link follows the theme. z-index keeps it above the Model iframe overlay (position: absolute inside #view-body).
Behaviour, states and error paths

Both controls are static markup with no runtime state and no failure path: a click is ordinary fragment navigation. `#footer` scrolls to the shell footer, and `#top` (no element carries that id) scrolls to the top of the document. On a page too short to scroll, both are no-ops. The fragment is added to the URL and joins history exactly as the strip's `#section-*` anchors already do. The reloader's scroll restore after a live refresh is untouched. The page view's archive / delete / status forms keep their own scrollTo(0, 0) on submit.

Bottom goes directly after "Child pages", before the pinned-child 🔗 links. Rejected: putting it last, after the 🔗 links. That would mix a scroll-this-page anchor in among the open-another-page links and depart from the literal ask ("after Child Pages").

Bottom targets the shell's `#footer`. Rejected: a new end-of-article anchor emitted by render_html. It would stop above page.html's page-actions row and footer, so it would not reach the bottom. The cost is accepted: the body renderer refers to one id the shell declares. `#footer` is on every view (error.html empties only the block inside it), so the target always exists where the strip is drawn.

The Top link is always visible. Rejected: hiding it until the reader scrolls. That needs a scroll listener and a new or extended script include, which nothing in the ask requires; it can be layered on later without changing the markup.
Top lives in _base.html, on every view. Rejected: only the page view via _nav.html. The ask names the web UI as a whole, and the workspace tree and index are the other views that grow long.

Top is `<a id="to-top" href="#top">`, a plain fragment link. Rejected: a `<button>` with window.scrollTo. That adds JS for one line of behaviour, and its Back-button behaviour would differ from the strip's anchors. It relies on no element having id `top`; render_html only emits `section-*` and `element-*` ids, and the templates use none.

feature-brief:mw985ekn-63568e.title: Epic executing-stage findings, in-place edits for findings and contracts, and a controller-only notice

summary.body:
Make the epic page workable while its subagents are building. Three gaps today: (1) once an epic reaches `executing`, nothing can be recorded on its review findings list, so problems a dispatched agent reports back (an integration collision, a contract that turned out wrong) have nowhere to land on the epic; (2) a recorded finding or shared contract cannot be corrected in place - the only route is remove and re-add, which loses the element's id and position and invites a second agent to work from a half-rewritten list; (3) nothing on the epic tells a dispatched subagent that the epic is the controller's page, so subagents end up writing to it instead of to their own feature-brief.

Outcome wanted: findings can be added (and edited) while the epic is executing; findings and contracts each gain an in-place edit command, and the guidance that today tells agents to remove-and-re-add points at the edit instead; and every epic carries, from the moment it is created, a fixed read-only notice stating that only the controlling agent edits this page and that each dispatched agent writes only to its own feature-brief and its children.

Tension to settle while grounding: 'report from an agent with addFinding' and 'agents edit only their own pages' are reconciled by reading the first as the controller recording what an agent reported back - the subagent itself never writes to the epic.

SetElementFieldCommand (kind SET_ELEMENT_FIELD) already carries element_map AND element_const via ElementWriteCommand, but the only factory, set_element_field_cmd, builds the const/flag shape (escalateQuestion, markCommitStale). An in-place element edit is a new factory here, not a new command kind. is_field_setter already excludes SET_ELEMENT_FIELD, so an edit stays out of the self-direction do list.

items.name: src/commands.py
items.text: Pure core. _apply_element_writes writes each mapped arg whose key is present in args (partial update, element id and position preserved) - including a key sent as null, which would blank the field; _validate_args treats null as absent only for the required check. create_page seeds sections via initial_sections, and apply_command backfills a page against its type via the same function on every write.

A static notice field needs a fixed initial value declared on the FieldSpec and seeded there.

Production page types are off-limits in tests: test mode empties REGISTRY and get_page_type raises ProductionTypeInTestError. Only the parametrized structural invariants in tests/test_pagetypes.py (PRODUCTION_TYPES incl. _EPIC, _AGENT_PLAN) run over production; new behaviour is tested through src/testtypes.py fixtures, and the epic declaration itself is recorded by the declaration and the architecture page.

Page types are data: the epic change is a declaration in epic.py, enforced uniformly by src/commands.py with no per-type logic. A field setter's description is a short one-line label and never repeats the field instruction (validate_pagetype_setter_descriptions); at most one do-eligible setter per (section, field) (validate_pagetype_field_setters); every element_map field must be declared on the list field (test_content_commands_target_real_fields over SET_ELEMENT_FIELD).

Declaration validation is one aggregated raise at load (validate_page_types via validate_registry) - PageType.__post_init__ never validates; spec dataclasses stay frozen values comparing by content (tuples, not dicts).

epic.py:171-175 - the findings list_cmds is legal_in=("planReview",). Opening it to executing collides with the field's own wording ('plan-review finding ... why it matters before any agent is dispatched') and with _EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS ('how the finding was applied to the plan': addWorkstream/addAgent/addDispatch/...), several of which are not even legal in executing (agent-plan structural edits are draft-only). The description and action set have to give, and setReviewVerdict must stay planReview-only so a finding added while executing never reopens the verdict.

No in-place edit exists for a finding or a contract: correcting one is removeX + addX, which creates a new element id (breaking anything that named the old one - a dispatch handoff or another workstream's brief quoting a contract) and moves it to the end unless re-anchored. set_element_field_cmd only stamps a constant, so the edit is a new factory over the existing SetElementFieldCommand kind; it must not become a do-eligible setter (is_field_setter already excludes SET_ELEMENT_FIELD).

src/commands.py _apply_element_writes writes a key present in args even when its value is null, so an all-optional edit sent with shape: null would blank a contract's required shape. The edit needs a defined null rule (reject a null for a field the add requires, or treat null as unchanged) and must reject an edit naming no field at all.

FieldSpec/initial_sections have no fixed-value concept: every field starts empty and every field is reachable by whatever command targets it. A static notice is new: it needs a declared value seeded at create, and a load-time rule that no command targets that field, otherwise it is just another prose field. Existing epics get it only through apply_command's backfill on their next write (renderPage does not backfill) - acceptable, no epic exists in this workspace.

tests/test_docsgen.py:237-266 pins the exact describe field dict (choices/elementFields/elementStates/...); surfacing a fixed value as a new describe key changes those expectations and the docsgen field line.

The ask reads 'report from an agent with addFinding' alongside 'agents edit their own pages only, not the controller epic page'. Read together: the controller records what a dispatched agent reported as an epic finding; the dispatched agent itself never writes the epic. The agent-plan's agents/reporting descriptions currently say only 'an agent reports by driving its own brief' and never forbid writing the epic, so that rule exists nowhere in text yet.

Page types & FSM implementation (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2): 'The command factories' paragraph lists set_element_field_cmd as 'the flag-setting shape' - add the in-place element edit factory; the Data model paragraph ('A field is a scalar ..., a prose body, a list ..., or a blocks field') and initial_sections' 'empty sections' wording - add the fixed-value field and the no-writer rule; 'Where a page type lives' - note the epic's controller notice.

In which epic statuses are addFinding / removeFinding / reorderFinding (and the new editFinding) legal - executing only on top of planReview, or also review, where the controller's integration review sends work back with requestChanges?
items.answer: planReview, executing and review. executing is what was asked; review is added because requestChanges (review -> executing) is the controller sending integrated work back, and the reason it gives is exactly a finding with nowhere else to land. setReviewVerdict stays planReview-only, so recording a finding later never reopens the plan verdict.

items.text: Which epic lists get an in-place edit command - only findings and contracts as asked, or every list (workstreams, constraints, components, conflicts, documentation) while we are there?
items.answer: Only findings and contracts, as asked: editFinding and editContract. They are the two lists that change while agents are building (contracts get corrected as agents hit them; findings get updated as fixes land). The other lists are settled before dispatch, and the new factory makes adding an edit to any of them a one-line declaration later.

items.text: What are the edit semantics: which args, partial or whole-element, what does a null value mean, and is an edit that names no field rejected?
items.answer: Partial, in place: edit<Noun>(<noun>Id, <every element field as an optional arg with the add's choices>). Only the fields sent are written; id, position and any element status are untouched. A null value means 'not sent' - the same rule _validate_args already applies to required args - so null can never blank a field (an optional field cannot be cleared by an edit; that is accepted). An edit that sends no field besides the id is rejected with a ValidationError, because it would silently do nothing.

items.text: How is the static controller notice modelled - a new field kind, a fixed value on an ordinary prose field, page-type description/stage guidance - and is it re-seeded when the declared text changes or frozen at the value the page was created with?
items.answer: A fixed value on an ordinary prose field: FieldSpec gains `fixed: str | None`, `_prose(..., fixed=...)` declares it, initial_sections seeds it, and a load-time validator rejects any command targeting a fixed field and any fixed value on a non-prose field. It is re-seeded, not frozen: initial_sections always writes the declared text for a fixed field (create and every apply_command backfill), because nothing else may write it and the declaration is its only source. On the epic it is a new first section, 'Controller notice', so it is the first thing anyone reading the page sees.

items.text: Does _EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS (the optional 'how the finding was applied' enum) need executing-stage values now that findings can be recorded while agents are building?
items.answer: Yes, two values: editContract (the finding was applied by correcting a shared contract in place) and redispatch (applied by sending the dispatch back for a fix round). Both are commands that exist in executing. Nothing else is added; 'edit' stays the catch-all.

items.text: Is 'dispatched agents edit only their own pages' enforced by the store, or is it an instruction carried by the notice and the agent-plan field descriptions?
items.answer: An instruction, not a store rule. Pasta has no notion of which agent is calling - the controller and a dispatched agent are the same MCP client - so there is nothing to enforce against. The rule is carried by the epic's fixed controller notice and by the agent-plan's agents and reporting field descriptions, which are what a dispatched agent's mission and reporting checklist are written from.

items.text: Where is a list's in-place edit declared - a separate edit_element_cmd factory that repeats the list's args, field, label and legal_in, or an option on list_cmds that derives all of them from the list it already describes?
items.answer: An option on list_cmds: editable: bool = False (the user's call, after PR review). The edit reuses the list's add_args (each made optional), noun, label and legal_in, so nothing is listed twice and the standalone edit_element_cmd factory goes away. An editable list that carries a ref_check is refused at declaration, because the store checks cross-page references on adds only and an edit would bypass it.

def edit_element_cmd(section: str, *, args: tuple[ArgSpec, ...], field: str = "items",
                     singular: str | None = None, label: str | None = None,
                     name: str | None = None,
                     legal_in: tuple[str, ...] | None = None) -> CommandSpec:
    """A SET_ELEMENT_FIELD command that edits the id'd element in place - the edit shape beside the
    flag shape above. Each of `args` becomes optional and is mapped onto its same-named element field,
    keeping its choices, so only the fields sent are written and the element keeps its id, position
    and status. Pass the list's add args to make every field editable. The noun is derived as in
    list_cmds (edit<Noun>, <noun>Id)."""
    noun = singular or _singular(field if field != "items" else section)
    label = label or noun
    editable = tuple(replace(arg, required=False) for arg in args)
    return SetElementFieldCommand(name=name or f"edit{_cap(noun)}",
                                  description=f"edit {_a(label)} {label} in place",
                                  section=section, field=field,
                                  args=(_text(f"{noun}Id"), *editable),
                                  element_map=_same_named(editable), legal_in=legal_in)

def _apply_element_writes(element: dict[str, Any], command: ElementWriteCommand,
                          args: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Set an element's mapped-arg fields and any literal `element_const` fields in place. A mapped
    arg sent as null counts as not sent - the same rule the arg validator applies - so a write
    never blanks a field."""
    for element_field, arg_name in command.element_map:
        if args.get(arg_name) is not None:
            element[element_field] = args[arg_name]
    for element_field, value in command.element_const:
        element[element_field] = value


def _set_element_field(page: Page, command: ElementWriteCommand, args: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Set fields on an existing list element (args[0] identifies it by id), id preserved. An edit -
    mapped args and no constant - must write at least one field, or it would silently do nothing."""
    if (command.element_map and not command.element_const
            and all(args.get(arg_name) is None for _, arg_name in command.element_map)):
        raise ValidationError(
            f"Command '{command.name}' names no field to change: send at least one of " +
            ", ".join(arg_name for _, arg_name in command.element_map) + ".")
    _apply_element_writes(_find_element(page, command, args), command, args)

body.text: 1. In-place element edit as a list_cmds option (pure, src/pagetypes/core/commands.py)

list_cmds gains editable: bool = False. When true it appends a fourth command, a SetElementFieldCommand edit<Noun>(<noun>Id, ...) over the list's own add_args, each made optional with dataclasses.replace (choices and description kept) and mapped onto its same-named element field. It inherits the noun, label and legal_in the list already derives, so nothing is declared twice. Element-block args stay on the add only. No new command kind: SET_ELEMENT_FIELD and the core's element write path already do a partial, id-preserving write, and is_field_setter already excludes it, so it never enters the do list. An editable list that carries a ref_check raises ValueError at declaration, because the store checks cross-page references on adds only and an edit would bypass it. Off by default, so no other list changes.

def list_cmds(section: str, *, ..., add_args: tuple[ArgSpec, ...] | None = None, ...,
              add: bool = True, remove: bool = True, reorder: bool = True,
              editable: bool = False, ...) -> tuple[CommandSpec, ...]:
    ...
    if editable:
        if ref_check is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"list_cmds({section!r}): an editable list cannot carry a ref_check - "
                             "references are checked on adds only, so an edit would bypass it")
        edit_args = tuple(replace(arg, required=False) for arg in add_args or ())
        out.append(SetElementFieldCommand(
            name=f"edit{cap}", description=f"edit {_a(label)} {label} in place",
            section=section, field=field, args=(_text(id_arg), *edit_args),
            element_map=_same_named(edit_args), legal_in=legal_in))

body.text: 2. Null and empty-edit rule (pure, src/commands.py)

The element write path writes a mapped arg only when its value is not null - the same 'null means not sent' rule the arg validator already applies to required args. Every existing element transition's extra args are required, so this changes nothing for them. A SET_ELEMENT_FIELD command that maps args and stamps no constant (an edit) must write at least one field: when every mapped arg is absent or null, the command is rejected before anything is written.
3. Fixed-value prose field (pure, core/fields.py, core/pagetype.py, core/validation.py, describe.py, docsgen.py)

FieldSpec gains fixed: str | None = None, normalized in post-init exactly like description (dedent, strip leading newlines, rstrip) when it is not None. The _prose helper takes fixed= and passes it through. initial_sections writes a fixed field's declared value unconditionally - before the 'already present' skip - so a page is seeded with it at create and re-seeded by apply_command's backfill on every write: the declaration is the field's only source. Two load-time rules join the aggregated raise: validate_field_spec reports a fixed value on any field that is not PROSE, and a new validate_pagetype_fixed_fields(page_type) reports every FieldCommand whose (section, field) is a fixed field, because a fixed field that a command can write is not fixed. describe_page_type adds a boolean fixed key to each field; docsgen's field line adds the note 'fixed - seeded from the page type, no command writes it' when it is true. Renderers need no change: the value is ordinary prose content.
4. Epic declaration (src/pagetypes/epic.py)

A new FIRST section, SectionSpec('notice', 'Controller notice', (_prose('body', description='Controller notice fixed text.', fixed=_CONTROLLER_NOTICE),)), with no command targeting it. The findings list moves from legal_in planReview to planReview, executing and review. The findings and contracts lists are declared editable=True, which gives editFinding and editContract (editContract is legal wherever the other contract commands are, i.e. every non-terminal status). _EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS gains editContract and editDispatch. setReviewVerdict stays planReview-only. The findings description is reworded to cover findings recorded while executing and in review and to name editFinding; the contracts description gains a sentence naming editContract and why a contract's id must stay stable.

body.source:
_CONTROLLER_NOTICE:
This epic is the controller's page. Only the controlling agent - the session that created
this epic and dispatches its agent plan - runs commands on it or on its agent plan. A
dispatched agent works only on its own feature-brief (its workstream's briefId) and that
brief's child pages; it never edits this epic, the agent plan, or another workstream's brief.
An agent reports by driving its own brief and handing its outcome back to the controller,
which records what came back: reportDispatch on the agent plan, addFinding or editFinding
here for a problem it raised, and editContract here for a shared contract it corrected.

body.text: 5. Agent-plan instructions (src/pagetypes/epic.py, _AGENT_PLAN)

The agents field description gains: confine every mission to the agent's own feature-brief and that brief's child pages - a dispatched agent never runs a command on the epic, this agent plan, or another workstream's brief, because those are the controller's pages. The reporting field description gains: the agent writes only its own brief; the controller, never the agent, records the result here (reportDispatch) and on the epic (addFinding, editFinding, editContract). No command or FSM change on the agent plan.
6. Error paths

body.source:
editFinding / editContract with an unknown id     -> NotFoundError  "No element with id '<id>' in <section>.<field>."  (existing)
edit with only the id, or every field null        -> ValidationError "Command 'editX' names no field to change: ..."
edit with a value outside the field's choices     -> ValidationError (existing arg validation)
editFinding / addFinding outside planReview/executing/review -> IllegalCommandError (existing legality)
any command declared against a fixed field         -> load-time ValueError listing it (aggregated raise)
fixed= on a scalar, list or blocks field           -> load-time ValueError (validate_field_spec)

body.text: Findings commands are legal in planReview, executing and review. Rejected: executing only (as literally asked) - review's requestChanges sends integrated work back and its reason is a finding with nowhere else to land, at the cost of one more status in a tuple. Rejected: every status - before planReview there is no plan to find fault with. setReviewVerdict stays planReview-only so a later finding never reopens the plan verdict.
Edit commands only for findings and contracts. Rejected: an edit on every list - the others are settled before any dispatch and nobody asked; editable=True makes adding one later a single flag.

Partial in-place edit: id plus every element field as an optional arg; only non-null fields are written; an edit writing nothing is rejected. Rejected: whole-element replace (forces resending unchanged fields and reintroduces the stale-read problem the edit exists to fix); null-clears-the-field (lets an agent blank a contract's required shape); a new EDIT_ELEMENT command kind (the SET_ELEMENT_FIELD kind already performs a partial id-preserving write, and a new kind would touch the CommandSpec union, apply dispatch, describe and every kind-set test for no behavioural gain).

A fixed value on a prose field, declared on FieldSpec, always re-seeded by initial_sections, with load-time rules that it is prose-only and that no command writes it; placed as the epic's first section. Rejected: a new STATIC field kind (every kind switch in render, search, describe and initial_sections would need a branch for what is just prose with no writer); putting the text in the page-type description or stage guidance (not on the page, so a human or agent reading the epic never sees it - the ask is explicitly a field on the page); freezing the created value (the text would drift from the declaration with no command able to fix it).

Add editContract and editDispatch to _EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS. editDispatch (settled at PR review) covers a dispatch changed by a fix round (redispatch) or by a rewording of its handoff, instead of naming only the redispatch transition; it is a label, since the agent plan has no editDispatch command. Rejected: leaving the enum plan-only (an executing-stage finding could only say 'edit'); reopenDecomposition or blockDispatch (a transition or a record, not a way of applying a finding). 'edit' stays the catch-all: an editFinding value would describe a finding applied by editing a finding, which is circular.

The own-pages-only rule is an instruction carried by the epic's fixed notice and the agent-plan's agents and reporting descriptions. Rejected: a store-level guard - pasta has no caller identity, the controller and a subagent are the same MCP client, so any guard would be either unenforceable or would also lock out the controller.

Declare the edit as list_cmds(..., editable=True), reusing the list's add_args, noun, label and legal_in; the standalone edit_element_cmd factory is removed. Rejected: the separate factory of the first build - it repeated each list's args, field, label and legal_in and needed module constants just to share the args; editable_args= naming a subset of the add args - every current use edits every field, so a bool is the smaller interface (settled by the user at PR review). An editable list with a ref_check is refused at declaration, because the store checks references on adds only and an edit would bypass that check.

feature-brief:mw9pn4a9-25ad3d.title: Split the epic's agent plan into one agent-plan page per agent, named by its page id

summary.body:
An epic's dispatched agents cannot work from the agent plan as it stands. The plan is one pinned page holding every agent definition, every dispatch and the reporting contract, so it is required reading for every dispatch: each agent reads all the other agents' missions and runs, and identifies itself by a pair of ids (an agent role element plus a workstream element) that it can mix up with a neighbour's.

Outcome wanted: one agent-plan page per agent, and that page is the whole of what the agent is handed - its role, its capability (model tier), the exact task, the worktree it creates, and links to the feature-brief pages it works on. The agent's identity is that page's id: the role and workstream pair collapses into a single agentId, and the agent reports back onto that same page as it starts, works and finishes, so it cannot address another agent's record by mistake.

This is a refactor that simplifies the epic workflow, not an addition on top of it: the agent-plan page type is reshaped from one pinned page per epic into one page per agent, created by the controller directly under the epic, and the dispatch list and the epic's workstreams list go away. The only rule change outside the declarations is that an epic's gates over its agent-plan pages cannot pass with no agents: a child guard ignores archived children and fails when none of its type is left.

items.name: src/pagetypes/epic.py
items.text: Pure declaration, the heart of the change. _EPIC: a fixed Controller notice naming 'the agent plan' and reportDispatch; a workstreams list (name, briefId, scope, dependsOn) with add/remove/reorder; contracts whose owner is 'the workstream that defines it'; _EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS = addWorkstream, addAgent, addDispatch, addContract, addConstraint, askQuestion, editContract, editDispatch, edit; submitPlan requires (workstreams.items, questions.items) plus ChildStateGuard('agent-plan', ready); submitForReview ChildStateGuard('agent-plan', accepted, section=dispatches); ship ChildStateGuard('feature-brief', shipped); auto_children=(AutoChildSpec('agent-plan'),). The components, constraints, conflicts, questions and review descriptions are worded around workstreams, dispatches and the agent plan. _AGENT_PLAN: an agents list (role, model in _MODEL_TIERS cheap/standard/capable, mission, reports), a dispatches list (agentId, workstreamId, wave, worktree, handoff, outcome, blocker, status) on _DISPATCH_FSM pending -> dispatched -> reported -> accepted with redispatch and block, a RefCheck tying workstreamId to the parent epic's workstreams, a reporting prose, and FSM draft/ready whose markReady is gated by the ParentStateGuard _EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER.

items.name: src/pagetypes/_registry.py
items.text: Pure. REGISTRY imports _AGENT_PLAN and _EPIC from .epic and maps both tags; is_auto_child_type reads AutoChildSpec off the parent type. Replacing the agent-plan type is a change to this import and map.

items.name: src/store.py Store._child_guard_failure (L1079-1102)
items.text: Pure over its inputs (a static method reading workspace pages, no I/O) though it lives in the effectful store. For each ChildStateGuard it walks page.child_ids, keeps the children whose type matches, and checks the page status (page form) or every element status (element form). It does not skip archived children, and over zero matching children it returns None - the guard passes vacuously. Every guard an epic declares on its agents is evaluated here, and only over DIRECT children.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/commands.py (list_cmds, set_scalar_cmd, set_prose_cmd, transition_cmd, transition_on_add_cmd)
items.text: Pure factories, reused as they are. transition_on_add_cmd builds a COMPOUND that adds one element to a list field and fires a page transition in one atomic command (used today by bug-report and simple-change close), which is the existing shape for an agent writing a report entry as it moves its own page's status. list_cmds supports add-only lists (remove=False) and an editable in-place edit.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/specs.py (ChildStateGuard, ParentStateGuard, AutoChildSpec, RefCheck)
items.text: Pure frozen declarations. ChildStateGuard's docstring states the 'for every child page of type X' semantics the store evaluates; ParentStateGuard is only enforced when the parent is of the named type; AutoChildSpec is what makes a child pinned; RefCheck(scope='parent') is used in production by addDispatch's workstreamId and by the feature-spec decision block's questionId, so it stays in use after the dispatch list goes.

items.name: src/instructions.py (L49-50, L90-92)
items.text: Pure text served by the instructions tool. L49-50 place an epic's feature-briefs under the epic; L90 summarizes epic as 'built by subagents dispatched from its pinned agent plan'; L92 is the agent-plan one-liner. Hand-written, not generated from the registry, and no test pins it to REGISTRY.

PRODUCTION_TYPES names _AGENT_PLAN by import and test_production_types_are_exactly_the_registered_ones holds that list equal to REGISTRY, so the new type must be added there. test_list_cmds_threads_ref_check_onto_the_add_only uses a 'dispatches'/'workstreamId' list only as example names and does not touch production.

items.name: src/testtypes.py + tests/test_store.py
items.text: Test-only. test-lifecycle declares ChildStateGuard in both forms over its pinned test-child (beginImplementation page form, submitForReview/ship element form) and test_ship_guard_blocks_until_child_complete exercises them. Every existing child guard, fixture and production alike, targets a pinned child that always exists, so a change to how the guard treats zero or archived children is tested here through fixtures.

items.name: scripts/gen_page_type_docs.py + src/docsgen.py + src/statecharts.py
items.text: Generated, no source change expected. docsite/page-types/ is gitignored and regenerated by the script, which never deletes stale files (agent-plan-*.md would linger locally only). statecharts serves a machine per registered type through a module __getattr__, so AgentPlanMachine disappears with the type and no bound list needs editing.

pyproject.toml: requires-python = ">=3.14", managed with uv; dev dependency pytest-testmon>=2.3.0 and CLAUDE.md 'Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing'; [tool.pyright] typeCheckingMode = "recommended".
CLAUDE.md copy rule: use the word "create" instead of "mint" when creating something - applies to every new description, notice and comment.

Production page types are off-limits in tests: test mode empties REGISTRY and get_page_type raises ProductionTypeInTestError. Only the parametrized structural invariants in tests/test_pagetypes.py run over production (PRODUCTION_TYPES, held equal to REGISTRY by test_production_types_are_exactly_the_registered_ones); behaviour is tested through src/testtypes.py fixtures, and the epic and agent declarations themselves are recorded by the declaration and the architecture page.

Page types are data: the change is a declaration in src/pagetypes/, enforced uniformly by src/commands.py and the store with no per-type logic. A field setter's description is a one-line label that never repeats the field instruction; at most one do-eligible setter per (section, field); a fixed field has no writer; declaration errors are one aggregated raise at load (validate_page_types via validate_registry).

ChildStateGuard sees only DIRECT children (architecture page invariant 'Lifecycle sequencing between sibling pinned children is expressed as a status on the parent'), so any page whose status an epic transition gates on must be a direct child of the epic.
The ask itself: a refactor that leaves the epic workflow simpler than today - fewer page types, sections and commands net, not a new layer beside the old one.

Vacuous guard. Store._child_guard_failure passes when no child of the guarded type exists. Today an epic cannot reach planReview without agents only because submitPlan requires workstreams.items and the pinned agent-plan (always present) must be ready, which in turn requires agents and dispatches. Once the workstream list and the pinned plan are replaced by ordinary agent pages, 'every agent page ready' and 'every agent page accepted' pass over zero agents. The same hole already exists at ship: 'every child feature-brief shipped' passes with no briefs, which the workstreams description warns about ('lets an epic ship having built nothing') but nothing enforces.

Archived children still count. _child_guard_failure walks every child_id without checking Page.archived. Dropping an agent today is removeAgent/removeDispatch on the plan; with a page per agent it is archivePage, and an archived draft or blocked agent page would then hold submitPlan or submitForReview shut with no way to clear it but unarchiving.

The agent-plan's own design goal 'Define a role once and dispatch it many times rather than writing a near-identical agent per workstream' is reversed by the ask: one page per agent run, carrying its role, capability, task and worktree. The dispatch's handoff and the per-run fix-round record (redispatch of the same element) have to land on that page instead.

Who writes what. The epic's Controller notice and the agent-plan agents/reporting descriptions say a dispatched agent writes only its own feature-brief and never the agent plan; the controller records results with reportDispatch. The ask has the agent write its own agent page as it starts and executes, so the notice, the reporting rule and the controller/agent split all change wording.

epic.py _EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS lists addWorkstream, addAgent, addDispatch and editDispatch; editDispatch already names a command that does not exist (dispatches is not declared editable). The contracts owner ('the workstream that defines it') and the findings text ('Say which workstream or agent') point at workstream ids that will no longer exist.

Stored data: no live workspace file in .pasta-data holds an epic or agent-plan page; only .pasta-data/backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6/20260821T190516Z.json holds one of each. Restoring that backup after the type is gone would carry a page whose type no longer resolves (get_page_type returns None). Accepted as backup-only history; no migration.

Page types & FSM implementation (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2): 'Where a page type lives' says 'epic.py holds epic with agent-plan' and 'epic and agent-plan share a ParentStateGuard outright' - becomes epic with its agent pages, which are ordinary (not pinned) children. 'Which cross-page rules the store enforces' gains the epic's agent guards. If the guard's treatment of zero or archived children changes, the 'Sequencing a lifecycle with parent statuses' paragraph and the invariant ending 'finds none of its type and passes vacuously' must be reworded to the new rule. The code-reference list has no epic entry today, so nothing to drop there.

Page types & FSM implementation (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2): the 'Guidance: per status, and per workspace' paragraph lists which types declare stage guidance ('architecture and decision-record ... the feature-brief for its seven working statuses, and simple-change and bug-report ...') - add the epic's decomposition guidance.

Page types & FSM implementation (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2): the epic gains a Scheduling prose section the controller dispatches its agent-plan pages from in waves; the decomposition stage guidance points at it.
Does the epic's workstreams list survive as the decomposition an agent page points at, or is it absorbed into the agent pages so the agent page id is the only id an agent run has?
items.answer: Absorbed: the epic's workstreams list is removed and the agent page is the workstream, so its page id is the only id a run has. See the spec decision.

items.text: Where do the agent pages sit: as direct children of the epic with the agent-plan type removed, or under a slimmed-down plan page kept as a container?
items.answer: Direct children of the epic; the agent-plan type and the epic's auto_children are removed, because the epic's guards see only direct children.

items.text: How is an epic kept from passing submitPlan and submitForReview with zero agent pages, now that the guard over them passes vacuously on an empty set?
items.answer: A ChildStateGuard fails when no non-archived child of its type exists. Existing guards all target always-present pinned children, so only the epic's gates change (submitPlan/submitForReview need an agent, ship needs a brief).

items.text: Should an archived child page be ignored by a ChildStateGuard, so archiving an agent page is how an agent is dropped?
items.answer: Yes: archived children are ignored by every ChildStateGuard, and archiving an agent page drops the agent.

items.text: What is an agent page's lifecycle - its statuses, which transitions the controller fires and which the dispatched agent fires, and how the agent's reports as it starts and executes are recorded on it?
items.answer: draft -> ready -> working -> finished -> accepted, blocked off working. Controller: setters in draft, markReady, reopen, accept, redispatch. Agent: start, addReport, finish, block. start/finish/block/redispatch each add a report entry atomically with the transition.

items.text: What does the agent page's 'capability' hold: the model tier the agent is dispatched on (today's cheap/standard/capable), or something else such as a tool or permission set?
items.answer: The model tier: a capability scalar with today's cheap / standard / capable choices.

items.text: With the dispatches list's wave gone, how is dispatch order between agents expressed?
items.answer: addLink role depends-on from an agent page to each agent page that must be accepted before it starts; the wave field is dropped.

items.text: Is the per-agent page type named `agent` or does it keep the `agent-plan` name?
items.answer: The user's call: keep the agent-plan name. The page type tag is agent-plan, its variables are _AGENT_PLAN (FSM AgentPlan), and prose that refers to the page says 'agent-plan page'. 'Agent' stays the word for the actor - the dispatched subagent that is handed its agent-plan page. Finding actions become addAgentPlan / editAgentPlan.

items.text: Where do the rules for where an epic's feature-briefs and agent-plan pages are created live: in the served instructions' Pasta setup list, or on the epic itself?
items.answer: The user's call: on the epic. Both notes leave the instructions' Pasta setup list and become the epic's stage guidance for decomposition (the status in which the briefs and agent-plan pages are created), as a DECOMPOSITION constant in _stage_guidance.py. The general rule that epics go under the Features toc stays in the instructions.

items.text: Where is the order an epic's agents are dispatched in documented, so the controller can dispatch them in waves?
items.answer: The user's call: in a new Scheduling section on the epic, a prose body written for the controller to read and dispatch the agent-plan pages from in waves. The decomposition stage guidance tells the controller to write it. The depends-on links between agent-plan pages stay as they are - they are what each agent sees; Scheduling is what the controller dispatches from. No wave field and no new guard.

def _lifecycle_in_review(store):
    """A test-lifecycle page in `review` whose pinned test-child step is done and check passed, so
    only ship's guard over its test-flow children is left to decide ship."""
    workspace = store.create_workspace("demo")
    result = store.create_page(workspace.id, "test-lifecycle", "Dark mode")
    parent, child = result.page, _child(result, "test-child")
    _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [
        {"command": "setSummary", "args": {"text": "A dark theme."}},
        {"command": "beginPlanning"},
    ])
    step_id = _mutate(store, workspace.id, child.id, [
        {"command": "addStep", "args": {"text": "build"}}]).created_ids[0]
    check_id = _mutate(store, workspace.id, child.id, [
        {"command": "addCheck", "args": {"text": "renders"}}]).created_ids[0]
    _mutate(store, workspace.id, child.id, [{"command": "markReady"}])
    _mutate(store, workspace.id, child.id, [
        {"command": "markStepDone", "args": {"stepId": step_id}},
        {"command": "markCheckPassed", "args": {"checkId": check_id}},
    ])
    _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [
        {"command": "addPart", "args": {"name": "Renderer"}},
        {"command": "beginImplementation"},
    ])
    _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [{"command": "submitForReview"}])
    return workspace, parent


def test_child_guard_refuses_a_page_with_no_child_of_its_type(store):
    workspace, parent = _lifecycle_in_review(store)
    with pytest.raises(IllegalCommandError, match="there is no 'test-flow' child page"):
        _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [{"command": "ship"}])


def test_child_guard_ignores_an_archived_child(store):
    workspace, parent = _lifecycle_in_review(store)
    stalled = store.create_page(workspace.id, "test-flow", "Stalled", parent_id=parent.id).page
    _mutate(store, workspace.id, stalled.id, [{"command": "open"}])
    _closed_flow_child(store, workspace.id, parent.id)
    with pytest.raises(IllegalCommandError, match="is 'open'"):
        _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [{"command": "ship"}])
    store.archive_page(workspace.id, stalled.id)
    shipped = _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [{"command": "ship"}]).page
    assert shipped.status == "done"


def test_child_guard_refuses_when_its_only_child_is_archived(store):
    workspace, parent = _lifecycle_in_review(store)
    flow = _closed_flow_child(store, workspace.id, parent.id)
    store.archive_page(workspace.id, flow.id)
    with pytest.raises(IllegalCommandError, match="there is no 'test-flow' child page"):
        _mutate(store, workspace.id, parent.id, [{"command": "ship"}])

detail.source:
"""A cross-page transition guard over the status of a page's children, evaluated in the store.

    It holds when the page has at least one non-archived child of type `child_type` and every such
    child passes, in one of two forms:
    - element form (`section`/`field` given): every element in that list field must have a status
      in `allowed`;
    - page form (`section`/`field` omitted): the child page's own status must be in `allowed`.
    An archived child is history and is not counted, and with no live child of the type the guard
    fails rather than passing over nothing. `allowed` is the set of statuses that satisfy the guard
    - usually one, but more than one lets a guard treat several as equivalent (e.g. a step counts as
    addressed when done or skipped). Otherwise the transition is rejected with `message`.
    """

# Seeded into every agent page as its first section and written by no command: who writes this page.
_AGENT_NOTICE = """
    This page is one dispatched agent's whole assignment, and its page id is the agent's id. The
    controller - the session that created the epic above it - writes the assignment, task and
    reporting contract, links the feature-briefs the agent works on, and is the only one to run
    markReady, reopen, accept or redispatch here. The dispatched agent creates the worktree named
    here and works only in it, runs start on this page as its first command, adds a report as each
    step lands, and ends with finish or block. It writes only this page and the feature-briefs this
    page links to, with their child pages, and never runs a command on the epic or on another
    agent's page.
    """


_AGENT = PageType(
    tag="agent",
    name="Agent",
    description=(
        "One subagent an epic dispatches: its role, capability, exact task and the worktree it "
        "creates, linked to the feature-briefs it works on. Its page id is the agent's id, and the "
        "agent reports back onto this page as it starts and works. Created by the controller as a "
        "direct child of its epic."
    ),
    sections=(
        SectionSpec("notice", "Agent notice", (
            _prose("body", description="Agent notice fixed text.", fixed=_AGENT_NOTICE),
        )),
        SectionSpec("assignment", "Assignment", (
            _scalar("role", description="""
                What this agent is, named as a role a reader recognises - implementer, test writer,
                integration reviewer. One agent page is one dispatch, so the role describes this run
                rather than a definition shared with other agents.
                """),
            _scalar("capability", choices=_MODEL_TIERS, description="""
                The model tier this agent is dispatched on. Name it on every agent: an omitted tier
                silently inherits the session's most capable and most expensive model. Use cheap for
                mechanical single-file work whose content is already written down, standard for
                multi-file integration and judgement, and capable for architecture and final review.
                """),
            _scalar("worktree", description="""
                The git worktree this agent creates and works in, by name. Give every agent a
                different one: two agents in one checkout overwrite each other's edits.
                """),
        )),
        SectionSpec("task", "Task", (
            _prose("body", description="""
                The exact work this agent does, written for a fresh agent with no history: it is
                handed this page id and nothing of the controller's context. Say which slice of the
                epic it owns and what done looks like, name the shared contracts it touches by their
                id on the epic, and add only the decisions it needs that its feature-briefs cannot
                tell it. Link each feature-brief it works on with addLink role works-on, and each
                agent page that must be accepted before it starts with role depends-on. Point at
                large artifacts by file path rather than pasting them.
                """),
        )),
        SectionSpec("reporting", "Reporting contract", (
            _prose("body", description="""
                What this agent must leave behind before it runs finish, written as a checklist the
                controller verifies before accepting: which commands it must have run on its linked
                feature-briefs, what status each brief and its plans must be left in, and what its
                finish report must say. An agent reports by driving its briefs and this page, not by
                handing prose back, so name the page status you expect rather than the summary you
                want to read.
                """),
        )),
        SectionSpec("reports", "Reports", (
            _list("items", element_fields=("text",), description="""
                Each one report written back onto this page while the agent works: start records
                that it began and the worktree it created, a report records each step as it lands,
                and finish or block records the outcome or what stopped it. The controller adds one
                when it redispatches, saying what the next round must fix, so the list is the record
                of every attempt this agent made.
                """),
        )),
    ),
    commands=(
        # The controller's fields are draft-only, so a dispatched agent's own nextActions never
        # offers them; reopen unlocks them again.
        set_scalar_cmd("assignment", "role", legal_in=("draft",)),
        set_scalar_cmd("assignment", "capability", choices=_MODEL_TIERS, legal_in=("draft",)),
        set_scalar_cmd("assignment", "worktree", legal_in=("draft",)),
        set_prose_cmd("task", legal_in=("draft",)),
        set_prose_cmd("reporting", label="reporting contract", legal_in=("draft",)),
        # The reports are the record of every attempt: they can be reordered, never removed.
        *list_cmds("reports", remove=False, add_args=(_text(),), legal_in=("working",)),
        transition_cmd("markReady", "draft -> ready",
                       requires=(("assignment", "role"), ("assignment", "capability"),
                                 ("assignment", "worktree"), ("task", "body"), ("reporting", "body")),
                       parent_guards=(_EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER,)),
        transition_cmd("reopen", "ready -> draft (unlocks the assignment, task and reporting contract)"),
        # Each status change past ready writes its reason as a report in the same command.
        transition_on_add_cmd("start", "ready -> working", section="reports", field="items",
                              description="report that the agent has started, with the worktree it created",
                              add_args=(_text(),)),
        transition_on_add_cmd("finish", "working -> finished", section="reports", field="items",
                              description="report the outcome AND finish", add_args=(_text(),)),
        transition_on_add_cmd("block", "working -> blocked", section="reports", field="items",
                              description="report what stopped the work AND block", add_args=(_text(),)),
        transition_cmd("accept", "finished -> accepted"),
        transition_on_add_cmd("redispatch", "finished or blocked -> ready", legal_in=("finished", "blocked"),
                              section="reports", field="items",
                              description="report what the next round must fix AND send the agent back",
                              add_args=(_text(),)),
        add_link_cmd(),
        set_title_cmd(),
    ),
    fsm=FSMSpec(
        name="Agent",
        initial="draft",
        states=("draft", "ready", "working", "finished", "blocked", "accepted"),
        terminal_states=("accepted",),
    ),
)
