"""The `epic` page type, and the `agent` pages created under it.

The two are declared together because they are designed against each other rather than
on their own, and reading one without the other would hide the coupling.
"""

_EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS = ("addAgent", "editAgent", "addContract", "addConstraint", "askQuestion",
                         "editContract", "edit")

_CONTROLLER_NOTICE = """
    This epic is the controller's page. Only the controlling agent - the session that created this
    epic and dispatches its agents - runs commands on it. Each dispatched agent is handed one agent
    page, a child of this epic whose page id is the agent's id; it works from that page, reports back
    onto it, and writes only that page and the feature-briefs it links to, with their child pages.
    It never edits this epic or another agent's page. The controller records here what an agent
    raises: addFinding or editFinding for a problem, and editContract for a shared contract it
    corrected.
    """

        "The root of a major feature too large for one feature-brief: it decomposes into several "
        "child feature-briefs and is built by subagents, each dispatched from an agent page of its "
        "own under the epic. Use it when the work splits into parts that each ship on their own; "
        "for one feature use a feature-brief, and for a small self-contained change use a "
        "simple-change."
    ),

        transition_cmd("submitPlan", "decomposition -> planReview",
                       requires=(("questions", "items"),),
                       guards=(ChildStateGuard("agent", _AGENT_PLANNED,
                                               "every agent page must be marked ready"),)),

import sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from src.errors import IllegalCommandError, ValidationError
from src.store import Store

store = Store(tempfile.mkdtemp())
ws = store.create_workspace("smoke")

def run(page_id, command, **args):
    token = store.get_page(ws.id, page_id).status_revision_token
    return store.mutate_page_batch(ws.id, page_id, [
        {"command": command, "args": {"statusRevisionToken": token, **args}}])

def refused(page_id, command, fragment, **args):
    try:
        run(page_id, command, **args)
    except (IllegalCommandError, ValidationError) as error:
        assert fragment in str(error), str(error)
        return
    raise AssertionError(f"{command} was not refused")

def author(agent_id):
    run(agent_id, "setRole", role="implementer")
    run(agent_id, "setCapability", capability="standard")
    run(agent_id, "setWorktree", worktree=f"wt-{agent_id[-6:]}")
    run(agent_id, "setTask", text="Build the thing.")
    run(agent_id, "setReporting", text="Leave the brief done.")

epic = store.create_page(ws.id, "epic", "Smoke epic")
assert epic.children == [], "an epic creates no pinned child any more"
epic_id = epic.page.id

early = store.create_page(ws.id, "agent", "Early", parent_id=epic_id).page
author(early.id)
refused(early.id, "markReady", "the epic must be in decomposition or later")

run(epic_id, "setSummary", text="A big feature.")
run(epic_id, "beginGrounding")
run(epic_id, "addComponent", name="src/x.py")
run(epic_id, "addConstraint", text="py3.14")
run(epic_id, "addConflict", text="none")
run(epic_id, "addDocumentation", text="none")
run(epic_id, "beginDecomposition")
run(epic_id, "askQuestion", text="Q?")
refused(epic_id, "submitPlan", "every agent page must be marked ready ('agent:")
store.archive_page(ws.id, early.id)
refused(epic_id, "submitPlan", "there is no 'agent' child page")

agent = store.create_page(ws.id, "agent", "Builder", parent_id=epic_id).page
assert agent.status == "draft" and "one dispatched agent" in agent.sections["notice"]["body"]
author(agent.id)
run(agent.id, "markReady")
refused(agent.id, "setTask", "", text="changed")            # controller fields are draft-only
run(epic_id, "submitPlan")
run(epic_id, "setReviewVerdict", verdict="build-ready")
run(epic_id, "approvePlan")
refused(epic_id, "submitForReview", "every agent must be accepted")

refused(agent.id, "addReport", "", text="too early")        # reports only while working
run(agent.id, "start", text="Started in worktree wt-a")      # 1
run(agent.id, "addReport", text="Step 1 landed")            # 2
run(agent.id, "finish", text="Done")                         # 3
run(agent.id, "redispatch", text="Fix the failing case")     # 4
run(agent.id, "start", text="Round two")                     # 5
run(agent.id, "block", text="Contract C1 is wrong")          # 6
run(agent.id, "redispatch", text="C1 corrected")             # 7
run(agent.id, "start", text="Round three")                   # 8
run(agent.id, "finish", text="Done again")                   # 9
run(agent.id, "accept")
page = store.get_page(ws.id, agent.id)
assert page.status == "accepted" and len(page.sections["reports"]["items"]) == 9

run(epic_id, "submitForReview")
refused(epic_id, "ship", "there is no 'feature-brief' child page")
print("smoke ok")

# expect: smoke ok

The epic carries a Scheduling section the decomposition guidance points at - describePageType('epic') lists 'scheduling' between 'contracts' and 'questions' with a setScheduling setter ('set the scheduling'); statusGuidance.decomposition ends with the Scheduling bullet; the registry validates and the six production-type test modules pass; on a temporary store setScheduling stores the body and an epic stored without the section is backfilled with an empty one on its next write.

overview.body: Replaces the epic's pinned agent-plan page with one `agent` page per dispatched agent, created by the controller as an ordinary direct child of the epic. An agent page holds the agent's role, capability (model tier), worktree, exact task and reporting contract, links the feature-briefs it works on, and carries the reports the agent writes as it starts, works and finishes; its page id is the agent's only id. The epic's workstreams list, the agent-plan type, the dispatch element FSM and the workstreamId ref check are removed, and the epic's two plan guards are pointed at its agent pages. One store rule changes so those guards cannot pass with no agents: a ChildStateGuard ignores archived children and fails when none of its type is left. Deliberately left out: any store enforcement of which agent writes which page (pasta has no caller identity), any change to the feature-brief family, and migration of stored agent-plan pages (no live workspace holds one).

body.text: Naming (supersedes the 'agent' tag below)

The per-agent page type keeps the agent-plan name: tag "agent-plan", declaration _AGENT_PLAN with _AGENT_PLAN_NOTICE, display name "Agent plan", FSM AgentPlan, and the epic's guards are ChildStateGuard("agent-plan", ...). Prose says "agent-plan page" only where it names the page itself; elsewhere it may speak of the agent, conflating the page with the subagent it is handed to. Everything else in this design stands as written with "agent" read as "agent-plan" wherever it is the type tag or variable.
Shape of the change

src/pagetypes/epic.py keeps _EPIC and replaces _AGENT_PLAN and _DISPATCH_FSM with one new page type _AGENT (tag "agent"). An agent page IS the workstream and the dispatch: the epic loses its workstreams section and its three commands, loses auto_children, and its submitPlan / submitForReview guards look at its agent children. _EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER and _MODEL_TIERS stay and move to the agent type's use. The registry swaps the import and the map entry. The only behaviour change outside page-type declarations is Store._child_guard_failure. Net surface: one page type out, one in; the epic drops one section and three commands; the dispatch element FSM, its five marks and the RefCheck on workstreamId disappear.
The agent page type

body.source:
tag="agent"  name="Agent"
description = "One subagent an epic dispatches: its role, capability, exact task and the worktree it
  creates, linked to the feature-briefs it works on. Its page id is the agent's id, and the agent
  reports back onto this page as it starts and works. Created by the controller as a direct child
  of its epic."

sections (in this order)
  notice      "Agent notice"        body       prose, fixed=_AGENT_NOTICE, description "Agent notice fixed text."
  assignment  "Assignment"          role       scalar
                                    capability scalar, choices=_MODEL_TIERS ("cheap", "standard", "capable")
                                    worktree   scalar
  task        "Task"                body       prose
  reporting   "Reporting contract"  body       prose
  reports     "Reports"             items      list, element_fields=("text",)

FSMSpec(name="Agent", initial="draft",
        states=("draft", "ready", "working", "finished", "blocked", "accepted"),
        terminal_states=("accepted",))

commands (every agency is "agent")
  set_scalar_cmd("assignment", "role", legal_in=("draft",))                       -> setRole
  set_scalar_cmd("assignment", "capability", choices=_MODEL_TIERS, legal_in=("draft",)) -> setCapability
  set_scalar_cmd("assignment", "worktree", legal_in=("draft",))                   -> setWorktree
  set_prose_cmd("task", legal_in=("draft",))                                      -> setTask
  set_prose_cmd("reporting", label="reporting contract", legal_in=("draft",))     -> setReporting
  list_cmds("reports", remove=False, add_args=(_text(),), legal_in=("working",))  -> addReport, reorderReport
  transition_cmd("markReady", "draft -> ready", requires=(("assignment","role"), ("assignment","capability"),
      ("assignment","worktree"), ("task","body"), ("reporting","body")),
      parent_guards=(_EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER,))
  transition_cmd("reopen", "ready -> draft (unlocks the assignment, task and reporting contract)")
  transition_on_add_cmd("start", "ready -> working", section="reports", field="items",
      add_args=(_text(),), description="report that the agent has started, with the worktree it created")
  transition_on_add_cmd("finish", "working -> finished", section="reports", field="items",
      add_args=(_text(),), description="report the outcome AND finish")
  transition_on_add_cmd("block", "working -> blocked", section="reports", field="items",
      add_args=(_text(),), description="report what stopped the work AND block")
  transition_cmd("accept", "finished -> accepted")
  transition_on_add_cmd("redispatch", "finished or blocked -> ready", legal_in=("finished", "blocked"),
      section="reports", field="items", add_args=(_text(),),
      description="report what the next round must fix AND send the agent back")
  add_link_cmd(), set_title_cmd()

body.text: Who fires what. The controller authors in draft (setRole, setCapability, setWorktree, setTask, setReporting), links each feature-brief the agent works on with addLink role works-on and each agent page that must be accepted first with addLink role depends-on, then runs markReady. After the plan review it hands the dispatched agent this page id and nothing else. The dispatched agent creates the named worktree, runs start (its first command; the report names the worktree), adds a report as each step lands, and ends with finish (the outcome, checked against the reporting contract) or block (what stopped it). The controller then runs accept, or redispatch with a report saying what the next round must fix; to change the task itself it runs reopen, edits in draft and runs markReady again. The controller-authored fields are draft-only so that a dispatched agent's nextActions on its own page offers start and its reports, never the controller's setters. The reports list keeps a reorder (every list field must have one) but no remove: it is the record of every attempt.
Agent page field text

body.source:
_AGENT_NOTICE =
  This page is one dispatched agent's whole assignment, and its page id is the agent's id. The
  controller - the session that created the epic above it - writes the assignment, task and
  reporting contract, links the feature-briefs the agent works on, and is the only one to run
  markReady, reopen, accept or redispatch here. The dispatched agent creates the worktree named
  here and works only in it, runs start on this page as its first command, adds a report as each
  step lands, and ends with finish or block. It writes only this page and the feature-briefs this
  page links to, with their child pages, and never runs a command on the epic or on another
  agent's page.

assignment.role =
  What this agent is, named as a role a reader recognises - implementer, test writer,
  integration reviewer. One agent page is one dispatch, so the role describes this run rather
  than a definition shared with other agents.

assignment.capability =
  The model tier this agent is dispatched on. Name it on every agent: an omitted tier silently
  inherits the session's most capable and most expensive model. Use cheap for mechanical
  single-file work whose content is already written down, standard for multi-file integration
  and judgement, and capable for architecture and final review.

assignment.worktree =
  The git worktree this agent creates and works in, by name. Give every agent a different one:
  two agents in one checkout overwrite each other's edits.

task.body =
  The exact work this agent does, written for a fresh agent with no history: it is handed this
  page id and nothing of the controller's context. Say which slice of the epic it owns and what
  done looks like, name the shared contracts it touches by their id on the epic, and add only
  the decisions it needs that its feature-briefs cannot tell it. Link each feature-brief it works
  on with addLink role works-on, and each agent page that must be accepted before it starts with
  role depends-on. Point at large artifacts by file path rather than pasting them.

reporting.body =
  What this agent must leave behind before it runs finish, written as a checklist the controller
  verifies before accepting: which commands it must have run on its linked feature-briefs, what
  status each brief and its plans must be left in, and what its finish report must say. An agent
  reports by driving its briefs and this page, not by handing prose back, so name the page status
  you expect rather than the summary you want to read.

reports.items =
  Each one report written back onto this page while the agent works: start records that it
  began and the worktree it created, a report records each step as it lands, and finish or
  block records the outcome or what stopped it. The controller adds one when it redispatches,
  saying what the next round must fix, so the list is the record of every attempt this agent
  made.

body.text: Epic changes (_EPIC)

body.source:
removed   SectionSpec("workstreams", ...) and *list_cmds("workstreams", ...)
removed   auto_children=(AutoChildSpec("agent-plan"),)   (and the AutoChildSpec, RefCheck, _integer,
          element_cmds and ElementFSMSpec imports only the agent plan used; _QUESTION_FSM stays)

_AGENT_PLANNED = ("ready", "working", "finished", "blocked", "accepted")   # every agent status but draft

submitPlan      "decomposition -> planReview"
                requires=(("questions", "items"),)
                guards=(ChildStateGuard("agent", _AGENT_PLANNED, "every agent page must be marked ready"),)
submitForReview "executing -> review"
                guards=(ChildStateGuard("agent", ("accepted",), "every agent must be accepted"),)
ship            unchanged: ChildStateGuard("feature-brief", ("shipped",), ...)

_EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS = ("addAgent", "editAgent", "addContract", "addConstraint", "askQuestion",
                         "editContract", "edit")

description = "The root of a major feature too large for one feature-brief: it decomposes into
  several child feature-briefs and is built by subagents, each dispatched from an agent page of
  its own under the epic. Use it when the work splits into parts that each ship on their own; for
  one feature use a feature-brief, and for a small self-contained change use a simple-change."

_CONTROLLER_NOTICE =
  This epic is the controller's page. Only the controlling agent - the session that created this
  epic and dispatches its agents - runs commands on it. Each dispatched agent is handed one agent
  page, a child of this epic whose page id is the agent's id; it works from that page, reports back
  onto it, and writes only that page and the feature-briefs it links to, with their child pages.
  It never edits this epic or another agent's page. The controller records here what an agent
  raises: addFinding or editFinding for a problem, and editContract for a shared contract it
  corrected.

body.text: _AGENT_PLANNED admits every status past draft rather than ready alone, because reopenDecomposition (executing -> decomposition) followed by submitPlan must not be refused by agents that are already working or accepted; what the plan review needs is that no agent page is still being written.

body.source:
epic field descriptions - only these sentences change, the rest of each text stays as is:

components.items   "a component missed here becomes a workstream nobody owns, and a component two
                   workstreams both touch is a collision"
               ->  "a component missed here is one no agent owns, and a component two agents both
                   touch is a collision"
constraints.items  "every workstream must respect" -> "every agent must respect"
conflicts.items    "Record collisions BETWEEN the intended workstreams here too"
               ->  "Record collisions BETWEEN the intended agents here too"
contracts.items    "Each one interface that crosses a workstream boundary: its name, the workstream that
                   defines it in owner, ... A dispatched agent sees only its own brief, so anything two
                   workstreams must agree on ... its id is what handoffs and briefs point at."
               ->  "Each one interface that crosses an agent boundary: its name, the page id of the agent
                   that defines it in owner, ... A dispatched agent sees only its own agent page and the
                   briefs it links, so anything two agents must agree on ... its id is what agent tasks

review.verdict     "for the decomposition and the agent plan together. build-ready: the workstreams cover
                   the epic with no gaps and no overlaps, and an agent could be dispatched against any
                   one of them without getting stuck"
               ->  "for the decomposition and its agent pages together. build-ready: the agents cover the
                   epic with no gaps and no overlaps, and each could be dispatched from its page alone
                   without getting stuck"
                   "a component no workstream owns, two workstreams owning the same file, a contract two
                   workstreams need that nobody defines, or an agent mission too vague to act on"
               ->  "a component no agent owns, two agents owning the same file, a contract two agents need
                   that nobody defines, or an agent task too vague to act on"
review.findings    "Say which workstream or agent it applies to." -> "Name the agent page it applies to."

comments: the review-section comment ("the decomposition and the agent plan are reviewed together"),
the beginDecomposition comment ("the child feature-briefs and the agent plan are authored"), and the
submitPlan / submitForReview comments are reworded to the agent pages; the ParentStateGuard comment
names the agent page's markReady; the module docstring reads "The `epic` page type, and the `agent`
pages created under it."

body.text: Store: the child guard over archived and absent children

The rule, stated once in the ChildStateGuard docstring in src/pagetypes/core/specs.py: the guard holds when the page has at least one non-archived child of child_type and every such child satisfies it. A pinned child's archived state mirrors its parent's, so while a parent is live its pinned children are present and unarchived - every feature-brief guard and every fixture guard over a pinned child behaves exactly as before. What changes: an epic cannot submitPlan or submitForReview with no live agent page, cannot ship with no live feature-brief, and an archived agent or brief no longer holds either gate. The function stays a pure read of workspace data; next_actions picks up the new message through the same function, so a blocked submitPlan tells the controller there is no agent page yet.
Registry, instructions and tests

body.source:
src/pagetypes/_registry.py   from .epic import _AGENT, _EPIC ; REGISTRY maps _AGENT.tag: _AGENT in place of _AGENT_PLAN

src/instructions.py
  after L50 add:  - An `epic`'s `agent` pages are created under the epic itself too, one per dispatched
                    agent - the epic's plan and review gates only see agent pages that are its own children.
  L90 epic:       epic: The root of a major feature too large for one feature-brief - it decomposes into
                  several child feature-briefs and is built by subagents, each dispatched from an agent
                  page of its own. Use it when the work splits into parts that each ship on their own;
                  when it does not, use a feature-brief.
  L92 replaced:   agent: One subagent an epic dispatches - its role, capability, exact task and worktree,
                  linked to the feature-briefs it works on. Its page id is the agent's id and the page it
                  reports back into as it starts and works. Created as a child of an epic.

tests/test_pagetypes.py      PRODUCTION_TYPES and its import name _AGENT in place of _AGENT_PLAN
new store tests (fixtures)   a guarded transition over a NON-pinned child type is refused with
                             "(there is no '<type>' child page)" when no such child exists, refused while a
                             live child is in a disallowed status, allowed once that child is archived and
                             another live child satisfies it, and refused again with the no-child message when
                             the only matching child is archived

body.text: Error paths

All through existing machinery, no new error type. markReady with an empty assignment field, task or reporting contract is refused by its requires; markReady under an epic still in draft or grounding is refused by the parent guard ('the epic must be in decomposition or later'); an agent page under any other parent is unconstrained by that guard, exactly as the agent plan was. A controller setter after markReady is illegal in ready (reopen first). addReport outside working is refused by legal_in; start, finish, block, accept and redispatch from the wrong status are refused by the FSM. Every command on an accepted page but its transitions is locked by the terminal status, and accepted has none. The epic's submitPlan with no agent page, or with one still in draft, is refused with its guard message; submitForReview likewise until every live agent page is accepted. addLink on an agent page keeps its existing check that the target page exists.
Where an epic's children are created: the decomposition stage guidance

The two rules for where an epic's feature-briefs and agent-plan pages are created leave the instructions' Pasta setup list (src/instructions.py keeps only the general rule that epics go under the Features toc) and become the epic's stage guidance for decomposition, the status in which both are created: a DECOMPOSITION constant in src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py under a new epic section, wired as FSMSpec(..., status_guidance=(("decomposition", DECOMPOSITION),)) on _EPIC. A bare name, because no other page type has a decomposition status.
Scheduling: the controller's wave plan

The epic gains a 'scheduling' section titled 'Scheduling', placed after Shared contracts: one prose body, written with setScheduling (no legal_in, like the other epic content), holding the instructions the controller follows to dispatch the agent-plan pages in waves - each wave's agent-plan pages named by id, and what must be true before the next wave starts (normally every agent in the earlier waves accepted and its work integrated into the branch the next wave starts from, which may be main or a worktree branch of the epic's own - the section does not assume main). The decomposition stage guidance gains a third bullet pointing at it, so the controller writes it in the same status it creates the children. The depends-on links between agent-plan pages are unchanged: they are what each agent sees, Scheduling is what the controller dispatches from. Nothing enforces the schedule and submitPlan does not require it - it is read by the controller and checked at the plan review.

Absorbed. The epic's workstreams list and its add/remove/reorder commands are removed; an agent page is the workstream: its task states the slice it owns and it links the feature-briefs it drives. The agent page id is then the only id a run has, which is what the ask means by collapsing workstreamId and the agent role into one agentId. Rejected: keeping workstreams as a list the agent page references - it keeps a second id per run (the confusion the ask removes) and duplicates the brief link and scope on two pages. The submitPlan requirement on workstreams.items is replaced by the agent-page guard (see the empty-set decision).

Direct children of the epic, and the agent-plan type is removed with the epic's auto_children. ChildStateGuard sees only direct children, so the epic's gates can only read agent pages that sit right under it. Rejected: a slimmed agent-plan kept as a pinned container - it keeps a page type the ask wants gone, and its children would be invisible to the epic's guards, needing either a grandchild guard (new machinery) or a status relay on the container (the old indirection).

A ChildStateGuard fails when the page has no non-archived child of its type: 'every agent must be ready' needs at least one agent. This keeps the gate the epic has today (it could not reach planReview without workstreams) and, at ship, closes the hole the old workstreams text warned about (an epic shipping with no briefs). Every existing guard targets a pinned child that is always present while its parent is live, so nothing else changes. Rejected: an opt-in flag on ChildStateGuard (configuration no current guard would leave off); relying on the plan review alone (drops an enforced gate the epic has now); a separate count requirement on the epic (new machinery for one use).

Yes: archived children are ignored by every ChildStateGuard, and archiving an agent page is how an agent is dropped (the page-level counterpart of the old removeAgent / removeDispatch). It follows the existing rule that archived pages are history (tree and search already hide them). Pinned children mirror their parent's archived state, so feature-brief guards are unaffected. Rejected: a 'dropped' terminal status on the agent page - an extra status and transition for what archive already does.

Statuses draft -> ready -> working -> finished -> accepted, with blocked off working. The controller authors in draft, runs markReady (parent-guarded on the epic being in decomposition or later), may reopen (ready -> draft) to change the task, and later runs accept or redispatch (finished or blocked -> ready). The dispatched agent runs start (ready -> working), addReport while working, and finish or block (working -> finished / blocked). start, finish, block and redispatch are transition_on_add compounds that write a report entry and move the status atomically, so every status change carries its reason in the reports list - the record of every attempt, replacing the dispatch element's outcome, blocker and redispatch count. Controller fields are draft-only so the agent's own nextActions never offers them. Rejected: separate outcome and blocker fields (three fields where one log does); keeping a controller-side markDispatched (the agent's start is the dispatch signal the ask describes).

The model tier: a scalar named capability with today's choices cheap / standard / capable (_MODEL_TIERS), carrying over the agent element's 'Name the tier on every agent' instruction. Tiers rather than model ids, for the reason the existing comment gives (an id rots between releases). Rejected: a tool or permission set - pasta has no notion of an agent's tools or caller identity, so the field could not be acted on or checked.

By links: an agent page that must wait for another links it with addLink role depends-on, and the controller starts an agent only once every page it depends on is accepted; agents with no dependency between them may run at once, each in its own worktree. Links are already integrity-checked (the target must exist) and show on the page the agent reads. Rejected: a wave field (a second ordering mechanism, and scalars are text-only today, so an integer wave would need a new setter); a free-text dependsOn field (unchecked ids, the confusion the ask is removing).

The user's call: keep the agent-plan name. Tag agent-plan, _AGENT_PLAN / _AGENT_PLAN_NOTICE, display name 'Agent plan', FSM AgentPlan; 'agent-plan page' in prose only where it names the page directly. Not renamed: the finding actions addAgent / editAgent, _AGENT_PLANNED, and prose about the agent, where conflating the page and the subagent is fine. This supersedes the answer recorded on the brief question, which over-specified addAgentPlan / editAgentPlan and a wider prose rewrite. Rejected: the 'agent' tag (the user wants the established name), and re-editing every mention of the type (churn the user declined).

The user's call: on the epic, as its decomposition stage guidance. It reaches the controller at the moment it creates the briefs and agent-plan pages, instead of sitting in a global list every session reads. Rejected: keeping the notes in the instructions (they are epic-only rules), and putting them in a field description (no single field is authored when the children are created).

The user's call: a Scheduling prose section on the epic, referenced from the decomposition stage guidance, with the depends-on links kept as they are. The controller is the only reader that dispatches, so its schedule lives on the controller's page in its own section rather than inside a Conflicts entry, agent-plan task prose and worktree names, where it had been scattered. Rejected: a wave integer on each agent-plan page with a store guard on start (new scalar and guard machinery, and it reverses the depends-on decision), and leaving the plan in prose spread across pages (not documented in one place).

epic:mw9s8ban-df841d.title: Interactive timeline replay of features being added, shipped and archived in the web UI

notice.body:
This epic is the controller's page. Only the controlling agent - the session that created this
epic and dispatches its agents - runs commands on it. Each dispatched agent is handed one
agent-plan page, a child of this epic whose page id is the agent's id; it works from that page,
reports back onto it, and writes only that page and the feature-briefs it links to, with their
child pages. It never edits this epic or another agent's page. The controller records here what
an agent raises: addFinding or editFinding for a problem, and editContract for a shared contract
it corrected.

summary.body: A timeline view in the web UI that replays how a workspace's features came and went: when each feature page was created, how it moved through its statuses, and when it shipped or was archived. It has two linked interactive surfaces: a player whose timeline can be scrubbed, played and paused, and a graph of the workspace's feature pages as they stood at the selected moment, where hovering a node shows the feature's title (and its status). It is worth building because the wiki today shows only where work stands now, not how it got there. Delivering it needs page history recorded over time and served to the web UI as replayable data, AND a player and graph that render it - two parts that can each ship on their own.

items.name: src/model.py - Page has no timestamps (id, type, title, status, parent_id, child_ids, sections, archived, links, expires_at, delete_scheduled, status_revision_token); Workspace has created_at/updated_at only. Pure.

src/ids.py - page ids are '<type>:<base36 ms timestamp>-<6 hex>', so an existing page's creation instant is recoverable from its id (new_token). Effectful (clock, randomness); parsing an id back is pure.

src/store.py - every write path that changes what a timeline shows: create_page (+ _create_auto_children), mutate_page_batch (status transitions via MutatePageResult.transitioned, setTitle renames), _set_page_archive_state (archive/unarchive, cascades to pinned children; schedule/unschedule deletion), set_page_status, reparent_page, rename_page, link_page / unlink_page, cleanup_workspace (deletes pages after write_backup). All persist through _touch_and_save -> _write_file (atomic replace of <root>/ws_<id>.json under the per-workspace ReadWriteLock); list_workspaces globs <root>/*.json; backups go to <root>/backups/. Effectful.
src/serialize.py - workspace_to_dict / workspace_from_dict, the JSON shape of the workspace file. Pure.

src/server.py - FastAPI web routes: GET / (index), /ws:{id} (tree), /ws:{id}/page/{pageId} (page), plus POST archive / unarchive / schedule-delete / unschedule-delete / status on a page; templates = Jinja2Templates('src/templates'); /static mounts src/static. Effectful shell over Store.

src/templates/ (_base.html, _nav.html, tree.html, page.html, index.html, _reloader.js, _theme.js, _view_toggle.js) - Jinja templates; scripts are plain JS inlined with {% include '<name>.js' %} inside a <script> tag; every page carries the live-reload socket from _base.html.

src/static/styles.css + src/static/water.css/ - vendored water.css light/dark sheets and the project stylesheet; structured-render styling is scoped under the pasta-page class and takes every colour from a water.css custom property.

tests/test_web.py (TestClient(server.app) with STORE repointed at a tmp_path Store), tests/test_store.py, tests/test_render_html.py - where route, store and render behaviour is tested; production page types are off-limits in tests, so behaviour is exercised through src/testtypes.py fixtures.
main.py - `uv run python main.py --port <n>` runs the combined HTTP dev server (MCP at /pasta/mcp + web UI) with hot reload; PASTA_DATA_DIR (default .pasta-data) chooses the data root.

items.text: pyproject.toml: requires-python = ">=3.14", managed with uv; dependencies fastapi[standard]>=0.162.0, jinja2>=3.1.6 (no new runtime dependency without asking); dev pytest>=9.2.0 and pytest-testmon>=2.3.0 - run tests with `uv run pytest --testmon` (CLAUDE.md); [tool.pyright] typeCheckingMode = "recommended" (basedpyright).

No JavaScript toolchain: there is no package.json or bundler. Browser code is plain JS kept in src/templates/_<name>.js and inlined with {% include %} inside a <script> tag, as _view_toggle.js is; third-party assets are vendored under src/static (water.css) and never loaded from a CDN.

Styling: new styles scoped under a class of their own (or pasta-page) and every colour taken from a water.css custom property that both the light and dark sheets define, so the view reads correctly in both themes; no literal colours.

Pure logic separate from effects: history diffing and timeline replay are pure functions of their inputs, unit-tested directly; the store and routes are thin shells that call them. Production page types are off-limits in tests - use the src/testtypes.py fixtures.

CLAUDE.md copy rule: use the word "create" instead of "mint" when creating something. Commits end with the session's Co-Authored-By trailer. Agents do not open pull requests: each pushes its worktree's branch to the origin remote (git@github.com:dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev.git) and reports the branch name back on its agent-plan page; the controller integrates branches into main.

No history exists to replay: the store keeps only each page's current state. Creation instants are recoverable from page ids, but no status change, rename, reparent or archive before history recording lands has a time. Existing workspaces get a reconstructed start (creation from ids, current state as a baseline) - decided in Questions.

Web UI read-only claim has drifted: architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5 says the web UI is strictly read-only, but src/server.py already has POST routes (archive, unarchive, schedule-delete, unschedule-delete, status). Those are write paths the history recorder must capture like the MCP ones; the new timeline routes are reads only.

cleanup_workspace deletes pages outright (cleanup.delete_subtree after a backup), so their history must outlive them: history cannot live inside the workspace JSON pages, and a deletion must be recorded as an event.

Storage collision: list_workspaces globs <root>/*.json and backups use <root>/backups/, so a per-workspace history file must not be a *.json in the root (it would be listed as a workspace). Put it in its own subdirectory.

Between agents: src/store.py, src/server.py, src/static/styles.css and the timeline template are each edited by exactly one agent; any agent needing another's code works against a shared contract on this epic instead of editing that file.

Batch methodology vs. a vertical feature: batch wants every unit mergeable with no dependency on another unit landing first. A new feature cannot fully meet that, so the units are split into three waves joined only by contracts on this epic - wave 1 (U1 history events, U2 history log, U4 timeline data) depends on nothing; wave 2 (U3 store recording, U5 page and player) depends on wave-1 branches being merged to main; wave 3 (U6 graph, U7 lanes, U8 chart) depends on U5. items.name: History event
items.shape:
One JSON object per event (a dict[str, JSONValue] in Python):
{"at": "<UTC ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-11-09T12:00:00.123000+00:00>",
 "kind": "baseline" | "created" | "status" | "renamed" | "moved" | "archived" | "unarchived" | "linked" | "unlinked" | "deleted",
 "page": {"id": str, "type": str, "title": str, "parentId": str | null, "status": str,
          "archived": bool, "links": [{"to": str, "role": str}, ...]}}
"page" is the page's state AFTER the event (for "deleted": its last state before deletion), so replaying a page is 'take the latest snapshot'. One event per (page, kind) that changed in a write; all events of one write share "at". Within one write, events are ordered by page id, then by the KINDS order below. "links" keeps the page's own order.

items.name: History functions (src/history.py, pure)
items.shape:
from src.model import JSONValue, Page
KINDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("baseline", "created", "status", "renamed", "moved", "archived", "unarchived", "linked", "unlinked", "deleted")
def page_snapshot(page: Page) -> dict[str, JSONValue]                 # the 'page' object of a History event
def created_at(page_id: str) -> str | None                            # UTC ISO-8601 of the base-36 ms timestamp in '<prefix>:<base36>-<hex>'; None if it does not decode
def baseline_events(pages: Mapping[str, Page], at: str) -> list[dict[str, JSONValue]]   # one 'baseline' event per page, ordered by page id
def diff_events(before: Mapping[str, Page], after: Mapping[str, Page], at: str) -> list[dict[str, JSONValue]]
    # created: id only in after; deleted: id only in before (snapshot of before); otherwise one event per changed aspect:
    # status (status differs), renamed (title), moved (parent_id), archived / unarchived (archived flag),
    # linked (a link in after not in before), unlinked (a link in before not in after); [] when nothing changed
def with_creations(events: Sequence[Mapping[str, JSONValue]], initial_status: Callable[[str], str | None]) -> list[dict[str, JSONValue]]
    # for every page whose FIRST event is 'baseline' and whose created_at(id) decodes, adds a 'created' event at that instant
    # carrying the baseline snapshot with status = initial_status(type) (the baseline's status when None) and archived = False;
    # returns all events stably sorted by 'at' (ISO strings with the same offset compare in time order)

items.name: History log (src/history_log.py)
items.shape:
class HistoryLog:
    def __init__(self, root: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None           # root = the store's data root
    def path_for(self, workspace_id: str) -> Path                       # <root>/history/<workspace_id with ':' replaced by '_'>.jsonl
    def exists(self, workspace_id: str) -> bool                         # the file exists and holds at least one event
    def append(self, workspace_id: str, events: Sequence[Mapping[str, JSONValue]]) -> None
        # one json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False) line per event, '\n'-terminated, in order; creates history/ on demand; no-op for []
        # appends from concurrent threads never interleave within a line (a per-workspace lock inside HistoryLog)
    def read(self, workspace_id: str) -> list[dict[str, JSONValue]]
        # every event in file order; [] when the file is absent; a final line that fails to parse is skipped (torn write), any other bad line raises PastaError
The log stores whatever JSON objects it is given and never interprets them.

items.name: Store recording (src/store.py)
items.shape:
Store.__init__ creates self.history = HistoryLog(self.root).
Every committed write - create_page (with its auto-children), mutate_page_batch, archive/unarchive, schedule/unschedule deletion, set_page_status, reparent_page, reorder_page, rename_page, link_page, unlink_page, cleanup_workspace - after the workspace file is saved and still inside the workspace transaction lock:
    now = one UTC ISO-8601 instant for the whole write
    if not self.history.exists(ws_id): self.history.append(ws_id, baseline_events(before_pages, now))
    self.history.append(ws_id, diff_events(before_pages, after_pages, now))
where before_pages is a deep copy of workspace.pages taken when the write loaded the workspace. A write that raises records nothing; a write that changes nothing appends nothing beyond a first baseline. create_workspace records nothing. Readers never go through the Store for history: they open HistoryLog(root) themselves.

items.name: Timeline JSON (src/timeline.py, pure)
items.shape:
def build_timeline(events: Sequence[Mapping[str, JSONValue]], types: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, JSONValue]]) -> dict[str, JSONValue]
  types[tag] = {"statuses": [str, ...] (FSM state order), "initial": str, "shipped": [str, ...]}
Returns:
{"start": iso | null, "end": iso | null,            # first and last event 'at'; null when there are no events
 "types": {tag: {"statuses": [...], "initial": str, "shipped": [...]}},   # copied through for the views
 "events": [History event, ...],                    # stably sorted by 'at'
 "counts": [{"added": int, "shipped": int, "archived": int}, ...]}
    # counts[i] is the state after events[0..i]: added = pages created so far (a 'created' or a first 'baseline'; never decreases),
    # shipped = present pages whose status is in their type's 'shipped' list, archived = present pages with archived true;
    # a 'deleted' page is no longer present. len(counts) == len(events).
A page whose type is missing from 'types' counts as added/archived but never shipped.

items.name: Timeline routes (src/server.py)
items.shape:
GET /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline.json -> 200 application/json, the Timeline JSON for that workspace:
    workspace = STORE.load_workspace(ws_id); logged = HistoryLog(STORE.root).read(ws_id)
    events = logged or baseline_events(workspace.pages, workspace.updated_at)
    events = with_creations(events, lambda tag: <registered type's fsm.initial, or None>)
    types = {tag: {"statuses": list(fsm.states), "initial": fsm.initial, "shipped": [s for s in fsm.terminal_states if s != "abandoned"]}} for every registered page type
    return build_timeline(events, types)
  unknown workspace -> the same not-found response the tree route gives.
GET /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline -> 200 text/html: src/templates/timeline.html (extends _base.html), linked from the workspace tree view; it fetches timeline.json and runs the player.
Both are reads only and need nothing from src/store.py beyond load_workspace and root.

items.name: Renderer interface (timeline page, browser JS)
items.shape:
src/templates/_timeline_player.js runs before any view script and defines:
  window.pastaTimeline = { register(view) }
  view = { id: string, label: string,
           mount(container: HTMLElement, data: TimelineJSON): void,
           render(frame: Frame): void,
           unmount(): void }
  Frame = { index: number,          // -1 before the first event
            at: string | null, event: HistoryEvent | null,
            pages: Map<string, PageSnapshot>,   // pages present after events[0..index], replayed by latest snapshot, 'deleted' removes
            counts: {added, shipped, archived} } // counts[index], zeros at -1
The player owns the time axis (with hoverable event ticks), scrubbing, play / pause / step / speed and a view switch listing registered views; it mounts the active view into <div id="timeline-view"> and calls render(frame) on every frame change and right after mount.
View files, each included by timeline.html AFTER the player with {% include '<file>' ignore missing %} inside a <script>: _timeline_graph.js (id "graph"), _timeline_lanes.js (id "lanes"), _timeline_chart.js (id "chart"). Each view's styles live in src/static/timeline-<id>.css, linked by timeline.html (a missing file is a harmless 404). Every view shows the title and status of the page under the pointer.

items.text: Which page types count as features on the timeline and in the graph?
items.answer: The user's call: every page type. 'Added' is a page's creation; 'shipped' is reaching one of its type's terminal statuses other than abandoned (feature-brief and epic shipped, simple-change and bug-report closed, feature-spec sealed, agent-plan accepted, and so on); 'archived' is the page's archive flag. A type with no terminal status never counts as shipped.

items.text: What does the graph show at the selected moment: a node-link graph of feature pages and their relations, features grouped into status lanes, or a cumulative chart of added / shipped / archived counts?
items.answer: The user's call: all three, as switchable views of one replay. A shared player owns the time axis and the mode switch; the node-link graph (nodes = pages, edges = parent/child and typed links), the status lanes and the cumulative added/shipped/archived chart are three renderers that plug into it, and each shows the title (and status) of whatever is under the pointer.

items.text: How does each dispatched agent verify its unit end to end, given it cannot ask anyone?
items.answer: The user's call: curl for every unit, plus a browser for the UI units. Each agent runs `uv run python main.py --port <its own port>` against a temporary PASTA_DATA_DIR holding a copy of a real workspace file and curls the routes it touches; library units with no route yet exercise their module against that copy with a short `uv run python -c` script; the timeline page and the three view agents also drive a browser (Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser) - play, scrub, switch view, hover - and screenshot the result.

items.text: What does an existing workspace replay before history recording lands?
items.answer: A reconstruction that claims nothing it cannot know. The first recorded write to a workspace appends a 'baseline' event per existing page with its state at that instant; before any write, the route builds the same baseline from the current pages at workspace.updated_at. Every page whose first event is a baseline also gets a synthesized 'created' event at the instant encoded in its id, in its type's initial status. Status changes, renames and archiving before recording began therefore show up at the baseline, not at their true time. Pages pruned before recording began never appear.

items.text: Where is a workspace's history stored and in what form?
items.answer: An append-only JSON Lines file per workspace at <data root>/history/<workspace id with ':' replaced by '_'>.jsonl, one event object per line (see the 'History event' contract). It lives outside the workspace JSON so a pruned page's history outlives it and the workspace file does not grow, and in its own subdirectory so list_workspaces (which globs <root>/*.json) never sees it.

feature-brief:mwao9kde-4a8483.title: Epic research and design stages: one solution investigation per direction, a pinned solution-design page, and human approach and design sign-off

summary.body: Give the epic a preparation phase that works out the right solution before it is split into workstreams. The user and the orchestrator first agree the goals and a handful of distinct solution directions from the intent alone. One investigator subagent per direction then grounds the codebase for that direction's scope, works it out and tests it on a solution-investigation page of its own - with an optional throwaway spike worktree - and one judge subagent checks all the investigations side by side. The orchestrator talks the digests through with the user until they pick a direction. A design subagent writes that direction up as a builder-ready design on the epic's pinned design page, and the user signs the design off before decomposition into feature-briefs and agent-plan pages begins. The point is twofold: the orchestrator keeps a small context because it reads digests rather than doing the research and design itself, and nothing is decomposed or built against an approach or design the user has not explicitly approved. The shape follows the superpowers brainstorming skill (why first, approaches in their own message, builder check, hard gate on design approval) and the context-engineering-kit plan-task skill (delegated analysis, a heavier design step, a separate judge per step).

items.name: src/pagetypes/epic.py
items.text: Pure declaration, the heart of the change. _EPIC today: fixed Controller notice; summary prose whose instruction says grounding searches the repo from it; components/constraints/conflicts/documentation lists filled in the grounding status; contracts (owner = an agent-plan page id, editable); scheduling prose; questions on _QUESTION_FSM with askQuestion/answerQuestion/escalateQuestion; review verdict (planReview) and findings (planReview, executing, review). FSM draft -> grounding -> decomposition -> planReview -> executing -> review -> shipped|abandoned; beginGrounding requires summary.body; beginDecomposition requires the four grounding lists; submitPlan requires questions.items plus ChildStateGuard('agent-plan', _AGENT_PLANNED); submitForReview ChildStateGuard('agent-plan', accepted); ship (human) ChildStateGuard('feature-brief', shipped); guidance only for decomposition; no auto_children. _AGENT_PLAN: one page per dispatched agent, created by the controller under the epic, its notice/task/reporting worded around 'the feature-briefs it links to'; markReady gated by ParentStateGuard _EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER. The rule 'a parent is declared together with the child types designed against it' puts the two new pinned child types in this module too.

items.name: src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py
items.text: Pure leaf module of guidance text constants, importing nothing. Naming rule: a bare constant is the only text for that status anywhere; a page-type prefix marks one type's take on a status name several types claim (draft is claimed by several, so the epic's would be EPIC_DRAFT). DECOMPOSITION (L196-206) is the epic's only guidance today. A test holds that every production guidance text is one of these constants.

items.name: src/pagetypes/_workspace_guidance.py
items.text: Pure leaf constants (field, label, description) for mergeProcess, testingTool and groundingTool. A field shared by several types must carry the same description and label everywhere (validate_workspace_guidance). The settable-field list in the served instructions is derived from the registry (server.py L365 via workspace_guidance_fields), so a new slot surfaces with no text edit.

items.name: src/pagetypes/_registry.py
items.text: Pure. REGISTRY imports each type from its module and maps tag -> PageType; is_auto_child_type reads AutoChildSpec off the parent type. The two new tags are added to the import and the map.

items.name: src/store.py next_actions (L436-511) and src/commands.py field_setter_edges (L199-250)
items.text: Pure rollup, reused unchanged. field_setter_edges collects requires from EVERY transition allowed from the current status, human edges included, so a human gate's required fields surface as do setters for the agent; events blocked by a ParentStateGuard are dropped first, so a pinned child waiting on its parent advertises no authoring. A human edge is bucketed in humanGates with a blockedReason when a guard fails.

items.name: src/store.py _child_guard_failure (L1007), _parent_guard_failure (L1030), _create_auto_children (L978)
items.text: Effectful store, reused unchanged. A ChildStateGuard checks only DIRECT, non-archived children and fails when none of its type exists; page form tests the child's status, element form every element's status. A ParentStateGuard is enforced only when the parent is of the named type. auto_children are created as pinned children in the same commit as the parent.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/commands.py (list_cmds, element_cmds, set_element_field_cmd, blocks_cmds, transition_cmd)
items.text: Pure factories, reused unchanged. list_cmds: add/remove/reorder with optional editable, ref_check and legal_in; an editable list cannot carry a ref_check. element_cmds: element-FSM marks whose extra args are written onto same-named element fields. set_element_field_cmd: a constant flag. blocks_cmds: add/remove/reorder of a blocks field, with distinct remove/reorder names needed when a type has two blocks fields. transition_cmd parses 'from -> to', legal_in overrides the source for a multi-source edge, and carries requires, guards and parent_guards.

items.name: src/instructions.py (L89-91)
items.text: Pure text served by the instructions tool: hand-written one-liners per page type (epic L89, agent-plan L91), not generated from the registry. The two new types need a line each and the epic line a reword.

items.name: tests/test_pagetypes.py (L111, L137, L1215)
items.text: Test-only. PRODUCTION_TYPES names each production type by import; test_production_types_are_exactly_the_registered_ones holds it equal to REGISTRY, so both new types must be imported and listed. The parametrized structural invariants (well-formed FSM, transitions declare source and dest, content commands target real fields, requires reference real fields, setter descriptions, one setter per field, guidance is a _stage_guidance constant) then run over them.

pyproject.toml: requires-python = ">=3.14", managed with uv; dev dependency pytest-testmon; CLAUDE.md: 'Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing'; [tool.pyright] typeCheckingMode = "recommended".
CLAUDE.md copy rule: use the word "create" instead of "mint" when creating something - applies to every new description, notice, guidance text and comment.

Production page types are off-limits in tests (test mode empties REGISTRY; get_page_type raises ProductionTypeInTestError). Only the parametrized structural invariants in tests/test_pagetypes.py run over production, via the hand-written PRODUCTION_TYPES. The epic's and its children's declarations are recorded by the declaration and the architecture page, not pinned by behaviour tests - the same stance #58 took.

Page types are data: no per-type logic in the store or core. At most one do-eligible setter per (section, field); a fixed field has no writer; a field setter's description is a one-line label; every guidance text is a _stage_guidance constant; a workspace-guidance field shared by several types carries the same description and label; all declaration errors raise once at load.

Cross-page model limits: ChildStateGuard sees only direct, non-archived children and fails with none; RefCheck scope is 'parent' only and sits on adds (or a block kind), so the epic cannot ref-check an element on its own child page, and an editable list cannot carry a ref_check. Ordering between sibling pinned children is expressed as a status on the parent, never by nesting.

Architecture invariant: docs/designing-page-types.md and .claude/skills/pasta-workflow-creation/SKILL.md describe the page-type model by hand and must be updated together, with identical brief text, when a page type is added or changed.

Grounding moves off the epic. The epic's components, constraints, conflicts and documentation lists and its grounding status are where the controller grounds today; delegating that to a research subagent means they move onto the new research page. The epic's review verdict text ('a component no agent owns') and its decomposition guidance point at the epic's own components and must be reworded to point at the research and design pages.

agent-plan markReady is gated by _EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER, so an agent created to research or design (while the epic is researching or designing) could never be marked ready. The guard's status set must widen to admit researching and designing.

agent-plan wording assumes every agent builds: its description, notice, task and reporting say the agent works on and writes 'the feature-briefs this page links to'. A research or design agent works on the epic's research or design page instead, so the wording must cover any page the agent-plan links with works-on.

Epic gates over agent-plan pages count research and design agents too: submitPlan needs every agent-plan page ready or later, submitForReview every one accepted. Prep agents end accepted, so they satisfy both - but only if the controller accepts them, which the guidance must say.

Stored data: the live workspace holds one epic, epic:mw9s8ban-df841d, archived in planReview with eight archived agent-plan pages and no research or design child. planReview survives, so it loads; if it were unarchived and sent back to decomposition, the new design-sealed guard on submitPlan would fail with no live design child. Accepted as archived history, no migration - the same stance #58 took.
#58 recorded the constraint 'leave the epic simpler - fewer page types net'. This ask reverses it on purpose: it adds two page types. The grounding lists leaving the epic offsets part of that.

Stored data: the live workspace holds one solution-research page, solution-research:mwav2lhv-2ddbe8 (reported), under epic:mwav2lhu-f00f56 (executing), created while this branch's code was served. Removing the solution-research type leaves it as a page of an unregistered type - the state main already serves it in today, since main has no such type - so the workspace still loads. Accepted as history, no migration, the same stance taken for the archived epic.

Page types & FSM implementation (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2): 'Where a page type lives' says epic.py holds epic with agent-plan - it gains the pinned solution-research and solution-design. 'Guidance: per status, and per workspace' lists the epic's guidance as decomposition only - it gains draft, researching, deciding, designing, designReview, and the two new types' working statuses, plus the new workspace slots. 'Which cross-page rules the store enforces' gains the epic's research/design child guards and the widened agent-plan markReady guard. 'Sequencing a lifecycle with parent statuses' gains the epic as a second worked example (research before design before decomposition). Code references gain the two new constants.

docs/designing-page-types.md L78-81 and the identical lines in .claude/skills/pasta-workflow-creation/SKILL.md L97-100: the Pinned children example names only the feature brief's children; add the epic's research and design pages so the two examples show both parents.

README.md L134 'Page types': the epic paragraph says it decomposes into child briefs dispatched to subagents - add that it first researches and designs the solution through delegated pages and a person signs off the design. Also the served instructions one-liners in src/instructions.py L89-91 (component above).

Page types & FSM implementation (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2), amended by the investigation fan-out: the epic pins only solution-design; solution-investigation pages are ordinary children, one per direction, gated by presentFindings' child guard and kept waiting by the researching parent guard; the investigation's fit list is a worked example of a parent-scope RefCheck onto the epic's outcomes; 'Sequencing a lifecycle with parent statuses' uses research (investigations) before design before decomposition.
How is a research or design subagent dispatched now that #58 made agent-plan one page per dispatched agent?
items.answer: Each run gets its own agent-plan page under the epic, linked works-on to the solution-research or solution-design page: researcher, research judge, designer and design reviewer alike. That keeps #58's 'the agent-plan page is the subagent page' model and matches the ask's 'subagent pages with separate pages for what to produce'. agent-plan's markReady guard widens to admit researching and designing, and its wording covers any works-on page, not just feature-briefs.

items.text: Which module declares solution-research and solution-design?
items.answer: src/pagetypes/epic.py, beside the epic and agent-plan, per the architecture rule that a parent is declared together with the child types designed against it (the epic's child guards and the children's parent guards read each other).

items.text: Do the epic's components, constraints, conflicts and documentation lists, and its grounding status, stay on the epic?
items.answer: No. They move to the solution-research page, which the research subagent fills, and the epic's grounding status is replaced by researching, deciding, designing and designReview. Keeping them on the epic would put the grounding back into the orchestrator's context, which is what the ask removes.

items.text: How does the epic's chosen approach point at an approach on its research page, when a RefCheck can only look up at a parent?
items.answer: As plain approachId text on the epic's chosen-approach list, unchecked. Adding a child-scope RefCheck would be a new store capability for one field. Instead the research page's approaches list is editable, so a revised approach keeps its id and the epic's pointer stays good; the chooseApproach human gate is the person confirming it.

items.text: How is a design builder question resolved, and how does it point at the epic question that answered it?
items.answer: The reviewer adds a builder question (question, why); the designer resolves it with resolveBuilderQuestion, an element transition open -> resolved that writes pile (answered | minor | theirs) and resolution, or flags it needsHuman with escalateBuilderQuestion while it waits on the person. A 'theirs' resolution names the epic question id in its text; a RefCheck is not used because the question is added before any epic answer exists.

items.text: How is the judge or reviewer kept separate from the agent that wrote the research or design page?
items.answer: By dispatch, not declaration: the judge or reviewer is its own agent-plan page, and the verdict and findings are locked to the judging/checking status the author hands off into. The model cannot tell one agent from another, so the stage guidance states the rule; enforcing it would be a new capability and is out of scope.

items.text: Are the researchSources and humanReach workspace-guidance slots built, and at which statuses?
items.answer: Yes, as designed: researchSources at solution-research investigating (which outside sources research may use, and whether web search is allowed), and humanReach at the epic's deciding, designReview and review (how to reach the person at a human gate). groundingTool is also declared at investigating, reusing its existing constants.

items.text: Does the design page keep separate reopen (from ready) and unseal (from sealed) edges?
items.answer: No: one reopen command legal from ready and sealed, back to drafting, guarded on the epic being in designing. The two edges had the same guard and destination, so one command says it once.

items.text: Should each research approach carry a prediction and a falsifier, so it can be checked rather than argued?
items.answer: Yes (the user's call, from comparing the inquiry-brief spec). solution-research approaches gain two required element fields: predicts - an observation that should hold if the approach is right - and falsifier - the observation that would show it wrong. The judge checks each falsifier is something that could actually be observed.

items.text: Should the epic's outcomes be required before research begins, instead of only at chooseApproach?
items.answer: Yes (the user's call): beginResearch requires framing.outcomes alongside the summary and the why, so the goals and anti-goals the approaches are judged against are written before the approaches exist and cannot be fitted to them. chooseApproach no longer lists outcomes - they are already present - and deciding refines them rather than first writing them.

items.text: Which research entries carry an observed / inferred / assumed basis?
items.answer: The four codebase-recon lists - components, constraints, conflicts and documentation - each gain a required basis element field in observed | inferred | assumed. Prior art is left as is: its instruction already admits only sources actually opened, and its bearing is an inference by nature.

items.text: At which statuses does the new subagentDispatch workspace guidance surface - the stages that create agent pages, label agent models or launch agents?
items.answer: The user asked for a subagentDispatch workspace-guidance slot at every stage that creates agent pages, labels agent models or launches agents. On the epic: researching and designing (the controller creates and launches the researcher, judge, designer and reviewer agent-plan pages), decomposition (it creates the build agent-plan pages and gives each a capability) and executing (it launches and redispatches them). On agent-plan: draft (the controller writes the role, capability and task) and ready (the controller launches the agent). Not deciding, designReview, planReview or review, where no agent is created or launched, and not the research or design pages, whose agents never create agents.

items.text: What word replaces 'person' in the epic, solution-research and solution-design text, guidance and enum values?
items.answer: The user's call: 'person' goes. Where the text means who the work is for - whose why, outcomes, words, reasons, decisions and picks they are, and who reads the digest - it says user. Where it means the one who crosses a gated action - signing off the design, firing approveDesign or chooseApproach, settling an escalated question at a human gate - it says human. The said-by and decided-by enum values become user | proposal, since they record whose word an entry is. Text that predates this feature on main is left as it is.

items.text: Should the epic's research run on one research page whose agent grounds the repo and brainstorms every approach, or as several solution investigations, one per agent?
items.answer: The user's call: one investigation per agent, each scoped to one solution direction. Grounding needs a target - a solution-neutral recon either reads only the obvious area or everything, and different solution scopes lead to different investigations (a library answer grounds in prior art, a new abstraction in callers across the codebase, a minimal patch in one module). So the pinned solution-research page is replaced by ordinary solution-investigation children of the epic, one per direction, each grounding the repo for its own direction and working that direction out. The directions are agreed with the user at draft, from the intent alone, before any code is read. One comparative judge, its own agent-plan page linked works-on to every investigation, sets each page's verdict and records contradictions between their facts and directions that converged. The controller recommends at deciding from the digests.

items.text: May an investigator create a spike worktree to test its falsifier by running code?
items.answer: Yes (the user's call): an investigation may name an optional throwaway spike worktree to test its falsifier by running code. Spike code is never integrated, and evidence that came from it cites it.

items.text: Does the fan-out land in this brief and PR #60, or in a follow-up brief after it ships?
items.answer: Folded into this brief and PR #60 before ship (the user's call), so the single-research-page shape never reaches main and the architecture page is reconciled once.

findings.issue: Steps 1, 2 and 4-7 verify with `uv run python -I -c "from src..."`, but -I drops the current directory from sys.path, so the import fails before anything is checked. The -I rule is for downloaded files, not this repo's own code; the builder runs the same checks as `uv run python -c`. The verification intent is unchanged, so the plan is not reopened for it.

The spec declares subagentDispatch at the epic's executing status, but the smoke-walk step only checks researching, designing and decomposition, because the walk stops at planReview. The builder extends the walk through approvePlan to executing and checks the guidance there too, so every declared status is exercised.

Fan-out round: the served-text step also updated README.md, docs/designing-page-types.md and the skill brief, which are file-based docs that belong at done, not in a build step. The step now covers src/instructions.py only (served text pinned by tests/test_instructions.py), and its testing case drops the docs diff; the README and brief updates happen at done.

Fan-out round: the solution-investigation declaration step did not say the groundingTool and researchSources workspace guidance carries over at investigating, which the spec keeps; an implementer replacing the type could drop it. Added to the step.
Fan-out round: the testing plan expects addDirection with said 'person' to be refused, but the smoke step did not exercise it. Added to the smoke step.

Each text follows the shape '<status> - what state the work is in and what it is for. The work of it:' then bullets, then what is not due here and when to fire the exit or send-back edge. Use 'create', never 'mint'.

detail.source:
EPIC_DRAFT     summary as the outcome; ask one open why question with nothing to pick from; no approaches yet; no code read
RESEARCHING    add researcher agent-plan (standard) works-on the research page, worktree none; fresh judge at same tier
               fires report/revise; accept prep agents; a long reply instead of a filled page is a failed run;
               one extra round for minor findings; read only digest and questions; presentFindings once reported
DECIDING       lift open research questions here flagged needsHuman, ask one at a time; play back chunks marking
               person vs proposal; record outcomes; approaches in a message of their own; record the pick as
               chosen approach AND as an answered question; reopenResearch if answers invalidate; human gate
DESIGNING      designer agent-plan at capable tier; reviewer agent-plan at the same tier reads cold, fires
               markReady/revise; redispatch designer to sort piles; bring escalated questions in one message;
               one round of questions for the person; submitDesign once ready
DESIGN_REVIEW  present digest + link + proposal decisions; requestDesignChanges / reconsiderApproach on request;
               'sounds good' to a digest is not approval; human gate
DECOMPOSITION  seal the design first; split along expected changes; every criterion delivered and every change
               owned once; contracts from crossing interfaces; feature-briefs and agent-plan pages under the epic;
               Scheduling for build waves (verifiable milestone, at most five wide, tier per agent);
               reopenDesign rather than patch a brief
INVESTIGATING  research agent: restate ask, read code to blast radius, outside sources allowed here, 2-3
               approaches culled and grounded, recommend one, questions only the person can answer, digest last
JUDGING        fresh judge: sample paths and sources, approaches differ and are grounded, digest matches; report/revise
DRAFTING       design agent: copy intent, grow strategy, decisions with by, exact interfaces, changes, criteria,
               smallest design; sort builder questions after a check, escalate theirs and stop
CHECKING       fresh reviewer reads cold; ranked builder questions; rubric findings; outcome and verdict afresh;
               markReady on pass with nothing left, else revise; second pass blocking findings only

detail.source:
EPIC_DRAFT     after the outcomes: brainstorm two to four solution directions with the user from the summary, the why
               and the outcomes alone - theirs first, yours marked proposal - each a distinct kind of solution whose
               scope says what it would change or add and what it assumes; two that would send an investigator to the
               same code with the same question are one. No code read. Begin research once the summary, the why, the
               outcomes and the directions are written.
RESEARCHING    create one solution-investigation page under the epic per direction, titled with its name, and one
               investigator agent-plan per investigation at standard, works-on it; its task carries the summary, the why,
               the direction's id and scope and any answered questions; worktree none, or a throwaway spike worktree of
               its own when testing needs code run - spike code is never integrated. Dispatch them together. Once every
               investigation is submitted for judging, create one fresh judge agent-plan at the same tier, works-on every
               investigation; it sets each verdict and fires report or revise on each; on revise redispatch that
               investigator, then the judge. Accept every finished agent-plan; a long reply instead of a filled page is a
               failed run; one extra round for minor findings; archive an investigation to drop its direction. Read only
               the digests, viabilities and questions. Present the findings once every investigation is reported.
DECIDING       read each investigation's digest, viability and questions and the judge's findings; ask the open ones
               flagged needsHuman one at a time; play back; refine outcomes; then, in a message of its own, lay out the
               directions with their trade-offs and your recommendation - each investigator argued one direction, so the
               comparison is yours; record the pick as the chosen approach by investigation page id, and as an answered
               question; if answers rule out every direction or change the ask, reopen research to add a direction or
               redispatch one rather than design on a stale set.
DESIGNING      the designer's task carries the chosen investigation page ids, the outcomes and the answered questions.
INVESTIGATING  you investigate one direction: record its id and restate it; read the code from where this direction
               lands until its blast radius stops growing, a basis on every entry; prior art for this direction; sketch it;
               cull its variants; assess every epic outcome by id; test it - a prediction and a falsifier, checked by
               reading or, when your assignment names a spike worktree, by running code there, never integrated; make the
               strongest honest case and say not-viable when that is what you found; questions only the user can settle;
               digest last. Stay inside your direction. Do not design, change code outside a spike, or run a command on the
               epic or an agent-plan page. Submit once a stranger could compare this direction with the others from it.
JUDGING        one fresh judge reads every investigation of the epic side by side: sample entries marked observed; where
               two investigations contradict each other on the same code, open it and record a blocking finding on the
               wrong page naming the other; the page stays in its direction, its sketch is grounded, every outcome is
               assessed, its test result is backed by its evidence; an unobservable falsifier is blocking; cost sizes
               are comparable; two directions that converged are a minor finding on both; the digest matches the page.
               Set the verdict afresh and fire report or revise on each page; minor findings alone are a pass.
DRAFTING       handed the chosen investigation page(s) to read; resolve builder questions the page, the epic or the
               investigations already answer.
CHECKING       open the chosen investigation page only to check the expected changes against its recon.
