overview.body: Covers the page-type declarations in src/pagetypes/ that give the epic a delegated research and design phase: the epic's new sections (framing, solution directions, decision), statuses, guards and stage guidance; a new solution-investigation type, created by the controller under the epic once per solution direction and checked side by side by one judge; a pinned solution-design child; the agent-plan changes that let investigators, their judge and the design agents be dispatched from it, including an optional throwaway spike worktree for an investigator; the new workspace-guidance slots; the registry entries, the served instructions one-liners and the production-type list in the tests. Everything is declaration - the store, the pure core and the self-direction rollup are reused unchanged. Deliberately left out: any new store capability (a child-scope ref check, enforcing that a judge is a different agent from the author, a minimum count of children, a digest projection on the tree), changes to feature-brief or its children, and migrating the one archived epic.

body.text: Epic

The epic keeps notice, summary, contracts, scheduling, questions and review, loses components, constraints, conflicts and documentation (moved to solution-research), and gains framing and decision. Its status set becomes draft, researching, deciding, designing, designReview, decomposition, planReview, executing, review, shipped, abandoned; grounding is removed. It pins solution-research and solution-design as auto_children, created with the epic.

body.source:
sections
  notice        body: fixed (reworded: research, design and build agents each work from an agent-plan page and the pages it links works-on)
  summary       body: prose            setSummary
  framing       why: prose             setWhy (label 'why')
                outcomes: list {text, kind in (goal|non-goal|anti-goal), said in (person|proposal)}   addOutcome/remove/reorder/editOutcome
  decision      chosen: list {approachId, takes}   addChosenApproach/remove/reorder, legal_in (deciding,)
  contracts     items {name, owner, shape}  (unchanged commands; instruction adds: start from the design's interfaces)
  scheduling    body (unchanged command; instruction: build waves only, prep agents follow stage guidance)
  questions     items {text, answer, needsHuman, status} on _QUESTION_FSM  (unchanged commands; instruction reworded)
  review        verdict (planReview), findings (planReview, executing, review)  (unchanged; verdict text points at the design's expected changes)

_EPIC_FINDING_ACTIONS = (addAgent, editAgent, addContract, askQuestion, editContract, reopenDesign, edit)

transitions
  beginResearch        draft -> researching            agent  requires summary.body, framing.why
  presentFindings      researching -> deciding         agent  guard ChildStateGuard(solution-research, (reported,))
  reopenResearch       deciding -> researching         either
  chooseApproach       deciding -> designing           human  requires framing.outcomes, decision.chosen, questions.items
  submitDesign         designing -> designReview       agent  guard ChildStateGuard(solution-design, (ready,))
  approveDesign        designReview -> decomposition   human
  requestDesignChanges designReview -> designing       either
  reconsiderApproach   designReview -> deciding        either
  reopenDesign         decomposition|planReview -> designing   either
  submitPlan           decomposition -> planReview     agent  requires questions.items; guards agent-plan in _AGENT_PLANNED, solution-design in (sealed,)
  approvePlan, reviseDecomposition, submitForReview, reopenDecomposition, requestChanges, ship   unchanged
  abandon              every non-terminal status -> abandoned   human

status_guidance: draft EPIC_DRAFT, researching RESEARCHING, deciding DECIDING, designing DESIGNING,
                 designReview DESIGN_REVIEW, decomposition DECOMPOSITION (reworded)
workspace_guidance: humanReach at (deciding, designReview, review)
auto_children: solution-research, solution-design

body.text: agent-plan

Only wording and one guard change. _EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION_OR_LATER becomes _EPIC_DISPATCHING with statuses researching, designing, decomposition, planReview, executing, review, shipped and message 'the epic must be researching, designing, or in decomposition or later'. The description, notice, task and reporting texts say the agent works on the pages its agent-plan links works-on - the epic's solution-research or solution-design page, or the feature-briefs it builds with their child pages - and the worktree instruction says an agent that only reads code names none.
solution-research

The delegated research and brainstorming page, pinned under the epic and filled by a research agent, then checked by a judge agent. Every section is a plain list or prose; approaches is editable so a revised approach keeps the id the epic's chosen approach points at.

body.source:
tag solution-research, name 'Solution research'
sections
  understanding  body: prose                                setUnderstanding
  components     items {name, role, side in (pure|effectful)}   addComponent/remove/reorder
  constraints    items {text}                              addConstraint/...
  conflicts      items {text}                              addConflict/...
  documentation  items {text}                              addDocumentation/...

  questions      items {text, why, changes}                addQuestion/...

fsm initial waiting; states waiting, investigating, judging, reported; terminal reported
  begin             waiting -> investigating    parent guard _EPIC_RESEARCHING (epic in researching)
  submitForJudging  investigating -> judging    requires understanding.body, components.items, constraints.items,
                                                conflicts.items, documentation.items, priorArt.items,

body.text: solution-design

The delegated design page, pinned under the epic, written by a design agent and checked cold by a reviewer agent. ready and sealed are both terminal, so the page the person signs off is frozen, and sealing at decomposition freezes it for the build.

body.source:
tag solution-design, name 'Solution design'
sections
  intent      body: blocks standard_blocks()      addIntent / removeIntentBlock / reorderIntentBlock
  approach    chosen: prose                       setChosenApproach (label 'chosen approach')
              alternatives {name, tradeoff, whyNot}   addAlternative/...
  strategy    body: blocks standard_blocks()      addStrategy / removeStrategyBlock / reorderStrategyBlock
  decisions   items {decision, alternatives, reason, by in (person|proposal)}   addDecision/.../editDecision
  interfaces  items {name, shape}                 addInterface/.../editInterface
  changes     items {path, change in (create|modify|delete), why}   addChange/...
  criteria    items {text, verify}                addCriterion/... (singular 'criterion')
  builder     items {text}                        addBuilderChoice/... (singular 'builderChoice')
  check       outcome in (nothing-important-left|questions-raised)   setCheckOutcome  legal_in (checking,)
              questions {question, why, pile, resolution, needsHuman, status} on _BUILDER_QUESTION_FSM
                addBuilderQuestion(question, why)/remove/reorder  legal_in (checking,)
                resolveBuilderQuestion(builderQuestionId, pile in (answered|minor|theirs), resolution)  open -> resolved
                escalateBuilderQuestion(builderQuestionId)  flag needsHuman
  digest      body: prose                         setDigest
  review      verdict in (pass|revise) setReviewVerdict, findings {issue, severity in (blocking|minor)}  legal_in (checking,)

_BUILDER_QUESTION_FSM: initial open, states open, resolved, ('resolve', open, resolved, agent), checkmark_done resolved

fsm initial waiting; states waiting, drafting, checking, ready, sealed; terminal ready, sealed
  begin           waiting -> drafting         parent guard _EPIC_DESIGNING (epic in designing)
  submitForCheck  drafting -> checking        requires intent.body, approach.chosen, approach.alternatives, strategy.body,
                                              decisions.items, interfaces.items, changes.items, criteria.items,
                                              builder.items, digest.body
  markReady       checking -> ready           requires check.outcome, review.verdict
  revise          checking -> drafting
  reopen          ready|sealed -> drafting    parent guard _EPIC_DESIGNING
  seal            ready -> sealed             parent guard _EPIC_IN_DECOMPOSITION (epic in decomposition)
status_guidance: drafting DRAFTING, checking CHECKING

body.text: Guidance, workspace slots, registry and served text

body.source:
src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py  (new constants under an '--- epic' and a '--- solution-research and solution-design' banner)
  EPIC_DRAFT       draft is claimed by several types, so the prefix
  RESEARCHING, DECIDING, DESIGNING, DESIGN_REVIEW   bare: no other type has these statuses
  DECOMPOSITION    reworded: seal the design first, split along its expected changes, contracts from its interfaces,
                   briefs and agent-plan pages created under the epic, Scheduling for build waves; reopenDesign if unbuildable
  INVESTIGATING, JUDGING     solution-research
  DRAFTING, CHECKING         solution-design

src/pagetypes/_workspace_guidance.py
  RESEARCH_SOURCES_FIELD = 'researchSources', RESEARCH_SOURCES_LABEL = 'RESEARCH SOURCES GUIDANCE: ', RESEARCH_SOURCES_DESC
  HUMAN_REACH_FIELD = 'humanReach', HUMAN_REACH_LABEL = 'HUMAN REACH GUIDANCE: ', HUMAN_REACH_DESC

src/pagetypes/_registry.py   import _SOLUTION_RESEARCH, _SOLUTION_DESIGN from .epic; add both tags to REGISTRY
src/instructions.py          reword the epic one-liner; add one line each for solution-research and solution-design
tests/test_pagetypes.py      import and list both in PRODUCTION_TYPES

body.text: Pure and effectful

Every change is a pure declaration or pure served text. The effectful store already evaluates ChildStateGuard (page form over direct live children), ParentStateGuard and auto_children generically, and the do rollup already surfaces a human edge's requires as setters, so no store, core or self-direction code changes. Error paths are the existing ones: a transition with unmet requires or a failing guard is refused with its reason, and a parent-guarded begin, reopen or seal is reported blocked with the parent status it waits for.
Amendment: checkable approaches, outcomes before research, evidence basis

Three ideas taken from the inquiry-brief comparison. They supersede the matching lines in the blocks above: the epic's beginResearch and chooseApproach requires, and the element fields of solution-research's approaches, components, constraints, conflicts and documentation.

body.source:
epic
  beginResearch   draft -> researching   requires summary.body, framing.why, framing.outcomes
  chooseApproach  deciding -> designing  human  requires decision.chosen, questions.items
  framing.outcomes instruction: written before research, so approaches are judged against goals they cannot reshape
  EPIC_DRAFT: draw out goals, non-goals and anti-goals too; record what you fill in as proposal
  DECIDING: refine the outcomes as the conversation settles them (not first-write them)

solution-research
  _BASES = (observed, inferred, assumed)
  components     items {name, role, side, basis}   addComponent(name, role, side, basis)
  constraints    items {text, basis}               addConstraint(text, basis)
  conflicts      items {text, basis}               addConflict(text, basis)
  documentation  items {text, basis}               addDocumentation(text, basis)
  approaches     items {name, sketch, tradeoffs, fit, predicts, falsifier, recommended}
                 addApproach(name, sketch, tradeoffs, fit, predicts, falsifier, recommended?), editApproach all optional
  basis: observed = you opened it; inferred = follows from something you opened; assumed = neither
  INVESTIGATING: record each entry's basis; give each approach a prediction and a falsifier
  JUDGING: an entry marked observed that does not check out is blocking; an approach whose falsifier
           could never be observed is blocking

body.text: Amendment: subagentDispatch workspace guidance

A new workspace-configurable guidance field, surfaced wherever the controller defines, model-labels or launches an agent, so a workspace can say once how its agents are defined and launched instead of each epic working it out. Pure declaration: one constant triple and two WorkspaceGuidanceSpec entries; the store, its setter and the guidance rollup are reused unchanged.

body.source:
src/pagetypes/_workspace_guidance.py
  SUBAGENT_DISPATCH_FIELD = 'subagentDispatch'
  SUBAGENT_DISPATCH_LABEL = 'SUBAGENT DISPATCH GUIDANCE: '
  SUBAGENT_DISPATCH_DESC  = how this workspace defines and launches subagents - e.g. which model each
                            capability tier maps to, the agent type or tool that launches them, whether
                            they run in parallel or in the background, and how a run is handed its
                            agent-plan page id

epic        workspace_guidance += WorkspaceGuidanceSpec(SUBAGENT_DISPATCH_FIELD,
                                    (researching, designing, decomposition, executing), ...)
agent-plan  workspace_guidance  = (WorkspaceGuidanceSpec(SUBAGENT_DISPATCH_FIELD, (draft, ready), ...),)

surfaced as next_actions(page)['guidance_subagentDispatch'] = SUBAGENT_DISPATCH_LABEL + stored text,
only while the page sits at one of those statuses and the workspace has set the field

body.text: Amendment: one investigation per solution direction

Research no longer runs as one agent that grounds the repo and brainstorms every approach on one pinned page. Grounding needs a target, and different solution scopes lead to different investigations, so the user and the controller agree the solution directions at draft from the intent alone, and each direction gets a solution-investigation page of its own, an ordinary child of the epic created by the controller, filled by one investigator agent that grounds the repo for that direction's scope, works it out and tests it. One judge agent checks every investigation side by side. The pinned solution-research type is removed; solution-design stays pinned. This supersedes the solution-research block above, the epic's beginResearch and presentFindings edges, its auto_children and decision.chosen fields, and every text that points at 'the research page'.

body.source:
epic
  sections
    directions   items {name, scope, said in (user|proposal)}   addDirection/removeDirection/reorderDirection/editDirection
                 new section after framing: each a distinct kind of solution, scope = what it would change or add and
                 what it assumes; written with the user from the intent before any code is read; one investigation each
    decision     chosen {investigationId, takes}   addChosenApproach(investigationId, takes?)  legal_in (deciding,)
                 approachId -> investigationId: the page id of a solution-investigation child of this epic (plain text)
  transitions
    beginResearch    draft -> researching     requires summary.body, framing.why, framing.outcomes, directions.items
    presentFindings  researching -> deciding  guard ChildStateGuard(solution-investigation, (reported,),
                                                                    'every investigation must be reported')
  auto_children: (solution-design,) - solution-research is removed
  description, notice, summary/why/outcomes/questions instructions: 'the research page' -> each direction's
    investigation page

solution-investigation   (replaces solution-research; ordinary child of the epic, one per direction)
  _COSTS = (small, medium, large); _HOLDS = (yes, partly, no); _VIABILITY = (viable, viable-with-caveats, not-viable)
  sections
    understanding  body: prose                                       setUnderstanding
    direction      directionId: scalar                               setDirectionId (the epic direction's element id, plain text)
    components     items {name, role, side, basis}                   as on solution-research, scoped to this direction
    constraints    items {text, basis}                               as on solution-research
    conflicts      items {text, basis}                               as on solution-research
    documentation  items {text, basis}                               as on solution-research
    priorArt       items {name, finding, bearing}                    as on solution-research
    sketch         body: prose                                       setSketch
    variants       items {name, reason}                              addVariant/removeVariant/reorderVariant
    assessment     tradeoffs: prose                                  setTradeoffs
                   cost: scalar in _COSTS                            setCost
                   fit {outcomeId, holds in _HOLDS, note}            addFit/removeFit/reorderFit
                       ref_check RefCheck(arg=outcomeId, scope=parent, section=framing, field=outcomes)
    test           predicts: scalar                                  setPredicts
                   falsifier: scalar                                 setFalsifier
                   result: scalar in (held|falsified|untested)       setResult
                   evidence: prose                                   setEvidence (cites the spike worktree and commit when one ran)
    conclusion     viability: scalar in _VIABILITY                   setViability
    questions      items {text, why, changes}                        addQuestion/removeQuestion/reorderQuestion
    digest         body: prose, at most 150 words                    setDigest
    review         verdict in (pass|revise) setReviewVerdict, findings {issue, severity in (blocking|minor)}  legal_in (judging,)
  fsm initial waiting; states waiting, investigating, judging, reported; terminal reported
    begin             waiting -> investigating    parent guard _EPIC_RESEARCHING
    submitForJudging  investigating -> judging    requires understanding.body, direction.directionId, components.items,
                                                  constraints.items, conflicts.items, documentation.items, priorArt.items,
                                                  sketch.body, variants.items, assessment.tradeoffs, assessment.cost,
                                                  assessment.fit, test.predicts, test.falsifier, test.result,
                                                  test.evidence, conclusion.viability, digest.body
    report            judging -> reported         requires review.verdict
    revise            judging -> investigating
    reopen            reported -> investigating   parent guard _EPIC_RESEARCHING
  status_guidance: investigating INVESTIGATING, judging JUDGING (rewritten: one direction; one comparative judge)
  workspace_guidance: groundingTool, researchSources at (investigating,)

agent-plan
  role examples: investigator, investigation judge, designer, design reviewer, implementer, integration reviewer
  worktree: a judge, a designer or a design reviewer names none; an investigator names none, or a throwaway spike
            worktree of its own when its test needs code run - spike code is never integrated
  notice, description, task: works-on pages are the epic's solution-investigation or solution-design pages, or the
            feature-briefs it builds; a judge links every investigation it judges

solution-design: approach.chosen, approach.alternatives, strategy, changes, check.questions and review.verdict texts point
                 at the chosen and the other investigation pages instead of the research page

guidance
  EPIC_DRAFT     + brainstorm two to four directions with the user from the intent alone, theirs first, yours as proposal
  RESEARCHING    one investigation page + one investigator agent-plan per direction, dispatched together; one judge
                 agent-plan works-on every investigation once all are submitted; archive an investigation to drop a direction
  DECIDING       compare the digests, viabilities and the judge's findings; the recommendation is the controller's, since
                 each investigator argued one direction; pick by investigation id; reopen research to add or redo a direction
  DESIGNING, DRAFTING, CHECKING   the research page -> the chosen investigation page(s)
  INVESTIGATING  one direction: ground its scope, sketch, cull variants, assess every outcome, test by reading or a spike,
                 make the strongest honest case, digest last; stay inside the direction
  JUDGING        side by side: sampled observed entries; contradicting facts settled by opening the code, blocking on the
                 wrong page; stays in its direction; every outcome assessed; test backed by evidence; comparable sizes;
                 two directions that converged are a minor finding on both
  RESEARCH_SOURCES_DESC: 'a research agent' -> 'an investigator'

src/pagetypes/_registry.py, tests/test_pagetypes.py PRODUCTION_TYPES, src/instructions.py, README.md,
docs/designing-page-types.md and the identical skill brief: solution-research -> solution-investigation; the epic pins only
its design page, and its investigations are ordinary children

body.text: Research, judge, design and review runs each get an agent-plan page under the epic linked works-on to the research or design page; agent-plan's markReady guard widens to researching and designing. Rejected: a dispatch record on the research and design pages themselves (duplicates agent-plan's role, tier and reports), and the controller judging in its own context (defeats the context-hygiene goal).

Both new types are declared in src/pagetypes/epic.py. Rejected: a separate solution.py module, which would split the guard wiring between the epic and its pinned children across two files, against the architecture page's grouping rule.

The four grounding lists move to solution-research and the epic's grounding status is removed. Rejected: keeping them on the epic and having the controller copy the research results across, which re-loads the orchestrator's context and duplicates the data.

chosen approach holds plain approachId text, and research approaches are editable so ids survive revision. Rejected: a child-scope RefCheck (a new store capability for one field) and copying the approaches onto the epic (duplicates the research page).

Builder questions are added by the reviewer and resolved by the designer with an element transition writing pile and resolution, or flagged needsHuman while waiting on the person; the epic question id is named in the resolution text. Rejected: an editable list with a parent RefCheck, which list_cmds forbids, and a ref on the add, which runs before any answer exists.

Judge separation is a dispatch rule in stage guidance plus status locks on verdict and findings, not an enforced identity check. Rejected for now: a new agent-identity capability on commands, which the declaration model does not have.

researchSources (solution-research investigating) and humanReach (epic deciding, designReview, review) are built as new workspace-guidance slots; groundingTool is reused at investigating. Rejected: folding research sources into groundingTool, which means a code index, not outside sources.
One reopen command, legal from ready and sealed, back to drafting, guarded on the epic in designing. Rejected: separate reopen and unseal events with identical guards and destination.

Approaches carry required predicts and falsifier fields, and the judge treats an unobservable falsifier as blocking. Rejected: a full option lifecycle with a shortlist and rubric scores, which would duplicate the person's choice already recorded on the epic.

framing.outcomes moves from chooseApproach's requires to beginResearch's, so goals and anti-goals precede the approaches. Rejected: requiring it at both edges, which adds nothing once it is present, and a separate weighted rubric section, which the person's anti-goals already play the part of.

components, constraints, conflicts and documentation carry a required basis in observed | inferred | assumed. Rejected: a confidence field beside it (the basis already says how far to trust an entry) and a basis on prior art, whose instruction already admits only opened sources.

subagentDispatch surfaces at the epic's researching, designing, decomposition and executing and at agent-plan's draft and ready - every status in which an agent page is created, its capability labelled, or the agent launched or relaunched. Rejected: also planReview and review (they read agent pages but do not define or launch them, so the text there would be noise), and folding it into the agent-plan capability instruction (a field instruction is fixed per type, while the model mapping and launch mechanics differ per workspace).

One solution-investigation page per direction, an ordinary child of the epic, each grounded for its own direction by its own investigator; directions agreed with the user at draft from the intent alone; one comparative judge across all of them; the epic's presentFindings guards on every investigation being reported. Rejected: a shared scout that grounds once and seeds candidates for the investigators (grounding with no solution in mind has no target, so it either reads only the obvious area or everything, and it biases every direction toward what the scout happened to read); one judge per investigation (2N agents, and no judge sees the pages side by side to catch contradictions or uneven effort); keeping solution-research pinned beside the investigations (two homes for recon); a new epic status between research and judging (the judge is sequenced by the controller's dispatch, and the page-level judging status already locks the verdict).

The spike is the investigator's agent-plan worktree: it names none, or a throwaway spike worktree of its own; the investigation's test.evidence cites the worktree and commit, and spike code is never integrated. Rejected: a spike field on the investigation page (duplicates agent-plan's worktree, which already says where an agent works), and allowing spikes only for some directions by declaration (the need depends on the falsifier, which the investigator writes).

Folded into this brief and PR #60 before ship: the brief goes back to planning, the spec is amended and resealed, and the plans gain steps and cases for the change. Rejected: shipping #60 with the single research page and reshaping it in a follow-up, which would put a page type on main that is removed straight after and reconcile the architecture page twice.

epic:mwav2lhu-f00f56.title: Interactive timeline of workspace changes in the web UI

notice.body:
This epic is the controller's page. Only the controlling agent - the session that created this
epic and dispatches its agents - runs commands on it. Research, design and every build are done
by dispatched agents: each is handed one agent-plan page, a child of this epic whose page id is
the agent's id, works from that page, reports back onto it, and writes only that page and the
pages it links to with works-on - this epic's solution-research or solution-design page, or the
feature-briefs it builds with their child pages. It never edits this epic or another agent's
page. The controller reads the research and design pages' digests rather than the whole pages,
and records here what an agent raises: addFinding or editFinding for a problem, and
editContract for a shared contract it corrected.

summary.body: A person viewing a workspace in the web UI can open an interactive timeline of the changes made to it - what changed, on which page, and when - drawn from a new record of events that the page actions themselves emit as they happen. Which timeline view and visualisation serves this best, and how it is built, are for this epic to work out.

framing.why: The timeline is primarily a wow-factor, so it should be very clean and impressive and be interactive. It should collect lots of activity in the form of status transitions and play it back on demand. We want to show the timeline for the whole workspace to show impressive activity and productivity of the workspace.

outcomes.text: The web UI shows an interactive timeline of the changes made to a workspace.
Changes are tracked as new events emitted by the page actions themselves, rather than inferred after the fact.

Every page action that changes a page (create, field/section edit, status transition, rename, reparent, archive/unarchive, link) records an event in the same commit as the change, so the timeline neither misses a change nor shows one that did not happen.
Each timeline entry says which page changed, what kind of change it was, and when, and opens that page from the entry.
Playback can be started, paused, scrubbed and sped up, and stopping on any moment shows what changed then - without reloading the whole history.
Undoing, reverting or restoring a page to an earlier point from the timeline.
Recording events makes page actions noticeably slower, or gives a valid page action a new way to fail.
On a busy workspace the timeline becomes an unreadable firehose of small edits in which a person cannot find what actually changed.
The timeline is a wow-factor showpiece: very clean, impressive and interactive.
The timeline collects lots of activity in the form of status transitions and plays it back on demand.
The timeline covers the whole workspace, so it shows the workspace's activity and productivity at a glance.
The timeline opens with one clearly labelled 'tracking began' marker showing the pages that already existed and their status at that moment; it never shows a fabricated earlier change.
Each timeline entry shows whether the change came from an agent (MCP) or a person (web UI), as visibly distinct marks with a filter for each; no individual agent or user identity is recorded.

Element-level marks (plan step done, test case passed, question answered) are recorded and shown as a secondary layer: small pulses on their page's lane that merge into a counted cluster when dense, on by default with a filter to hide them, while page status transitions stay the primary marks.

chosen.takes: The whole approach, picked by the person: a bounded event log inside the workspace file, appended at the store transactions in the same atomic write as each change (covering MCP tools and the web UI POST routes alike), shown on a new full-screen hand-built canvas timeline with lanes, play/pause/scrub/speed and click-through, live-updated without a full tab reload. Carries the person's answers: a 'tracking began' baseline marker instead of backfill; each event marked agent (MCP) or person (web UI); element-level marks as a secondary, clustering layer. Fallback noted by research and accepted with the pick: if the hand-built drawing proves too costly, swap the display for a vendored vis-timeline while keeping this recording scheme.

items.name: Event record (one dict in Workspace.events / Workspace.element_marks) - design interface mwb2rxv7-bbd64e
items.shape:
{
  "at": str,            # UTC ISO-8601, exactly _now() format, e.g. "2026-11-10T19:41:02.113+00:00"
  "kind": str,          # one of: page.created page.status page.field page.renamed page.reparented
                        #         page.reordered page.archived page.unarchived page.delete_scheduled
                        #         page.delete_cancelled page.deleted page.link_added page.link_removed
                        #         element.mark workspace.created workspace.status
  "pageId": str | None,     # None only for workspace.* kinds
  "pageType": str | None,   # the page's type tag; None for workspace.* kinds
  "title": str | None,      # the page title AT EVENT TIME, so a later rename does not rewrite history
  "actor": "agent" | "person",
  "from": str | None,    # page.status: previous status. element.mark: previous element status.
                         # page.renamed: previous title. page.reparented: previous parent id.
                         # page.link_removed: None. Others: None.
  "to": str | None,      # matching new value; page.link_* : the target page id
  "event": str | None,   # the FSM event / command name that fired it, e.g. "markReady", "markStepDone",
                         # "adminOverride"; None for structural kinds with no command
  "section": str | None, # element.mark only: e.g. "steps"
  "field": str | None,   # element.mark only: e.g. "items"; page.field: the authored "section.field"
  "elementId": str | None  # element.mark only
}
Every key is always present (missing facts are null) so the client can key off a fixed shape. No per-agent or per-session identity is ever stored.

items.name: Store transaction hook, its handle, and actor keyword - design interface mwb2rxvd-81027b
items.shape:
# src/store.py
@dataclass
class Tx:
    workspace: Workspace
    actor: str          # "agent" | "person"; anything else raises ValidationError before any write
    at: str             # _now(), the one timestamp every event of this transaction shares

@contextmanager
def _transaction(self, workspace_id: str, *, actor: str = "agent") -> Iterator[Tx]
    # Raises NotFoundError (from load_workspace) exactly as before when the file is missing.
    # Yields the handle; on normal exit only (no exception) it seeds Workspace.tracking_began
    # via eventlog.baseline(workspace, at=tx.at) iff it is None, then calls _touch_and_save.
    # An exception in the body writes nothing, records nothing, seeds nothing.

# Every mutating method gains ONE keyword-only parameter, defaulted so all 25 MCP tools
# keep working unchanged:
def create_page(self, workspace_id, type_tag, title, parent_id=None, *, actor: str = "agent") -> CreatePageResult
def mutate_page_batch(self, workspace_id, page_id, batch, *, actor: str = "agent") -> MutatePageResult
def _set_page_archive_state(self, workspace_id, page_id, *, archived=None, delete_scheduled=None, actor: str = "agent") -> Page
    # archive_page / unarchive_page / schedule_page_deletion / unschedule_page_deletion
    # forward the same keyword.
def set_page_status(self, workspace_id, page_id, status, *, actor: str = "agent") -> Page
def rename_page(..., *, actor: str = "agent") -> Page
def reparent_page(..., *, actor: str = "agent") -> tuple[Page, list[str]]
def reorder_page(..., *, actor: str = "agent") -> tuple[Page, list[str]]
def link_page(..., *, actor: str = "agent") -> tuple[Page, list[dict[str, Any]]]
def unlink_page(..., *, actor: str = "agent") -> tuple[Page, list[dict[str, Any]]]
def cleanup_workspace(..., *, actor: str = "agent") -> cleanup.SweepReport
def _set_workspace_status(self, workspace_id, status, *, actor: str = "agent") -> Workspace

# create_workspace keeps its own lock and its single _write_file; it sets
# workspace.tracking_began = eventlog.baseline(workspace, at=_now()) and appends
# the workspace.created event before that write, and takes no actor argument.

# The five POST routes are the ONLY callers that pass actor="person" (wired by agent-plan:mwb4w0h6-a78273):
STORE.archive_page(workspace_id, pageId, actor="person")
STORE.unarchive_page(workspace_id, pageId, actor="person")
STORE.schedule_page_deletion(workspace_id, pageId, actor="person")
STORE.unschedule_page_deletion(workspace_id, pageId, actor="person")
STORE.set_page_status(workspace_id, pageId, status, actor="person")

items.name: Timeline payload: Store.timeline_payload and the JSON the timeline routes serve - from design interface mwb2rxvk-d427d4
items.shape:
# src/store.py  (owned by agent-plan:mwb4vznv-3c3f94)
def timeline_payload(self, workspace_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]
    # Read-only, no lock, no write. trackingBegan = workspace.tracking_began when set,
    # otherwise eventlog.baseline(workspace, at=_now()) derived in memory (design Part 1b).
    # Raises NotFoundError when the workspace is missing, like load_workspace.

# Payload (exact keys):
{
  "workspaceId": str,
  "name": str,
  "generatedAt": str,                 # _now()
  "trackingBegan": {"at": str, "pages": [{"id": str, "type": str, "title": str, "status": str}]},
                                      # never null: persisted value, else derived at generatedAt
  "events": [EventRecord],            # Workspace.events, oldest first
  "elementMarks": [EventRecord],      # Workspace.element_marks, oldest first, kind always "element.mark"
  "pages": {pageId: {"title": str, "type": str, "status": str, "archived": bool}},
  "truncated": bool,                  # Workspace.events_truncated
  "caps": {"events": 1000, "elementMarks": 1500}
}
# Neither route and no payload ever contains page section content.

# Consumed by agent-plan:mwb4w0h6-a78273, whose routes serve exactly this dict unchanged:
# GET /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline       -> timeline.html with the payload json.dumps'd into the page
# GET /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline.json  -> JSONResponse(payload)
# (workspace_id = f"ws:{workspaceIdPart}"; read-only, no lock, no write)

scheduling.body:
Two waves, one build agent each, dispatched in order. The depends-on link agent-plan:mwb4w0h6-a78273 -> agent-plan:mwb4vznv-3c3f94 is why they cannot run at once: the timeline page consumes the three contracts the recording agent defines (mwb4wk8f-f224f6, mwb4wk8i-275faf, mwb4wk8j-9fd775).

Wave 1 - agent-plan:mwb4vznv-3c3f94 (builds feature-brief:mwb4vimq-9d0dd3, event recording). Starts from origin/main on git@github.com:dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev.git, on branch timeline/record-events in its Agent Zero checkout timeline-build-events. Leaves a working, verifiable state: every store transaction records its events and the full test suite passes, with no UI yet.

Before wave 2 is dispatched:
1. agent-plan:mwb4vznv-3c3f94 is finished and accepted against its reporting contract, and feature-brief:mwb4vimq-9d0dd3 is in status done.
2. The controller reviews the diff in C:\Users\Dennis Schneidermann\agent-zero\agent-zero-instance\usr\workdir\timeline-build-events (git log and git diff against origin/main), fetches branch timeline/record-events from that checkout into a worktree of its own, and creates branch epic/workspace-timeline with those commits rebased linearly onto the current origin/main.
3. `uv run pytest --testmon` passes on epic/workspace-timeline.
4. epic/workspace-timeline is pushed to origin (pasta-dev).

Wave 2 - agent-plan:mwb4w0h6-a78273 (builds feature-brief:mwb4vji2-a8a514, the timeline page). Starts from origin/epic/workspace-timeline, on branch timeline/timeline-page in its Agent Zero checkout timeline-build-page. Leaves the epic complete: the timeline page works end to end in the browser and the full suite passes.

After wave 2:
1. agent-plan:mwb4w0h6-a78273 is finished and accepted against its reporting contract, and feature-brief:mwb4vji2-a8a514 is in status done.
2. The controller integrates timeline/timeline-page onto epic/workspace-timeline the same way (review the diff, rebase linearly, `uv run pytest --testmon` green, push).
3. Following the workspace merge process, the controller opens one pull request from epic/workspace-timeline into main through the github MCP, records its URL on both briefs, and submits the epic for review. Shipping is the person merging that pull request (squash) - the epic's human ship gate.

Each wave runs a single agent, well within the five-at-once limit.

items.text: Should activity from before event tracking ships be backfilled onto the timeline - if the existing records allow it - so the workspace's timeline is not empty on day one?
items.answer: "yes, use the tracking began marker" - No fabricated history. The timeline opens with one clearly labelled 'tracking began' marker showing the pages that already existed and their status at that moment; real activity fills in from there. No backfill from backups and no invented per-page timestamps.

items.text: Should a timeline entry say who made the change - a person clicking in the web UI, or an agent over MCP?
items.answer: "agent vs person only, as you proposed" - Each entry records which surface the change came through: agent (an MCP tool) or person (a web UI POST route). No individual identity (no per-agent or per-session id). The timeline shows the two distinctly (e.g. filled vs hollow marks) with a filter for each.

items.text: Do element-level marks count as timeline activity - a plan step marked done, a test case passed, a question answered - or only page-level changes?
items.answer: "secondary layer, as you proposed" - Element-level marks (plan step done, test case passed, question answered) are recorded as their own kind of event, distinct from the page's own status transitions. On the timeline they are a secondary layer: small pulses on their page's lane that merge into a counted cluster (e.g. '6 steps done') when dense, on by default with a filter to hide them. Page status transitions stay the primary, large marks. Retention is sized for the higher volume.

items.text: Which approach should the design build on: (1) bounded event log inside the workspace file + hand-built canvas timeline, (2) sidecar events file + vendored vis-timeline, or (3) per-page history shown in the tree view?
items.answer: "approach 1, as you recommended" - Bounded event log inside the workspace file + hand-built canvas timeline (solution-research approach mwb0bb0a-f0631b), with the vis-timeline display swap as the fallback if hand-drawing proves too costly.

findings.issue: Acceptance criterion mwb2sy9i-8bc810 (architecture pages 'Web UI, HMR & live reload' architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5 and 'Authoring & mutation' architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4 updated in the same change) is not delivered by either build agent: both agent-plan pages (agent-plan:mwb4vznv-3c3f94, agent-plan:mwb4w0h6-a78273) are told to leave documentation alone, because the feature-brief lifecycle reconciles the stale pages its briefs name at ship. It is still delivered - each brief names its stale page while grounding and the pages are reconciled when the epic ships, alongside the single pull request - so this is ordering, not a gap. Coverage otherwise checked: all 15 expected changes owned exactly once (7 by the recording agent, 8 by the timeline-page agent, no shared file); the 12 other criteria each delivered by at least one brief; the three interfaces crossing the two briefs are contracts mwb4wk8f-f224f6, mwb4wk8i-275faf, mwb4wk8j-9fd775 with an owner and the design's shapes; the scheduling waves match the depends-on link.

understanding.body:
The epic asks for an interactive timeline of the changes made to a whole workspace, shown in the web UI: what changed, on which page and when. The changes are to be recorded as new events that the page actions themselves emit as they happen, in the same commit as the change, rather than reconstructed afterwards.

In the person's words the timeline is 'primarily a wow-factor' - very clean, impressive, interactive - it should collect lots of activity (mainly status transitions) and play it back on demand (start, pause, scrub, speed), it covers the whole workspace so a workspace's activity and productivity show at a glance, and each entry says which page changed, what kind of change it was and when, and opens that page. Anti-goals: page writes must not become noticeably slower or gain a new way to fail, and the timeline must not degrade into an unreadable firehose of small edits. Undo/revert/restore from the timeline is explicitly a non-goal.

What is already true in this checkout (observed, commit 9ada650): there is no change history anywhere. `Page` carries no created_at/updated_at and no revision list, `serialize.page_to_dict` stores only current state, the whole workspace lives in ONE JSON file that every write replaces atomically, and the only two existing 'event' notions are the store-owned `status_revision_token` (a concurrency stamp that moves iff status moves) and the in-process, non-persistent `EventCache` (guidance delivery bookkeeping). So the epic starts from zero history and must add the record as well as the view.

Decided already: events come from the page actions (not inferred). Still open for this epic: the exact event shape and where it is stored, the timeline view/visualisation, how playback works, and whether pre-tracking activity is backfilled (an epic-level question the person must settle; see Questions).

items.name: src/store.py — Store.mutate_page_batch
items.role: Runs a page's batch as one atomic commit on a working copy. By the time it saves, it already holds everything a change event needs: the page and its type, each command's name and args, the status before and after (its `transitioned` flag is exactly that comparison), and the created ids. It is the one place where a status event is known without extra work.

items.name: src/commands.py — apply_command / _apply
items.role: The pure command core: edits a copied page and returns a CommandResult. It reads no clock, writes no status_revision_token and touches no storage, so it cannot by itself timestamp or persist an event - the store must supply time and the write.

items.name: src/model.py (Page, Workspace) and src/serialize.py
items.role: Page holds id/type/title/status/parent/children/sections/archived/links/expires_at/delete_scheduled/status_revision_token - no timestamps and no history. Workspace holds only created_at/updated_at. serialize.page_to_dict/page_from_dict are a near-identity mapping, so any newly stored field must be added to both, and a missing key must default so existing workspace files keep loading.

items.name: src/event_cache.py — EventCache / page_events
items.role: A transient, in-process record of per-page events with per-entry TTL (used for GUIDANCE_EMITTED at 300 s). It imports nothing from the package so it survives a hot reload, stores nothing on disk, and treats a missing entry as due - i.e. losing it is harmless by design. It is the closest existing thing to an event record and shows the codebase's own precedent for 'events are not history'.

items.name: src/render_html.py — render_page_html / Store.render_html
items.role: The second renderer: builds a page's BODY as structured HTML for the web view (scoped under .pasta-page), while renderPage keeps returning Markdown byte-for-byte. The nav sidebar, index and tree all still come through the Markdown renderer. A new visualisation that is not a page body has no home here.

items.name: src/templates/ (_base, _nav, page, tree, index) and src/static/styles.css
items.role: The page shell (footer source link, floating Top link, theme radios, reloader script), the two-column layout with sidebar, the page-actions row (archive / set-to-delete / status dropdown forms), and the workspace tree view - the only whole-workspace view that exists today. All structured-render styling is scoped under .pasta-page and every colour is a water.css custom property defined in both the light and dark sheets. There is no JS build step: every script is a plain file included by a template.

items.name: src/cleanup.py + Store.write_backup
items.role: The only snapshot mechanism in the system: the hourly sweep (at :05) writes a full workspace copy under .pasta-data/backups/<ws>/<UTC stamp>.json, and only when that pass prunes pages. Backups are therefore sparse, irregular and prune-driven, not a per-change record.

items.name: src/store.py — Store._write_file and its 12 _touch_and_save call sites
items.role: The write funnel, but NOT a single one. Every mutating Store transaction ends in _touch_and_save (:172), which stamps workspace.updated_at and calls _write_file (:160) - serializing the whole workspace and os.replace-ing it under the per-workspace readers-writer lock. _touch_and_save has 12 call sites in src/store.py: :560 mutate_page_batch, :635, :692 cleanup_workspace, :730 _set_page_archive_state (the one transaction behind archive, unarchive, schedule-delete and unschedule-delete - reachable from both the MCP tools and the four POST routes), :772 set_page_status (the POST /status override), :827 reparent_page, :853 reorder_page, :871 rename_page, :926 link_page, :945 unlink_page, :952 _set_workspace_status, :974 set_workspace_guidance. Two paths bypass it and call _write_file directly: create_workspace (:220) - a brand-new workspace, whose file must therefore be seeded with its own created entry before that write if the timeline is to show it - and write_backup (:187), which writes under .pasta-data/backups/ and never touches the live workspace file, so it changes nothing a person would see. Anything that must land in the same commit as a change has to be inside a _touch_and_save caller, or in create_workspace for the create case.

items.name: src/server.py — 3 GET routes, 5 POST mutation routes, 25 MCP tools, _guard_http, ws_reloader.refresh
items.role: The web surface and the tool surface. Read routes: GET / (:165 index), GET /ws:{id} (:180 tree), GET /ws:{id}/page/{pageId} (:200 page). Mutation routes: five POSTs that call the store directly - archive (:240), unarchive (:249), schedule-delete (:262), unschedule-delete (:271) and status (:284, STORE.set_page_status). All 25 MCP tools are async; every mutating tool AND every mutating POST calls ws_reloader.refresh() after the write, which tells every open tab to reload. Every route body runs inside _guard_http, which refuses when the page-type declarations do not validate. DATA_DIR is PASTA_DATA_DIR or .pasta-data. The five POST routes are change ENTRY POINTS any recording scheme has to cover, alongside the 25 tools.

items.name: src/templates/_reloader.js + src/hmr_live_refresh.py + the /ws/reloader heartbeat
items.role: The live channel that already exists: a WebSocket to /ws/reloader. A data mutation (tool or POST) or a source change sends {refresh: 1}; the client's `case 1` closes the socket and calls location.reload(true), so today the UI reacts to a change by reloading the whole tab. The server ALSO sends {refresh: 0} every 5 seconds from an asyncio task in fastapi_reloader (src/server.py:137-148), which the client swallows in its `case 0`: a keepalive that proves the socket is alive but carries no data. So there is no incremental 'append one new entry' channel and no polling endpoint - but an approach that wants to ride this socket has a 5 s heartbeat to ride for a cheap 'something changed?' nudge without a full reload.

items.text: Every change is one atomic whole-file replace: copy -> edit -> serialize -> os.replace, serialized per workspace by a threading.Lock. Recording an event in a SECOND file for the same action means either a window where one of the two writes landed and the other did not, or extra fsync/replace cost on the page-action path - which directly hits the anti-goal 'no slower writes, no new way to fail'.

Reads cost whole-file work: load_workspace parses the entire workspace JSON for every getPage/tree/render/search call, and list_workspaces parses every workspace file. An event record embedded in that file is therefore paid for on every read, so it has to be bounded (a ring buffer or retention window) or it must live outside the file.

There is no front-end build pipeline (no package.json, no node_modules, no bundler in pyproject/justfile): templates include plain .js files and /static serves files directly. A visualisation therefore has to be vanilla JS, or a vendored library committed into src/static - not an npm dependency built at deploy time.

There is no actor identity anywhere in the store: no user, session or agent id on a Page or in a write. An entry can say which page, what kind and when, but 'who' is not available without inventing and threading a new identity from the MCP session.

The renderPage Markdown output is a returned contract that agents read; the structured HTML renderer is deliberately separate. Any timeline work must not change the bytes renderPage returns, and the page body renderer is the wrong place for a workspace-wide visualisation.

Hot reload shapes where a new module may live: a module re-executes when it or a name it read changes, and in-process state survives only if the module imports nothing from the package (src/event_cache.py is the precedent). A new persistent record is stored on disk, so it does not depend on that trick - but any new in-process cache must either follow the same rule or accept being reset on a reload.

Backfill facts (asked for by the task). What the store keeps today: (a) workspace.created_at/updated_at only, no per-page timestamps; (b) no revisions, no change journal, no history file; (c) .pasta-data/ is gitignored, so the workspace JSON is NOT in version control and the git log holds no page history; (d) the only historical artefacts are sparse prune-time backups under .pasta-data/backups/, each a full workspace snapshot at one instant, written at most hourly and only on passes that delete something; (e) status_revision_token records that a status changed, not when or to what. Consequence: there is essentially nothing to reconstruct a truthful pre-tracking timeline from. A 'backfill' could only be (i) one synthetic baseline entry per existing page anchored on workspace.updated_at - a fabricated instant - or (ii) reconstructing change points by diffing successive backups, which yields only the sparse instants where a prune happened, mixes unrelated changes into one moment, and cannot see anything between them. Both are cheap to compute (a page map diff over a handful of files) but neither is real activity, so the epic-level question stands and is recorded in Questions.

Status transitions are the activity the person cares about, and they are already cheaply detectable: mutate_page_batch compares the working status against the stored one, and set_page_status is the web admin override that bypasses the FSM (and also regenerates the token). A record keyed on that comparison captures the main event class for free; element-level status changes (a plan step marked done) are a separate, much higher-frequency class that the firehose anti-goal warns against.

The web UI is NOT read-only at 9ada650, and this is the drift the earlier round missed. It reads through three GET projections (index, tree, page) but also carries FIVE POST admin routes that mutate through the store, in src/server.py: archive (:240 -> STORE.archive_page), unarchive (:249 -> unarchive_page), schedule-delete (:262 -> schedule_page_deletion), unschedule-delete (:271 -> unschedule_page_deletion) and status (:284-291, which calls STORE.set_page_status and then `await ws_reloader.refresh()`). Each runs inside _guard_http and refreshes open tabs exactly as a tool call does; src/templates/page.html:10-22 posts them from the page-actions row, and tests/test_web.py:98-195 exercises all five. What is still true is narrower: a workspace-wide timeline VIEW should be a GET projection rather than a form post. The recording scheme must treat a person clicking Archive / Set-to-delete / Apply-status as an event source alongside the MCP tools, or the timeline silently omits every human action.

src/event_cache.py already IS an in-process event record keyed (workspaceId, pageId, event) with TTLs, and it exists for a different purpose (guidance delivery). If a new event log reuses that name or that module, one of the two has to give: either the guidance cache is folded into a general record-and-read event store (a real change to a documented hot-reload invariant - the module imports nothing so it survives reloads, and its semantics are 'a missing entry is harmless'), or the new log must be a separate store with its own persistence so the guidance semantics are untouched. Recorded here so no approach silently retypes the other.

src/model.py's status_revision_token already means 'the status moved' and is already emitted, echoed on every describeMutations arg schema, every nextActions edge and both renderers' meta line. A timeline that also records 'the status moved' duplicates that fact in a second place; the two must not disagree about whether a transition happened, or the token stops being evidence and the timeline starts lying. The safe reading: the token is a concurrency stamp, the event is history - both derive from the same before/after comparison in mutate_page_batch, so they cannot drift if the event is recorded inside that same funnel.

src/render_html.py deliberately exists so the page BODY is structured HTML while renderPage keeps returning Markdown byte-for-byte. A timeline drawn as markup inside the page body would put a workspace-wide visualisation inside a per-page renderer whose contract is 'this page's sections'; the web-only shell (templates + static) is the surface that already owns cross-page chrome (sidebar, page-actions, footer) and is where a workspace-level view belongs.

src/templates/_reloader.js reacts to every data mutation by reloading the whole tab (location.reload(true)). While that stays the only channel, any in-page playback state - a scrubber mid-play, a paused moment - is destroyed by the next agent write. Either the timeline view has to tolerate reload-on-change (accepting that playback restarts), or the refresh channel has to become incremental, which is a change to a documented live-reload invariant.

The workspace-root route GET /ws:{id} is the tree view, rendered through the Markdown renderer (render_workspace_links), and GET / renders the workspace index as a Markdown list. Both are the natural doorways to a whole-workspace timeline, and both are Markdown-first surfaces: adding a rich visualisation to either means either a new template/route (leaving the tree as is) or feeding non-Markdown chrome through a renderer whose job is Markdown.

The hourly sweep in src/cleanup.py writes backups only when it prunes, and every read parses whole files. This collides with the obvious 'keep every event forever in the workspace file' shape twice: unbounded growth slows every read (anti-goal), and the only existing retention machinery (cleanup) is a page-deletion sweep with a backup step, not an event-retention window - so retention has to be designed, not inherited.

Searched for anything that already records change or time per page and found none: no created_at/updated_at on Page (model.py), no revision history in serialize.py, no journal or log module under src/ (grep for history/revision/audit/timeline/changelog across src/ returns only FSM transition and revision-token code), .pasta-data/ is gitignored so the workspace file is not versioned, and cleanup.py writes only prune-time backups. So there is no in-flight competing change and no existing history to reconcile - only the absence.

Three separate store transactions can change what a person sees, and each is reachable from more than one surface: mutate_page_batch (:563, MCP only), set_page_status (:749, store - reached only from the POST /status route), and _set_page_archive_state (:698, store - reached from the four POST archive/unarchive/schedule-delete/unschedule-delete routes AND from the archive/unarchive MCP tools). An event scheme hooked on the MCP tools or on mutate_page_batch alone would record agent transitions and silently drop every human one, which is the failure mode the blocking finding named. Hooking the store transactions instead covers both surfaces without touching a route - and is why the stale read-only invariant on 'Web UI, HMR & live reload' (mt4hhv74-832211) cannot be spent as a fact in any approach.

Pasta architecture page 'Authoring & mutation' (architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4), synced at commit 948c6bd. Its 'How pinned children are protected', 'What actually serializes concurrent writers', 'The revision token, end to end' and every invariant about atomic whole-file writes are the sections an event record lands inside. It would go stale the moment a write also records an event or a second file exists: its invariants 'Every write is copy -> edit -> atomic overwrite' and 'A batch is all-or-nothing' would need to say what happens to the event record when a batch aborts.

Pasta architecture page 'Page types & FSM implementation' (architecture:mrtjuul6-5221b2), synced at 9ada650 - the page that defines what a status transition IS (declared once on its command, table derived, machine fired in the pure core) and how element FSMs render their states. If an event names 'the transition' by FSM event, this page is the definition it must agree with; if events come from element marks too, its element-lifecycle section is where the frequency question belongs.

Pasta architecture page 'Self-direction' (architecture:mrtqsthj-dfd190), synced at 948c6bd - it documents src/event_cache.py, GUIDANCE_EMITTED, the five-minute TTL and 'a missing entry counts as lapsed'. That is the closest existing 'event' concept, so any approach that reuses or retypes the event cache has to reconcile with this page, and the page's 'How the event cache is disabled' section is the precedent for making a record switchable.

Code-level docs that would need the same change: .claude/skills/pasta-workflow-creation/SKILL.md and docs/designing-page-types.md - the hand-written pair the architecture page says must be updated together whenever a field kind, page type, command kind or guard changes. An event record that adds no page-type surface leaves them alone; an approach that adds a new command kind or a new field kind (e.g. an event tied to a command spec) makes both stale in the same commit.

Pasta architecture page 'Web UI, HMR & live reload' (architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5), synced at f2e095f - it has DRIFTED from 9ada650. Its invariant mt4hhv74-832211 states 'The web UI is strictly read-only ... State changes only ever through the MCP command path', and its purpose section says the front end 'is deliberately not a second path for changing state'. Both are false: src/server.py defines five POST routes that mutate through the store (archive :240, unarchive :249, schedule-delete :262, unschedule-delete :271, status :284). The rest of the page still holds the invariants a timeline view sits under - the two-renderer rule, 'All structured-render styling is scoped under the pasta-page class and takes every colour from a water.css custom property', the browser-refresh triggers, and 'The inner FastAPI app's lifespan never fires' (so anything new that needs startup must start from reloader_lifespan) - but its read-only claim and its 'not a second path for changing state' rationale must be corrected in the same change that adds a new route: a new route, a new static asset or a new vendored library makes this page stale first.

tests/ is the executable documentation of the invariants an event record must not break: tests/test_store.py (write path, atomicity, readers/writers, and one _touch_and_save use at :2085), tests/test_serialize.py (round-trip and backward-compatible defaults), tests/test_event_cache.py (cache semantics), tests/test_web.py (:98-195 posts to all five mutating routes - archive, unarchive, schedule-delete, unschedule-delete, status - so it pins the web write path, not read-only-ness), tests/test_hmr_server.py (the two private framework internals the dev server wraps), tests/test_cleanup.py (backups written only on a prune pass). A new event file or a new event field is a new thing to test in the same style, and any recording scheme that hooks a store transaction will be pinned by test_store.py before it is pinned anywhere else.

items.name: Martin Fowler, 'Event Sourcing' (martinfowler.com/eaaDev/EventSourcing.html, opened 2026-11-10)
items.finding: Defines event sourcing as capturing all changes to application state as a sequence of events, precisely because there are times we do not just want to see where we are but how we got there. It also frames the two costs that matter here: you rebuild state from a replay of events, and you therefore own their storage and retention rather than getting them free from the current state.
items.bearing: Validates the epic's 'emit, do not infer' instinct and names its price. It is also the argument for NOT going all the way: full event sourcing would make the log the source of truth and page state a projection, rewriting the copy-edit-replace path and putting every read behind a replay. This epic needs append-only history BESIDE current state - the timeline is a read model, not the system of record.

items.name: vis.js Timeline (vis-timeline npm 8.5.6; docs visjs.github.io/vis-timeline, README opened 2026-11-10)
items.finding: An interactive timeline chart rendering items and ranges over an automatically adjusted time axis supporting milliseconds to years, freely zoomable and draggable, drawn with regular HTML DOM so CSS can style it. Dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT, so licence-compatible with AGPL-3.0 Pasta. Its own README warns the 'standalone' build 'has no dependencies and therefore is great for things like MWEs but has more issues with interoperability and bundle bloat' - the drop-in build is the heavy one.
items.bearing: Makes the hard part (axis, zoom, drag, range layout) a vendored file plus a JSON array of items - exactly the shape that fits a repo with no JS build step. The cost is a large hand-maintained asset in src/static and a chart-library look rather than a bespoke 'wow' piece. It is the cheap, low-risk route to a genuinely interactive timeline.

items.name: d3-scale scaleTime (d3js.org/d3-scale/time, ISC licence, docs opened 2026-11-10)
items.finding: A time scale maps a temporal domain to a pixel range and 'implements ticks based on calendar intervals, taking the pain out of generating axes for temporal domains' - the calendar-aware tick logic that keeps an axis readable across 'three days' and 'three months' without hand-written interval maths.
items.bearing: Shows the mid path: hand-build the visualisation (marks, playback, scrubber) and take only the axis maths from a small ISC dependency, or reimplement that one function where no bundler exists. It bounds the 'roll our own' cost honestly - the expensive piece is calendar ticks, not the scatter of dots.

items.name: MDN, Element.animate() / Web Animations (developer.mozilla.org, opened 2026-11-10)
items.finding: The Web Animations API animates an element by keyframes and timing options with no library at all, and browsers interpolate simple properties off the main thread.
items.bearing: A 'wow' playback does not require an animation dependency in a repo with no build step: advancing a playhead and animating marks can be plain JS, which keeps the dependency count at zero for playback itself and makes the bespoke approach credible.

items.name: Grounding-tool check: graphify absent from this checkout (no graphify-out/graph.json, no binary on PATH)
items.finding: Nothing to report from that tool this round; the checkout has no graph and no graphify binary, so src/ was read directly.
items.bearing: Every component above carries basis 'observed' because it was read in the file named, not taken from a graph. A later reader comparing this page against a graph query may find the same symbols with a different call-flow emphasis.

items.name: Bounded event log inside the workspace file, rendered as a full-screen swimlane canvas with a scrubber
items.sketch: RECORDING: a new pure module src/eventlog.py holds the event shape ({at, pageId, pageType, kind, from, to, title, actor?}) and a bounded append (the last N per workspace). The entries are built AT THE STORE TRANSACTIONS, not inside _touch_and_save, because only the caller knows what changed - and hooking the transactions rather than the tools is what makes the recording cover the web admin write path and the MCP path with one hook. The twelve call sites: mutate_page_batch (:560 - status_before vs working.status, the command names, the page type and the created ids; the only place a modelled transition is known without extra work), set_page_status (:772 - the POST /status override that bypasses the FSM), _set_page_archive_state (:730 - one transaction behind archive, unarchive, schedule-delete and unschedule-delete, reached from the four POST routes AND the archive/unarchive MCP tools), _set_workspace_status (:952), cleanup_workspace's prune (:692, a page-deleted event), create_page, rename_page, reparent_page, reorder_page, link_page and unlink_page. Each appends in memory before the existing _touch_and_save, so the commit stays atomic, one os.replace still lands it, and the write path gains no new failure mode. Two direct _write_file paths need a decision each: create_workspace (:220) bypasses _touch_and_save, so it seeds Workspace.events with one workspace-created entry before that write - a brand-new workspace is otherwise a hole in the timeline; write_backup (:187) is deliberately LEFT OUT, because it writes a snapshot under .pasta-data/backups/ and changes nothing a person sees. set_workspace_guidance (:974) is left out too - configuration, not page activity. serialize.py gains the events key with a [] default so existing files load. Timestamp from the store's _now() (UTC ISO-8601), the call that already stamps workspace.updated_at. DISPLAY: a new route GET /ws:{id}/timeline renders a template that extends _base.html (not _nav.html - it is workspace-wide) and embeds the events as JSON. src/static/timeline.js draws a horizontal time axis with one lane per page type (or per page), each event a dot coloured by kind, status transitions a connector from status to status, all scoped under .pasta-page with water.css custom properties so light and dark both work. PLAYBACK: a playhead advanced by requestAnimationFrame (or Element.animate), with play/pause, a range slider that scrubs the time domain, and speed buttons; clicking a dot opens its page. Filtering is client-side over the embedded array. LIVE UPDATES: ride the existing /ws/reloader socket, which already sends a {refresh: 0} heartbeat every 5 s (src/server.py:137-148) - treat that tick as 'poll for more events' rather than a full reload, so a mid-playback scrubber is not destroyed by the next agent write.
items.tradeoffs: Buys: the strongest guarantee that an event and its change cannot diverge (same commit, same file, one os.replace), no new dependency, no new failure mode, full control of the look, and - after the read-only correction - automatic coverage of the five web admin POST routes, which enter through the same store transactions as the tools and so need no route-level hook at all. Costs: the append must be authored at twelve call sites plus create_workspace, so a future store transaction is a place to forget the event and the scheme needs a test that enumerates the mutating transactions; a bounded log (no truthful pre-tracking history, long-lived workspaces lose the tail); a slightly larger parse on every read; and the most hand-written front-end code (axis, zoom, lanes, playback).
items.fit: Serves every outcome: whole-workspace view (one array, all pages), status transitions as the main activity (recorded from the exact before/after mutate_page_batch already computes), playback with start/pause/scrub/speed (client-side over an embedded array), each entry names page + kind + time and opens the page. Avoids both anti-goals by construction: the write path adds one in-memory append to a file it was already replacing, and the firehose is answered by lanes + kind filters + a bounded window. It is also the only approach whose recording needs no separate handling of the five POST routes, because it hooks the store transactions those routes call - a person clicking Archive or Apply-status is recorded by the same line of code as the MCP tool. RECOMMENDED, and the read-only correction did NOT change the recommendation: it strengthened it, since it showed the competing sidecar would need its second-file append wired into both surfaces while this one gets both for free.
items.predicts: If right: after a batch that moves a page's status, the workspace JSON contains exactly one new event whose from/to match the status before and after, and the file is still written once per action. A POST to /ws:{id}/page/{pageId}/status and a POST to .../archive each add exactly one event too, with the same shape as the tool-driven ones. A batch that aborts adds none. createWorkspace yields a workspace whose events list is non-empty; a cleanup pass that prunes adds a page-deleted event.
items.falsifier: The approach is wrong if a realistic workspace's events list cannot be bounded without losing the transitions a person wants to see (the cap is hit within days of normal use), or if the added bytes make whole-file reads measurably slower, or if the hand-built axis/playback cannot be made to look clean within the epic's appetite - in which case the vendored-library variant of this same recording scheme is the fallback, not a different recording design. It is also wrong if a store transaction can change a page without the timeline noticing: enumerate the mutating transactions and check each appends.

items.name: Sidecar append-only event file per workspace, read by its own route, rendered with a vendored vis-timeline
items.sketch: RECORDING: each workspace gets .pasta-data/events/<ws>.jsonl, appended one line per event. src/store.py gains a small EventStore (a thin file-append under the same per-workspace transaction lock, opened and closed per write, no read-modify-write), called from the SAME twelve transactions the first approach hooks - including the three the web admin path enters by: set_page_status (:772, POST /status), _set_page_archive_state (:730, the four POST archive/schedule routes plus the matching tools) and _set_workspace_status (:952) - plus create_page, rename, reparent, reorder, link, unlink and mutate_page_batch. create_workspace (:220) must also append its workspace-created line, as a second write inside its own transaction lock beside the workspace file it is creating; write_backup (:187) is deliberately left out (it writes only under backups/ and changes nothing a person sees), as is set_workspace_guidance (:974). The workspace JSON is untouched, so reads stay exactly as fast and existing files need no migration; serialize.py does not change. Retention is a periodic truncate or a size check on append. DISPLAY: GET /ws:{id}/timeline parses the lines and loads a vendored vis-timeline (src/static/vendor/vis-timeline-graph2d.min.js + .css, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, AGPL-compatible) with items = events and groups = page types. PLAYBACK: vis-timeline's own zoom/pan, plus a custom playhead advancing the window's start with a timer; play/pause/speed, the range slider is the window. Clicking an item opens the page. Live updates: prefer the /ws/reloader heartbeat ({refresh: 0} every 5 s) as a cheap 'refetch?' nudge over the full-reload {refresh: 1}.
items.tradeoffs: Buys: unchanged read cost, no migration, a mature interactive timeline for little front-end code, and one advantage over the first approach - a corrupt or truncated event file cannot take the wiki down. Costs: the write path now touches a SECOND file per action, on every one of the thirteen entry points including all five web admin POST routes and workspace creation - either inside the same lock and after the page file (a crash between the two loses an event, which the epic's 'same commit' outcome forbids) or before it (a crash leaves an event for a change that never landed, which is worse); appending has its own new failure modes (disk full, permissions, concurrent truncate) on paths that today cannot fail except on the page file itself, and one of those paths is a button in the browser; plus a large vendored asset maintained by hand in a repo with no build step, and a library look that is harder to make bespoke.
items.fit: Serves the whole-workspace view, the interactivity and the playback well, and the entry shape is natural for vis-timeline. It fails the one outcome that is a person-stated goal in spirit - events emitted in the same commit as the change - and it risks the anti-goal about a valid action gaining a new failure mode, and the read-only correction made that risk WORSE rather than better: there are now thirteen write entry points to wire a second file into, five of them a person's button clicks, where the first approach covers all thirteen by hooking the transactions themselves. Not recommended; keep it as the fallback if the hand-built axis proves too expensive, because the recording scheme can be swapped under an unchanged view.
items.predicts: If right: no read latency regression, and vis-timeline renders a workspace's events with working zoom/pan and a moving playhead for almost no custom drawing code. If the atomicity worry is real, a read-only events directory makes a valid mutatePageBatch fail - or, worse, makes the browser's Archive button fail - or the timeline shows an event for a change that did not persist.
items.falsifier: Wrong if a single test can make a valid action fail or record a phantom event purely because the events file could not be written - that alone kills it against the anti-goal, and it is now the same test repeated for each of the thirteen entry points. Also wrong if the vendored standalone build cannot ship in src/static without a bundler step, or if its payload is disproportionate to a local wiki.

items.name: Per-page bounded history stamped on the page, played back inside the workspace tree view
items.sketch: RECORDING: no central log. src/model.py's Page gains a small history list (last K entries: {at, kind, from, to, command}), appended by src/store.py in the same twelve transactions the first approach hooks - mutate_page_batch (:560), set_page_status (:772, the POST /status override), _set_page_archive_state (:730, the four POST archive/schedule routes plus the matching tools), _set_workspace_status (:952), cleanup_workspace's prune (:692), create_page, rename, reparent, reorder, link and unlink - before the existing _touch_and_save, and carried through serialize.py with a [] default. The page is the unit of storage, so an event lives where its change lives and the workspace file keeps one write per action, and a web admin POST is recorded by exactly the same line as the MCP tool. create_workspace (:220) has no page to hang history on and bypasses _touch_and_save: it either seeds a single synthetic root-level entry or, more honestly, leaves a new workspace with an empty history and lets the first page's creation be the first event - a decision this shape forces and the other two do not. write_backup (:187) and set_workspace_guidance (:974) are left out (a backup changes nothing a person sees; guidance is configuration). DISPLAY: the existing workspace tree route GET /ws:{id} (src/templates/tree.html) gains a second column: a compact per-page strip of recent status dots, plus a workspace-wide activity band assembled client-side by merging the pages' histories - no new route, no new page. PLAYBACK: scrubbing the band sets a cutoff instant and every strip re-renders to the state it had then (client-side filter); play advances the cutoff with a timer; speed changes the step. Clicking a strip opens the page. The page-actions row's Archive / Set-to-delete / status dropdown keep working unchanged and their effects appear in the strip because they land on the same page history.
items.tradeoffs: Buys: minimal new surface, no new route or dependency, history that travels with the page it describes (so a page view could show its own story later), and automatic coverage of the five web admin POST routes for the same reason as the first approach.
