Payload shape: timeline_payload returns exactly the nine keys workspaceId, name, generatedAt, trackingBegan, events, elementMarks, pages, truncated and caps, with caps == {"events": 1000, "elementMarks": 1500}, a pages map of title/type/status/archived with no sections, and trackingBegan equal to the stored field when it is set. overview.body:
This spec covers the recording half of the workspace timeline: a bounded, persisted event log carried inside the workspace file, written by the store's own write transactions in the same atomic commit as the change it describes. It specifies one new pure module (the event record, the bounded append, the tracking-began baseline, the page summary), the four fields the workspace file gains, the transaction hook that gives recording a single choke point and carries the actor, exactly which events each mutating store method appends, how an element FSM transition is detected inside a batch, and the read-only timeline payload that derives the baseline in memory when nothing has been written yet.

It deliberately leaves out everything that renders: no timeline route, no template, no canvas, no JavaScript, no styling, and no change to src/server.py or src/commands.py. The page that consumes this payload owns all of that. It also leaves out documenting the change on the pasta architecture pages, which happens at ship, and any migration of existing workspace files, which the backward-compatible serialization defaults make unnecessary.

body.text: Where the line between pure logic and effects falls

src/eventlog.py is pure. It takes facts that are already known plus a timestamp string and returns dicts, and it imports only from src.model. It never reads the clock, never touches disk, and never mutates the workspace it is handed. Every rule about what an event looks like, how a cap trims, and what the baseline snapshot contains lives there.

src/store.py stays the only place that decides when an event is recorded and the only place that writes it. It takes the clock from the existing _now() and it holds the one lock. timeline_payload is a read projection on the store and writes nothing.
The event record

One event is a flat, JSON-able dict with a fixed key set. Every key is always present and a fact that does not apply to that kind is null, so the client can key off a fixed shape. No per-agent or per-session identity is ever stored: the only identity is which surface the change came through.

body.text: kind is one of exactly these values: page.created, page.status, page.field, page.renamed, page.reparented, page.reordered, page.archived, page.unarchived, page.delete_scheduled, page.delete_cancelled, page.deleted, page.link_added, page.link_removed, element.mark, workspace.created, workspace.status. actor is "agent" or "person" and nothing else.

Per-kind meaning of the optional facts. page.status carries the previous and new status in from and to and the FSM event name in event. element.mark carries the element's previous and new status in from and to, the element FSM event name in event, and section, field and elementId. page.renamed carries the previous title as from and the new title as to. page.reparented carries the previous parent id as from and the new parent id as to. page.reordered carries the previous and new index as from and to. page.link_added and page.link_removed carry the target page id as to and the link role as from; page.link_removed does not carry the removed role separately. page.field carries the authored "section.field" in field and the command name that authored it in event. page.archived, page.unarchived, page.delete_scheduled and page.delete_cancelled carry the boolean flag that moved in to. workspace.status carries the previous and new workspace status. page.created, page.deleted and workspace.created carry no extra fact. Every page-scoped event carries the page title at event time, so a later rename never rewrites history.

body.source:
from typing import Any, Final

from .model import Page, Workspace

EVENT_CAP: Final[int] = 1000
ELEMENT_CAP: Final[int] = 1500
BYTE_BUDGET: Final[int] = 256 * 1024


def make(
    kind: str,
    at: str,
    *,
    page: Page | None = None,
    actor: str = "agent",
    from_: str | bool | int | None = None,
    to: str | bool | int | None = None,
    event: str | None = None,
    section: str | None = None,
    field: str | None = None,
    element_id: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One event dict carrying every key of the record shape."""


def append(events: list[dict[str, Any]], event: dict[str, Any], cap: int) -> bool:
    """Append `event`, then trim oldest-first to `cap` and to BYTE_BUDGET.

    Returns True when anything was trimmed. Never raises on a well-formed event.
    """


def baseline(workspace: Workspace, at: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The one-time tracking-began snapshot: {"at": at, "pages": [...]}."""


def page_summary(workspace: Workspace) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """{pageId: {"title", "type", "status", "archived"}} for every page."""

body.text: make reads nothing and decides nothing. When page is given it takes pageId, pageType and title from it; when page is None it writes null for all three, which is the workspace.* case. from_ and to are typed loosely because page.reordered carries integers and page.archived carries a boolean; every other kind passes a string or null. The event is stamped with the caller's at and actor exactly as given.

append does two trims on the list it is handed. First, while the list is longer than cap it drops the oldest entry. Second, while the sum of json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False) lengths exceeds BYTE_BUDGET it drops the oldest entry, so BYTE_BUDGET is a ceiling on each buffer as it is appended to and neither buffer may exceed 256 KiB. append returns True as soon as it has dropped anything, and the store ORs that into the workspace's events_truncated flag.

baseline walks workspace.root_page_ids depth-first through the child id lists and emits, for every page it reaches, an object with exactly the keys id, type, title and status, taken from the page as it stands. Archived pages are included and are not flagged separately: status is the only thing it claims. The walk tracks visited ids so a corrupt file cannot make it loop. baseline stamps at as given and invents no per-page timestamp and no ordering between pre-existing pages.

page_summary iterates workspace.pages and emits {"title": page.title, "type": page.type, "status": page.status, "archived": page.archived} keyed by page id. It is the payload's click-through map and it never contains section content.

body.text: Page is not changed: no timestamps and no history on a page, so a page stays exactly the thing a page-type command edits.
The transaction hook and its handle

One context manager replaces the repeated lock-load-mutate-save preamble of the twelve _touch_and_save transactions and gives recording a single choke point. It yields a handle carrying the working workspace, the actor and the one timestamp every event of that transaction shares. The caller mutates the workspace and appends its events to it; on normal exit the helper seeds the baseline if it is still unset and saves once.

The actor check happens before the lock is taken, so an unknown actor fails without touching the file. A body that raises propagates its own PastaError unchanged and the save never runs, so an aborted transaction records nothing and seeds nothing. The commit stays one serialize plus one os.replace because events are appended to the same in-memory workspace that the same single write then stores: no new I/O call and no new exception source on the write path.
Every mutating method gains one keyword-only parameter, defaulted so all 25 MCP tools keep working unchanged.

body.text: Nothing is recorded for set_workspace_guidance, for write_backup, or for cleanup's expiry stamping and clearing: configuration, an invisible copy, and scheduling metadata the sweep sets for itself are none of them a change to a page's content or lifecycle. Pruning is recorded because it destroys pages.
Detecting an element mark inside a batch

mutate_page_batch already builds a check_specs list per entry: the entry's own CommandSpec plus the CommandSpec of every CompoundCommand step. The store iterates that same list around the existing apply_command call. For each ElementTransitionCommand in it, read the target element's status from the working page by matching spec.args[0] as the element id, then apply the entry exactly as today, then read the status again. When the two differ, append an element.mark. Both reads are in-memory scans over a page that is already loaded, so no extra I/O happens and src/commands.py is untouched. A compound step therefore records exactly like a top-level command.

Reading the status of a missing element returns None rather than raising: the mark records something that happened and must never turn a write that would have succeeded into one that fails. When the element is found before and after and its status differs, the mark carries section, field, elementId, event = the ElementTransitionCommand's event, and the two statuses.
The one page.field event of a batch

A batch is one atomic commit and one write. When it authored typed content and did not move the page's status, it appends exactly one page.field event naming the batch's first field setter: field is that command's section.field and event is its command name. A batch that moved the status appends no page.field - the transition is the event that matters - and a batch that only removed, reordered or fired an element FSM appends none either, which keeps structural churn and element marks out of the ordinary firehose. The first setter is found with the existing is_field_setter classifier over the batch's command specs.
Workspace.timeline_payload

body.source:
def timeline_payload(self, workspace_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    # The whole timeline as one JSON-able dict. Read-only: no lock, no write.
    workspace = self.load_workspace(workspace_id)     # NotFoundError exactly as today
    generated_at = _now()
    began = workspace.tracking_began or eventlog.baseline(workspace, at=generated_at)
    return {
        'workspaceId': workspace.id,
        'name': workspace.name,
        'generatedAt': generated_at,
        'trackingBegan': began,
        'events': list(workspace.events),
        'elementMarks': list(workspace.element_marks),
        'pages': eventlog.page_summary(workspace),
        'truncated': workspace.events_truncated,
        'caps': {'events': eventlog.EVENT_CAP, 'elementMarks': eventlog.ELEMENT_CAP},
    }

body.text: trackingBegan is never null. When the field is set, the persisted marker wins, so the marker time stops at the instant tracking really started. When it is still None - a workspace nobody has written since this shipped - the identical value is derived in memory at generatedAt. That is not fabricated history: baseline states only what is true at the instant it is derived, inventing no per-page timestamp and no ordering, and the payload provably writes nothing, so a GET can never fail because the disk was full.

Neither the payload nor any route it feeds ever carries page section content. events and elementMarks are the records as stored, oldest first, and their dicts come from eventlog.make, so the shape contract holds end to end.

The twelve lock-load-save preambles collapse into one _transaction context manager that also seeds the baseline and carries the actor. Rejected: a hand-inserted record call in each transaction (twelve places to forget the baseline, each repeating the same check), and hooking _touch_and_save (it does not know what changed, so it could not build a typed event). One helper gives recording a single choke point and adds exactly one keyword to each signature.

An element mark is detected from the check_specs list mutate_page_batch already builds, by reading each ElementTransitionCommand's element status before and after the apply. Rejected: returning the element status change from the pure core (it is deliberately clock-free and storage-free), adding a hook to apply_command, and scanning top-level commands only (it would silently drop a nested compound step, which the command model legally admits). Two in-memory scans, no extra I/O, src/commands.py untouched.

The tracking-began marker is unconditional and a GET never writes: _transaction persists it on the first write, create_workspace seeds it at creation, and timeline_payload derives the identical value in memory at generatedAt while the field is still None. Rejected: seeding from the read route (a write, and a new write failure mode, on a GET - exactly the anti-goal), an empty state until the first write (breaks the stated outcome), and a startup sweep (writes every workspace unasked and misses ones created while the server runs). The derived marker invents no per-page timestamp and no ordering, so it is not fabricated history.

The payload carries events, elementMarks, trackingBegan, a page map of title/type/status/archived, generatedAt, truncated and caps - never page bodies or section content. Rejected: sending the whole workspace so the chart could read any field, and streaming one event per request while scrubbing. The chart needs labels, kinds, times and a click-through target; keeping bodies out bounds the payload and stops the display becoming a second content view.

The 256 KiB budget is enforced per buffer, inside append: append takes one list and one cap and trims it until it is within both cap and BYTE_BUDGET, so neither buffer can exceed 256 KiB and the two together are bounded at 512 KiB in the worst case, far below it in practice. Rejected: a joint budget the store would have to measure, which needs a second pure function whose only caller is the store and which would put a retention rule back on the effectful side.

Only commands the existing is_field_setter classifier accepts count as authoring content for the single page.field event: setScalar, setProse, addElement (including the element-FSM adds) and a page-level addBlocks. setTitle does not count because it records page.renamed, and addLink does not count because it records page.link_added. So a batch of only setTitle or addLink commands records no page.field, and a batch that moved the status records none either.

A cleanup prune records one page.deleted per page actually destroyed - the root and every descendant removed with it - each carrying its own title at event time. Rejected: one event for the maximal pruned root, which would leave the descendants' last state unexplained on a timeline that is a record of pages. The design's own precedent for a cascade (the archive flag reaching pinned children) is one event per affected page.

The persisted event log is a new pure module, src/eventlog.py, deliberately kept apart from src/event_cache.py, which already owns the word 'event' for a transient in-process TTL cache used to de-duplicate delivery. Rejected: extending the cache into the persisted log, which would put an explicitly disposable, reload-surviving object on the write path and make the timeline depend on something designed to be lost. Two modules, two docstrings, two clearly different lifetimes.

The person actor is proven at the store layer in this slice: the branch accepts actor and its store tests show agent and person both landing. Rejected: asserting it through the five POST routes in tests/test_web.py here, because that file is outside this brief's seven owned paths and belongs to feature-brief:mwb4vji2-a8a514, whose slice actually edits src/server.py to pass actor='person'.

report.version: main 6815f7d; seen when moving to PR 60's branch epic-research-design (7d13b26), which drops the epic's grounding state

summary.body: After a page type loses a state, running scripts/gen_page_type_docs.py leaves that state's docsite/page-types/<tag>-<state>.md in place, and the next Sphinx build warns that the leftover document isn't included in any toctree.

steps.text: Start from a checkout of main (6815f7d), where the epic page type still has a grounding state, with no docsite/page-types directory.
Run `uv run python scripts/gen_page_type_docs.py`. docsite/page-types/epic-grounding.md is written along with the other state pages and states.md.
Check out the branch epic-research-design (PR 60, 7d13b26), whose epic FSM no longer has a grounding state. docsite/page-types/ is gitignored, so the generated files stay.
Run `uv run python scripts/gen_page_type_docs.py` again, then `uv run sphinx-build -a docsite -b html docsite/_build/html`.

expected.body: docsite/page-types/ holds exactly the pages the registry generates - one per reachable state plus states.md - so epic-grounding.md is gone after the second generation and Sphinx builds without a toc.not_included warning. Grounding: the architecture page 'Page-type documentation generation' (architecture:mry456ug-6b1c0b) states as an invariant that 'every docsite/page-types/<tag>-<state>.md and the states.md index come from docsgen over the registry', with the only hand-authored docsite pages being index.md and page-types.md, both outside that directory. The `just docs` recipe already treats the directory that way: it runs `rm -rf docsite/page-types` before generating.

observed.body:
epic-grounding.md is still there after the second generation (the run reports '27 files written ... (32 unchanged)' and removes nothing). An incremental Sphinx build prints:

    C:\Repos\pasta\docsite\page-types\epic-grounding.md: WARNING: document isn't included in any toctree [toc.not_included]

A clean build (`-a` into a fresh output directory) fails outright instead, while reading page-types/epic-grounding - the stale page's statemachine-diagram replays its old event path on the new epic machine:

    statemachine.exceptions.TransitionNotAllowed: Can't beginGrounding when in draft.

Reproduced every time by the steps above (reproduced in a worktree at 6815f7d, then detached at 7d13b26). `just docs` hides it by wiping the directory first. The script's docstring documents the gap: 'it does not delete previously generated files - remove a stale <tag>-<state>.md by hand if a state is ever dropped from a page type.'

fixCommits.message: Remove generated page-type docs the registry no longer produces (#63)

bug-report:mwj6yk8q-1ce666.title: HMR reload fails when a new page type or field references a constant added in another file in the same save

report.component: Web UI, HMR & live reload - the dev server's hot reload (src/hmr_server.py Reloader, built on reactivity.hmr AsyncReloader and its watchfiles awatch loop)
report.platform: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045; Python 3.14.6; hmr (reactivity.hmr) 0.7.6.3; watchfiles 1.3.0; uvicorn 0.54.0; fastmcp 4.1.6. Dev server started with `uv run python main.py` from the main checkout C:\Repos\pasta.
report.version: Reported at main cbc395e. Logged occurrences span 2026-09-29 to 2026-11-10, while main was updated to 872ebd4, origin/main (2026-10-15), 3f4e965, f2e095f, ef61f14, 9ada650 (#58) and f36dc2b.

summary.body: When one git operation (`git pull --ff-only` or `git reset`) updates several source files under the running dev server at once, and one of them adds a constant or field that another updated file uses, the hot reload intermittently fails with `ImportError: cannot import name '<X>' from '<module>'` (or `AttributeError: 'FieldSpec' object has no attribute '<field>'`), even though the files on disk do define that name.

steps.text: Starting state: a separate checkout of the repo at 8c9d97a, the parent of #58, so the user's main checkout is not touched: `git worktree add ../pasta-hmr-repro 8c9d97a`, then `cd ../pasta-hmr-repro && uv sync`. No dev server running from that directory yet.

Start the dev server from that checkout: `uv run python main.py`. Wait until it serves http://localhost:8000 and hmr_debug.log in the checkout root has a single 'HMR reload-error capture armed' entry.
Open http://localhost:8000 in a browser so a /ws/reloader socket is live (optional; the failure does not depend on it).

In a second shell in the same checkout, move to #58 in one git operation: `git checkout --detach 9ada650`. That one checkout rewrites src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py (which gains `DECOMPOSITION = """...` at about line 196) together with src/pagetypes/epic.py (which gains `from ._stage_guidance import DECOMPOSITION`), src/pagetypes/core/specs.py, src/store.py, src/instructions.py and src/testtypes.py.

Read the server console and the new entries in hmr_debug.log. If no error appears, run `git checkout --detach 8c9d97a` and then `git checkout --detach 9ada650` again a few times, because the failure is intermittent. The defect shows as a `sys.excepthook` entry ending in `ImportError: cannot import name 'DECOMPOSITION' from 'src.pagetypes._stage_guidance'`, logged about a second after the checkout.

expected.body:
After the git operation finishes, the reloaded server should match a cold start of the same tree: page types load, and no ImportError or AttributeError is raised for a name the checked-out files define.

The basis for that:

- The 'Web UI, HMR & live reload' architecture page (architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5) gives hot reload's purpose as: "On a source edit the running server reloads its modules in place - MCP client sessions and browser tabs stay connected and refresh themselves rather than the process respawning." Its first invariant says hot reload happens in-process and "a source change never respawns the process".
- The same tree does load cleanly. After every logged failure, the next cold start (an 'armed' entry in hmr_debug.log, at the same commit) records no error, so the files on disk are consistent and only the hot reload fails on them.
- src/_hmr_debug.py already names this class of failure as a known one that the log exists to diagnose: "notably the load-ordering races a multi-file change can trigger".

observed.body:
About a second after the git operation, the reload of one module fails and the reloader swallows the error, which hmr_debug.log (repo root) records. Literal examples from C:\Repos\pasta\hmr_debug.log:

```
===== 2026-11-10T13:33:32.849 sys.excepthook =====
  File "C:\Repos\pasta\src\pagetypes\epic.py", line 9, in <module>
    from ._stage_guidance import DECOMPOSITION
ImportError: cannot import name 'DECOMPOSITION' from 'src.pagetypes._stage_guidance' (C:\Repos\pasta\src\pagetypes\_stage_guidance.py)
```

```
===== 2026-09-29T12:27:14.886 sys.excepthook =====
  File "C:\Repos\pasta\src\pagetypes\simple_change.py", line 5, in <module>
    from ._stage_guidance import DONE, REVIEW, SIMPLE_CHANGE_DRAFT, SIMPLE_CHANGE_OPEN
ImportError: cannot import name 'DONE' from 'src.pagetypes._stage_guidance' (C:\Repos\pasta\src\pagetypes\_stage_guidance.py)
```

```
===== 2026-11-09T21:19:43.455 sys.excepthook =====
  File "C:\Repos\pasta\src\server.py", line 48, in <module>
    validate_registry()
  File "C:\Repos\pasta\src\pagetypes\core\validation.py", line 535, in validate_field_spec
    if field.fixed is not None and field.kind != PROSE:
AttributeError: 'FieldSpec' object has no attribute 'fixed'
```

Each of the eight occurrences since 2026-09-29 comes within about a second of a reflog entry that rewrote the main checkout:

| git operation (reflog time) | failure logged | final exception |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-29 12:27:14 reset | 12:27:14.886 | ImportError: cannot import name 'DONE' from 'src.pagetypes._stage_guidance' |
| 2026-10-15 20:48:44 reset to origin/main | 20:48:45.081 | ImportError: cannot import name 'JSONValue' from 'src.model' |
| 2026-11-09 20:21:42 reset | 20:21:43.017 | AttributeError: 'FieldSpec' object has no attribute 'fixed' (raised while handling ImportError: cannot import name 'edit_element_cmd' from 'src.pagetypes.core.commands') |
| 2026-11-09 20:56:10 reset | 20:56:10.459 | AttributeError: 'FieldSpec' object has no attribute 'fixed' |
| 2026-11-09 21:19:42 pull --ff-only | 21:19:43.455 | AttributeError: 'FieldSpec' object has no attribute 'fixed' |
| 2026-11-09 22:23:40 reset | 22:23:41.703 | ImportError: cannot import name 'DECOMPOSITION' from 'src.pagetypes._stage_guidance' |
| 2026-11-10 13:33:31 pull --ff-only | 13:33:32.849 | ImportError: cannot import name 'DECOMPOSITION' from 'src.pagetypes._stage_guidance' |
| 2026-11-10 16:29:12 reset | 16:29:12.838 | ImportError: cannot import name '_SOLUTION_DESIGN' from 'src.pagetypes.epic' |

In each case the missing name is a constant or field that the same update added. Current source defines all of them except the two that were renamed later (`_SOLUTION_DESIGN`, `edit_element_cmd`): `DECOMPOSITION` at src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py:196, `DONE` at :240, `JSONValue` at src/model.py:17 and `FieldSpec.fixed` at src/pagetypes/core/fields.py:33. `DECOMPOSITION` and its importer epic.py were added in the same commit (9ada650, #58). Nine earlier `cannot import name` entries (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-12) have the same shape but were not matched against the reflog.

The server does not recover on its own. Every occurrence is followed by a cold restart (a new 'armed' entry) 16 s to 3 min later, for example 22:23:41 to 22:24:01, 13:33:32 to 13:33:48 and 16:29:12 to 16:29:59. Until the restart, the modules from before the update keep serving, or both surfaces refuse with the declaration-errors 503.

Reproducibility: intermittent on the live server. It shows up on some multi-file git updates of the watched checkout, not on every one.

### Reproduced in open (2026-11-16, at cbc395e, hmr 0.7.6.3)

The failure reproduces deterministically without a server or file watcher. Set up a two-module package: a.py exports `OLD`, b.py does `from .a import OLD`. Load it through hmr's real reactive finder (`SyncReloader(..., includes=[root])`), with an `effect` that reads `rpkg.b`. Rewrite both files completely: a.py gains `NEW`, and b.py switches to `from .a import NEW`. Then call the reloader's `on_changes` on the two paths.

- Order `[b.py, a.py]` (importer first) fails: `ImportError: cannot import name 'NEW' from 'rpkg.a'`. a.py is never re-executed. It still lacks `NEW` after a later, unrelated change, which is the stuck-until-restart behaviour above.
- Order `[a.py, b.py]` (exporter first) reloads cleanly.
- A package shaped like the `FieldSpec.fixed` case fails in both orders with `AttributeError: 'F' object has no attribute 'fixed'`. In that package fields.py's class gains a field, an unchanged kinds.py builds an instance of it, validation.py's new code reads the field, and an unchanged top.py runs that validation on the instance.
- The same two files arriving in separate batches (importer first, exporter in the next batch) recover on their own. Batch 1 raises the ImportError. In batch 2 the importer re-runs and reads `NEW`, because its failed read of the missing name subscribed it to that name.

In the real repo, the order of `{_stage_guidance.py, epic.py, _registry.py}` inside a `set[Path]` differs between PYTHONHASHSEED values, so the same update can fail in one server process and pass in the next.

### Real modules replayed (2026-11-16)

The logged transitions were replayed against the real modules, without a server. Each starting tree was cold-loaded through hmr's reactive finder, with an effect reading `src.server.mcp` and `.app` as the dev server does. Every changed file was then overwritten with its new version, and the changed paths went to `on_changes` as one set. Each run is an independent process with its own random set order.

- hmr 0.7.6.3, 8c9d97a → 9ada650 (#58): 4 of 8 runs converged. The other 4 raised the logged `ImportError: cannot import name 'DECOMPOSITION'`, and `_stage_guidance.py`, `epic.py` and other changed modules stayed stale.
- hmr 0.7.6.3, f2e095f → c6c1af2: 1 of 8 runs converged. The failures were `AttributeError: 'FieldSpec' object has no attribute 'fixed'`, `TypeError: _prose() got an unexpected keyword argument 'fixed'`, `TypeError: list_cmds() got an unexpected keyword argument 'editable'` and `ValueError: Invalid page-type declarations`.

### Cause

The cause is in hmr's change propagation (`reactivity.hmr.core.BaseReloader.on_changes` and `reactivity.primitives`). hmr 0.7.6.3 is the latest release.

1. `on_changes` walks the changed files as a set and calls `load.invalidate()` on each in turn. `Derived.trigger()` re-executes a module that something downstream reads at once, before the rest of the batch has been marked dirty. hmr does pull a dirty module fresh when one of its names is read (`Name.get` runs `_sync_dirty_deps`). But a sibling from the same change is not dirty yet, so the importer reads its old namespace.
2. The same thing happens one level down. Inside the reload's batch, `notify` only queues the unchanged dependents. `Batch.flush` then triggers each one once, in set order, so a module such as server.py can run before an unchanged module it reads, such as a page-type module building `FieldSpec` instances, has re-run.
3. The whole loop sits under one `ErrorFilter`, and `Batch.flush` has no per-computation guard, so the first exception ends the batch. The remaining changed modules and queued dependents are never re-executed. Their old code keeps serving until a cold restart, and a later change to any other file does not bring them back.

### Upstream hmr main evaluated (2026-11-16, commit 2e209f7)

Upstream `main` has newer reactivity primitives: `Batch.flush` marks queued dependents dirty before running them, `Derived.notify` marks subscribers dirty, and `_sync_dirty_deps` recurses. `BaseReloader.on_changes` is unchanged. Results against the same harness:

- Synthetic packages: the field shape converges in both orders. The import shape still fails importer-first.
- 8c9d97a → 9ada650 (#58): 0 of 8 runs converged. Some raised the same `DECOMPOSITION` ImportError. The rest left an invalid registry, for example "architecture: the status machine could not be built: There are unreachable states. The statemachine graph should have a single component. Disconnected states: ['current']", and the same for decision-record, feature-brief and feature-spec.
- f2e095f → 3f4e965: the reload does not finish. A stack dump after 20 s shows it deep in recursive `_sync_dirty_deps` calls from `on_changes` → `invalidate`. The recursion guards only the current path and does not remember nodes it has already synced, so shared dependencies are walked again and again.
- A cold start of the real server takes about 20 s on main, against about 10.6 s on 0.7.6.3.

Upgrading to upstream main is not a fix.

### Reporter's suggested fix, evaluated

The reporter suggested a forced settle delay of about 100 ms before any reload. That does not address the cause. Every reproduced failure happens with all files already fully on disk. A delay only merges writes that would otherwise arrive as separate watcher batches (watchfiles `step=50`), and separate batches already recover by themselves, as above. Merging them puts more of an update into the single, order-dependent batch that fails. The fix has to make one batch converge whatever order it arrives in, which means changing how the dev server propagates a multi-module reload.

document:mwjaoeow-2ab6d5.title: Evaluation: replace hmr with a debounced full reload of every module

inlines.text: Verdict: small-to-medium effort, low risk, and it fixes the open HMR bug's cause. One file is rewritten (src/hmr_server.py), three get small edits, the hmr dependency goes, and about eight tests are replaced or added. Replaying the two logged transitions where hmr failed most often, a full reload ended identical to a cold start in 16 of 16 runs, including the worst case of one file per batch.
What the full reload does
On each watcher batch, after a quiet window, the dev server refreshes browsers for any change under src/, and for a change to a

file it first re-imports the whole package: snapshot every src module in sys.modules, drop all of them except a small keep set, and import src.server again from disk. On success it swaps the new mcp and app in, exactly as the current mount swap does. On failure it puts the snapshot back, so the last good module set keeps serving whole, and reports the error.
The replay harness below ran the same purge, import and restore logic, without the keep-unless-changed set and the pyc step.
Why this removes the bug's cause:

items.text: No set-ordered propagation. Python's import system runs each module depth-first from what is on disk, so an importer can never read a sibling's old namespace. Causes 1 and 2 on the bug report (on_changes walking a set, Batch.flush triggering dependents in set order) have nothing to act on.

No half-applied batch. The swap happens only after src.server imported cleanly, and a failure restores the whole previous set. Cause 3 (the first exception ends the batch and leaves stale modules serving) cannot happen.

Self-healing. Every reload is a fresh import of the whole tree, so the state after the last batch is always a cold import of the final tree. A batch that saw a half-written checkout fails, rolls back, and the next batch heals it. The delay becomes an optimisation, not a correctness requirement - the opposite of the settle-delay idea against hmr.

inlines.text: Measured (2026-11-16, main checkout, Python 3.14.6)

rows.text: Re-import of all 38 src modules, third-party cached
Cold start: third-party imports / src modules
validate_registry / git remote lookup per reload
4/4 seeds identical to a cold start
8c9d97a -> 9ada650, one file per batch, random order
4/4 identical; 13 intermediate ImportError DECOMPOSITION, each rolled back
f2e095f -> c6c1af2, whole update in one batch
f2e095f -> c6c1af2, one file per batch, random order
4/4 identical; 15 intermediate failures (FieldSpec.fixed, _prose() 'fixed', list_cmds() 'editable'), each rolled back

inlines.text: Identical means the same describe_page_type fingerprint for all 12 page types, the same MCP tool list, and declaration_errors() returning None, compared with a fresh cold start of the target tree. Harness: each tree extracted with git archive, the changed src files overwritten in place, then src modules purged and src.server re-imported in the same process, PYTHONHASHSEED 1-4. The one-file-per-batch runs are the worst case of a delay that is far too short.
A suitable delay
hmr runs watchfiles awatch with its defaults:
ms of quiet before a batch is yielded, capped at
ms. Recommended:

with the default cap, so a git checkout or pull lands as one batch. A save then takes about 0.3 s of quiet plus 0.45 s of re-import, under a second end to end. Because a full reload heals itself, a window that turns out too short costs one extra reload and one transient logged error, never a stuck server.
What changes, file by file

rows.text: Replace the reactive core - the Reloader(AsyncReloader) subclass, the derived/async_effect handles, the pre/post reload hooks and _LoggingErrorFilter - with an awatch loop, reload_all and an explicit swap step. The proxy, _mount, connection capture, _notify_list_changed and fastapi_dispatch stay as they are.
Drop the on_dispose import and the _stop_for_reload block. The reloader awaits the old module's stop_scheduler() before the swap and calls the new module's start_scheduler(STORE) after it.
No edit. They go in the keep-unless-changed set, so page_events keeps its entries and the 'armed' entry in hmr_debug.log still marks a cold start.
hmr out, watchfiles in as a direct dependency. watchfiles 1.3.0 is already locked through fastapi[standard], so no new package arrives.

Replace the 5 _LoggingErrorFilter tests. Add the bug's regression tests on a temp package: importer-first and exporter-first both converge, the FieldSpec-shaped 4-module package converges, a failing batch restores the previous module set, keep-set modules keep their identity. These run with no server or watcher, which hmr's machinery never allowed. test_hmr_debug.py and the log-path test in test_server.py stay unchanged.
Architecture page 'Web UI, HMR & live reload'

Rewrite the Data model paragraph and the subscriber, event-cache, failed-reload and reporting details. Drop the finder-only-import and active-subscriber invariants, and restate the excludes invariant as the keep set.
No logic change. The README's hot-reload paragraph stays true.

inlines.text: What is lost or changes

items.text: Granularity. Every .py save re-runs all 38 modules, about 0.45 s with the event loop blocked. In practice hmr already re-ran src.server and most of the graph on most edits, because src.server imports nearly everything, and it too re-executes synchronously on the loop.

Module state is rebuilt on every reload unless kept. The keep sets and the explicit cleanup stop/start cover all of it: no other src module holds module-level state except _registry's test-mode stash, which only pytest uses.

Failed-reload behaviour - a decision. Today a failed reload leaves a mixed module set, so both surfaces refuse with a 503 or a tool error naming the declaration errors. A full reload is all-or-nothing, so after a failure the last good build keeps serving consistently and the refusal gate never trips. The developer then sees the failure only in the console and hmr_debug.log. To keep the visible signal, hold the last reload error in hmr_live_refresh (never reloaded) and have the existing gate refuse while it is set, about 10 lines. Recommended.
An edit to hmr_server.py or hmr_live_refresh.py still needs a restart, as today.

inlines.text: Risks

items.text: Stale bytecode. A cached pyc is validated against its source's mtime in whole seconds plus its size, so a same-size rewrite within the same second as the previous compile could load old bytecode. reload_all unlinks the pyc of every changed path first.

Third-party registries re-registered on each import (FastMCP, FastAPI, python-statemachine). Low: hmr already re-executes src.server and the page-type modules on most reloads, so these paths already run repeatedly, and the replay saw no drift.
In-flight requests finish on the old STORE and its locks while the new one starts. Unchanged from today: src.server rebuilds STORE on every hmr reload too.

inlines.text: Alternatives considered

items.text: Upgrade to upstream hmr main: evaluated on the bug report - 0 of 8 runs converge on #58, and it hangs in _sync_dirty_deps on f2e095f -> 3f4e965.

Patch hmr's on_changes to mark every changed module dirty before triggering any: fixes only the first of the three causes. Batch.flush ordering and the single ErrorFilter abort remain, and it means maintaining a patch against hmr internals.
Process respawn (uvicorn --reload): drops every MCP session, against the in-process invariant on the architecture page.
A settle delay on top of hmr: evaluated on the bug report - every reproduced failure happens with all files already on disk.

inlines.text: Recommendation

Replace hmr with the debounced full reload, as a feature-brief that resolves this bug report. The cause is the reload design rather than a local defect, which the bug-report guidance routes to a feature brief. Two decisions go into it: how a failed reload shows (refuse with the error until the next good reload - recommended - or keep serving the last good build silently), and the quiet window (300 ms recommended).

feature-brief:mwjazomw-805d3a.title: Replace hmr's reactive reload with a debounced full reload of every module

summary.body: Make the dev server's hot reload converge on what is on disk for any source change, however many files one git operation rewrites and in whatever order the watcher reports them. Today hmr's reactive propagation re-runs changed modules in set order, so a multi-file update intermittently leaves an importer reading a sibling's old namespace and the server stuck on a mixed module set until a cold restart (bug-report:mwj6yk8q-1ce666). The replacement re-imports every src module from disk after a 300 ms quiet window, swaps the reloaded server in only when the whole import succeeds, and otherwise keeps the last good build loaded while both surfaces refuse with the reload error until the next reload that succeeds. MCP sessions and browser tabs stay connected across reloads as they do now, and the process is never respawned. Evaluation with measurements: document:mwjaoeow-2ab6d5.

items.name: src/hmr_server.py
items.text: Effectful shell of the dev server: build_dev_app builds the stable outer Starlette app (Mount /pasta -> FastMCP proxy http_app, Mount / -> fastapi_dispatch) and reloader_lifespan; run_dev_server calls uvicorn.run. The reactive core to replace: Reloader(AsyncReloader) with includes=[src], excludes=[hmr_live_refresh.py] and an on_changes override that refreshes browsers unconditionally; derived current_mcp/current_fastapi over import_module('src.server'); async_effect mcp_reload_effect (stop old mount, mount new, log) and cleanup_reload_effect (stop_scheduler, start_scheduler(STORE)); call_pre/post_reload_hooks; _LoggingErrorFilter(ErrorFilter) logging '[HMR] reload FAILED...' to logger 'uvicorn.error'. Kept as is: _capture_connections, _notify_list_changed, _mount, serve_mcp's mount_lock/stop/finish pattern, fastapi_dispatch's identity-change log line. hmr's watcher is awatch(src) with watchfiles defaults (step=50, debounce=1600). The new purge-set decision (which src modules to drop given the changed paths) is pure; importing, swapping and watching are effects.

items.name: src/hmr_live_refresh.py
items.text: The one module never reloaded: imports only fastapi.WebSocket, holds the process-wide ws_reloader (ReloaderConnectionManager of live browser sockets; refresh() sends {"refresh": 1}). Imported by both src.server and src.hmr_server, so it is where state that must outlive a reload and be readable from the reloaded server can live - the last reload failure. Effects: WebSocket sends.

items.name: src/server.py (declaration quarantine)
items.text: Reloaded module, effectful surface. Module body runs validate_registry() first (a cold start fails outright) and builds STORE, mcp, app, templates, source_link. Two per-request gates ask declaration_errors(): the HTTP middleware refuse_invalid_declarations (503 via error.html, /static exempt, registered ahead of add_no_cache_headers) and the fastmcp Middleware _RefuseInvalidDeclarations.on_call_tool (ToolError naming the errors and LOG_PATH from src._hmr_debug). Both will also have to refuse on a recorded reload failure. Ends with `from . import _hmr_debug`.

items.name: src/cleanup.py
items.text: Reloaded module owning one asyncio task (_task). start_scheduler(store) is idempotent and stop_scheduler() awaits cancellation; both lifespans call them. Imports `from reactivity.hmr.hooks import on_dispose` at module top and registers _stop_for_reload under suppress(KeyError) - that import breaks once hmr is uninstalled. Classification is pure; the scheduler is an effect (clock, task).

items.name: src/event_cache.py
items.text: Pure in-memory structure with module-level state: page_events = EventCache() and _enabled. Imports nothing from src, which is what keeps it across an hmr reload today. A full reload would rebuild it each time unless the module is kept when its own file did not change. conftest's event-cache fixture monkeypatches server.page_events.

items.name: src/_hmr_debug.py
items.text: Import-time effects only: tees sys.excepthook, sys.unraisablehook and the running loop's exception handler to hmr_debug.log (LOG_PATH = repo root), idempotent via attributes on sys and the loop, and appends an 'armed' entry on every execution - the bug report reads that entry as a cold-start marker. Imports nothing from src. LOG_PATH is read by server.py's tool refusal and pinned by tests/test_server.py and tests/test_hmr_debug.py.

items.name: pyproject.toml / uv.lock
items.text: dependencies list `"hmr>=0.7.6.3"`; watchfiles 1.3.0 is already in uv.lock as a dependency of fastapi[standard]/uvicorn independent of hmr, so dropping hmr loses no watcher. No code outside hmr_server.py and cleanup.py imports reactivity.

items.text: test_hmr_server.py: 5 tests drive _LoggingErrorFilter (go with it); _mount and connection-capture tests pin fastmcp/mcp internals (stay). The quarantine tests in test_server.py (ToolError match 'page-type declarations', 'setPlatform', LOG_PATH) and test_web.py (503, reloader socket kept, no-cache, floating top link) use conftest's invalid_declarations fixture, which patches _registry.registered_pagetypes - the pattern a reload-failure refusal test follows.
pyproject.toml: requires-python = ">=3.14". Remove `"hmr>=0.7.6.3"`; add watchfiles as a direct dependency at the locked version (watchfiles 1.3.0 in uv.lock).
User decision (2026-11-16): the watcher's quiet window defaults to 300 ms (watchfiles awatch step) before a batch reloads.
User decision (2026-11-16): after a failed reload both surfaces refuse - browser 503, tool call ToolError - naming the reload error, until the next reload that succeeds.

Architecture invariant: one process serves both surfaces and hot reload happens in-process - a source change never respawns the process. MCP sessions survive a reload: old mount torn down, reloaded server mounted, every captured Connection sent tools/resources/prompts list_changed; browser tabs are refreshed over their existing /ws/reloader socket, on a failed reload too.

Architecture invariants: the inner FastAPI app's lifespan never runs under the dev server, so the cleanup sweep starts from reloader_lifespan; a cold start still raises out of validate_registry() and never binds a port; a failed reload is reported at error level through logger 'uvicorn.error', never left as a bare traceback; the traceback still reaches sys.excepthook so _hmr_debug tees it to hmr_debug.log.
Workspace testing guidance: `uv run pytest --testmon` for red/green; trust testmon's deselection.

Project hint (CLAUDE.md): use the word "create" instead of "mint". Delivery (user memory): feature branch pushed to the pasta-dev remote, rebased onto main with no merge commit, PR opened through the github MCP.

src/server.py's quarantine comment and both gates assume a failed reload surfaces as an invalid live registry ('the page types can reload invalid while this module's own re-exec fails'). With an all-or-nothing reload the registry after a failure is the last good one, so declaration_errors() alone never trips. The gates must also check the recorded reload failure; the declaration_errors() check stays, since it is the only check under stdio and pytest.

Both refusal messages say 'The page-type declarations are invalid', and test_server.py matches that text. A reload that fails for another reason (the bug's ImportError) needs its own wording; the declaration wording and its tests stay for the declaration path.

src/cleanup.py imports reactivity.hmr.hooks.on_dispose at module top; it fails to import once hmr is removed, so the hook and _stop_for_reload must go and the reloader takes over stopping the old sweep before a swap.

src/hmr_live_refresh.py's docstring defines it as the browser-socket manager excluded from 'the reactive import finder'. Holding the reload failure there widens its purpose to 'state that outlives a reload'; the alternative is a second never-reloaded module. To settle in the spec.

An earlier worktree branch, worktree-hmr-settle-delay, holds a settle-delay attempt on top of hmr. The bug report's evaluation found a settle delay does not address the cause; this feature supersedes it. Not inspected, per the user's instruction to drop that state.

Found while building step 8: src/_hmr_debug.py's module docstring and its excepthook section comment described hmr's reloader (reactivity.hmr, ErrorFilter swallowing a re-exec error), which the step removed. The spec listed the file as 'no edit'; only those two comment spots were reworded, in the step 8 commit, to describe the dev server handing a failed reload's traceback to sys.excepthook. No code in the file changed.

items.text: After a failed reload, do both surfaces refuse with the reload error until the next reload that succeeds, or keep serving the last good build and report only to the console and hmr_debug.log?
items.answer: Refuse (user, 2026-11-16: 'The failed reload should stay with refusal until the next good reload').

items.text: How long a quiet window does the watcher wait for before reloading a batch?
items.answer: 300 ms (user, 2026-11-16: '300ms is fine as the default').

items.text: Where is the last reload failure held, so that the gates of the restored (last good) src.server can read it?
items.answer: In src/hmr_live_refresh.py, the module that is never reloaded and that both src.server and src.hmr_server already import.

items.text: Which src modules survive a reload instead of being re-imported?
items.answer: Always: src.hmr_server and src.hmr_live_refresh. Unless their own file changed: src.event_cache and src._hmr_debug. Every other loaded src module, the src package included, is re-imported.

items.text: What is left in sys.modules when the re-import fails part-way?
items.answer: Exactly the module set loaded before the reload: every src entry is removed and the snapshot is put back, so nothing half-imported can be picked up by a lazy import in the last good code.

items.text: Which file changes re-import the package, and which only refresh browsers?
items.answer: A batch with any .py path re-imports, then refreshes browsers. A batch with no .py path (templates, static, css) only refreshes browsers, as today.

items.text: Is the quiet window configurable at run time (CLI flag or environment variable), or a module constant?
items.answer: A module constant, QUIET_WINDOW_MS = 300 in src/hmr_server.py. No flag or variable was asked for.

# Why the last hot reload failed, until one succeeds. Both refusal gates read it, and they may be
# the gates of the build a failed reload rolled back to, so it lives here rather than in either.
_reload_failure: str | None = None


def set_reload_failure(summary: str | None) -> None:
    """Record why the last reload failed, or clear it once a reload succeeds."""
    global _reload_failure
    _reload_failure = summary


def reload_failure() -> str | None:
    """Why the last reload failed, while no reload has succeeded since; otherwise None."""
    return _reload_failure

from src.hmr_live_refresh import reload_failure, set_reload_failure


def test_a_recorded_reload_failure_holds_until_cleared():
    assert reload_failure() is None
    set_reload_failure("ImportError: boom")
    try:
        assert reload_failure() == "ImportError: boom"
    finally:
        set_reload_failure(None)
    assert reload_failure() is None

def _report_reload_failure(error: BaseException) -> None:
    """Say on the dev console what a failed reload cost, and hand its traceback to sys.excepthook,
    which tees it to the reload log."""
    logger.error(
        "[HMR] reload FAILED - the edit did not take; the build loaded before it stays loaded " +
        "and both surfaces refuse until a reload succeeds:\n%s", reload_failure_summary(error))
    sys.excepthook(type(error), error, error.__traceback__)

# Names deliberately differ from _LoggingErrorFilter's tests, which stay in this module until step 8.
from src.hmr_server import _report_reload_failure


@pytest.fixture
def report(caplog, monkeypatch):
    """Report a reload failure, capturing the console text and what reached sys.excepthook."""
    hooked: list[BaseException] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "excepthook", lambda _type, value, _tb: hooked.append(value))

    def _run(error: BaseException):
        with caplog.at_level(logging.ERROR, logger="uvicorn.error"):
            _report_reload_failure(error)
        return caplog.text, hooked
    return _run


def test_a_failed_reload_reaches_the_console_as_an_error(report):
    text, _ = report(ImportError("cannot import name 'NEW'"))
    assert "ERROR" in text
    assert "[HMR]" in text


def test_a_failed_reload_report_names_its_error(report):
    text, _ = report(ValueError("Invalid page-type declarations:\n- bug-report: bad setter"))
    assert "Invalid page-type declarations" in text
    assert "bad setter" in text


def test_a_failed_reload_report_states_what_it_cost(report):
    text, _ = report(ValueError("boom"))
    assert "did not take" in text
    assert "refuse" in text


def test_the_traceback_is_handed_to_the_excepthook_that_tees_the_reload_log(report):
    error = ValueError("boom")
    _, hooked = report(error)
    assert hooked == [error]

# inside build_dev_app, replacing everything from the derived handles down to fastapi_dispatch
    # (serve_mcp and mcp_asgi stay as they are)

    # The src.server module serving now; a reload that imports cleanly replaces it.
    serving: ModuleType | None = None
    mount_lock = Lock()
    task_group: TaskGroup | None = None
    stop_event: Event | None = None
    finish_event: Event | None = None
    watch_stop = Event()

    async def swap_in(server: ModuleType) -> None:
        """Serve `server`: mount its tools in place of the previous ones and route to its app."""
        nonlocal serving, stop_event, finish_event
        is_reload = stop_event is not None and finish_event is not None
        if stop_event is not None and finish_event is not None:
            stop_event.set()
            _ = await finish_event.wait()
        if is_reload:
            logger.info("[HMR] FastMCP server reloaded (src.server.mcp)")
        serving = server
        stop_event, finish_event = Event(), Event()
        assert task_group is not None
        _ = task_group.create_task(serve_mcp(server.mcp, stop_event, finish_event))

    async def reload(changed: frozenset[str]) -> None:
        """Re-import the package and serve the result, or keep the last good build and refuse."""
        assert serving is not None
        previous = serving
        error = reimport(SCOPE, changed)
        if error is not None:
            set_reload_failure(reload_failure_summary(error))
            _report_reload_failure(error)
            return
        server = sys.modules[SCOPE.entry]
        await previous.cleanup.stop_scheduler()
        await swap_in(server)
        server.cleanup.start_scheduler(server.STORE)
        set_reload_failure(None)

    async def watch() -> None:
        # Browsers are refreshed after every batch, a failed reload included: what a tab should land
        # on then is the refusal, and since that page keeps the socket it is also how the tab recovers.
        async for changes in awatch(_PACKAGE_DIR, step=QUIET_WINDOW_MS, stop_event=watch_stop):
            changed = frozenset(_normalise(path) for _, path in changes)
            if needs_reimport(changed):
                try:
                    await reload(changed)
                except Exception as error:  # a failed swap must not end the watcher
                    set_reload_failure(reload_failure_summary(error))
                    _report_reload_failure(error)
            await ws_reloader.refresh()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def reloader_lifespan(_app: Starlette):
        nonlocal task_group
        restore_connection_init = _capture_connections()
        async with TaskGroup() as tg:
            task_group = tg
            # A cold start that cannot import raises out of here, before uvicorn binds the port.
            server = import_module(SCOPE.entry)
            await swap_in(server)
            server.cleanup.start_scheduler(server.STORE)
            watch_task = tg.create_task(watch())
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                watch_stop.set()
                if serving is not None:
                    await serving.cleanup.stop_scheduler()
                if stop_event is not None:
                    stop_event.set()
                _ = watch_task.cancel()
                restore_connection_init()

    last_fastapi_app: object = None

    async def fastapi_dispatch(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send):
        # Forward every non-/pasta/mcp request (incl. the /ws/reloader websocket) to the app of the
        # build serving now.
        nonlocal last_fastapi_app
        assert serving is not None
        fastapi_app = serving.app
        # (the existing identity-change log and the forward stay exactly as they are)

import asyncio, json, sys, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from fastmcp import Client
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError

S = Path(sys.argv[1]); LOG = S / "server.log"
GUIDE, EPIC, CSS = S / "src/pagetypes/_stage_guidance.py", S / "src/pagetypes/epic.py", S / "src/static/styles.css"

def status() -> tuple[int, str]:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:8765/") as r:
            return r.status, r.read().decode()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.read().decode()

def log_since(mark: int) -> str:
    return LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[mark:]

def append(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    path.write_text(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + text, encoding="utf-8")

async def main():
    for _ in range(60):  # wait for the cold start
        try:
            if status()[0] == 200: break
        except OSError: time.sleep(1)
    async with Client("http://localhost:8765/pasta/mcp") as mcp:  # one session for the whole run
        await mcp.call_tool("listWorkspaces", {})
        # (a) exporter and importer in one burst: one clean reload
        mark = len(LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        append(GUIDE, '\nSMOKE_NEW = "x"\n'); append(EPIC, "\nfrom ._stage_guidance import SMOKE_NEW\n")
        time.sleep(3)
        out = log_since(mark)
        assert "FastMCP server reloaded" in out and "reload FAILED" not in out, out
        assert status()[0] == 200
        await mcp.call_tool("listWorkspaces", {})
        # (b) importer alone: the reload fails, both surfaces refuse naming the error
        mark = len(LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        append(EPIC, "\nfrom ._stage_guidance import SMOKE_LATE\n")
        time.sleep(3)
        assert "reload FAILED" in log_since(mark)
        code, body = status()
        assert code == 503 and "SMOKE_LATE" in body, (code, body[:300])
        try:
            await mcp.call_tool("listWorkspaces", {})
            raise AssertionError("tool call was not refused")
        except ToolError as e:
            assert "last hot reload failed" in str(e) and "SMOKE_LATE" in str(e), str(e)
        # (c) the exporter arrives: the next reload recovers, on the same session
        append(GUIDE, '\nSMOKE_LATE = "y"\n')
        time.sleep(3)
        assert status()[0] == 200
        await mcp.call_tool("listWorkspaces", {})
        # (d) a CSS edit refreshes browsers without re-importing
        mark = len(LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        append(CSS, "\n/* smoke */\n")
        time.sleep(3)
        assert "server reloaded" not in log_since(mark)
    print("SMOKE OK")

asyncio.run(main())

overview.body: Covers the dev server's hot reload (src/hmr_server.py) and what it touches: hmr's reactive propagation is replaced by a full re-import of the src package after a 300 ms quiet window, all-or-nothing, with the last good build kept loaded on failure while both surfaces refuse with the reload error until a reload succeeds. The cleanup sweep's hmr hook goes, the failure state lives in src/hmr_live_refresh.py, both refusal gates in src/server.py learn the new refusal, and the hmr dependency is swapped for watchfiles. Deliberately left out: removing the page-type declaration quarantine (it stays as is), renaming the hmr_* modules or hmr_debug.log, any run-time configuration of the window, the stdio transport (which has no reload), and the architecture pages, which are reconciled at ship.

body.text: Behaviour

The watcher yields a batch once src/ has been quiet for 300 ms (capped by watchfiles' 1600 ms debounce). A batch containing any .py path re-imports the package, then refreshes browsers; a batch with no .py path only refreshes browsers. A re-import drops every loaded src module except the kept ones and imports src.server again from disk. When that import succeeds the reloaded mcp is mounted in place of the old one (clients are sent list_changed), the cleanup sweep moves to the new module and STORE, fastapi_dispatch starts forwarding to the new app, and any recorded failure is cleared. When it raises, sys.modules is put back exactly as it was, the old mount, app and sweep stay untouched, the failure is recorded and reported, and from then on every browser request answers 503 and every tool call raises ToolError, both naming the error, until a later reload succeeds. Browsers are refreshed after every batch, failed or not, so a tab lands on the refusal and leaves it on its own. The process never respawns; a cold start whose import raises still fails out of the lifespan before uvicorn binds the port.
Pure logic (src/hmr_server.py)

body.source:
TARGET_MODULE = "src.server"  # unchanged
QUIET_WINDOW_MS = 300        # watchfiles awatch step: quiet time before a batch is yielded


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReloadScope:
    """The package a reload re-imports, the module it imports through, and what it leaves loaded."""
    package: str
    entry: str
    always_kept: frozenset[str]
    kept_unless_changed: frozenset[str]


SCOPE = ReloadScope(
    package="src",
    entry=TARGET_MODULE,
    always_kept=frozenset({"src.hmr_server", "src.hmr_live_refresh"}),
    kept_unless_changed=frozenset({"src.event_cache", "src._hmr_debug"}),
)


def modules_to_drop(scope: ReloadScope, loaded: Mapping[str, str | None],
                    changed: AbstractSet[str]) -> list[str]:
    """The loaded modules a reload re-imports, sorted by name.

    `loaded` maps module names to their normalised file path (None when a module has no file);
    `changed` holds the batch's normalised paths. A name in the package (the package itself or
    any `package.` descendant) is dropped unless it is always kept, or kept unless changed and
    its path is not in `changed`. Names outside the package are never returned."""


def needs_reimport(changed: AbstractSet[str]) -> bool:
    """Whether a batch touches Python source: any path ending in `.py`."""


def reload_failure_summary(error: BaseException) -> str:
    """The exception's own lines without the traceback, stripped:
    "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(error)).strip(). Both refusals and the log line
    quote this."""

body.text: Re-import with rollback (src/hmr_server.py, effectful)

body.source:
def _normalise(path: str) -> str:
    """os.path.normcase(str(Path(path).resolve())) - how watcher paths and module __file__s are
    made comparable on Windows."""


def reimport(scope: ReloadScope, changed: AbstractSet[str]) -> Exception | None:
    """Re-import scope.entry from disk with every droppable module dropped first.

    1. snapshot = every sys.modules entry in the package
    2. loaded = {name: _normalise(module.__file__) or None}; drop modules_to_drop(scope, loaded, changed)
    3. for each changed path ending in .py: unlink importlib.util.cache_from_source(path), missing_ok
    4. importlib.invalidate_caches(); importlib.import_module(scope.entry)
    5. on Exception: delete every package entry from sys.modules, sys.modules.update(snapshot),
       return the exception. BaseException (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit) propagates.
    Returns None on success, leaving the new modules in sys.modules."""

body.text: Failure state (src/hmr_live_refresh.py, never reloaded)
The module docstring is widened from the browser-socket manager to the dev server's state that has to outlive a reload: the live sockets and the last reload failure.
Dev server loop (build_dev_app, effectful)

Closure state: serving (the src.server module object in use, None before startup), mount_lock, task_group, stop_event and finish_event of the live mount, and watch_stop (asyncio.Event). serve_mcp, _mount, _capture_connections and _notify_list_changed are unchanged.

body.source:
async def swap_in(server: ModuleType) -> None:
    # stop the previous mount (stop_event.set(); await finish_event.wait()) when there is one,
    # create task serve_mcp(server.mcp, new stop, new finish), set serving = server, and log
    # "[HMR] FastMCP server reloaded (src.server.mcp)" when it replaced a previous mount.

async def reload(changed: frozenset[str]) -> None:
    previous = serving
    error = reimport(SCOPE, changed)
    if error is None:
        server = sys.modules[SCOPE.entry]
        await previous.cleanup.stop_scheduler()
        await swap_in(server)
        server.cleanup.start_scheduler(server.STORE)
        set_reload_failure(None)
    else:
        set_reload_failure(reload_failure_summary(error))
        _report_reload_failure(error)

async def watch() -> None:
    async for changes in awatch(_PACKAGE_DIR, step=QUIET_WINDOW_MS, stop_event=watch_stop):
        changed = frozenset(_normalise(path) for _, path in changes)
        if needs_reimport(changed):
            try:
                await reload(changed)
            except Exception as error:  # a swap step failing must not end the watcher
                set_reload_failure(reload_failure_summary(error))
                _report_reload_failure(error)
        await ws_reloader.refresh()

@asynccontextmanager
async def reloader_lifespan(_app):
    restore_connection_init = _capture_connections()
    async with TaskGroup() as tg:
        task_group = tg
        server = import_module(SCOPE.entry)  # cold start: raises out, the port is never bound
        await swap_in(server)
        server.cleanup.start_scheduler(server.STORE)
        watch_task = tg.create_task(watch())
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            watch_stop.set()
            await serving.cleanup.stop_scheduler()
            stop_event.set()
            watch_task.cancel()
            restore_connection_init()

async def fastapi_dispatch(scope, receive, send):
    # forwards to serving.app; the identity-change "[HMR] FastAPI app reloaded" log is unchanged

def _report_reload_failure(error: BaseException) -> None:
    logger.error("[HMR] reload FAILED - the edit did not take; the build loaded before it stays " +
                 "loaded and both surfaces refuse until a reload succeeds:\n%s",
                 reload_failure_summary(error))
    sys.excepthook(type(error), error, error.__traceback__)  # tees the traceback to hmr_debug.log

body.text: Removed from src/hmr_server.py: the reactivity imports, _LoggingErrorFilter, the derived current_mcp/current_fastapi, mcp_reload_effect, cleanup_reload_effect, the Reloader subclass, call_pre_reload_hooks/call_post_reload_hooks and _LIVE_REFRESH_FILE. The module docstring describes the full reload instead of hmr's reactive modules. reimport runs synchronously on the event loop for about 0.45 s; batches are handled one at a time because the async for awaits each before taking the next.
Refusal gates (src/server.py)
Cleanup sweep (src/cleanup.py)

Delete the reactivity.hmr.hooks import, the '# --- hot reload' section with _stop_for_reload, and its on_dispose registration. start_scheduler and stop_scheduler are unchanged. The module docstring's sentence on the hot-reload hook becomes: the dev server stops the sweep on the old module before a reload swaps it out and starts it on the new one.
Dependencies
pyproject.toml: remove "hmr>=0.7.6.3"; add "watchfiles>=1.3.0" in alphabetical position (after "sphinxcontrib-mermaid>=2.1.1"); then uv lock, which drops hmr and keeps watchfiles 1.3.0.
Error paths

Import raises Exception: rolled back, failure recorded and reported, browsers refreshed onto the 503. A later batch whose import succeeds clears it. A swap step raises after a clean import: caught in watch, recorded and reported like an import failure, and the watcher keeps going; the next successful reload swaps fully. KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit during import: propagates and shuts the server down. Cold-start import raises: out of reloader_lifespan, uvicorn reports startup failure and never binds. A deleted .py file: its pyc unlink is a no-op and the import either succeeds without it or fails and rolls back. A new .py file: importable after invalidate_caches. An edit to src/hmr_server.py or src/hmr_live_refresh.py re-imports the rest but takes effect only after a restart, as today.

Replace hmr with a full re-import of the src package (user decision). Rejected: upgrading to upstream hmr main (0/8 converge on #58 and it hangs in _sync_dirty_deps on f2e095f -> 3f4e965); patching on_changes to mark every changed module dirty first (fixes only the first of three causes and means carrying a patch against hmr internals); uvicorn --reload process respawn (drops every MCP session, against the in-process invariant); a settle delay on hmr (every reproduced failure had all files on disk). Why: the full reload ended identical to a cold start in 16/16 replays of the logged transitions, including one file per batch, at about 0.45 s per reload.

After a failed reload both surfaces refuse, naming the error, until a reload succeeds (user decision). Rejected: keep serving the last good build and report only to the console and hmr_debug.log - an agent calling tools never sees the console, so it would keep working against code the developer believes was replaced. The refusal reuses the existing gates and error template rather than a new surface.

A 300 ms quiet window (user decision), passed as watchfiles awatch step, with the default 1600 ms debounce cap. Rejected: hmr's 50 ms default, which splits a git checkout into several batches and so several reloads with transient failures. Correctness does not depend on the window: a batch that sees a half-written tree rolls back and the next batch heals it.

The last reload failure lives in src/hmr_live_refresh.py behind set_reload_failure / reload_failure. Rejected: a new never-reloaded module, which would need a second always-kept entry and a second import in server.py for one variable; a module global in src/server.py or src/hmr_server.py, since server.py is the module a failed reload rolls back to and hmr_server cannot be imported by server.py without pinning the reload set. hmr_live_refresh is already the one module both sides import that never reloads; its docstring is widened to say so.

Always kept: src.hmr_server (the reloader itself) and src.hmr_live_refresh (live sockets, failure state). Kept unless their own file changed: src.event_cache (page_events survives a reload as it does today) and src._hmr_debug (its 'armed' entry keeps marking a cold start). Rejected: re-importing those two every time (an extra full guidance echo per page per reload, and an 'armed' line per reload); keeping them always (an edit to either would silently take nothing until a restart, which the architecture page already rejected for the event cache).

A failed re-import restores the exact module set loaded before it: every package entry removed, the snapshot put back. Rejected: leaving the partial new modules in sys.modules, where a lazy import inside the last good code (server.py imports _hmr_debug's LOG_PATH at call time; _registry imports testtypes at call time) would pick up a half-imported module and mix builds again.

A batch with any .py path re-imports, then refreshes browsers; a batch with none only refreshes browsers, which keeps today's live refresh for template, CSS and static edits. Rejected: re-importing on every change (0.45 s of blocked loop for an edit Python never reads). The pyc of each changed .py path is unlinked before the import, because bytecode is validated by source mtime in whole seconds plus size and a same-size rewrite within one second could otherwise load stale code; sys.dont_write_bytecode was rejected because it does not stop reading a stale pyc already on disk.
QUIET_WINDOW_MS = 300 is a module constant in src/hmr_server.py. Rejected: a main.py flag or environment variable - nobody asked to vary it, and changing the constant is a one-line edit.

bug-report:mwjb2nuq-8f9cfc.title: The Workspace link in the nav tree does not keep the archived= query parameter

report.component: Web UI, HMR & live reload (page view nav sidebar: src/templates/_nav.html, rendered by route_page in src/server.py)
report.platform: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045; Python 3.14.6 via uv 0.11.29; FastAPI 0.162.0 / Starlette 1.10.0 / Jinja2 3.1.6; observed with curl 8.23.0 against the running dev server at http://127.0.0.1:8000 (browser-independent: the wrong href is in the served HTML)

summary.body: In the web UI, the Workspace link at the top of the nav tree does not carry the archived= query parameter, so following it from a view with archived pages shown (?archived=true) loses that setting and returns to the live-only view, while the other nav tree links keep it.

steps.text: Starting state: the pasta dev server running at http://127.0.0.1:8000 (main.py, default HTTP mode) serving workspace ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6, which has at least one page (e.g. bug-report:mwjb2nuq-8f9cfc).

Open a page view with archived pages shown: GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/page/bug-report:mwjb2nuq-8f9cfc?archived=true (for example `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/page/bug-report:mwjb2nuq-8f9cfc?archived=true"`).
In the response, look at the nav sidebar (`<nav id="sidebar">`): the page links in its tree list carry `?archived=true`, and the toggle reads "Hide archived", confirming the archived view is active.

Read the href of the first link in the sidebar, the Workspace link (`Workspace`), and follow it: GET that href (http://127.0.0.1:8000/ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6). The tree view it returns shows a "Show archived" toggle, so it is the live-only view and the archived setting is lost.

expected.body: On a page view requested with `?archived=true`, the Workspace link should carry the same flag, `href="/ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6?archived=true"`, so following it lands on the workspace tree with archived pages still shown (the tree route honours the flag: GET /ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6?archived=true serves the archived view with a "Hide archived" toggle). Without the flag the link stays `/ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6`. Grounding: every other link in the same nav tree already keeps the flag, by documented and tested contract. `render_workspace_links` in src/render.py documents "`show_archived=True` lists links with `?archived=true` query parameter", and tests/test_render.py pins it ("show_archived flows onto the link as ?archived=true; default omits it", asserting `[Page title](/ws:demo/page/test-fields:abc?archived=true)`). The served sidebar in the repro shows exactly that, e.g. `Documentation`. The Web UI, HMR & live reload architecture page records the same intent for the page view: route_page threads the page view archived state onto its links "so an inline reference keeps the archived view when a reader follows it".

observed.body:
The sidebar of GET /ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/page/bug-report:mwjb2nuq-8f9cfc?archived=true (HTTP 200) is served as: ```html
Workspace Hide archived
  • Documentation ``` The Workspace href is `/ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6` with no `?archived=true`, while the tree links below it carry it. Following that href returns the live-only tree, whose toggle is `Show archived`. Reproduces every time: the output is deterministic for any page view requested with `?archived=true`.
