bug-report:mwjolnfp-190524.title: An unwanted "connection open" line is logged every time a websocket connection is accepted

report.component: Web UI, HMR & live reload - the HMR dev server (src/hmr_server.py) and its /ws/reloader WebSocket (src/hmr_live_refresh.py)
report.platform: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, Python 3.14.6, uvicorn 0.54.0 (auto-selected websockets-sansio WebSocket implementation), websockets 17.4, starlette 1.10.0, fastapi 0.162.0

summary.body: Every time the HTTP dev server accepts a WebSocket connection (each browser tab opening /ws/reloader), the console prints an extra bare `INFO:     connection open` line, naming neither client nor path, directly after uvicorn's own `"WebSocket /ws/reloader" [accepted]` line for the same connection.

steps.text: Start from a checkout of main at cbc395e with dependencies installed (`uv sync`) and nothing listening on port 8767.
Start the HTTP dev server: `uv run python main.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8767`, and wait for its console to print `Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8767 (Press CTRL+C to quit)`.

From a second terminal in the same checkout, open one WebSocket to the live-reload endpoint: `uv run python -c "import asyncio, websockets; asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(websockets.connect('ws://127.0.0.1:8767/ws/reloader'), 5))"`. (Opening any page such as http://127.0.0.1:8767/ in a browser does the same, since every served page connects to /ws/reloader.)
Read the dev server's console from step 2: the last two lines are uvicorn's accept line followed by a bare `INFO:     connection open`.

expected.body:
An accepted WebSocket is logged once, by uvicorn's own access-style line, which names the client and the path: `INFO:     127.0.0.1:<port> - "WebSocket /ws/reloader" [accepted]`. uvicorn emits that line on `websocket.accept` in its WebSocket protocol (uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py, the `[accepted]` info call), so the accept is already recorded with full context.

The dev server treats this console, the `uvicorn.error` logger, as its status log. src/hmr_server.py routes the `[HMR]` reload notifications through it on purpose so they land next to uvicorn's own lines. The Web UI, HMR & live reload architecture page also holds that a failed reload must stand out there rather than sit buried among INFO lines. A second, context-free line for the same accept carries nothing the access line lacks and adds one line of noise per open tab and per hot reload (every reload refreshes each tab, which reconnects).

observed.body:
Console of the dev server after one client connects (step 4), verbatim:

```
INFO:     Started server process [18244]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     [cleanup] scheduled hourly at :05 UTC
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8767 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
INFO:     127.0.0.1:58681 - "WebSocket /ws/reloader" [accepted]
INFO:     connection open
```

It reproduces every time: 4 of 4 runs, each accept followed by exactly one `INFO:     connection open`. The line carries no client address, path or connection id, so with several tabs open there is no telling which connection it belongs to. When the client disconnected, no matching `connection closed` line appeared within 3 seconds. The text `connection open` occurs nowhere in the repository's own source (src/, main.py, tests/), which suggests a line built into a dependency rather than one the project writes.

fixCommits.message: Keep websockets' connection open/closed lines off the dev console
Keep websockets' connection open/closed lines off the dev console (#66)

epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b.title: Timeline replay of a workspace: a scrubbable player linked to a graph of everything in it at each moment

notice.body:
This epic is the controller's page. Only the controlling agent - the session that created this
epic and dispatches its agents - runs commands on it. Research, design and every build are done
by dispatched agents: each is handed one agent-plan page, a child of this epic whose page id is
the agent's id, works from that page, reports back onto it, and writes only that page and the
pages it links to with works-on - this epic's solution-investigation or solution-design pages,
or the feature-briefs it builds with their child pages. It never edits this epic or another
agent's page. The controller reads the investigation and design pages' digests rather than the
whole pages, and records here what an agent raises: addFinding or editFinding for a problem, and
editContract for a shared contract it corrected.

summary.body: A timeline view in the web UI that replays how a workspace came to be: when each page was created, how it moved through its statuses, how it was nested and linked, the activity on it, and when it shipped or was archived. Two linked interactive surfaces carry it - a player whose timeline can be scrubbed, played and paused, and a graph of the workspace as it stood at the selected moment, where hovering a node shows the page's title and status. Feature pages are its heart, but for the most WOW everything pasta records that can be visualized is shown. It is worth building because the wiki today shows only where work stands now, not how it got there - and it has to wow whoever watches it.

framing.why: In the user's words: "It is worth building because the wiki today shows only where work stands now, not how it got there." And: "The WOW factor is the important part for the user." The user framed delivery as two halves that both have to land: "Delivering it needs page history recorded over time and served to the web UI as replayable data, AND a player and graph that render it." Asked whether the graph should go beyond feature pages, the user said: "To get the maximum WOW out of using pasta, everything that is possible to visualize should be shown."

outcomes.text: From the web UI, a user can open a timeline view for a workspace and replay how its feature pages came and went: when each feature page was created, every status it moved through, and when it shipped or was archived.
The player's timeline can be scrubbed to any moment, played and paused.

The view shows the workspace exactly as it stood at the player's selected moment - only the pages that existed then, each in the status it had then - and it follows the playhead as it plays or is scrubbed.
Hovering a node in the view shows that page's title and its status at the selected moment.
The replay is driven by page history recorded over time and served to the web UI as replayable data - not reconstructed from the pages' current state.
The view has a WOW factor: someone watching a replay of the pasta workspace for the first time finds it visually striking, and that matters more than any other quality of this epic.

The visual is 2D and incorporates time: the pages are drawn as a timeline of nodes laid out along time, not as a force-directed node graph. In the user's words: "2D definitely but the visual has to incorporate time ... The force node graph should be replaced with a timeline of nodes."

The view is the Metro layout: a page branches off its parent's track when it is created and merges back when it finishes. It plays at 0.25 days per second by default and speeds through stretches where no nodes are near the playhead. In the user's words: "I agree with the Metro display, at 0.25 days/second speed ... I appreciate the exta speedup when no nods are near the current time - it works great."

Each change is drawn cleanly and appears exactly when the playhead reaches it, with no animated circles - no rings that expand and fade, no nodes that pop in. In the user's words: "For the visual, remove the animated circles, they are slightly buggy in when they appear."
Playing and scrubbing stay smooth - no visible stutter or blank frames - on a workspace the size of pasta's own, in a current desktop browser.

Everything about the workspace's history that can be visualized is shown, not only feature pages - in the user's words: "To get the maximum WOW out of using pasta, everything that is possible to visualize should be shown."

"Everything" covers at least: every page of every type (feature-briefs, epics, simple-changes, bug reports, architecture and document pages, decision records, toc pages, and the child pages under them such as plans, specs, investigations and agent-plans); every status each page moved through; every parent-child nesting and typed reference link as it was made and removed; renames, reparents, archives and unarchives; and the finer-grained activity on a page that pasta records, such as questions asked and answered, plan steps done, test cases passed, human gates crossed and content edits. A reviewer can check each of these appears in a replay of pasta's own workspace.

The existing workspace's history is back-filled once: the dataset built from this repo's GitHub PR history and collected dates is written as the initial lifecycle-log file (events/<ws>.jsonl) of pasta's own workspace and played by the normal renderer at /ws:<id>/timeline, not by a separate test page. In the user's words: "Include the testing dataset as the initial backfill, that is, create the jsonl file for the existing workspace PR history and collected dates and it will be played with the normal renderer at /ws:.../timeline, not with a separate test page." This replaces the earlier non-goal that left back-filling to follow-up work.

A dataset built from this repo's real history - not generated at load time - is the initial back-fill of pasta's own workspace (outcome mwjq5k9h-c0b064) and the history the look is judged on; building it is part of this epic's work, and there is no separate test page. It is as sparse as real history: for each of the 127 real moments of this repo (one per pull request #1-#65 of dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev, read through the GitHub MCP, plus each dated line of the initial commit's message) one page - a feature-brief, a simple-change or a bug-report - titled with that PR's title or that commit line, with a feature-brief's implementation-plan and testing-plan created with it and finished before it. Its change and ship dates are the real moments; its create time is its correct start, reverse-engineered from the id of the feature-brief, simple-change or bug-report page that carries that PR's GitHub link in the repo's backup folder, so some pages are created and wait a long while before they are worked on. In the user's words: "From the repo backup folder, collect all the github PR links and reverse engineer the create timestamps from the feature-briefs/simple-change/bug-report id per PR. Keep the already existing change and ship dates, only the create date should be altered, so some of the nodes will be created and then wait a long while to be worked on. Decompose this as part of the features to build."
Scheduled workspace cleanup never erases the history the timeline replays: a replay of the same period looks the same before and after a cleanup run.
The timeline view is read-only: nothing on it creates, edits, transitions or archives a page.
No MCP tool exposes the timeline to agents; it is a view for humans in the web UI.
The view technically works but looks like a generic chart - a static table of dates, a plain Gantt bar, or a graph that jumps from frame to frame - so nobody watching it would say wow.
The replay shows a moment the workspace never actually had: a page shown before it was created or after it was archived, or in a status it did not hold at that time.
Recording history makes page mutations noticeably slower, or lets a mutation fail because its history could not be recorded.
The recorded history grows without bound and makes the workspace store steadily slower or larger - the very problem scheduled workspace cleanup was built to remove.
The WOW leans on bloom, glow or excessive lighting instead of a clean, sharp visual. In the user's words: "WOW factor is not bloom and excessive lighting. It should be clean, sharp."

items.name: Replay the history pasta already stores for the workspace
items.scope: Derive the timeline from the change history pasta already keeps for each workspace - the history scheduled workspace cleanup compacts - by walking it and extracting, with the time each happened, every page's creation, status transitions, reparenting, links made and removed, renames, archive and unarchive, and the element-level activity on a page (questions asked and answered, steps done, cases passed, gates crossed, content edits), then serve that ordered event stream to the web UI. Adds nothing to the write path. Assumes the stored history carries a time for each change and enough to recover each page's type, parent, status and elements at that change, and that it reaches back far enough to replay pasta's own workspace (ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6). The investigator should find out what history exists today and how far back it goes for that workspace, which of those facts it can recover, what cleanup removes and whether it could be made to keep them, and what reading the whole history costs for a workspace of pasta's size.

items.name: Record a lifecycle event log as pages change
items.scope: Add a dedicated, append-only log of page events - created, status changed, reparented, linked or unlinked, renamed, archived or unarchived, and element-level activity such as questions asked and answered, steps done, cases passed, gates crossed and content edits - written in the same commit as the mutation that causes each, kept where scheduled cleanup does not compact it, and served to the web UI as replayable data. Assumes replay starts on the day it ships unless the log is backfilled once from whatever history already exists. The investigator should find where every mutation commits and whether one hook there sees every such change, where the log would live and how it stays bounded, what it costs per write, and how much of the past a one-time backfill could recover.

items.name: A clean, sharp timeline of nodes in the web UI
items.scope: The rendering half, reshaped by the user's answer: "2D definitely but the visual has to incorporate time. WOW factor is not bloom and excessive lighting. It should be clean, sharp. The force node graph should be replaced with a timeline of nodes." A 2D view in the existing web UI where time is an axis: pages are nodes laid out along time - their creation, every status they move through, ship and archive - with nesting, typed links and element-level activity drawn on that timeline, a play/pause/scrub player whose playhead moves through it, and hover showing a page's title and status at the selected moment. The look is crisp lines and type, not glow or bloom. Assumes the replay data is the lifecycle-log event vocabulary from solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744, and that a generated long fake history drives it for visual testing. The investigator should find which time-axis node layouts stay legible and striking at pasta's scale (for example one lane per page grouped under its parent; a branching git-graph or metro-map shape where children branch off their parents; or nodes placed by time and banded by type, with links as arcs), how the playhead and 'the workspace as it stood at that moment' coexist on a time axis, and which rendering approach (SVG, or Canvas at device pixel ratio) keeps it sharp and smooth - and should build each candidate as a page the user can open directly from the spike worktree to judge the look.

chosen.takes: The rendering half - the user's pick: the Metro layout of the timeline of nodes (a page branches off its parent's track at creation and merges back when it finishes), 2D Canvas, flat, clean and sharp with no glow and no animated circles, a playhead player at 0.25 days per second by default that speeds through stretches with no nodes near the playhead, hover with title and status, as built in the spike at commit 6556fb1 (.claude/worktrees/spike-timeline-node-timeline/spike/timeline/metro.html); plus its static visual-test dataset of the 127 real merges, with create times corrected as outcome mwjrq59n-1afef5 says.

The history source: an append-only lifecycle log written by the store in each mutation's commit and served read-only to the web UI as the replay data, in the event vocabulary the Metro renderer already consumes. The controller's call: it is the only viable source of true event times (stored history is not viable alone) and is what the user named as 'page history recorded over time and served to the web UI as replayable data'; the user said to go on with Metro as the pick. No back-fill of the past (non-goal mwjq5k9h-c0b064).

Only for the static visual-test dataset, never as the replay source: its finding that a page's creation time is the base-36 millisecond timestamp in its id, and that the backups under the data folder hold pages gone from the live file. Per the user, each dataset page's create time is reverse-engineered from the id of the feature-brief, simple-change or bug-report that carries that PR's GitHub link in the repo's backup folder; change and ship dates stay as they are.

items.name: Lifecycle log event line on disk (<PASTA_DATA_DIR>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl)
items.shape:
Copied verbatim from the sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae, interface mwksnddc-36abef.

File: <PASTA_DATA_DIR>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl, ws_token = workspace id with ':' replaced by '_' (e.g. events/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl).
Encoding: UTF-8; one JSON object per line; every line ends with "\n"; written as json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) with keys in the order listed.

Common keys, on every line:
  seq   int  >= 1; +1 per event across the whole file, except where a hole was left (served as a gap)
  ts    int  the commit instant, Unix epoch milliseconds UTC; the same for every line of one commit; never less than
             the ts of any earlier line - guaranteed by _touch_and_save taking max(clock now, the document's
             updated_at as loaded) as the commit instant, and by installing a back-fill only when its last ts is not
             later than the installing commit's instant
  page  str  id of the page the event is about
  kind  str  one of the kinds below

kind        extra keys (exactly these, in this order)
created     type: str, title: str, parent: str|null, status: str
present     type: str, title: str, parent: str|null, status: str, archived: bool, links: [{"to": str, "role": str}]   (baseline only)
status      from: str, to: str
renamed     from: str, title: str          (old title, new title)
moved       from_parent: str|null, to_parent: str|null
linked      to: str, role: str             (page is the link's source)
unlinked    to: str, role: str
archived    -                              (only the page whose own archived flag changed; descendants are hidden by the renderer's subtree rule)
unarchived  -
deleted     type: str, title: str, status: str   (last values; the page is gone from the document)
edited      section: str, field: str       (a scalar, prose or blocks field changed)
el_added    section: str, field: str, el: str, status: str|null   (null when the list has no element FSM)
el_status   section: str, field: str, el: str, from: str, to: str
el_edited   section: str, field: str, el: str
el_removed  section: str, field: str, el: str

Example: {"seq":412,"ts":1794931023123,"page":"feature-brief:mwkx1a2b-0c3d4e","kind":"status","from":"building","to":"review"}

Rules: the lines of one commit are contiguous and share ts, except that the commit which starts a log may begin with
the back-fill's lines 1..N, which keep their own ts; the baseline's present lines all share one ts, the instant recording
started. A page's created or present line precedes every other line about it, and a parent's precedes its children's;
in a mutate_page_batch commit the status line is last. Lines are never rewritten or removed. A reader skips a line that
does not parse as a JSON object with an integer seq and never treats a final piece without "\n" as a line. Later
changes may add kinds or keys, never rename or drop one; readers ignore unknown kinds and keys.

items.name: Replay JSON served by GET /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline.json
items.shape:
Copied verbatim from the sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae, interface mwksndde-93cd95. Built by lifecycle_log.timeline_payload (owned by agent-plan:mwkzv8cx-8273c4); served by the route in src/server.py and consumed by the renderer (both owned by agent-plan:mwkzvaab-928193).

200 application/json:
{
  "workspace": {"id": str, "name": str},
  "t0": int|null,     // ts of the first served event; null when there are none
  "t1": int|null,     // ts of the last served event
  "types": {          // every registered page type, from lifecycle_log.timeline_types()
    "<type tag>": {
      "initial": str,                                              // page_type.fsm.initial
      "finish": [str, ...],                                         // fsm.terminal_states if any, else [fsm.states[-1]] when it differs from initial, else []
      "elements": {"<section>.<field>": "<ElementFSMSpec.name>"},   // each list field with an element FSM, e.g. "questions.items": "Question"; names today: Step, Case, Question, BuilderQuestion
      "gates": [["<from status>", "<to status>"], ...]              // status edges whose agency is "human" (page_type.fsm.transitions), unique, sorted
    }
  },
  "events": [Event, ...]   // ascending seq: every parsed log line (the event-line shape), plus gap events
}

Gap event, served only, never written:
  {"seq": int, "ts": int, "page": null, "kind": "gap", "missing": int}
  seq = the first missing seq; ts = ts of the line after the hole; missing >= 1. Inserted wherever a line's seq exceeds the previous line's seq + 1, and before the first line when its seq > 1.

No log file: "events": [], "t0": null, "t1": null (200).
404 application/json {"detail": "Workspace 'ws:<id>' not found."} when the workspace document does not exist.
The route only reads: it takes the workspace read-write lock's read half, never the transaction lock, never writes a file, and never triggers the baseline.

items.name: Initial back-fill file (backfill/<ws_token>.jsonl, committed; today only backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl)
Store and model changes (src/store.py, src/model.py, src/serialize.py)
items.shape:
Copied verbatim from the sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae, interface mwkso7p2-be3127. agent-plan:mwkzvaab-928193 uses Store(..., backfill_dir=...) when it builds STORE in src/server.py and Store.read_lifecycle_log in the timeline.json route.

# src/model.py
@dataclass
class Workspace:
    ...existing fields unchanged...
    event_seq: int = 0     # seq of the last lifecycle-log event this document reflects

# src/serialize.py
workspace_to_dict(ws)   -> also "event_seq": ws.event_seq
workspace_from_dict(d)  -> event_seq = int(d.get("event_seq", 0))   (documents written before ship load as 0)

# src/store.py
EVENTS_DIRNAME = "events"

class Store:
    def __init__(self, root, id_factory=default_id_factory, revision_factory=default_revision_factory,
                 backfill_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> None
        # backfill_dir: folder of committed <ws_token>.jsonl back-fills; None (the default, used by tests) = none

def _events_path_for(self, workspace_id: str) -> Path
    # self.root / EVENTS_DIRNAME / f"{workspace_id.replace(':', '_')}.jsonl"

def _load_for_write(self, workspace_id: str) -> Workspace
    # Called by every writer in place of load_workspace, with _transaction_lock_for(workspace_id) held.
    # When the document's event_seq == 0 it starts the log, once:
    #   a. log file non-empty: never write it; workspace.event_seq = seq of its last complete line (read from its tail);
    #      nothing else is recorded here (the caller's commit persists the adopted seq).
    #   b. log absent or empty: backfill = lifecycle_log.check_backfill(text of backfill_dir/<ws_token>.jsonl) when that
    #      file exists, else []; a None result (file fails the check) is logged and treated as [].
    #      baseline = lifecycle_log.baseline(workspace).
    #      If backfill or baseline: self._touch_and_save(workspace, baseline, backfill=backfill).
    # Returns the workspace. Raises exactly what load_workspace raises (NotFoundError, PastaError for a corrupt file).

def _guarded_events(self, build: Callable[[], list[Event]]) -> list[Event] | None
    # Runs build(); on any exception logs a warning and returns None.

def _touch_and_save(self, workspace: Workspace, events: list[Event] | None,
                    backfill: list[Event] = ()) -> None
    # events: this commit's unstamped events, dicts {"page", "kind", ...kind keys}; [] when there is nothing to
    # record; None when computing them failed. backfill: already-stamped lines (seq 1..N), passed only by
    # _load_for_write when event_seq == 0. Steps:
    #   1. instant = max(datetime.now(timezone.utc), the instant of workspace.updated_at as loaded, when it parses)
    #      workspace.updated_at = instant.isoformat(); ts = instant in epoch ms
    #      if backfill and backfill[-1]["ts"] > ts: log a warning and drop backfill
    #      workspace.event_seq += len(backfill)
    #      lines = backfill + lifecycle_log.stamp(events, workspace.event_seq + 1, ts)   (no stamped lines for None)
    #      workspace.event_seq += len(events) if events is not None else 1
    #   2. self._write_file(self._path_for(workspace.id), workspace)          # the commit; may raise as today
    #   3. with self._rw_lock_for(workspace.id).write(): append the encoded lines to _events_path_for(...)
    #      (mkdir parents; if the file is non-empty and its last byte is not b"\n", write "\n" first; one write call)
    #      any exception in step 3 is logged and swallowed.
    # If step 2 raises, nothing is appended and the in-memory event_seq is discarded with the workspace.

def read_lifecycle_log(self, workspace_id: str) -> list[Event]
    # Raises NotFoundError when the workspace document does not exist. Reads the log file under
    # self._rw_lock_for(workspace_id).read() ([] when absent) and returns lifecycle_log.serve_lines(text).

Every one of the 12 _touch_and_save call sites passes its events (see the strategy's table); create_workspace and write_backup keep calling _write_file directly and record nothing.

items.name: Pure lifecycle-log module (src/lifecycle_log.py)
items.shape:
Copied verbatim from the sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae, interface mwkso7p4-57fa26. agent-plan:mwkzv9e2-e3c586 uses encode (to write the back-fill) and check_backfill (in its test); agent-plan:mwkzvaab-928193 uses timeline_payload (in the timeline.json route).

# Pure core: imports src.model and the page-type registry only; no file, clock or network access.
type Event = dict[str, Any]     # one event; keys per the event-line contract (unstamped: no seq/ts)

def created(page: Page) -> Event                          # {"page", "kind": "created", "type", "title", "parent", "status"}
def present(page: Page) -> Event                          # kind present, with archived and links
def status(page_id: str, from_: str, to: str) -> Event
def renamed(page_id: str, old: str, new: str) -> Event
def moved(page_id: str, from_parent: str | None, to_parent: str | None) -> Event
def linked(page_id: str, to: str, role: str) -> Event
def unlinked(page_id: str, to: str, role: str) -> Event
def archived(page_id: str) -> Event
def unarchived(page_id: str) -> Event
def deleted(page: Page) -> Event                          # last type, title, status
def diff_page(before: Page, after: Page, page_type: PageType | None) -> list[Event]
    # With a page_type, before's sections are first taken as initial_sections(page_type, before.sections) - the
    # normalisation apply_command gives its working copy - so backfilled sections and refreshed fixed fields are
    # not edits. Then: renamed, linked/unlinked, edited, el_added/el_status/el_edited/el_removed (by element "id";
    # element status is element["status"]), status last. With page_type None only title, links and status are diffed.
def baseline(workspace: Workspace) -> list[Event]
    # one present event per page, tree pre-order from workspace.root_page_ids through child_ids, archived pages included;
    # pages filed nowhere follow in id order.
def stamp(events: list[Event], first_seq: int, ts: int) -> list[Event]
    # new dicts with keys seq, ts, page, kind, then the kind keys; seq = first_seq, first_seq + 1, ...
def encode(event: Event) -> str                           # json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
def check_backfill(text: str) -> list[Event] | None
    # the parsed lines of a back-fill file, or None when any line does not parse as an event of the event-line
    # format, the seqs are not exactly 1..N, a ts decreases, or the text does not end with "\n"
def serve_lines(text: str) -> list[Event]                 # parse; skip bad lines; drop an unterminated tail; insert gap events
def timeline_types() -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
    # {"<tag>": {"initial": str, "finish": [str], "elements": {"<section>.<field>": name}, "gates": [[from, to], ...]}}
def timeline_payload(workspace_id: str, name: str, events: list[Event]) -> dict[str, Any]   # the replay JSON's 200 body

scheduling.body:
Dispatch: every agent runs on Opus (capable) - the user: "Switch the subagents to Opus all" - launched in the background and handed only its agent-plan page id; it reports by driving that page and the brief it builds.

Integration branch: timeline-replay, created from origin/main at ddb8912 (#65) and pushed to origin (dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev). The user replaced per-brief pull requests for this epic: "Branch from origin/main, not the local main, and skip creating PRs for each of the features but just register the branches and merge them in." So each agent pushes its own branch to origin and registers it - the brief's pull-request url field holds the branch's GitHub URL - and opens no pull request. Once its agent-plan is accepted, the controller merges the branch into timeline-replay as a fast-forward (every branch starts at the integration tip, so the history stays linear) and pushes timeline-replay. No agent or controller merges into main: main receives the epic at the epic's own human ship gate.

Wave 1 - agent-plan:mwkzv8cx-8273c4: builds feature-brief:mwkzuows-54b6c4 (the lifecycle log on the write path) in worktree timeline-lifecycle-log, branched from timeline-replay. Before wave 2: that agent-plan is accepted - its brief at done with every implementation step done and every testing case passed, its branch pushed and registered - and the branch is merged into timeline-replay.

Wave 2 - agent-plan:mwkzv9e2-e3c586: builds feature-brief:mwkzuptb-70b114 (the back-fill of pasta's own workspace) in worktree timeline-backfill, branched from timeline-replay after wave 1 is merged in (its build writes with lifecycle_log.encode and its test runs lifecycle_log.check_backfill). Before wave 3: accepted and merged in likewise.

Wave 3 - agent-plan:mwkzvaab-928193: builds feature-brief:mwkzuqrd-6afdef (the timeline view and Metro renderer) in worktree timeline-view, branched from timeline-replay after wave 2 is merged in (its route calls Store.read_lifecycle_log and lifecycle_log.timeline_payload, and its node check replays the committed back-fill). After it: accepted and merged in likewise; then the epic goes to review.

One agent per wave: each later brief needs the earlier brief's code to run its own tests, so no two can run at once, and each wave leaves a working, verified state on timeline-replay.

items.text: Should the graph show only the workspace's feature pages (feature-briefs, epics, simple-changes), or more of what pasta records - bug reports and the other page types too?
items.answer: More - everything. In the user's words: "To get the maximum WOW out of using pasta, everything that is possible to visualize should be shown."

items.text: Pasta keeps no change history today, so true event times can only be recorded from the day this ships. Should the replay of the time before that be back-filled once from what pasta still has - exact creation times of every page and element back to 2026-07-20, plus statuses sampled at 13 snapshot instants from 2026-08-21, drawn visibly as approximate (dimmed, hatched on the scrubber) - or should the replay start on ship day? (Raised by solution-investigation:mwjqeeod-1aa130 and solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744.)
items.answer: No. In the user's words: "I think we should back-fill it but not as part of this, for the visual testing we can fake a long history of changes, back fill can be done from github PR merge dates correlated with pages PR links, which will find all create dates and all ship dates. The answer is no"

items.text: For the WOW, should the replay be a 2D glowing graph that reads clearly (sharp hover, status colours, ~17 KB of vendored d3, no build step, medium cost) or a 3D scene with camera flight and depth that looks more spectacular but is harder to read, needs WebGL, a 1.4 MB three.js library and a front-end build step (large cost)? (Raised by solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c.)
items.answer: 2D. In the user's words: "2D definitely but the visual has to incorporate time. WOW factor is not bloom and excessive lighting. It should be clean, sharp. The force node graph should be replaced with a timeline of nodes."

items.text: At what rate should the generated fake history used for visual testing put its changes on the timeline?
items.answer: At the real rate of this repo's history. In the user's words: "The history is going to be much more sparse. Change the spike to show events at the exact rate of the git merged of this repo (every origin/main PR, every one of the 65 PR dates in git) plus every date from the initial commit of the repo, which has a dated commit message. This will give a much better idea of what the spike should actually represent." And: "Use the github mcp to get the PR dates as some have been squashed."

items.text: Which timeline layout should be built - Lanes (one lane per page, grouped under its parent), Metro (git-graph: a page branches off its parent's track and merges back on ship) or Bands (a band per page type, links as arcs)? Each plays the real-cadence fake history from disk: C:/Repos/pasta/.claude/worktrees/spike-timeline-node-timeline/spike/timeline/lanes.html, metro.html and bands.html. (Raised by solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c.)
items.answer: Metro. In the user's words: "I agree with the Metro display, at 0.25 days/second speed. This is a great find. I appreciate the exta speedup when no nods are near the current time - it works great."

items.text: What should the history that the trial layout pages replay contain, so the layouts can be judged?
items.answer: A static dataset, much sparser. In the user's words: "To evaluate I need it to be much sparser. For the 127 real merges, assume there has been 1 feature OR simple change OR bug-report. For each of those, register the create event and one hour later the finished event. The feature ofcourse has the implementation plan and testing plan pages created also at the same time and finished before. Create a realistic output of the graph nodes, use the real PR names for each commit, don't fake generate the data any more but create a static dataset to replay. For the visual, remove the animated circles, they are slightly buggy in when they appear."

items.text: Which approach should be designed?
items.answer: The Metro timeline of nodes (solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c) fed by the lifecycle event log (solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744), with the stored-history finding used only to correct the static dataset's create times (solution-investigation:mwjqeeod-1aa130). In the user's words: "Decompose this as part of the features to build, and go on to the next stage now, with the Metro display as the pick."

inlines: Summary (copied from the epic)

A timeline view in the web UI that replays how a workspace came to be: when each page was created, how it moved through its statuses, how it was nested and linked, the activity on it, and when it shipped or was archived. Two linked interactive surfaces carry it - a player whose timeline can be scrubbed, played and paused, and a graph of the workspace as it stood at the selected moment, where hovering a node shows the page's title and status. Feature pages are its heart, but for the most WOW everything pasta records that can be visualized is shown. It is worth building because the wiki today shows only where work stands now, not how it got there - and it has to wow whoever watches it.
Why (copied from the epic)

In the user's words: "It is worth building because the wiki today shows only where work stands now, not how it got there." And: "The WOW factor is the important part for the user." The user framed delivery as two halves that both have to land: "Delivering it needs page history recorded over time and served to the web UI as replayable data, AND a player and graph that render it." Asked whether the graph should go beyond feature pages, the user said: "To get the maximum WOW out of using pasta, everything that is possible to visualize should be shown."
Each outcome below is copied verbatim from the epic with its outcome id;

approach.chosen:
The user chose a hybrid on the epic (question mwkrzcx6-2d8b82): "The Metro timeline of nodes fed by the lifecycle event log, with the stored-history finding used only to correct the static dataset's create times." At sign-off (question mwkyxzm2-bcbf16) they approved the design with one change: "Include the testing dataset as the initial backfill, that is, create the jsonl file for the existing workspace PR history and collected dates and it will be played with the normal renderer at /ws:.../timeline, not with a separate test page." What is built, and where each part comes from:

1. THE HISTORY SOURCE - from solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744 (lifecycle event log). Pasta stores no change history today: a workspace is one JSON document (<PASTA_DATA_DIR>/ws_<token>.json) rewritten whole on every write. From the day this ships, the store appends one JSON line per lifecycle event of every page - created, status changed, moved (reparented), linked, unlinked, renamed, archived, unarchived, deleted by cleanup, page-level content edited, and element-level activity (element added, element status changed - a question answered, a step done, a case passed -, element edited, element removed) - to a separate append-only file <PASTA_DATA_DIR>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl, in the same locked transaction as the mutation that causes it. Every persisted mutation already funnels through Store._touch_and_save in src/store.py (12 call sites, which the MCP tools, the web POST routes and the hourly cleanup sweep all reach), so each of those call sites passes the events it knows to _touch_and_save; mutate_page_batch derives its events from a scoped diff of the one page it holds before and after. The cleanup sweep records a deleted event per pruned page and never touches the events folder, so a replay of a period looks the same before and after a sweep. The first write to a workspace after ship starts its log: it copies the workspace's committed back-fill file, if the repo has one (part 3), as the log's first lines, then records a one-time baseline of present events - every page that exists at that instant - so the replay continues from the workspace exactly as it stood when recording began. A read-only GET route serves the log, plus a small table read from the page-type registry, as the replay JSON.

2. THE RENDERER AND PLAYER - from solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c (a clean, sharp timeline of nodes), the Metro candidate the user picked from the spike at commit 6556fb1 (.claude/worktrees/spike-timeline-node-timeline/spike/timeline/metro.html, tl.js, app.js - a throwaway precedent to re-implement, never code to merge). A new page in the existing web UI, /ws:<id>/timeline, opened from the workspace tree view - the only timeline page; there is no separate test page. Time is the horizontal axis; each page is a node on a track that branches off its parent's track when it is created and curves back into the parent's track when it first reaches a finished status; root pages (the toc pages) are the trunks. One Canvas2D at device pixel ratio, flat fills, 1 px hairlines and system type - no glow, bloom, gradient, shadow or animated circle: every mark is drawn at its final size the instant the playhead reaches its time. A vertical playhead sweeps the view at 0.25 days per second by default and runs 6 times faster whenever the next event is more than 6 hours ahead; the player plays, pauses, scrubs on an overview strip, steps and zooms; hovering a node shows the page's title and status at the playhead. Left of the playhead the past is solid status colour; right of it the known future is a faint grey ghost that G hides. Element activity, links, renames, moves, archives and deletions have their own marks, as the spike's renderer drew them. A single hairline marks the instant recording started, so the back-filled stretch before it reads as history rebuilt from PRs.

3. THE INITIAL BACK-FILL OF PASTA'S OWN WORKSPACE - the static dataset of solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c, with its create times corrected by the finding of solution-investigation:mwjqeeod-1aa130 (stored history) that a page's creation time is the base-36 millisecond timestamp in its id and that the backups hold pages gone from the live file. One page per each of the 127 real moments of this repo (PRs #1-#65 of dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev, read through the GitHub MCP, plus the 62 dated lines of initial commit 463cf4f), titled with the real PR title or commit line, a feature-brief with its implementation-plan and testing-plan; change and ship dates exactly as in the spike dataset (plans ready at moment +30 and +45 minutes, the page finished at moment +1 hour). Where a PR's GitHub link is carried in the pull_request.url field of a feature-brief, simple-change or bug-report page in the live workspace file or the backup folder (57 of the 65 PRs today), the back-filled page is that real page - its id, its type, its real plan ids - and its create time is its id's timestamp (the longest wait is PR #25, created 2026-09-01 and closed 2026-10-12, 41 days); every other moment gets a back-fill-only page created at the moment. The trunks are the workspace's real Features and Bug Reports toc pages. A build script writes it in the log's own line format as the committed file backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl, which becomes the start of pasta's own workspace's log when recording ships and is played by the normal route and renderer at /ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/timeline. The stored-history direction contributes nothing else: it is never a replay source.

4. THE DOCS - the architecture pages the investigations name as going stale are updated with the log, its commit order, the start-of-log back-fill and baseline, the cleanup rule and the new routes.

alternatives.name: Replay the history pasta already stores (solution-investigation:mwjqeeod-1aa130) as the replay source
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds nothing to the write path and recovers exact creation times of all 585 pages ever seen and 8,783 elements back to 2026-07-20 from id timestamps, but no other fact has a true time: status moves, reparents, renames, links, gates, steps and cases exist only as diffs between 13 sparse snapshots (14 status and 105 archive changes, dated to snapshot instants days or weeks apart), and nothing after the last snapshot on 2026-11-10. Its test was falsified and it was judged not viable alone.
alternatives.whyNot: It cannot meet the goal that the replay is driven by history recorded over time, not reconstructed from current state (mwjq5k99-bab387), and it would show statuses at moments the workspace never had them. For the past before recording, the user later chose the PR-history back-fill (question mwkyxzm2-bcbf16: 'Include the testing dataset as the initial backfill ...') rather than mining these snapshots, so only this direction's id-timestamp finding is kept, to set the back-fill's create times.

alternatives.name: Lanes layout (one lane per page, grouped under its parent) - a candidate of solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c
alternatives.tradeoff: Easiest to label and steadiest at several times pasta's size, with a vertical camera that follows activity; but one row per page ever created makes it 4,354 px tall on the static dataset and 26,334 px at 1,881 generated pages, and every finished page stays as a line to the end of history, so it risks reading as a Gantt chart.
alternatives.whyNot: The user picked Metro after opening all three candidate pages: "I agree with the Metro display, at 0.25 days/second speed. This is a great find."

alternatives.name: Bands layout (a band per page type, links as arcs) - a candidate of solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c
alternatives.tradeoff: Densest and one screen tall (607 px on the static dataset), but nesting is shown only on hover, so a feature, its plans and its parent no longer read as one gesture.
alternatives.whyNot: The user picked Metro: "I agree with the Metro display ..."

alternatives.name: Force-directed glowing node graph in 2D, or a 3D WebGL scene (round 1 of solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c)
alternatives.tradeoff: A glowing d3-force graph (about 17 KB of vendored d3) or a three.js scene with camera flight (1.4 MB library and a front-end build step) looks spectacular in a still frame, but time is not an axis, the layout jumps as pages arrive, and the 3D scene is harder to read.
alternatives.whyNot: The user: "2D definitely but the visual has to incorporate time. WOW factor is not bloom and excessive lighting. It should be clean, sharp. The force node graph should be replaced with a timeline of nodes."

alternatives.name: Back-fill the time before recording ships from stored snapshots, drawn as approximate (raised by solution-investigation:mwjqeeod-1aa130 and solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744)
alternatives.tradeoff: A replay of pasta's own workspace from 2026-07-20 with exact creation times of every page and statuses sampled at 13 snapshot instants, drawn dimmed and hatched; costs a mining script and an approximate-event drawing, and still shows statuses only at snapshot instants.
alternatives.whyNot: The user first declined back-filling in this epic: "back fill can be done from github PR merge dates correlated with pages PR links ... The answer is no." At sign-off they chose the PR-history back-fill instead: "Include the testing dataset as the initial backfill ... played with the normal renderer at /ws:.../timeline." So the back-fill is the PR-history dataset, not snapshot mining, and it is drawn by the normal renderer.

inlines: How data moves

body.source:
WRITE SIDE (one locked transaction per mutation)
  MCP tools / web POST routes / hourly cleanup sweep
    -> a Store writer in src/store.py (12 of them)
         workspace = self._load_for_write(id)   # once per workspace (event_seq == 0): start the log =
                                                #   committed back-fill lines (if any) + baseline of present events
         ...mutate...
         events = lifecycle_log.<constructor or diff_page>(...)   # pure, src/lifecycle_log.py
    -> Store._touch_and_save(workspace, events)
         1. stamp: ts = commit instant (epoch ms), seq = event_seq+1..; event_seq += n
         2. _write_file(workspace document)          # THE COMMIT (atomic replace, as today)
         3. append lines to <data>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl  # best effort, never raises

READ SIDE (GET only, shared read lock)
  GET /ws:<id>/timeline       -> templates/timeline.html  (data-src=/ws:<id>/timeline.json)
  GET /ws:<id>/timeline.json  -> Store.read_lifecycle_log -> lifecycle_log.timeline_payload
  /static/timeline/timeline.js: fetch(data-src) -> fold -> Metro layout -> Canvas2D draw loop

BUILT ONCE, COMMITTED
  scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py collect   (reads, never writes, the live and backup workspace files)
    -> scripts/timeline_dataset/workspace-pages.json
  scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py build     (pure over the committed inputs)
    -> backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl       (event lines; the first write after ship copies them into events/)

rows: src/lifecycle_log.py: event constructors, diff_page, baseline, stamping, line encoding and checking a back-fill's lines

inlines.text: Commit order.

inlines: Inside the transaction lock _touch_and_save (1) takes one commit instant - the clock's now, or the instant of the document's updated_at as loaded when the clock reads earlier than that (a clock stepped backwards), so ts never decreases along seq - writes it to updated_at as today, and stamps every event with ts = that instant in epoch milliseconds and seq = event_seq + 1, + 2, ...; event_seq advances by the count; (2) writes the workspace document - this is the commit; (3) appends the stamped lines to the log while holding the workspace's read-write lock write half: open in append mode (creating the events folder if needed), if the file is non-empty and its last byte is not a newline write one first, then write all the commit's lines in one call. Any exception in step 3 is logged and swallowed. If computing a commit's events raised, the writer passes None instead of a list: event_seq advances by 1 and no line is written. In both cases the hole in seq is served as a gap. So the log is never ahead of the document - a crash between (2) and (3) loses that commit's events, shown as a gap once a later line lands - and the write path never reads the log beyond its last byte, so its cost does not depend on the log's size.

inlines.text: Starting the log: back-fill, then baseline.

inlines: A new
replaces

in the 12 writers, called with the transaction lock held. When the loaded document has event_seq 0 it starts the workspace's log, once. (a) If the log file already has content (the document was restored from an older copy), it never touches the file: it sets event_seq to the seq of the file's last complete line, read once from its tail, and starts nothing. (b) Otherwise, if the store was built with a back-fill folder (the server passes the repo's backfill/) holding <ws_token>.jsonl, it reads and checks that file - every line a valid event, seq 1..N with no hole, ts never decreasing, the last ts not later than this commit's instant - and, when the check passes, commits in one _touch_and_save the back-fill's N lines exactly as written followed by the baseline: one present event per page, archived pages included, in tree pre-order, stamped seq N+1, N+2, ... at the commit instant. A file that fails the check is logged and skipped; the baseline is still written. Without a back-fill the commit is the baseline alone, when the workspace has pages. Then it returns the workspace for the mutation. This runs once per workspace, at its first write after ship (within the hour, since the cleanup sweep is a writer too). Only pasta's own workspace has a back-fill file; every other workspace starts with its baseline. The copy only ever goes into an empty log, so the back-fill file must ship in the same release as recording - once a log has started, nothing is back-filled into it. Present events carry no creation time: the baseline states what existed at that instant and claims nothing earlier.

inlines.text: diff_page.

inlines: Pure, over one page before and after. The before side is first normalised the way commands.apply_command (src/commands.py) normalises its working copy: its sections are taken as initial_sections(page_type, before.sections), so a section or field the type gained after the page was created, and a fixed field the backfill rewrites, never count as an edit. Title differs: renamed. Links: an added (to, role) pair is linked, a removed one unlinked. For each section field the page type declares: a LIST field is diffed by element id - an id only in after is el_added (with the element's status, or null when the list has no element FSM), only in before el_removed, in both with a different status el_status, otherwise with any other key different el_edited; every other field kind (scalar, prose, blocks) that differs is one edited event. Status differs: status, last. A page type of None diffs title, links and status only, with no normalisation.

inlines.text: Fold (pure).

inlines: timeline.js fetches data-src and folds the events in array order into one record per page: born (ts of its created event, or of its first present event when it has none), title segments (renamed), parent segments (moved), status segments, its own archived intervals (archived, unarchived, the present event's archived flag), marks, links with a start and an end, activity ticks and the gaps. The present events of a log all share one ts, the instant recording started (Model.recordingStart; null when the log has none). A present event for a page the fold does not know yet makes that page born at that instant - never earlier - with no created mark. A present event for a page the fold already knows (a back-filled page that still exists) is a silent resync: from that instant the page's title, parent, status and own archived flag take the present values, and no created, status, rename or move mark is drawn for it. Every page the fold knows that no present event names (a back-fill-only page, or a real page pruned since) ends at that instant without a mark. A page is shown at moment T exactly when born <= T, it has not ended or been deleted at or before T, and neither it nor any ancestor - following the parent each had at T - is archived at T: the subtree rule every wiki view applies (Store._archived_in_ancestry, src/store.py line 383). A parent id the fold has not seen ends the walk. Its status and title at T are binary searches into its segments. Events for a page the fold has not seen, and kinds it does not know, are ignored. A page's finish is its first move into one of types[type].finish; that move is drawn as the finish (ship) node. A status move whose [from, to] pair is in types[type].gates is a gate mark. Activity: el_added in a list whose elements entry is Question is a question asked; el_status to answered in a Question list is answered, to done in a Step list a step done, to passed in a Case list a case passed; every other el_ event and edited is a content-edit tick. Each status gets a colour class from the types table, the first rule that matches:

body.source:
warn     blocked, drifted, superseded, abandoned, failed
done     a status in types[type].finish
review   a status whose name contains "review" in any case (review, planReview, designReview), or judging, checking, shipping, verified
idle     types[type].initial
active   any other status
(a type missing from the table has no finish and no initial status)

inlines.text: Metro layout (pure).

inlines: As the spike's layoutMetro: every root page (parent null) is a trunk on its own fixed row; every other page takes the free track nearest its parent's track, alternating sides, branches off the parent's track on a curve at born, runs until its finish, curves back into the parent's track and from then on is a small settled glyph there; its track is free again 30 minutes after it finishes. A page that never finishes keeps its track to the end. A page first seen at the baseline gets a track from the recording-start instant (not from the left edge) with no created glyph when its present status is not a finish status, or is a settled glyph on its parent's track from that instant when it is; a back-filled page resynced at the baseline keeps the track or settled glyph it already has and moves with a changed parent. Every mark and activity tick on a page after its finish - a later status move, a step done or case passed on a plan that finished at ready, a rename - is drawn at its time on the parent's track it merged into, beside its settled glyph (the spike's pageY rule), so building-stage steps and cases show on their feature's track. Hiding: a page that is hidden from its first moment and never shown before t1 (archived itself, or under an archived ancestor, when created or first seen) gets no track; a page whose hiding or end starts and is never undone before t1 ends its lane at that moment - an archived page stops being drawn at its archive time, a deleted page ends with a cross at its deletion, a page the baseline does not name stops at the recording-start instant; a page hidden only for a while keeps its track and is not drawn, hovered or counted in the status chips while hidden.

inlines.text: Drawing (effectful) - the look the user approved.

inlines: One Canvas2D sized by devicePixelRatio, 1 px lines on half-pixel offsets, flat fills, system font. Never shadowBlur, gradients, a globalCompositeOperation other than source-over, or a canvas or CSS filter. No mark's size or opacity depends on the time since its event: every mark has a fixed size and is drawn exactly when mark.ts <= T and not when the playhead is scrubbed back before it; right of the playhead the future is drawn only as faint grey ghost lines and dots. The only motion is the playhead sweep, the follow pan, the vertical camera's easing and the status bar lengthening behind the playhead. Marks, as in the spike: created glyph by type, status dot (gate dots carry a ring), ship check node, archive and delete crosses, rename tick, move square, link brackets between two tracks, activity ticks coloured by kind, gap ticks on the axis. When Model.recordingStart is set, one static hairline in the muted text colour runs down the stage at that instant, labelled recording started on the axis, with a tick on the overview strip: left of it is the back-fill rebuilt from the repo's PR history (creations, plans and finishes only), right of it is recorded history; a hover before it adds the note from PR history. Colours are read with getComputedStyle(document.body) from water.css's properties (background, text, muted text, border) and the timeline's own properties for the status classes, gate, link and playhead accent, and the canvas redraws when the shell's Light/Dark toggle changes the body's class.

inlines.text: Player.

inlines: While following, the playhead stands at 62 percent of the width and the world scrolls under it. Header: Play/Pause (Space), speeds 0.25, 1, 4 and 16 days per second (keys 1-4; 0.25 is selected on load), Follow (F), Future (G, on by default), status chips counting the pages shown at the playhead per status class, and the playhead's date and time on its handle. Each frame the playhead advances by playheadStep: speed x 6 whenever the next event lies more than 6 hours after the playhead, else speed; it stops at t1. The overview strip under the stage shows event density, the count of pages shown, the viewport box and the playhead; click or drag on it scrubs. Arrow keys step 1 day (Shift: 7). The wheel zooms the window between 1.5 and 400 days (3 days on load); dragging the stage pans and turns Follow off. On load the playhead is at t0 and playing starts. An empty log shows the line: No history recorded yet for this workspace.

then turns the three committed inputs, and nothing else, into
by these rules:

items: Moments, unchanged: a PR's moment is merged_at, else closed_at, else created_at; commit line i (from 0) of the k lines dated day d is at d 09:00 UTC + (i + 0.5) / k x 12 hours; all 127 sorted ascending (PRs before commit lines on a tie); a moment not later than the previous one becomes the previous + 1 second; milliseconds, rounded.

Pages: a PR with linked pages maps to the one with the earliest id timestamp - the back-filled page is that real page, with its id and its real type, and its parent is the real Features toc (feature-brief, simple-change) or Bug Reports toc (bug-report). PRs that map to the same page (#20 and #21 share simple-change:mtisbfq5-9c02c8) are one page. Every other moment - PRs #7, #14, #16, #18, #19, #33, #35, #59 and the 62 commit lines - gets a back-fill-only page with id <type>:bf-<4-digit counter> in moment order, typed by the title rule: a title starting with Add is a feature-brief; otherwise one matching the case-insensitive pattern \b(fix|crash|crashing|error)\b|against the write|rejected batch|instead of (rejecting|crashing) is a bug-report; otherwise one whose first word is Rename, Retire, Move, Clarify, Drop, Remove, Bump, Label, Keep, Convert, Link, Include, Show, Upgrade, Write, Read, Resolve, Match, Carry, Send, Allow, Store or Replace, or that starts with PEP8 style cleanup or Review guidance, is a simple-change; everything else is a feature-brief.

Titles: the PR's title (the latest PR's, for a shared page) or the commit line - not the real page's own title, which the baseline brings in at the recording-start instant. A feature-brief's plans are titled <title> - implementation plan and <title> - testing plan.

Times, unchanged except the create time: a linked page is created at its id timestamp (base-36 milliseconds before the '-' of the token after the type prefix), or at its first moment if that is earlier; a back-fill-only page at its moment. A feature-brief's implementation-plan and testing-plan - the real child ids for a linked feature-brief, <type>:bf-NNNN otherwise - are created with it, parent the feature, and go draft to ready at moment + 30 min and + 45 min; the page goes draft to shipped (feature-brief) or draft to closed (simple-change, bug-report) at moment + 60 min, its last moment for a shared page.
Trunks: the real Features and Bug Reports toc pages, created at the earliest create time of any back-filled page, status active.
Lines: kinds created and status only, in the event-line format, written with lifecycle_log.encode; sorted by ts, ties in build order (tocs first, then per moment the page and its plans); seq 1..N.

inlines: Expected today, from the data folder on 2026-11-17: 314 pages - 126 moment pages (56 real: 31 feature-briefs, 15 simple-changes, 10 bug-reports; 70 back-fill-only: 62 feature-briefs, 6 simple-changes, 2 bug-reports), 186 plans (62 real, 124 back-fill-only) and 2 real tocs - in 626 lines. 57 of the 65 PRs map to a real page (PR #13 has two, a bug-report and a feature-brief, and takes the earlier); 23 of the real types differ from what the title rule would say; every decoded time precedes its moment; the median wait is 0.23 days and the longest is PR #25's, 41.2 days. The tocs' own ids date them 2026-07-31, but the back-fill creates them on 2026-07-20 with the first commit line, so every page has its trunk. At the baseline, 33 of the 56 real pages still exist (29 under an archived ancestor, so hidden from then on); the other real pages and every back-fill-only page end at the recording-start instant. Played at /ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/timeline once the first write after ship has started the log.

items.decision: Build the hybrid: the lifecycle event log is the only replay source, the Metro timeline of nodes is the view, and the stored-history finding (a page's creation time is the base-36 millisecond timestamp in its id; backups hold pages gone from the live file) is used only to set the back-fill's create times.
items.alternatives: Stored history as the replay source; the event log drawn with the Lanes or Bands layout; the dataset left with its uncorrected create times.
items.reason: The user's answer to the epic's question mwkrzcx6-2d8b82: 'Decompose this as part of the features to build, and go on to the next stage now, with the Metro display as the pick.'

items.decision: Draw a 2D timeline of nodes with time as the horizontal axis, flat and sharp, with no force layout, no 3D and no glow, bloom or lighting effects.
items.alternatives: A glowing d3-force graph; a three.js 3D scene with camera flight.
items.reason: The user: '2D definitely but the visual has to incorporate time. WOW factor is not bloom and excessive lighting. It should be clean, sharp. The force node graph should be replaced with a timeline of nodes.'

items.decision: Use the Metro layout (a page branches off its parent's track at creation and merges back when it finishes), play at 0.25 days per second by default, and keep the spike's idle speed-up: the playhead moves 6 times faster whenever the next event is more than 6 hours ahead.
items.alternatives: Lanes; Bands; a constant play speed; another default speed.
items.reason: The user, after opening all three candidates: 'I agree with the Metro display, at 0.25 days/second speed. This is a great find. I appreciate the exta speedup when no nods are near the current time - it works great.' The 6 hours and 6 times are the rule of the spike page the user judged.

items.decision: Draw every mark at its final size and full strength the instant the playhead reaches its time, with no expanding or fading rings, no scale-in and no pop.
items.alternatives: The round-2 spike's pulses, scale-in with overshoot and status rings at the playhead.
items.reason: The user: 'For the visual, remove the animated circles, they are slightly buggy in when they appear.'
