The user can reject this at sign-off.

items.decision: Store the log as JSON Lines in <PASTA_DATA_DIR>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl, one file per workspace, never segmented, compacted or pruned.
items.alternatives: A key inside the workspace document (atomic, but the 2.8 MB document is re-serialized on every write, so every write gets slower for ever, and backups copy it); SQLite from the stdlib (a second storage technology, and still not atomic with the JSON document); monthly segment files with gzip (only worth it if one file grows too large to serve); a file per page.
items.reason: Dependency-free, human-diffable, matches the repo's plain-file persistence and the backups/ subfolder precedent, invisible to list_workspaces' non-recursive *.json glob and outside everything cleanup touches. At pasta's activity it grows a few MB a year.

items.decision: Have each Store writer pass the events it knows to a new required argument of _touch_and_save, with mutate_page_batch diffing only the one page it holds before and after.
items.alternatives: A whole-workspace diff at _touch_and_save against a pre-image taken at load (cannot miss a mutation, but measured at +50-100% per write on pasta's 2.8 MB document - deepcopy 85 ms plus diff 67 ms - and cannot tell a rename from a delete and create).
items.reason: Near-zero cost per write (a scoped page diff is under a millisecond), exact intent per event, and a forgotten call site becomes a type error because the argument is required.

items.decision: Commit the workspace document first and append the commit's event lines after it, with seq numbers taken from a persisted event_seq in the document; serve any hole in seq as a gap event.
items.alternatives: Append first and replace second, then on the next write truncate any log tail beyond the document's event_seq (the investigation's sketch: needs a tail read and a repair step on the write path); fsync both files; one combined file.
items.reason: The log can never describe a commit that did not land, the write path never reads the log beyond its last byte, and a crash between the two steps loses at most one commit's events, which the view then marks as a gap. A persisted counter survives hot reloads, which drop module state.

items.decision: Never let recording fail or slow a mutation: an exception while computing a commit's events reserves one seq and writes no line; an exception while appending is logged and swallowed.
items.alternatives: Fail the mutation when its history cannot be recorded; retry the append inside the lock.
items.reason: Anti-goal mwjq5k9s-1bc2cd; the reserved seq turns into a visible gap, so the replay stays honest about what it missed.

items.decision: Start every workspace's log, at its first write after ship, with a one-time baseline of present events (type, title, parent, status, archived, links) for every page it has then, committed by Store._load_for_write before that first mutation - after the committed back-fill lines when the workspace has a back-fill file. A page first seen in the baseline is born at that instant, never earlier.
items.alternatives: No baseline: the pages that exist on ship day (199 in pasta's own workspace) would never appear and every later event on them would be dropped. Give present pages their id-decoded creation time (claims a status before recording that nothing recorded). A migration hook at server start (misses writers that run outside the server).
items.reason: Goal mwjq5k97-712194 asks for the workspace exactly as it stood from the first recorded instant; present events state what existed at that instant and invent nothing earlier, so the only history before it is the PR back-fill the user asked for.

items.decision: Keep event lines payload-free: ids, kinds and status values, with titles only on created, present, renamed and deleted; record no reorder, expires_at stamp, delete scheduling, guidance or workspace-status change.
items.alternatives: Record element and body text (a content history, but it copies page text into a second file and grows fast); record every write including reorders.
items.reason: Lines of roughly 150 to 300 bytes, nothing the view does not draw, and no page text duplicated outside the workspace document.

items.decision: Stamp every event of one commit with the same ts - the commit instant in integer epoch milliseconds, the instant written to updated_at - and order events by seq.
items.alternatives: ISO-8601 strings like updated_at (longer lines, parsing in the browser); a clock read per event.
items.reason: Compact, sortable, the same unit as the id timestamps the dataset decodes; everything in a commit did happen at one instant.

items.decision: Use the log's own key names (seq, ts, page, kind and the kind fields) on disk, in the route JSON and in the back-fill file, and have the renderer read them directly.
items.alternatives: The spike's names (seq, t, id, k) with a mapping in the route or the fold.
items.reason: One contract shared by the store, the route, the back-fill builder and the renderer, so no two agents can drift apart on it; the back-fill can be copied into the log line for line.

items.decision: Serve the whole log in one JSON response per request, parsed and gap-filled on the fly, together with a per-type table read from the page-type registry.
items.alternatives: after/until windows; a streaming response; keyframe snapshots; a server-side cache keyed by file size.
items.reason: The log is a few MB a year at pasta's activity and the browser folds tens of thousands of events in about 100 ms (the spike folded 26k generated events in 88 to 110 ms); windows and caches would be generality nobody needs yet.

items.decision: Serve, per page type from the registry, its initial status, its finish statuses (terminal_states when declared, else its last status when that differs from the initial one), its element-FSM lists and its human-agency status edges; derive a status's colour class in the renderer from that table by fixed ordered rules (warn names, finish, names containing review, initial, else active).
items.alternatives: A hard-coded status-name-to-class table in the renderer, as the spike had (it treats agent-plan's ready as done, so agent-plans would merge back before they are worked, and it misses camelCase statuses such as planReview); serving full colour classes from Python.
items.reason: Exact per type: agent-plans finish at accepted, plans at ready, features at shipped or abandoned, and a status added later still gets a sensible class with no table to update.

items.decision: Accept that the log grows without a total bound and keep every cost off it instead: the write path reads at most its last byte, the workspace document grows by one integer (event_seq), and cleanup never reads, rewrites or deletes it.
items.alternatives: A retention window or compaction of old events (erases replayable history, against mwjq5k9k-d543aa); a size cap that stops recording; monthly segments.
items.reason: The harm the anti-goal mwjq5k9t-1f8a0e names is a workspace store that gets steadily slower or larger; with this design neither the document nor any write grows with the log, and the log grows with activity, not with time or document size (estimated single-digit MB a year for pasta's own workspace).

items.decision: Record the sweep's effects in Store.cleanup_workspace - unlinked for every link a surviving page loses, then deleted with the page's last type, title and status - computed before cleanup.delete_subtree runs, and leave src/cleanup.py unchanged.
items.alternatives: Make cleanup.delete_subtree return the events; record only deleted and let the renderer end links at a deleted endpoint.
items.reason: The store already holds the pre-image inside the lock, cleanup stays a pure classifier and deleter, and every link that was removed is recorded as removed.

items.decision: Opt the timeline page out of live reload by wrapping _base.html's reloader include in a block that timeline.html leaves empty; the replay shows the history as of page load.
items.alternatives: Keep the reload and restore the playhead from sessionStorage (the page would reload mid-play on every agent write, a visible stutter and blank frame); append live events over the reloader socket.
items.reason: Smooth play (goal mwjq5k9d-6b6bde) with the smallest change; reloading the page shows newer history.

items.decision: Render with one hand-written Canvas2D script and stylesheet under src/static/timeline/, with no third-party library and no build step.
items.alternatives: Vendored d3 modules (scale, axis, zoom, shape - convenience only, each replaced in the spike by under 40 lines); an SVG renderer (fine at 311 pages, but 32,686 elements and 278 of about 540 frames over 33 ms at 1,881 generated pages).
items.reason: The spike measured steady 17 ms frames at device pixel ratio 1 and 2 on the dataset, the repo has no front-end toolchain, and nothing needs vendoring.

items.decision: Show the known future right of the playhead as a faint grey ghost by default, hidden with G.
items.alternatives: Hide the future by default and show it with G.
items.reason: It is how the user saw and approved metro.html; the ghost has no nodes or colour, so the solid picture is still exactly the workspace at the playhead.

items.decision: Open the view with the playhead at the first event and start playing at once.
items.alternatives: Open paused at the latest moment, showing the present state.
items.reason: As in the approved spike page; the first impression is the replay, which is what has to wow.

items.decision: Install the back-fill in the server, once: commit it as backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl, and have Store._load_for_write copy it, line for line, as the start of the workspace's log in the first write after recording ships - only when the document's event_seq is 0 and the log file is absent or empty. An existing log is never written into: a non-empty log only lends its last seq to the document.
items.alternatives: A one-off script that writes events/ and bumps event_seq in the data folder (no script writes the data folder today, and with only in-process locks it needs the server stopped); an admin POST route (a write surface for a one-time act); prepending the back-fill at serve time (then it is not the workspace's log file the user asked for); a separate visual-test page (what the user replaced).
items.reason: The copy runs under the store's own transaction and read-write locks in the server process, needs no manual step and no stopped server, and the empty-log condition makes it happen at most once and never over recorded history. The cost: the back-fill must ship in the same release as recording.

items.decision: Build the back-fill with scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py in two steps: collect reads (never writes) the live and backup workspace files into the committed scripts/timeline_dataset/workspace-pages.json; build turns that and the two GitHub inputs, fetched once through the GitHub MCP, into the committed backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl.
items.alternatives: One step that reads the data folder and writes the back-fill directly (a test could then not rebuild it without the gitignored data folder); a node script like the spike's build-dataset.mjs (the repo has no node toolchain); calling GitHub from the script (the PR list comes through the GitHub MCP, which a script cannot call).
items.reason: Reproducible with uv run python, and with every input committed a test can rebuild the back-fill byte for byte and check each create time against its page id.

items.decision: When several pages carry one PR's link take the one with the earliest id; make PRs that share a page one page, finished at the later PR's moment + 1 h and titled with the later PR's title; never create a page later than its first moment; leave moments without a linked page (PRs #7, #14, #16, #18, #19, #33, #35, #59 and the 62 commit lines) at create = moment; create a feature-brief's plans with it at its corrected time.
items.alternatives: The latest id; the linked page whose type matches the title rule; two pages for a shared real page (one id cannot be created twice); dropping moments with no linked page; leaving plans at the moment.
items.reason: The earliest linked page is when the work started; one real page has one life; the never-later guard keeps every page created before its first change (no case today - all 57 decoded times precede their moments); unlinked moments keep the existing dates because there is nothing to correct them from; plans are 'created with it' per the outcome.

items.decision: Check the renderer's pure fold, Metro layout and playhead step with a dependency-free node script under tests/timeline/, run from pytest when node is on PATH and skipped otherwise.
items.alternatives: Manual checks only; porting the fold to Python to test it there.
items.reason: Anti-goal mwjq5k9r-d69675 (a moment the workspace never had) needs an automated brute-force comparison; the spike's check.js is the precedent; no npm package is needed.

items.decision: Show a page's title as of the playhead in the hover (renames folded), not its title today.
items.alternatives: The page's latest title, as the spike did.
items.reason: Goal mwjq5k98-9a1d89 asks for the page as it was at the selected moment, and renamed events make the earlier title known.

items.decision: Put the only entry to the view on the workspace tree page, as a Timeline link beside Show archived.
items.alternatives: Also link it from every page's sidebar or the index page.
items.reason: The timeline is per workspace and the tree page is the workspace's front page; there is no other timeline page to reach.

items.decision: Hide a page at moment T whenever it or any of its ancestors (by the parents it had at T) is archived at T - the subtree rule the wiki already applies in Store.tree and search (Store._archived_in_ancestry, src/store.py line 383) - and record no extra events for the hidden descendants: the fold derives the hiding from the archived, unarchived and moved events it already has. A page hidden for good from its first recorded moment (itself archived, or under an archived ancestor, at the baseline or at creation, and not revealed before t1) gets no Metro track; a page that becomes hidden for good ends its lane at that moment; a page hidden for a while keeps its track and is simply not drawn, hovered or counted while hidden.
items.alternatives: Judge only the page's own archived flag and draw such pages hanging off a parent track that is not drawn (53 live pages today, among them 10 feature-briefs with their 30 plans and specs and 10 agent-plans); record an archived event for every descendant when a page is archived (writes per-descendant facts the store itself does not hold, and an unarchive would have to undo them); draw them as roots.
items.reason: 'The workspace exactly as it stood' (mwjq5k97-712194) is what the wiki showed at that moment, and every wiki view hides an archived page's subtree; this keeps the replay from showing pages the wiki was hiding (anti-goal mwjq5k9r-d69675) without a second copy of the archive state in the log.

items.decision: Take each commit's instant as the later of the clock's now and the document's updated_at as loaded, so ts never decreases along seq.
items.alternatives: Drop the ordering promise and have the renderer sort events by ts (seq and ts could then disagree, and a later commit could land before an earlier one in the replay); keep a separate last-ts field in the document.
items.reason: The renderer's binary searches assume time order; updated_at is already written with every commit, so the guard needs no new state.

items.decision: Normalise the before side of diff_page with initial_sections(page_type, before.sections), as apply_command normalises its working copy, before diffing.
items.alternatives: Treat a missing section or field as its empty default inside the diff (still counts a refreshed fixed field as an edit); diff the raw stored page (records spurious edited events on an older page's first batch after its type gained a field).
items.reason: Only what the batch's commands changed is recorded; the backfill is bookkeeping, not an edit.

items.decision: Draw every mark and activity tick on a page after its finish on the parent's track it merged into, beside its settled glyph - so the steps done and cases passed of plans that finish at ready show on their feature's track while it builds.
items.alternatives: Keep a finished plan's track open until its last activity (more tracks, and a plan would look unfinished); hide activity after finish (loses the most frequent activity mwjqdpi7-2c4835 names).
items.reason: It is the spike's pageY rule, keeps Metro's one-branch-per-page look, and puts the building-stage activity on the feature that is being built.

items.decision: Meet the back-fill and the baseline in the fold, not in the file: a present event for a page the back-fill already created is a silent resync (its title, parent, status and archived flag take the present values at the recording-start instant, with no created, status, rename or move mark); a present event for a page not seen before makes it born at that instant; every page the fold knows that the baseline does not name - each back-fill-only page, and each real page pruned since - ends at that instant without a mark.
items.alternatives: Leave present pages out of the baseline when the back-fill already has them (the back-fill's assumed status - every page finished an hour after its PR - would stand for ever, and archives since would never show); drop the back-fill's pages from the baseline's view by rewriting the back-fill at install (no longer the file the user asked for); keep back-fill-only pages alive after the baseline (the replay would show 70 pages the workspace never held).
items.reason: No page is drawn twice (one id, one record), the replay after recording starts is exactly the recorded workspace, and the back-fill's simplifications never leak past the instant recording began. Of the 56 real back-filled pages, 33 still exist (29 under an archived ancestor, hidden from then on).

items.decision: Title every back-filled page with its PR's title or commit line (a feature-brief's plans: <title> - implementation plan and - testing plan), and let the real page's own current title take over at the recording-start instant through the baseline's resync.
items.alternatives: The real page's own title from the start (not the PR names the user asked for); the PR title for ever (the baseline would then contradict the recorded title).
items.reason: The user asked for the real PR names in the dataset they judged; the resync keeps the recorded part exact.

items.decision: Use the workspace's real Features and Bug Reports toc pages as the back-fill's trunks, created at the back-fill's earliest create time (2026-07-20, with the first commit line), although their ids date them 2026-07-31.
items.alternatives: Back-fill-only toc pages (the baseline would add the real tocs as a second pair of trunks); creating the tocs at their id time (the 2026-07-20 to 07-31 pages would have no trunk to branch from).
items.reason: One pair of trunks across the back-fill and the recorded history, and every back-filled page has a parent to branch from; the 11 days are inside the stretch the recording-started hairline marks as rebuilt from PR history.

items.decision: Number the back-fill seq 1..N in ts order and stamp the baseline and every later event after it (seq N+1 onward, at their commit instants); install the back-fill only when its last ts is not later than the installing commit's instant.
items.alternatives: Number recorded events from 1 and give the back-fill negative or separate numbers (two sequences for one file, and the gap rule would misread them); interleave by time (the back-fill ends 2026-11-16, before ship, so there is nothing to interleave).
items.reason: The log keeps one gap-free sequence whose ts never decreases, which is what the reader's gap rule and the renderer's binary searches rely on.

items.decision: Draw the back-filled stretch with the normal renderer exactly like recorded history, and mark only the instant recording started: one static hairline in the muted text colour labelled recording started, a tick on the overview strip, and a from PR history note in the hover before it. No new event key or route field: the instant is the ts of the baseline's present events.
items.alternatives: Dim or hatch the back-filled stretch (a second look the user did not ask for: 'played with the normal renderer'); no marker at all (a viewer would read the back-fill's one-hour features and missing archives as recorded fact); an approximate flag on every back-filled line.
items.reason: Honest about where rebuilt history ends and recorded history begins, with the smallest change to the look the user approved and none to the shared contracts.

items.name: Lifecycle log event line on disk (<PASTA_DATA_DIR>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl)
items.shape:
File: <PASTA_DATA_DIR>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl, ws_token = workspace id with ':' replaced by '_' (e.g. events/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl).
Encoding: UTF-8; one JSON object per line; every line ends with "\n"; written as json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) with keys in the order listed.

Common keys, on every line:
  seq   int  >= 1; +1 per event across the whole file, except where a hole was left (served as a gap)
  ts    int  the commit instant, Unix epoch milliseconds UTC; the same for every line of one commit; never less than
             the ts of any earlier line - guaranteed by _touch_and_save taking max(clock now, the document's
             updated_at as loaded) as the commit instant, and by installing a back-fill only when its last ts is not
             later than the installing commit's instant
  page  str  id of the page the event is about
  kind  str  one of the kinds below

kind        extra keys (exactly these, in this order)
created     type: str, title: str, parent: str|null, status: str
present     type: str, title: str, parent: str|null, status: str, archived: bool, links: [{"to": str, "role": str}]   (baseline only)
status      from: str, to: str
renamed     from: str, title: str          (old title, new title)
moved       from_parent: str|null, to_parent: str|null
linked      to: str, role: str             (page is the link's source)
unlinked    to: str, role: str
archived    -                              (only the page whose own archived flag changed; descendants are hidden by the renderer's subtree rule)
unarchived  -
deleted     type: str, title: str, status: str   (last values; the page is gone from the document)
edited      section: str, field: str       (a scalar, prose or blocks field changed)
el_added    section: str, field: str, el: str, status: str|null   (null when the list has no element FSM)
el_status   section: str, field: str, el: str, from: str, to: str
el_edited   section: str, field: str, el: str
el_removed  section: str, field: str, el: str

Example: {"seq":412,"ts":1794931023123,"page":"feature-brief:mwkx1a2b-0c3d4e","kind":"status","from":"building","to":"review"}

Rules: the lines of one commit are contiguous and share ts, except that the commit which starts a log may begin with
the back-fill's lines 1..N, which keep their own ts; the baseline's present lines all share one ts, the instant recording
started. A page's created or present line precedes every other line about it, and a parent's precedes its children's;
in a mutate_page_batch commit the status line is last. Lines are never rewritten or removed. A reader skips a line that
does not parse as a JSON object with an integer seq and never treats a final piece without "\n" as a line. Later
changes may add kinds or keys, never rename or drop one; readers ignore unknown kinds and keys.

items.name: Replay JSON served by GET /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline.json
items.shape:
200 application/json:
{
  "workspace": {"id": str, "name": str},
  "t0": int|null,     // ts of the first served event; null when there are none
  "t1": int|null,     // ts of the last served event
  "types": {          // every registered page type, from lifecycle_log.timeline_types()
    "<type tag>": {
      "initial": str,                                              // page_type.fsm.initial
      "finish": [str, ...],                                         // fsm.terminal_states if any, else [fsm.states[-1]] when it differs from initial, else []
      "elements": {"<section>.<field>": "<ElementFSMSpec.name>"},   // each list field with an element FSM, e.g. "questions.items": "Question"; names today: Step, Case, Question, BuilderQuestion
      "gates": [["<from status>", "<to status>"], ...]              // status edges whose agency is "human" (page_type.fsm.transitions), unique, sorted
    }
  },
  "events": [Event, ...]   // ascending seq: every parsed log line (the event-line shape), plus gap events
}

Gap event, served only, never written:
  {"seq": int, "ts": int, "page": null, "kind": "gap", "missing": int}
  seq = the first missing seq; ts = ts of the line after the hole; missing >= 1. Inserted wherever a line's seq exceeds the previous line's seq + 1, and before the first line when its seq > 1.

No log file: "events": [], "t0": null, "t1": null (200).
404 application/json {"detail": "Workspace 'ws:<id>' not found."} when the workspace document does not exist.
The route only reads: it takes the workspace read-write lock's read half, never the transaction lock, never writes a file, and never triggers the baseline.

# src/model.py
@dataclass
class Workspace:
    ...existing fields unchanged...
    event_seq: int = 0     # seq of the last lifecycle-log event this document reflects

# src/serialize.py
workspace_to_dict(ws)   -> also "event_seq": ws.event_seq
workspace_from_dict(d)  -> event_seq = int(d.get("event_seq", 0))   (documents written before ship load as 0)

# src/store.py
EVENTS_DIRNAME = "events"

class Store:
    def __init__(self, root, id_factory=default_id_factory, revision_factory=default_revision_factory,
                 backfill_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> None
        # backfill_dir: folder of committed <ws_token>.jsonl back-fills; None (the default, used by tests) = none

def _events_path_for(self, workspace_id: str) -> Path
    # self.root / EVENTS_DIRNAME / f"{workspace_id.replace(':', '_')}.jsonl"

def _load_for_write(self, workspace_id: str) -> Workspace
    # Called by every writer in place of load_workspace, with _transaction_lock_for(workspace_id) held.
    # When the document's event_seq == 0 it starts the log, once:
    #   a. log file non-empty: never write it; workspace.event_seq = seq of its last complete line (read from its tail);
    #      nothing else is recorded here (the caller's commit persists the adopted seq).
    #   b. log absent or empty: backfill = lifecycle_log.check_backfill(text of backfill_dir/<ws_token>.jsonl) when that
    #      file exists, else []; a None result (file fails the check) is logged and treated as [].
    #      baseline = lifecycle_log.baseline(workspace).
    #      If backfill or baseline: self._touch_and_save(workspace, baseline, backfill=backfill).
    # Returns the workspace. Raises exactly what load_workspace raises (NotFoundError, PastaError for a corrupt file).

def _guarded_events(self, build: Callable[[], list[Event]]) -> list[Event] | None
    # Runs build(); on any exception logs a warning and returns None.

def _touch_and_save(self, workspace: Workspace, events: list[Event] | None,
                    backfill: list[Event] = ()) -> None
    # events: this commit's unstamped events, dicts {"page", "kind", ...kind keys}; [] when there is nothing to
    # record; None when computing them failed. backfill: already-stamped lines (seq 1..N), passed only by
    # _load_for_write when event_seq == 0. Steps:
    #   1. instant = max(datetime.now(timezone.utc), the instant of workspace.updated_at as loaded, when it parses)
    #      workspace.updated_at = instant.isoformat(); ts = instant in epoch ms
    #      if backfill and backfill[-1]["ts"] > ts: log a warning and drop backfill
    #      workspace.event_seq += len(backfill)
    #      lines = backfill + lifecycle_log.stamp(events, workspace.event_seq + 1, ts)   (no stamped lines for None)
    #      workspace.event_seq += len(events) if events is not None else 1
    #   2. self._write_file(self._path_for(workspace.id), workspace)          # the commit; may raise as today
    #   3. with self._rw_lock_for(workspace.id).write(): append the encoded lines to _events_path_for(...)
    #      (mkdir parents; if the file is non-empty and its last byte is not b"\n", write "\n" first; one write call)
    #      any exception in step 3 is logged and swallowed.
    # If step 2 raises, nothing is appended and the in-memory event_seq is discarded with the workspace.

def read_lifecycle_log(self, workspace_id: str) -> list[Event]
    # Raises NotFoundError when the workspace document does not exist. Reads the log file under
    # self._rw_lock_for(workspace_id).read() ([] when absent) and returns lifecycle_log.serve_lines(text).

Every one of the 12 _touch_and_save call sites passes its events (see the strategy's table); create_workspace and write_backup keep calling _write_file directly and record nothing.

items.name: Pure lifecycle-log module (src/lifecycle_log.py)
items.shape:
# Pure core: imports src.model and the page-type registry only; no file, clock or network access.
type Event = dict[str, Any]     # one event; keys per the event-line contract (unstamped: no seq/ts)

def created(page: Page) -> Event                          # {"page", "kind": "created", "type", "title", "parent", "status"}
def present(page: Page) -> Event                          # kind present, with archived and links
def status(page_id: str, from_: str, to: str) -> Event
def renamed(page_id: str, old: str, new: str) -> Event
def moved(page_id: str, from_parent: str | None, to_parent: str | None) -> Event
def linked(page_id: str, to: str, role: str) -> Event
def unlinked(page_id: str, to: str, role: str) -> Event
def archived(page_id: str) -> Event
def unarchived(page_id: str) -> Event
def deleted(page: Page) -> Event                          # last type, title, status
def diff_page(before: Page, after: Page, page_type: PageType | None) -> list[Event]
    # With a page_type, before's sections are first taken as initial_sections(page_type, before.sections) - the
    # normalisation apply_command gives its working copy - so backfilled sections and refreshed fixed fields are
    # not edits. Then: renamed, linked/unlinked, edited, el_added/el_status/el_edited/el_removed (by element "id";
    # element status is element["status"]), status last. With page_type None only title, links and status are diffed.
def baseline(workspace: Workspace) -> list[Event]
    # one present event per page, tree pre-order from workspace.root_page_ids through child_ids, archived pages included;
    # pages filed nowhere follow in id order.
def stamp(events: list[Event], first_seq: int, ts: int) -> list[Event]
    # new dicts with keys seq, ts, page, kind, then the kind keys; seq = first_seq, first_seq + 1, ...
def encode(event: Event) -> str                           # json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
def check_backfill(text: str) -> list[Event] | None
    # the parsed lines of a back-fill file, or None when any line does not parse as an event of the event-line
    # format, the seqs are not exactly 1..N, a ts decreases, or the text does not end with "\n"
def serve_lines(text: str) -> list[Event]                 # parse; skip bad lines; drop an unterminated tail; insert gap events
def timeline_types() -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
    # {"<tag>": {"initial": str, "finish": [str], "elements": {"<section>.<field>": name}, "gates": [[from, to], ...]}}
def timeline_payload(workspace_id: str, name: str, events: list[Event]) -> dict[str, Any]   # the replay JSON's 200 body

items.name: Timeline colour properties (src/static/timeline/timeline.css)
items.shape:
Defined for both body.light and body.dark, each a hex colour:
  --tl-idle --tl-active --tl-review --tl-done --tl-warn --tl-archived --tl-gate --tl-link --tl-accent
The canvas reads them, and water.css's --background-body, --background, --text-main, --text-muted and --border, with getComputedStyle(document.body), and re-reads and redraws whenever the body's class attribute changes (the shell's Light/Dark toggle). No colour is hard-coded in timeline.js.

items.why: The pure core of recording and serving: event constructors, diff_page, baseline, stamp, encode, serve_lines (parse and gaps), timeline_types and timeline_payload. No I/O, so the event rules are unit-testable.
Workspace gains event_seq: int = 0, the persisted counter that numbers the log and makes holes detectable across restarts and hot reloads.
workspace_to_dict writes event_seq; workspace_from_dict loads a missing key as 0, so documents written before ship still load.

The timeline view: extends _base.html with body class timeline, empties the reloader and footer blocks, holds the header controls, stage and overview canvases and tooltip inside div#timeline data-src, links timeline.css and mounts timeline.js.
Wrap the include of _reloader.js in a reloader block so the timeline can opt out of the reload every mutation broadcasts; every other view renders as before.
The entry point: a Timeline link to /ws:<id>/timeline beside the Show archived link.

The renderer and player, re-implemented from the spike's tl.js and app.js (precedent only): fold, Metro layout, Canvas2D drawing at device pixel ratio, player, overview scrubber, hover; exports its pure functions for the node check.
Full-viewport layout for body.timeline, hides the floating Top link there, styles the header controls and tooltip from water.css properties, and defines the --tl-* colours for light and dark.
Committed input: PRs #1-#65 of dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev (number, title, created_at, merged_at, closed_at), fetched once through the GitHub MCP.
Committed input: the 62 dated lines of initial commit 463cf4f's message, fetched through the GitHub MCP.
event_seq round-trips and a document without it loads as 0.

A pruning sweep appends unlinked and deleted events, leaves every earlier log line byte-identical, never deletes or rewrites the events folder, and the replay JSON for the period before the sweep is unchanged.
Runs node tests/timeline/check_timeline.js when node is on PATH (skips otherwise), and greps timeline.js and timeline.css for forbidden glow and animation constructs.
The sweep records unlinked and deleted events for what it prunes and never reads, rewrites or deletes events/; it is still the one path that destroys workspace data.
Its data model ('One JSON document per workspace') and on-disk layout gain events/<ws_token>.jsonl and the document's event_seq; the browser-view paragraph names the timeline.

Owns the non-goal check that no MCP tool exposes the timeline: list the MCP server's registered tools and assert none is named after or serves the timeline (no tool list assertion exists there today).

The write path: EVENTS_DIRNAME, the backfill_dir constructor argument, _events_path_for, _load_for_write in place of load_workspace in the 12 writers (starts the log once: the committed back-fill, checked, then the baseline; a non-empty log only lends its last seq), _guarded_events, _touch_and_save(workspace, events, backfill=) with document-first-then-append, the events each writer passes (cleanup_workspace computing unlinked and deleted before delete_subtree), and read_lifecycle_log for the route.

Two GET routes beside route_tree: /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline (HTML) and /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline.json (the replay JSON, 404 for a missing workspace); STORE built with backfill_dir=Path("backfill"). No other timeline route and no MCP tool.

Builds the initial back-fill: collect reads, never writes, the live and backup workspace files into workspace-pages.json; build turns the three committed inputs into backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl (real ids and types for PR-linked pages, decoded create times, PR titles, the spike dataset's change and ship times).

Committed input written by collect: per PR #1-#65 the pages carrying its link (id, type, real plan ids) and the real Features and Bug Reports toc ids, so the back-fill rebuilds without the gitignored data folder.

Unit tests of the pure module: each constructor's keys and order, diff_page per field kind with the initial_sections normalisation, baseline order, stamp, encode, check_backfill (good file, a hole, a decreasing ts, a bad line, a missing final newline), serve_lines (bad line, unterminated tail, holes and a leading hole as gaps), timeline_types against the registry.

Each of the 12 writers records its events; a rejected batch records nothing; the log starts once - back-fill lines verbatim then the baseline at seq N+1, a back-fill that fails the check or ends after the commit instant skipped with the baseline still written, a non-empty log never written into and its last seq adopted, no back-fill without backfill_dir; an append that raises and an event build that raises leave the mutation committed and a gap served; the log is never ahead of the document; write overhead stays flat with a large log.

Timeline routes: the tree page links to the timeline; /ws:<id>/timeline renders data-src and no reloader script; timeline.json shape, empty log, 404; /static/timeline assets are served; no other timeline route answers; reading leaves the workspace and log files unchanged.

Dependency-free node check of timeline.js's pure functions: brute-force isShown, statusAt and titleAt against a replay of the events at random moments, on the committed back-fill followed by a synthetic baseline and on a small fixture with every kind; the present rules (born at recordingStart, silent resync, unnamed pages end); Metro tracks never overlap; playheadStep's speed and 6x idle rule.

Its invariant that every write is one atomic overwrite gains the lifecycle-log rule: document first, then append; event_seq; holes served as gaps; how the first write starts the log with the committed back-fill and the baseline; the events each writer records.

questions.question: Is a page shown in the replay while one of its ancestors is archived but it is not, and if so, on which track is it drawn once the parent's track has stopped being drawn?
questions.why: Part 3's isShown checks only the page's own archived flag, and Store._set_page_archive_state (src/store.py line 715) cascades the flag only onto pinned children. So archiving an epic leaves its feature-briefs and agent-plans unarchived, and the web tree hides them only through their archived ancestry. In pasta's live workspace today 53 unarchived pages sit under an archived ancestor: 10 feature-briefs and their 30 plans and specs, 10 agent-plans, and 3 others. The baseline would draw all of them from t0, while their archived parents are not drawn. Finished ones would be settled glyphs on a parent track that is not drawn, and unfinished ones would branch off it. The answer changes isShown and its brute-force node check, and the Metro track rules. It may also decide whether archiving should record archived events for the hidden descendants. Part of it is the user's call: is a page hidden under an archived parent part of 'the workspace exactly as it stood' (mwjq5k97-712194, anti-goal mwjq5k9r-d69675)?
questions.resolution: Settled as a proposal decision: a page is hidden at T when it or any ancestor at T is archived at T, the wiki's own subtree rule (Store._archived_in_ancestry, used by tree and search), with no extra events recorded for descendants. A page hidden for good from its first moment gets no Metro track; one hidden for good later ends its lane then; one hidden for a while keeps its track and is not drawn, hovered or counted meanwhile. Folded into Part 3 (Fold and Metro layout), the renderer interface's isShown and the node check in the mwjq5k97 criterion. It is a proposal the user can reject at sign-off; it does not need the user before planning because it follows the rule every wiki view already applies.

digest.body:
Built: the store appends one JSON line per page lifecycle event to events/<ws>.jsonl in each mutation's transaction, served read-only at /ws:<id>/timeline.json; a hand-written Canvas2D Metro view at /ws:<id>/timeline replays it at 0.25 days per second with the idle speed-up, no glow, no animated circles. Pasta's own log starts with the PR-history back-fill (126 moment pages, real page ids where a PR links one, 626 lines), committed as backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl and played by that same view - no separate test page.

New or changed proposals to check: the store copies the back-fill into an empty log at the first write after ship, never into an existing one; the baseline follows it, silently resyncing back-filled pages that still exist and ending back-fill-only or pruned pages at recording start; PR-linked pages take the real page's id, type and plan ids (23 types change from the title rule); PR titles until recording starts; the real Features and Bug Reports tocs as trunks from 20 Jul; seq 1..N, then recorded events; a recording-started hairline, no new event field; two-step collect/build; PRs sharing a page merged. 32 of 39 decisions are proposals.

Left to the builder: helper names, file splits, pixel constants, palette, glyph stacking, wording.

findings.issue: Strategy Part 3 (Fold and Metro layout): the visibility and track rules leave out pages whose ancestor is archived but which are not archived themselves. 53 of pasta's live pages are in that state today, so the gap shows on the first replay of pasta's own workspace, not only in an edge case. A builder has to guess between three options: draw them hanging off a parent track that is not drawn, hide them by ancestry as the tree does, or record events for them. Each guess gives a different fold, layout and node check. See the first builder question.

Interfaces, event line: the contract says ts is 'non-decreasing with seq'. _touch_and_save takes a fresh wall-clock instant for each commit, and nothing stops a backwards clock step from giving a later seq an earlier ts. The renderer's binary searches into status and title segments assume ts order. Name the guard, for example ts = max(now, the document's previous updated_at), or drop the promise.

Strategy Part 1, diff_page: commands.apply_command (src/commands.py line 284) copies the page and then backfills it with initial_sections. The backfill adds any section or field the type gained since the page was created and rewrites every fixed field. Diffing the raw pre-image `page` against `working` therefore records spurious edited events on an older page's first batch after a page-type change. Diff against initial_sections(page_type, before.sections), or treat a missing field as its empty default.

Strategy Part 3: implementation-plan and testing-plan finish at ready, which is before building starts. So every step done and case passed - the most frequent activity the goal mwjqdpi7-2c4835 lists - arrives after the plan has merged back into its feature's track as a settled glyph. The page does not say where those ticks are drawn. The static dataset the user judged has no element events, so this look has never been seen. Say where the ticks go, or list it under Left to the builder.

Expected changes: tests/test_store.py, tests/test_serialize.py, tests/test_cleanup.py and README.md are existing paths that no investigation lists as a component; only tests/test_web.py is listed. That is fine for test and doc companions. But the non-goals criterion verifies 'the MCP tool list has no new tool' in tests/test_server.py, which is not in Expected changes, and no test there lists the tools today. So no feature-brief owns that assertion. Add tests/test_server.py as a modify, or verify the non-goal in tests/test_web.py.

Acceptance criteria, non-goals mwjq5k9n-fee441 and mwjq5k9o-ab2c91: the text still says 'its three routes are GET'. That count belongs to the removed test page. The strategy (Part 2), the web-routes interface and Expected changes all say two GET routes and 'no other timeline route'. A reviewer checking this criterion would look for a third route that must not exist. Say 'its two routes' (/ws:<id>/timeline and /ws:<id>/timeline.json).

Approach, first alternative (Replay the history pasta already stores), whyNot: it still says 'The user also ruled out back-filling the past in this epic: ... The answer is no.' That is no longer true. Goal mwjq5k9h-c0b064 now back-fills the existing workspace once in this epic, and the fifth alternative and the back-fill decision both record the user's sign-off answer. The section exists to stop the choice being reopened during the build, so it must not contradict the goal. Say instead that the user later chose the PR-history back-fill (question mwkyxzm2-bcbf16) rather than snapshot mining, and that only the id-timestamp finding is kept, to set the back-fill's create times.

solution-investigation:mwjqeeod-1aa130.title: Replay the history pasta already stores for the workspace

understanding.body: Build the timeline without touching the write path: walk whatever change history pasta already stores for a workspace, extract time-stamped events (page created, status moved, reparented, linked/unlinked, renamed, archived/unarchived, element activity), and serve the ordered stream to the web UI. The ask (outcome mwjq5k99) is a replay driven by history recorded over time, not reconstructed from current state. The direction as written diverges from the code on its core assumption: pasta stores no change history. The scope calls it 'the history scheduled workspace cleanup compacts', but cleanup compacts nothing - it deletes whole pruned page subtrees after writing a full pre-prune snapshot. A workspace is one JSON snapshot file overwritten on every write; there is no event log, no per-page timestamps, no revision chain. What survives of the past is (1) times embedded in generated ids, (2) up to a dozen snapshot backups. So this direction is a forensic reconstruction from current state plus sparse snapshots, which is what the user's wording rules out.

items.name: src/store.py
items.role: Store: per-workspace JSON snapshot persistence. _write_file atomically replaces the whole file on every commit; _touch_and_save stamps only workspace.updated_at; write_backup writes <data>/backups/<ws_token>/<UTC stamp>.json; cleanup_workspace writes a backup only when it will prune. Holds no history of its own, so a replay reader would be a new read-only method here or beside it.

items.name: src/model.py
items.role: Page and Workspace dataclasses. Page has no created/updated timestamp, no status history; Workspace has only created_at/updated_at. This is why there is nothing to walk.

items.name: src/serialize.py
items.role: Workspace <-> dict mapping used for live files and backups alike; a replay reader would reuse workspace_from_dict to load each snapshot.

items.name: src/ids.py
items.role: new_token builds ids as <base36 ms timestamp>-<random>, used for page ids (type:token) and list-element ids. It is the only place a creation time survives in the data; the replay would decode it.

items.name: src/cleanup.py
items.role: Sweep classification and delete_subtree. Deletes pruned pages after writing the backup; the backup is the only record of a pruned page. Making cleanup keep history would mean changing this module and store.cleanup_workspace.

items.name: src/server.py
items.role: FastAPI app and web routes (route_tree, route_page and POST archive/status routes); a replay endpoint serving the event stream would be a new GET route here. Data dir comes from PASTA_DATA_DIR (default .pasta-data).

items.name: src/event_cache.py
items.role: Transient in-process TTL record of recent per-page events used to throttle repeated guidance delivery; not persisted and not a history. Looked at as a candidate source and ruled out.

items.name: spike/replay_spike.py (spike worktree only)
items.role: Throwaway reader: loads a COPY of the live file and its backups, decodes id timestamps, diffs consecutive snapshots, and counts what is recoverable. Not integrated.

items.text: Workspace data is one JSON file per workspace, replaced whole on each write (src/store.py _write_file: tmp file then os.replace); backups live under <data dir>/backups/<ws_token>/ as colon-free UTC stamps, e.g. 20260921T190516Z.json, via write_backup.

Page ids and element ids are '<base36 ms>-<6 hex>' (src/ids.py new_token); this is the only per-entity time in stored data. status_revision_token is 6 random digits (new_revision_token), carries no time.
requires-python >=3.14 and dependencies in pyproject.toml are fixed (fastapi, fastmcp, jinja2 ...); a reader of JSON files needs none beyond the stdlib.
The direction must add nothing to the write path (direction scope); so no new fields, no hook in mutate_page_batch and no new file may be written on commit.

Backups are never deleted by cleanup (architecture:msrxuvy1-990b09) and write_backup only runs before a prune, so cadence follows pruning, not changes. On disk for pasta's workspace: 12 write_backup snapshots under backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6/ (2026-08-21 to 2026-09-27) plus one stray full root-level document backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json (mtime 2026-11-10, 2.39 MB, not written by write_backup; origin unknown, so a reader cannot rely on such files existing). Two more stray root files belong to other workspaces.

The direction's premise ('history scheduled cleanup compacts', 'enough to recover each page's type, parent, status and elements at that change') collides with src/model.py and src/store.py: no per-change record exists, so status, parent, link, rename and archive changes have no times.
Outcome mwjq5k99 ('not reconstructed from the pages' current state') cannot be met by this direction: every fact except creation times is reconstructed from the current page plus sparse snapshots.

Outcome mwjq5k9k (cleanup never erases replayed history) would need cleanup to keep deleted pages' state; src/cleanup.py delete_subtree removes pages and the unfiltered backup is the only remnant. Making cleanup keep them is a write-path change, which this direction forbids. No in-flight page found that changes this: searched pasta workspace for history/timeline pages; only this epic's three investigations.

architecture:msrxuvy1-990b09 Scheduled workspace cleanup: calls backups 'full timestamped workspace backup before any deletion' and says every workspace 'carried its whole history forever'; the latter is about page count, not change history. Would need a note that backups are the only past a replay can use if this direction is built.

architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4 Authoring & mutation: describes copy -> edit -> atomic overwrite with no log; stays accurate under this direction (write path untouched), and is the page that would go stale under the event-log direction instead.

architecture:mrtqsu5j-4643c4 Archiving and architecture:mrteq39m-de7a49 Pasta Project Overview: not opened in full; archive flags are visible as the archived/delete_scheduled booleans in src/model.py, which carry no time.

items.name: Event sourcing versus state snapshots (known pattern)
items.finding: A timeline of past states is derived from an append-only event log, or from periodic snapshots with diffs; deriving it from the latest state alone is impossible, and snapshots only give state at snapshot instants.
items.bearing: Pasta has snapshots only (12 sparse backups) and no log, so this direction is the weak snapshot-diff half of the pattern; the log half is the other investigator's direction.

items.name: Opened nothing outside the repo (no web search allowed)
items.finding: The question is internal: what the store keeps. I checked the store source, the live data and the backups instead of outside sources.
items.bearing: No library changes the answer; JSON files loaded with the stdlib are enough for the reader.

sketch.body: A read-only module (new, beside src/store.py) loads the workspace's live JSON via serialize.workspace_from_dict plus every snapshot found under backups/: the write_backup files in backups/<ws_token>/ ordered by stamp, and any stray root-level backups/<ws_token>.json, dated by file mtime (the spike now reads both). It emits events: page_created and element_added from decoding the base36 timestamp in each page id and element id (exact to the millisecond); and, for each pair of consecutive snapshots, status_changed, parent changed, archived toggled, title changed and link added/removed - stamped with the SNAPSHOT time, not the true change time. Pages missing from the next snapshot become removed events. A new GET route in src/server.py returns the sorted stream as JSON to the UI, cached per file mtime. Spike on a copy (spike/replay_spike.py, commit bc4d65b): load 14.5 MB (live + 13 snapshots) in about 0.5s, whole build under 0.8s, about 9,400 events. Nothing is added to the write path, but the status history of the 157 pages now past draft/active is unrecoverable between snapshot instants; the newest snapshot is the 2026-11-10 stray file, so state changes after 2026-11-10 have no snapshot at all and creation times only.

items.name: Interpolate statuses between snapshots
items.reason: Ruled out: it would show statuses the page may never have held at those moments, which is anti-goal mwjq5k9r.

items.name: Show only creation, element_added and snapshot diffs honestly (this sketch)
items.reason: Kept: it never fabricates a moment, but is thin.

items.name: Make cleanup also write a backup on every sweep (not only before prune)
items.reason: Dominated by the event-log direction: it still changes persistence, grows disk by 0.5 to 3 MB per sweep per workspace, and gives hourly snapshots rather than true change times.

items.name: Use git history of the repo or the in-memory event_cache
items.reason: Ruled out: .pasta-data/ is gitignored (.gitignore line 7) and event_cache.py is a transient TTL throttle that is never persisted.

assessment.tradeoffs: Buys: zero write-path change, no new storage, no mutation slowdown, and a one-off exact recovery of all 585 pages ever seen and 8,783 element creation times back to 2026-07-20 (the start of the workspace). Costs: no status transitions, reparents, renames, link changes, gate or step completions with true times; only 14 status, 105 archive, 3 title and 2 link changes are detectable between snapshots, each dated to a snapshot instant (days to weeks apart). The graph colours would be flat for most of the replay, the user's anti-goal 'a graph that jumps frame to frame'. Snapshots exist only through 2026-11-10 and the last one is an unexplained stray file, so after it only creation is replayable, and pages pruned after the last write_backup snapshot (2026-09-27) that were not captured by the stray one are lost for ever. It cannot satisfy outcome mwjq5k99 by construction. Useful as the one-time backfill input of the lifecycle-event-log direction, not as the source of the timeline.

fit.note: Scrub, play and pause are UI work over an ordered event stream, which this serves; unaffected by the thin content.
Existence at a moment is right, but status at a moment is unknown between snapshots; any colour shown would be a guess.
Title and type are known; the status shown on hover is correct only at snapshot instants and the creation default.
Nothing is recorded over time; every non-creation fact is reconstructed from the current page and 12 snapshots, exactly what the outcome excludes.
584 pages growing in over four months is visually rich, but without status changes or activity the replay is mostly nodes appearing.
Grow-in on creation and departure on removal can animate; recolouring and pulses have almost no events to drive them.
Spike: whole stream built in 0.64s, about 9,300 events; precompute once and cache per file mtime, so playback is client-side.
Renames, reparents, link changes, gates crossed, steps done, cases passed and content edits have no recoverable time; only creation of elements is dated.

Of the listed facts, page creation, page type and element creation appear; status history, link/nesting history, renames, archives and gate, step and case activity do not, except as coarse snapshot diffs.

Pruned pages survive in the pre-prune backups (386 of 584 pages exist only there), so a replay still sees them, but cleanup keeps nothing but those snapshots and nothing prevents a future change removing them.
Pure read of copies of stored files; no write route.
The stream is served from a web route only; no MCP tool added.
The data alone does not cause a generic chart, but with flat statuses and few events the replay is at risk of looking like pages appearing on a calendar.
A faithful reader avoids false statuses, but a replay must then show a page's final or unknown status from creation, or interpolate between snapshots; either shows a moment the workspace never had.
Write path untouched, so mutations are no slower and cannot fail on recording.
Adds no stored data; existing backups already grow without a retention rule but that is cleanup's pre-existing state.

Creation times are exact for every page; statuses and shipping only appear as snapshot diffs (14 detected across 13 snapshots), so a feature's path through its statuses is mostly missing (sketch; spike).

Replay reaches the workspace's start (2026-07-20) for creations; state changes only from 2026-08-21 through the stray 2026-11-10 snapshot, none after, and the last snapshot is an undocumented stray file rather than a mechanism.

test.predicts: If the direction is right, walking a copy of the stored data for ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6 recovers, with true times, each page's creation, status transitions, reparents, links, renames, archives and element activity.
test.falsifier: Finding that the stored data has no timestamp for status transitions (and the like), so only creation times and snapshot-instant diffs are recoverable.
test.evidence: Worktree .claude/worktrees/spike-timeline-stored-history, commit bc4d65b (branch spike/timeline-stored-history, not pushed; earlier commit 8a55d17 did not read the root-level backup). Read src/model.py, src/serialize.py, src/ids.py, src/store.py (_write_file, write_backup, cleanup_workspace), src/event_cache.py. Copied .pasta-data with timestamps preserved to /tmp/spk/data and ran: python spike/replay_spike.py /tmp/spk/data ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6. Output as of the run: load live + 13 snapshots (12 in backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6/, 1 stray root-level backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json dated 2026-11-10) 0.52s, 14.5 MB; pages ever seen 585, live 199, only in backups 386; events: element_added 8783, page_created 585, archived_changed_by_snapshot 105, status_changed_by_snapshot 14, title_changed_by_snapshot 3 (2 link diffs); snapshots 08-21 to 09-27, 11-10, live 11-16; span 2026-07-20 15:56 to 2026-11-16; 157 live pages carry a non-draft/active status whose transition time is unrecoverable; build 0.78s. The only time-bearing keys in the live file are workspace created_at/updated_at and per-page expires_at (cleanup stamp); page records carry no timestamp. The extra snapshot adds detail but no true change times, so the result is unchanged. The live store was only copied, never written.

items.text: Would the user accept a replay of the past that is only page creations, element growth and coarse snapshot-dated status changes (with true status history only from the day recording ships)?
items.why: Stored data cannot give true status history; only the user can say if a thin history of the past still meets the WOW bar.
items.changes: If yes, this direction can feed a one-time backfill into the lifecycle event log; if no, the past starts on ship day and this direction is dropped.

digest.body: Direction: derive the timeline from stored history, adding nothing to writes. Finding: pasta stores no change history. A workspace is one JSON snapshot rewritten each commit; pages carry no timestamps; cleanup deletes pruned subtrees after a pre-prune backup rather than compacting history. As of the spike run: exact creation times of all 585 pages ever seen and 8,783 elements (decoded from base36 ids, back to 2026-07-20), plus 13 snapshots (12 backups 2026-08-21 to 09-27 and one stray 2026-11-10 file) whose diffs show only 14 status and 105 archive changes, dated to snapshot instants. Status, reparent, link, rename, gate and step history is unrecoverable. Build 0.8s. Cost medium. Fit: 6 yes, 7 partly, 5 no, including the 'recorded over time' goal. Test falsified. Not-viable alone; useful only as a one-time backfill for the event-log direction. One question waits.

findings.issue: The observed claim that no backup exists after 2026-09-27 ('last on 2026-09-27', 'none since', 'everything after 2026-09-27 has creation times only') contradicts solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744, which found a root-level snapshot backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json dated 2026-11-10 (169 pages, 2.39 MB). I opened it: it exists, is a full workspace document for ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6, and holds no page absent from the other snapshots plus live. The recovery window, the fit notes for mwjq5k9h and mwjq5k94, and the sketch must account for the 3 stray snapshots under backups/, which the spike reader does not read. The not-viable call is unaffected, since one more snapshot still gives no true change times.
Counts drift: the page says 198 live pages and 584 ever seen; the live workspace now has 199 and 585. Not an error, but the digest should say 'as of the spike run'.

Sampled and confirmed as observed: Page has no timestamp fields (src/model.py), _write_file replaces the whole file, write_backup only runs before a prune (cleanup_workspace), 12 backups of 259 down to 31 pages, 245 of the oldest snapshot's pages gone from live, 386 pages only in backups. The not-viable call rests on these facts and its falsifier was observable. All 18 outcomes are assessed and the digest counts (6 yes, 7 partly, 5 no) match the fit list.

Earlier blocking finding resolved: the constraint, sketch, tradeoffs, evidence and digest now account for the stray 2026-11-10 snapshot, and spike commit bc4d65b (exists) reads the root-level file by mtime. Counts (585 pages, 199 live, 386 only in backups, 13 snapshots) match the data dir. Remaining nit: the fit notes for mwjq5k99 and mwjq5k9b and the fit for mwjq5k9k still say '12 snapshots' and '584 pages'; the not-viable call is unaffected.

solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744.title: Record a lifecycle event log as pages change

understanding.body: This direction would make pasta write down, at the moment it happens, every lifecycle event of every page - created, status changed, reparented, linked/unlinked, renamed, archived/unarchived, deleted by cleanup, plus element-level activity (a question asked or answered, a step done, a case passed, a content edit) - into a separate append-only log that the cleanup sweep never touches, and serve that log to the web UI as the replay stream. It serves the epic's why directly: the wiki shows only where work stands now, because today pasta stores NO history at all - only the current workspace document, which is rewritten in full on every write, plus a handful of pre-prune snapshots. The user's own framing ("page history recorded over time and served to the web UI as replayable data") names exactly this recording half, so direction and ask agree. One divergence worth knowing: the epic's sibling direction speaks of 'the change history pasta already keeps ... that cleanup compacts'; I found no such change history in the code - the only retained past is the 12 timestamped full-workspace backups the sweep writes before pruning (plus ms timestamps embedded in every page and element id). That makes this direction the only one that yields true event times for anything going forward; the past can only be partly recovered (see backfill in the sketch).

items.name: src/store.py::Store._touch_and_save (line 187)
items.role: The single choke point every persisted workspace mutation goes through: stamps updated_at and calls _write_file. Called from create_page, mutate_page_batch, cleanup_workspace, _set_page_archive_state, set_page_status, reparent_page, reorder_page, rename_page, link_page, unlink_page, _set_workspace_status and set_workspace_guidance (12 sites). The hook would live here or just beside it.

items.name: src/store.py::Store.mutate_page_batch (line 580)
items.role: Runs every page command, compound and addLink/setTitle command inside one transaction lock. Holds both the pre-image (`page`) and post-image (`working`) of the one page, so a scoped diff of status, title, links and per-element sections yields the batch's events with no extra load. Status transitions already detected here (status_before vs working.status).

items.name: src/store.py::create_page / _create_auto_children / reparent_page / reorder_page / rename_page / link_page / unlink_page / _set_page_archive_state / set_page_status
items.role: The non-batch writers. Each knows exactly what it changed (new page + pinned children, old/new parent, old/new title, edge added/removed, archived/delete_scheduled flags with the pinned-child cascade, direct admin status override), so each can emit its own event list into the same save call. set_page_status is the web UI's FSM-bypass override and is not reachable by any command.

items.name: src/store.py::Store.cleanup_workspace + src/cleanup.py::delete_subtree
items.role: The only deleter: prunes whole subtrees and strips links to them inside one lock. The log must record a 'deleted' event per removed page (with its last title, type and status, so a replay can still draw it) and the link strips; it must also not be itself pruned. Stamping expires_at is a hidden page attribute, not a lifecycle event to log.

items.name: src/store.py::Store._write_file / write_backup / create_workspace (lines 175-236)
items.role: _write_file serializes the whole workspace with indent=2 to a pid/thread temp file and os.replace's it under the exclusive rw lock; write_backup reuses it for backups/<ws_token>/<stamp>.json; create_workspace writes the first empty document. The log append would be a second, much smaller I/O beside this one, so the two files are not one atomic commit.

items.name: src/model.py + src/serialize.py (Workspace, workspace_to_dict / workspace_from_dict)
items.role: The on-disk document shape. A small new Workspace field (the sequence number of the last log entry the document reflects) would let a reader detect and truncate log lines written by a transaction whose workspace replace never landed. serialize already loads a missing key as a default, so adding it is backward compatible.

items.name: src/server.py (FastAPI routes, lines 171-300; STORE; ws_reloader websocket)
items.role: The read-only web front door that already serves HTML per workspace and POSTs archive/status overrides straight to Store methods (so those writes are covered by the store hook). A new GET route would return the log (or a time-windowed slice) as JSON for the player. No MCP tool is added (non-goal).

items.name: <PASTA_DATA_DIR>/ (default .pasta-data) listing and cleanup isolation: Store.list_workspaces glob '*.json'; backups/ subdir
items.role: list_workspaces globs *.json non-recursively, which is why backups live in a subdirectory. A log file must likewise not end in .json at the top level: a <data>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl is invisible to the glob and untouched by cleanup, which only ever reads/writes the workspace document and backups/.

items.name: .pasta-data/backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6/*.json (12 snapshots, Aug 21 - Sep 27) + backups/ws_*.json (3 stray root snapshots) + src/ids.py (base-36 ms timestamp in every page and element id)
items.role: The only pre-existing history, and what a one-time backfill would mine: 12 full snapshots of pasta's own workspace (259 pages in the oldest, Aug 21), one stray 2.39 MB snapshot dated Nov 10, and creation times decodable from ids.

items.text: Every workspace write already holds Store._transaction_lock_for(workspace_id) across load-mutate-save; the log append must happen inside that same lock so events are ordered exactly as commits are (src/store.py, create_page .. set_workspace_guidance).

list_workspaces enumerates workspaces with `self.root.glob("*.json")` (non-recursive, src/store.py line 220); any new file next to the workspace document must not match *.json or it shows up as a duplicate workspace, and must not live where cleanup could treat it as a backup.

The pure core (model, pagetypes, fsm, commands, serialize) does no I/O; the layering is server -> store -> pure core (architecture:mrteq39m-de7a49 invariant). Event detection by diff may be a pure function; the append must be in the store.

No new dependencies are needed or wanted: the project requires Python >=3.14 and only FastMCP/statemachine-style deps (pyproject.toml line 6); plain JSON Lines needs only the stdlib. Persistence is deliberately plain files with in-process locking only; cross-process safety is not provided.

Hot reload: src/hmr_server.py keeps only src.event_cache and src._hmr_debug across reloads (kept_unless_changed); any in-memory event counter would be lost on reload, so the next sequence number must be derived from the persisted state, not kept in a module global.

Non-goal / anti-goals from the epic: the timeline is read-only and not exposed over MCP; recording must not make a mutation noticeably slower or let it fail; the log must not grow without bound (epic outcomes mwjq5k9n-fee441, mwjq5k9o-ab2c91, mwjq5k9s-1bc2cd, mwjq5k9t-1f8a0e).

architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4 invariant 'Every write is copy -> edit -> atomic overwrite ... a crash mid-write cannot corrupt the workspace file' - a second file cannot be inside that atomic replace. Two-file commits are only crash-consistent via a reconciliation rule (workspace stores the last sequence it reflects; readers/writers truncate a log tail beyond it). That is a new invariant the architecture page would need.

Scheduled cleanup (src/cleanup.py, architecture:msrxuvy1-990b09) 'Workspaces only ever grew' - its Purpose is bounding storage. An append-only log is by construction unbounded; it must be kept small by coalescing and payload-free events, and its retention is a policy cleanup would have to be told about (cleanup must never compact it, outcome mwjq5k9k-d543aa) - a deliberate exception to 'the one path that destroys data'.

src/event_cache.py already exists but is unrelated: a transient in-process TTL cache (page_events) used only to decide when to repeat stage guidance in server.py (lines 59, 546). Name collision risk only; it is non-persistent and keyed per (workspace, page, event), so it cannot be extended into a log. The new log needs a different name (e.g. 'lifecycle log').

Competing in-flight change: searched the workspace for other pages touching history or event recording (search 'history', 'event log', 'timeline') and found only this epic; the sibling investigations (replay existing history; cinematic UI) are directions of the same epic, not code changes. No conflicting feature-brief found.

architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4 Authoring & mutation: its invariant that every write is a single atomic overwrite, and its description of mutate_page_batch's result and the per-workspace lock, would need a paragraph on the log append and the reconciliation rule; the code-references list would gain the new emit function.
