items.name: Event sourcing / append-only audit log (known pattern; no external page opened)
items.finding: No outside source was opened - web search is barred and no named upstream URL was needed. The pattern itself: an append-only journal of immutable, timestamped, ordered events with a monotonically increasing sequence number, from which state at any instant is rebuilt by folding events up to that instant.
items.bearing: Maps one-to-one onto a scrubbable player: state-at-time-T is a fold over events <= T; keyframe snapshots every N events keep scrubbing O(window) rather than O(history). Pitfall known from the pattern: a log written separately from the state it describes needs a sequence/commit reconciliation rule.

items.name: In-repo precedent: cleanup backups and src/event_cache.py
items.finding: Opened both. Backups are full timestamped snapshots under backups/<ws_token>/ written with the same serializer; event_cache keeps transient per-page records and is explicitly not persisted. Neither is a log, but the backups dir proves a sibling subdirectory is the accepted way to keep files out of the *.json workspace glob.
items.bearing: Gives the file-placement precedent (subdirectory, colon-free names for Windows) and confirms no existing mechanism to reuse for persistence.

items.name: Installed dependencies (pyproject.toml)
items.finding: Checked the dependency list: nothing for event stores or databases; the stdlib covers JSON Lines and file append. sqlite3 is in the stdlib but not used anywhere.
items.bearing: Keeps the direction dependency-free; JSONL fits the repo's plain-file, human-diffable persistence style, whereas sqlite would introduce a second storage technology.

sketch.body:
WHERE EVERY MUTATION COMMITS. All persisted writes funnel through Store._touch_and_save (src/store.py:187) -> _write_file; the only other _write_file callers are create_workspace (empty doc) and write_backup. Twelve store methods call _touch_and_save, and the MCP tools, the web POST routes (archive, unarchive, schedule-delete, status override) and the hourly sweep all reach the store only through those methods - so one hook does see every change, including createPage + pinned auto-children, reparent, rename, link/unlink, archive/unarchive (with the pinned-child cascade), the web status override, cleanup deletes, and compounds (a compound is applied inside mutate_page_batch). Caveat found: 'one hook' is one call site, not one automatic detector - _touch_and_save receives only the mutated workspace, not what changed. Two ways to get the events: (a) whole-workspace diff against a pre-image taken at load; or (b) each method passes the events it knows. Measured on pasta's own 2.8 MB / 198-page / ~4,000-element workspace (read-only, in memory): json.loads 56-140 ms, a deepcopy pre-image 85 ms, a naive whole-workspace diff 67 ms, against the 113 ms json.dumps the write already pays - so (a) adds roughly +50-100% per write; (b) adds almost nothing. Sketch picks (b) with a scoped diff for the batch: mutate_page_batch already holds `page` (pre) and `working` (post), and diffing one page's status/title/links/elements is sub-millisecond; every other method emits a fixed event. Safety net: a test that drives each store method and asserts a non-empty event list, and an assertion that _touch_and_save was given events.

WHAT IS NEW. (1) src/lifecycle_log.py (pure): event schema {seq, ts, page, kind, ...kind-specific fields} and the pure functions diff_page(before, after) and the fixed event constructors; kinds: created (type, title, parent, status), status (from, to), moved (from_parent, to_parent), linked/unlinked (to, role), renamed (title), archived/unarchived, scheduled/unscheduled-delete, deleted (title, type, last status - so a replay can still draw it), and element-level el_added/el_status/el_edited keyed by section, field and element id (questions asked -> answered, steps -> done, cases -> passed, gate-like human decisions) with NO content text, only ids and the element's status value, to keep lines small and avoid leaking page text into a second file. (2) Store gains _append_events(workspace, events) called from _touch_and_save inside the transaction lock; it opens <data>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl in append mode and writes one line per event, with seq = workspace.event_seq + n. (3) Workspace/serialize gain event_seq (default 0) = last seq the saved document reflects. (4) server.py gains a read-only GET e.g. /ws:{id}/timeline.json that streams the log, with optional ?after=<seq>&until=<ts> windows; no MCP tool.

COMMIT ORDER AND CRASH CONSISTENCY. Inside the lock: append events (fsync optional) THEN os.replace the workspace with event_seq advanced. A crash between leaves log lines with seq > workspace.event_seq: the next transaction (or the reader) truncates the tail beyond event_seq, so the log never describes a commit that did not land. Opposite failure - replace done, event append failed - cannot occur in this order; if the append itself raises, the mutation proceeds and a single 'gap' marker is recorded at the next success (recording must never fail a write, outcome mwjq5k9s-1bc2cd), and the replay shows that stretch as approximate. Reads of the log take the existing rw lock shared half; the web route never takes the transaction lock.

HOW IT STAYS BOUNDED AND OUTSIDE CLEANUP. It lives in <PASTA_DATA_DIR>/events/ - a subdirectory so list_workspaces' *.json glob cannot see it, and not under backups/. cleanup.py and Store.cleanup_workspace never read or write it; cleanup_workspace gains one hook to append 'deleted' events for every pruned page in the same locked pass, so a replay of a period looks identical before and after a sweep. Size: events are ~100-200 bytes, no text bodies; coalescing consecutive same-element edits within a short window (say 60 s) and not logging expires_at stamps, reorder-only moves or guidance edits keeps the rate to the order of a few thousand lines a month for a workspace like pasta's own (visible lower bound: 315 elements added, 58 changed, 102 removed and 184 pages created in the Aug 21 -> Nov 16 span alone) - single-digit MB a year, against a 2.8 MB document rewritten on every write. Segment by month (events/<ws>/<yyyymm>.jsonl) if a single file ever gets too large to serve; old segments can be gzipped, never dropped by cleanup. It is bounded in growth rate, not in total size, which is the honest limit of any append-only log.

COST PER WRITE. Append of 1-10 lines (~1 KB) inside a lock that already holds a 113 ms serialize plus a ~2.8 MB temp write and replace: well under 1-2 ms with approach (b), so no noticeable slowdown. The one real cost is the scoped diff on mutate_page_batch (<1 ms).

BACKFILL (one-time script, quick look only). What exists: 12 timestamped full snapshots of ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6 (Aug 21 -> Sep 27; 259 pages in the oldest, 31 in the last), 3 stray root-level snapshots under backups/ (one for pasta's own workspace, Nov 10, 2.39 MB), the live document (Jul 20 -> Nov 16, 198 pages), and base-36 millisecond timestamps in every page id and element id (checked: the earliest live page id decodes to 2026-07-20 15:56:24, the workspace's created_at). Recoverable: a created event with real ms time for every page or element that appears in any snapshot or the live file; status-at-snapshot for each of 13 sample instants since Aug 21 (a status change is knowable only as 'between snapshot A and B'); link, parent, archived and rename differences between snapshots; deletions as 'disappeared between A and B' (245 pages present in the Aug 21 snapshot are gone from the live file). Not recoverable: anything from Jul 20 to Aug 21 other than creation times of pages that survived to a snapshot; pages created and deleted between snapshots; intermediate statuses and exact times of status changes, renames, link changes; any element edits. So backfill reaches back to Jul 20 for existence and to Aug 21 for sampled status - enough for a partial replay, not for a true one. Backfilled events must be flagged approximate so the player does not show a status a page never held at that instant (anti-goal mwjq5k9r-d69675). Mining the snapshots in depth belongs to the sibling investigator.

items.name: Embed the event list inside the workspace document (one more top-level key)
items.reason: Gives true atomicity with the page commit and needs no second file or reconciliation. Ruled out: the document is re-serialized with indent=2 in full on every write (2.8 MB, 113 ms), so an ever-growing list makes every write slower for ever (anti-goal mwjq5k9t-1f8a0e), and cleanup/backups would copy it. Only worth reconsidering for a tiny bounded recent-events ring, which does not meet the replay goal.

items.name: Whole-workspace diff at _touch_and_save against a pre-image taken at load (automatic, cannot miss a mutation)
items.reason: Strongest completeness guarantee, but measured at +50-100% per write (deepcopy 85 ms + diff 67 ms on the live 2.8 MB workspace) and it infers what happened (cannot tell a rename from delete+create, nor the actor/intent behind a direct status override). Kept only as a test oracle: a test replaying events must equal a diff of before/after.

items.name: SQLite (stdlib) event table instead of JSON Lines
items.reason: Would give atomic multi-row commits and indexed range queries, but is a second storage technology in a project whose persistence is deliberately plain human-readable files with only in-process locks, and two files still would not commit atomically with the JSON workspace. Dominated by JSONL plus the event_seq reconciliation rule for this scale.

items.name: In-memory event cache extended (src/event_cache.py)
items.reason: Transient by design and keyed per (workspace, page, event) with a TTL; it is lost on restart and, unlike the rest of the process, is explicitly allowed to forget. Cannot be a replay source.

items.name: Log as page content (a 'history' page or section written via mutatePageBatch)
items.reason: Would make every mutation write a second page transaction, change the user-visible wiki, be exposed over MCP (a non-goal), and be pruned/archived by the page lifecycle. Works against the why.

assessment.tradeoffs:
BUYS: the only direction that records TRUE event times and ordering (not just snapshots) for everything from the day it ships - every status move, nesting, link, rename, archive, deletion and element-level activity - as ready-to-serve, ordered, replay-shaped data with no reconstruction at read time; cheap per write (an append of ~1 KB beside a 2.8 MB rewrite); immune to cleanup by placement and by emitting 'deleted' events; no new dependency; keeps the pure core pure. Also unlocks later things for free: activity heatmaps, 'what changed since' views, an audit trail.

COSTS / RISKS: (1) Touches all 12 write paths in store.py plus cleanup - an omitted emit is silent (mitigated by a per-method test and a diff-oracle test). (2) A second file cannot be in the atomic replace, so a new invariant (event_seq reconciliation, truncate the tail) is needed and the architecture pages updated; crash-safety is eventual, not atomic. (3) Replay begins on ship day: without the backfill the demo workspace would be nearly empty for the first weeks, which hurts the WOW goal; the backfill only partly rescues it (Jul 20 existence, Aug 21+ sampled statuses, approximate flags) and is itself a one-off script to write and trust. (4) The log is unbounded in total size by nature; kept to ~single-digit MB a year by payload-free, coalesced events and monthly segments. (5) Element-level activity needs a generic element diff keyed by id/status, tied to each page type's element FSMs (questions, steps, cases) - modest but real coupling to page-type shape. (6) Event schema becomes a contract: renames or new kinds must stay backward compatible, since old events are never rewritten.

COMPARED BESIDE the 'replay stored history' direction: that one adds nothing to the write path but, per what I found, has only 13 sparse snapshots to mine and no true timestamps; this direction costs more code but is the only one that makes the replay accurate and complete for new activity. The two compose: backfill = the other investigator's snapshot mining writing into this log.

fit.note: Created, every status and ship/archive/delete events are recorded with true times from ship day (sketch: event kinds created/status/archived/deleted); the past before ship is outcome mwjq5k9h-c0b064.

Ordered, seq-numbered events with timestamps are exactly what scrub/play/pause folds over; the log serves them via a read-only /timeline.json with after/until windows. The player itself is the other investigator's.

Exact for everything recorded after ship (event_seq reconciliation keeps the log free of uncommitted events). Backfilled stretches are only snapshot-sampled, so a status could be shown at the wrong instant; they must be flagged approximate.

Created and status events carry type, title, status and renames carry the new title, so title+status at any moment is derivable; deleted events keep last title/type/status so even pruned pages hover correctly.
This direction is the outcome: history is recorded over time at write and served as data, not reconstructed from current state.

The log supplies rich, accurately timed and typed raw material (including activity events for pulses) but WOW is delivered by the renderer; with an empty or sparse early history the first impression suffers until backfill/activity accrues.
Discrete typed events (created, status from->to, deleted, archived) are the triggers for grow-in, recolour and depart animations; from/to values let the renderer tween a recolour rather than cut.

Smoothness is a rendering matter, but the data side is helped: payload-free ~150-byte events, windowed fetches and periodic keyframes keep client folding cheap. Not proven here; no spike of playback was run.
The log is type-agnostic: every page type, status, parent/link edge and element activity is an event; nothing is filtered to feature pages.

Each listed item has an event kind: page creation per type incl. auto-children, status, nesting (moved), links made/removed, renames, archive/unarchive, and element-level questions asked/answered, steps done, cases passed, gates crossed (status events), content edits (el_edited). Verifiable in a replay of pasta's own workspace once data exists.

Backfill reaches Jul 20 for existence (ids carry ms timestamps) and Aug 21 onward for sampled statuses (12 snapshots + 1 stray + live); pages created and deleted between snapshots, exact status times and element edits are unrecoverable. Not 'earliest history', only the earliest recoverable.

The log lives in <data>/events/, which cleanup never touches, and the sweep appends 'deleted' events with the page's last title/type/status in the same locked pass, so a period replays identically before and after a sweep.
The only new surface is a GET route that reads the log; the log is written by the store as a side effect of existing mutations, never from the timeline view.
No MCP tool is added; serving is a FastAPI route only.
Not decided by the data layer: the log itself neither causes nor prevents a generic-looking view; it only guarantees real, fine-grained, timed events for the renderer to make striking.

Avoided for recorded history by construction (events written in the commit, reconciled by event_seq); not avoided for backfilled periods, where a status is only known at snapshot instants and must be marked approximate rather than drawn as exact.

Append of ~1 KB beside a write that already serializes 2.8 MB in ~113 ms (measured); scoped diff <1 ms; an append failure is swallowed and recorded as a gap marker so a mutation never fails because of the log.

Growth is linear in activity not in total workspace size, payload-free and coalesced (est. single-digit MB per year for pasta's own), and every write path stays untouched by log size; but an append-only log is unbounded in total by definition and needs monthly segments/gzip if it ever grows.

test.predicts: Every persisted workspace change passes through Store._touch_and_save (the only other _write_file callers being create_workspace and write_backup), so one hook there sees createPage, batches and compounds, reparent, rename, link/unlink, archive/unarchive, the web status override and cleanup deletes; and recording costs far less than the 113 ms serialize each write already pays.
test.falsifier: A code path that changes a persisted workspace without going through _touch_and_save, or a mutation (for example a compound step or a pinned-child cascade) whose effect cannot be named from the pre-state and post-state of the page it touches; or a measured per-write recording cost comparable to the existing serialize.
test.evidence: Read-only; no worktree, no spike, no files written, live store untouched (opened .pasta-data files only for reading and for in-memory timing). (1) Read src/store.py in full around every writer (lines 175-1000) and grepped for _write_file/_touch_and_save across src, scripts and tests: _write_file is called only from _touch_and_save, create_workspace and write_backup; _touch_and_save is called from 12 store methods; scripts/ do not write workspaces; server.py reaches the store only via STORE.* methods (archive, unarchive, schedule/unschedule delete, set_page_status), so the web routes are covered. mutate_page_batch applies compounds inside the same transaction and holds page (pre) and working (post). (2) In-memory timing on the live 2,817,777-byte workspace (198 pages, ~4,039 id-bearing nodes): file read + json.loads 140 ms (second parse 56 ms), json.dumps(indent=2) 113 ms, deepcopy 85 ms, naive element-level diff of two full workspaces 67 ms. (3) Diff of the oldest backup (Aug 21, 259 pages) against live gave 184 pages created, 245 deleted, 315 elements added, 102 removed, 58 changed, 1 rename - showing element-level events are derivable by id/status diff, and how much the snapshots miss. (4) Id decoding: base-36 ms prefix of the earliest live page id = 2026-07-20 15:56:24 UTC = workspace created_at. (5) Backups listed: 12 snapshots Aug 21 - Sep 27 with page counts 259, 115, 112, 65, 70, 60, 65, 73, 45, 42, 29, 31, plus 3 stray root snapshots. Untested: an actual hook, playback, and real log growth rate (the single-digit MB/year figure is an estimate from snapshot diffs, not a measurement).

items.text: Is a replay that is exact only from ship day, with the earlier past shown as approximate (snapshot-sampled from Aug 21, existence-only from Jul 20), acceptable for the first release?
items.why: No history with true event times exists today, so the backfill can only approximate the past; only the user can say whether an approximate early replay of pasta's own workspace is worth showing or whether to wait until real events accrue.
items.changes: If approximate is acceptable the one-time backfill is built and its events flagged approximate; if not, the backfill is dropped and cost falls, but the replay starts empty on ship day.

digest.body: Direction: a dedicated append-only JSONL lifecycle log (<data>/events/<ws>.jsonl) written by the store in each mutation's lock and served read-only to the web UI. Shaping facts: pasta stores no history today, only the live 2.8 MB document plus 12 sparse cleanup snapshots; every persisted write funnels through Store._touch_and_save (12 callers, web and sweep included), so one hook sees all changes; recording is ~1 KB against a 113 ms serialize. Cost: medium. Fit: 11 yes, 7 partly, 0 no - partly on WOW, smoothness, anti-generic, backfill reach, replay of approximate stretches and unbounded total size. Backfill recovers existence from Jul 20 and sampled statuses from Aug 21 only. Test: held (read and timed, no spike). Viability: viable-with-caveats - accept replay exact only from ship day, a reconciliation rule for the second file, and a partial, approximate backfill. Questions: 1.

findings.issue: Sampled observed entries checked out: _write_file is called only from _touch_and_save, create_workspace and write_backup; _touch_and_save has exactly 12 callers; list_workspaces globs *.json non-recursively; the 12 backups (259 down to 31 pages), the 3 stray root snapshots including the Nov 10 one, and the 245 pages gone since the oldest snapshot all match the data dir. The direction stays in scope, all 18 outcomes are assessed, and the digest counts (11 yes, 7 partly, 0 no) match.

The test is marked held, but the per-write cost of the chosen approach (b) was not measured; only serialize, deepcopy and whole-diff times were. 'Well under 1-2 ms' and the single-digit MB a year are estimates. The evidence says so, but the digest and the fit notes state them as findings.

The event vocabulary (created, moved, linked, el_added/el_status/el_edited without text) differs from the one the graph investigation (solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c) assumes (create, reparent, link, activity with a what). The gap and approximate markers are also absent from that shape. The blocking mismatch is recorded on the graph page; this page should name the mapping when revised.

solution-investigation:mwjqegei-6e465c.title: A clean, sharp timeline of nodes in the web UI

understanding.body: Build only the rendering half, as the user reshaped it: a 2D page in the existing read-only web UI where time is the horizontal axis. Every page is a node laid out along time - a node at its creation and a node at each status move, with a ship or finish marker, and the renderer also has marks for archive, delete, rename, move, typed links and element activity - and a vertical playhead that a play/pause/scrub player moves through it. Left of the playhead is the recorded past in solid status colour; right of it is the known future as a faint grey ghost (toggleable); a header chip row counts the workspace by status so a moment reads at a glance. Hovering a page gives its title and status at the playhead and at the cursor. The look is flat fills, hairlines and type: no glow, bloom, gradient or additive light, and, since round 3, no animated circles: every mark is fully drawn and static the instant the playhead reaches it. The browser is handed the ordered lifecycle-log event list and folds it per page; where history comes from belongs to the other two directions. For judging the look the user asked for a much sparser static dataset: one page per each of the 127 real moments of this repo, titled with the real PR title or commit line, created then and finished one hour later (a feature-brief with its implementation plan and testing plan). The user's why (the wiki shows where work stands, not how it got there; WOW matters most) is served by the layouts built here as three candidate pages the user can open from disk and judge. The direction and the ask do not diverge.

items.name: src/server.py
items.role: FastAPI app: routes /, /ws:<id>, /ws:<id>/page/<id>; StaticFiles mounts /static and /sphinx; no-cache middleware; /ws/reloader websocket. A timeline adds one read-only HTML route and one JSON route for the event list beside route_tree, taking the shared read lock like them.

items.name: src/templates/_base.html
items.role: Shell every view extends: water.css startup and dynamic stylesheets, styles.css, inline reloader script, theme form, footer, floating Top link. The timeline template extends it but needs a full-viewport body, so its head block and #content width get overridden.

items.name: src/templates/tree.html and src/templates/_nav.html
items.role: Workspace tree view and page-view sidebar; the natural places for an entry link to the timeline (next to Show archived).

items.name: src/templates/_theme.js and src/static/styles.css
items.role: Light/Dark toggle sets class light|dark on body and swaps /static/water.css/<theme>.min.css; styles.css overrides use water.css custom properties (--background-body, --links, --text-main ...). The graph canvas reads those properties via getComputedStyle at theme change so it follows the theme; status hues are a small new palette block beside body.light/body.dark.

items.name: src/templates/_reloader.js, src/hmr_live_refresh.py
items.role: Every page opens /ws/reloader and does location.reload() on refresh=1, fired after every mutation. On a timeline page that would restart playback each time an agent writes; the timeline template needs to keep playhead position (sessionStorage like the scroll position already is) or listen without reloading, and could later use the same socket to append live events.

items.name: src/pagetypes/core/pagetype.py and src/pagetypes/_registry.py
items.role: Declare every page type's status machine (20 distinct statuses occur in pasta's own workspace). The status colour and type size tables for the graph are keyed by these names; a fallback hue covers any status the table does not know, so a new page type never breaks the view.

items.name: src/store.py (event source, not owned by this direction)
items.role: Store.tree/load_workspace/get_page read the workspace JSON under the readers-writer lock. Whichever history source is chosen produces the ordered events this renderer consumes; its output is the only coupling.

items.name: tests/test_web.py
items.role: Existing web-surface tests with a client fixture; would gain route and static-asset checks for the timeline page and the JSON endpoint shape.

items.name: src/static/timeline/ (new: timeline.js, timeline.css; spike precedent spike/timeline/tl.js 30 KB, app.js 9 KB)
items.role: The renderer: event fold into per-page lifetimes, three layout functions (lanes, metro, bands), a Canvas2D drawer at device pixel ratio, playhead player, hover hit-test, theme tokens. Hand-written with no third-party library, so nothing is vendored and nothing needs a build step; served by the existing /static mount. The spike files in .claude/worktrees/spike-timeline-node-timeline/spike/timeline/ are the throwaway precedent, not code to merge.

items.name: spike/timeline/dataset.js, build-dataset.mjs, data/ (spike only; later a test fixture)
items.role: The static dataset the three candidate pages replay as their only data, loaded by relative path with no generator at load: 620 lifecycle-log events (only created and status) for 311 pages, one page per each of the 127 real moments (PRs #1-#65 of dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev and the 62 dated lines of initial commit 463cf4f), titled with the real PR title or commit line. build-dataset.mjs derives it from real-dates.js, data/pr-titles.json (titles re-read through the GitHub MCP) and data/initial-commit-463cf4f-message.txt; data/page-types-by-moment.txt lists the type chosen per moment.

items.name: spike/timeline/check.js, bench.mjs, run-all.sh (spike only)
items.role: check.js is the committed correctness command for the static dataset (every created event on a real moment, finish one hour later, plans finish before their feature, real titles, parents, fold never shows a page outside its lifetime, metro tracks never overlap, layout heights); bench.mjs and run-all.sh are the headless-Edge frame-pacing driver over the static dataset.

items.name: spike/timeline/gen.js, real-dates.js, check-stress.js (stress measurements only; no page loads them)
items.role: The seeded generator of rounds 1 and 2 and its check, kept only so the stress figures at commit e40aa12 (generated history of 191, 567 and 1,881 pages on the same 120 real days) stay reproducible. real-dates.js is still read by build-dataset.mjs for the 127 moments. The candidate pages do not load gen.js.

items.text: No front-end build step: pyproject.toml lists only Python dependencies, the repo has no package.json or node_modules, and the UI is Jinja templates (src/templates) plus plain files served from src/static through app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="src/static")) in src/server.py. Third-party front-end code is therefore vendored as committed minified files, the precedent being src/static/water.css/.

The web UI is strictly read-only (architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5 invariant): routes project store data and take only the shared half of the workspace readers-writer lock; the timeline view and any JSON route must make no change.

Styling rule: every colour comes from a water.css custom property so both themes follow (styles.css .pasta-page block, architecture invariant). A canvas cannot use CSS directly, so the renderer must read the properties with getComputedStyle and redraw on the theme toggle; status hues that no water.css property provides need an explicit light and dark value each.

Smoothness target (epic outcome mwjq5k9d-6b6bde): no visible stutter or blank frames on a workspace the size of pasta's own in a current desktop browser. Pasta's own workspace file ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json, re-counted in round 2: 199 pages (35 feature-briefs each with plan/testing/spec children, 22 agent-plans, 10 architecture, 9 bug-reports...), 52 typed links, 22 distinct statuses. The live figures drift as agents work; the design should size for hundreds of nodes, not for exactly 199.

Static assets are served with 'Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate' for everything but .css (add_no_cache_headers in src/server.py), so a timeline script is refetched on every load; the hand-written renderer is about 30 KB unminified (spike tl.js 29.9 KB, app.js 9.1 KB) and needs no other file. Re-opened src/server.py in round 3: /static mount at line 77, no Content-Security-Policy set anywhere.

Licences: the pick needs no third-party JS, so no licence question arises; the d3 modules weighed (d3-scale, d3-axis, d3-zoom, d3-shape) are ISC, compatible with the AGPL-3.0 footer notice, and npm shows them at 15.7, 3.1, 9.9 and 30.9 KB minified (4.9, 1.3, 3.4, 7.7 KB gzipped) before their own dependencies.

Canvas cost scales with pixel area, not node count. On the static dataset (311 pages) a full redraw per frame stays clean at device pixel ratio 2 too (steady p99 16.9 to 17.1 ms, none over 33 ms, draw body p95 1.8 to 3.2 ms), but a software raster still misses (10, 33 and 18 of about 540 steady frames over 33 ms for lanes, metro and bands). At the generated stress case (567 pages, commit e40aa12) ratio 2 missed 37, 413 and 31 of about 540 for lanes, metro and bands.

The user's dataset (epic answer, recorded in round 3): replay the 127 real moments of this repo, 119.5 days from 2026-07-20 to 2026-11-16 on 43 distinct days (median gap 0.17 days, 90th percentile 2.0 days, longest 16.1 days), one feature-brief, simple-change or bug-report per moment titled with the real PR title or commit line, created then finished one hour later, no generator at load. Consequence for the view: at a 3-day window a one-hour life is about 17 px wide and most of the 120 days is empty, so the player must skip idle stretches (done: a next moment more than 6 hours ahead plays 6 times faster) and every page is a short burst. Dates and titles read through the GitHub MCP, not local git.

src/templates/_reloader.js reloads the whole page on every refresh=1 broadcast (fired by each MCP mutation and each source change). A timeline page left playing would be reset every time an agent writes. Needs the timeline to persist the playhead across the reload or opt out; touches a shared script every view includes.

src/templates/_base.html assumes the water.css reading column (body.page max-width 1000px, h1 title, footer, Top link). A full-viewport canvas conflicts with that, so the timeline needs its own body class and template block rather than reusing page layout; the Top link and footer would overlay the player bar.

Colour tokens: the Pink theme brief (feature-brief:mvfc3sbi-d512cc, feature-spec:mvfc3sbi-f7f8ed) describes :root:has(> body.light|dark) overrides of the water.css custom properties, but those blocks are not in src/static/styles.css at main 64f88f4 (grep for pink finds nothing). The graph should read tokens via getComputedStyle so it works with whichever palette is live; it should not hardcode a pink.

Searched for competing in-flight work on the same files: the only open sibling pages are the two other solution-investigations and agent-plans of this epic (history source), which own src/store.py and src/cleanup.py, not the UI. No other brief touches src/templates or src/static/ for a timeline.

The epic says the view shows the workspace 'exactly as it stood at the selected moment' (mwjq5k97-712194) while a time axis shows the whole history at once. The playhead model resolves it (solid past, grey ghost future, status rings and the status count row at the playhead) but a viewer can still read the future as fact unless it is dimmed or hidden; the ghost is a toggle (key G) and its default is a user taste call.

Legibility versus 'everything is shown' (outcome mwjqdpi7-2c4835). On the static dataset (311 pages over 119.5 days) the layouts size very differently: lanes 4,354 px tall (one row per page ever created, so it needs a vertical camera that follows the activity), metro 635 px (14 tracks including 2 trunks, 12 without; one screen) and bands 607 px (6 type bands; one screen). The layout is not the limit: the user's dataset has only created and status events for six page types, so links, element activity, archives and renames, which the renderer can draw, are not on the screen to judge. At the generated stress case (e40aa12, same 120 days) heights grow with the page count: lanes 2,674 / 7,938 / 26,334 px, metro 1,026 / 1,213 / 2,930 px (35 / 70 / 171 tracks including 4 trunks), bands 750 / 1,355 / 2,664 px at 191 / 567 / 1,881 pages.

sketch.body:
REPLAY DATA SHAPE: the lifecycle-log vocabulary of solution-investigation:mwjqeflc-60f744, with a key mapping instead of a claim of identity. That page fixes a line as {seq, ts, page, kind, ...}; the spike uses {seq, t, id, k, ...} for the same fields, so a production fold either renames at the JSON route or reads the log's names (one function). Kinds and payloads agree: created {type,title,parent,status}; status {from,to}; moved; linked/unlinked; renamed; archived/unarchived; deleted; el_added/el_status/el_edited; gap. The renderer needs three things the log page does not serve and the timeline.json route of this direction would add from src/pagetypes: a header {workspace, t0, t1}, a types table {type: {size, elements, gateEdges}} and the list of done-class statuses (hard-coded in tl.js, line 9, as the ship test; 'ready' and 'closed' were added for the plan and simple-change finish statuses). The static dataset uses only created and status.

THE DATASET IT PLAYS (the only data of the three candidate pages, spike/timeline/dataset.js, no generator at load). The user's words: for the 127 real merges assume one feature OR simple change OR bug-report; register the create event and one hour later the finished event; a feature has its implementation plan and testing plan created at the same time and finished before; use the real PR names; static dataset. Built by build-dataset.mjs. The 127 moments are the merge or close date of each PR #1-#65 of dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev (created_at for open #44 and #60) and the 62 dated lines of initial commit 463cf4f (spread over 09:00-21:00 UTC of their day, an assumption); titles are the real PR titles (re-read through the GitHub MCP list_pull_requests) and the real commit lines. TYPE RULE, applied to the title only: a title starting with Add is a feature-brief (a new capability); otherwise a title naming a repair (fix, crash, error, 'against the write', 'rejected batch', 'instead of rejecting/crashing') is a bug-report; otherwise a title whose first word is a small-edit verb (Rename, Retire, Move, Clarify, Drop, Remove, Bump, Label, Keep, Convert, Link, Include, Show, Upgrade, Write, Read, Resolve, Match, Carry, Send, Allow, Store, Replace) or that is a style-cleanup or review-guidance note is a simple-change; everything else is a feature-brief. COUNTS: 91 feature-briefs, 31 simple-changes, 5 bug-reports = 127 pages, plus 182 plans (an implementation-plan and a testing-plan per feature-brief) and 2 toc pages (Features, Bug Reports) = 311 pages; 620 events, only created and status. STATUSES, read from src/pagetypes with graphify and grep: feature-brief initial draft, finished shipped (feature.py lines 289-293, terminal_states shipped and abandoned); simple-change and bug-report initial draft, finished closed (the last status of the machine, simple_change.py line 125 and bug_report.py line 138, draft -> open -> review -> done -> closed); implementation-plan and testing-plan initial draft, finished ready (feature.py lines 466-467 and 508-509); toc active (toc.py line 24). EVENTS PER PAGE: created at the moment in the initial status; one status event one hour later straight to the finished status (the real machines pass through intermediate statuses; the user asked for one finished event, so the dataset skips them); a feature's plans are created with it and move to ready at +30 and +45 minutes, before the feature's +60. Features and simple-changes sit under the Features toc, bug-reports under Bug Reports, both created at the first moment. No links, element activity, archives, gaps or approximate events. Overlapping hours simply overlap. SPARSE: events fall on 43 distinct days, median gap between moments 0.17 days, 90th percentile 2.0, longest 16.1.

FOLD: one pass turns the events into a page record per id: born, status segments, marks (created, each status move, first move into a done-class status = finish marker) and the other kinds the renderer supports. 'The state at moment T' is a binary search into the segments, so scrubbing costs one draw. 620 events fold with layout in 9 to 13 ms.

THREE CANDIDATE LAYOUTS (same fold, renderer and player; each page opens from disk):
1. Lanes (lanes.html): one lane per page, depth-first under its parent in creation order; a status-coloured bar that stays at the finished colour to the end of history, elbow from the parent at each child's birth, sticky titles with indent by depth, a vertical camera that eases toward recent activity. 4,354 px tall on this dataset.
2. Metro (metro.html): git-graph. Two trunk tracks (Features, Bug Reports); each page takes the free track nearest its parent, leaves it on a curve at birth, runs one hour, and curves back into the parent track at the finished status as a small glyph, freeing the track; a feature's plans branch off it the same way. 12 tracks besides the trunks, 635 px, one screen. Titles are printed to the right of each birth node.
3. Bands (bands.html): a band per page type (6), pages packed into sub-rows and released at the finished status, sticky band labels; 607 px, one screen.

PLAYHEAD MODEL: one vertical line at 62 percent of the width while the view follows (the world scrolls under it); drag pans and stops following (F returns). Left of it the past is solid status colour; right of it the known future is a 1 px grey ghost (G hides it). A chip row counts alive pages by status class at that moment; the handle shows date and time; ticks under the axis mark the 127 real moments; an overview strip shows event density and the viewport and scrubs on click or drag. Default window 3 days across the stage (a one-hour life is about 17 px), wheel zoom 1.5 to 400 days. Idle stretches (next moment more than 6 hours ahead) play 6 times faster.

THE STATIC LOOK (round 3). REMOVED, in tl.js: (a) the rings that expanded and faded on a status move, ship, gate, archive, delete, link and element event (the 'pulses' block); (b) the scale-in with overshoot of a created node and the pop of a shipped node (functions back() and ease() deleted); (c) the status rings drawn on every live page at the playhead (they came and went at lane boundaries); the playhead is now only its vertical line, handle and the status chip counts. KEPT: static nodes (created glyph by type, status dot, finish check node, cross for archive and delete), the status bar that lengthens as the playhead passes, the ghost, ticks, and two non-circle motions: the follow pan and the easing of the vertical camera. A mark is drawn fully, at its final size, exactly when the playhead reaches its time (t <= T) and is not drawn when the playhead is scrubbed back before it (check by reading the code: every mark test is m.t > T, no age or fade).

RENDERING: one Canvas2D per stage sized by devicePixelRatio, 1 px lines on half-pixel offsets, flat fills, system font; no glow, gradient, shadow or composite mode. Light and dark palettes in the script (T key); production would read water.css custom properties.

HOVER: nearest lane within 9 px; tooltip with title, type, created and ended dates, status at the playhead and at the cursor.

WEB UI: production route GET /ws:<id>/timeline (template extending _base.html with a full-viewport body class) and GET /ws:<id>/timeline.json under the shared read lock; the reloader script must keep the playhead (sessionStorage) instead of restarting playback on every mutation.

Its aggregate form, a stacked area of counts per status, is kept as a possible scrubber background, and the header chips already give that count at the playhead.

items.reason: Dominated at this size: the spike's own scale, ticks, zoom and path code is small, a library timeline brings its own look and DOM cost, and the no-build-step rule makes each dependency a vendored file. Not measured beyond d3 sizes.

items.name: Retained-mode SVG renderer for the lanes geometry
items.reason: Measured in spike/timeline/bench-svg.html. On the static dataset (311 pages) it is fine: 1,240 DOM elements, build 29 ms, group-transform pan steady p99 17.2 ms, none over 33 ms. At the generated stress case (commit e40aa12, same 120 days) 567 pages make 10,171 elements (p99 17 ms) but 1,881 pages make 32,686 elements (build 581 ms) and 278 of about 540 steady frames miss 33 ms (p99 66.5 ms). SVG is crisp and gives native hover, but cannot carry several times pasta's size unless culled by hand to the visible window, which makes it a canvas-like renderer with DOM cost on top. A possible fallback for the sparse dataset.

assessment.tradeoffs:
BUYS: a clean, sharp, time-based picture with no dependency: about 30 KB of hand-written script, no build step, no Python dependency, no vendored library, read-only, and now a static look with no animated circles. Time is the real axis, so the playhead sweeps a static layout: scrubbing is a binary search plus one draw (p50 under 1.4 ms, p95 under 4 ms on the static dataset), there is no simulation to settle, and the same view zooms from one merge to the whole 120 days. On the user's sparse dataset all three layouts play at the display rate at device pixel ratio 1 and 2 on the GPU path (steady p99 about 17 ms, none of about 840 frames over 33 ms). The sparse dataset also makes two layouts fit one screen: metro 635 px (14 tracks) and bands 607 px (6 bands), lanes 4,354 px with a follow camera.

COSTS: (1) The user's dataset narrows what can be judged: only created and status events for six page types, no links, element activity, archives, renames, gaps or approximate events, so those drawings (all written and exercised only by the generated history at commit e40aa12) are not on the screen. (2) The dataset is very sparse: 127 moments on 43 of 119.5 days, each page lives one hour, so at the default 3-day window a page is a short stub of about 17 px and most screens between merge days are empty; the player skips idle stretches 6 times faster. How that reads is a look question nobody has judged. (3) Lanes has a lane per page ever created (4,354 px) and keeps every finished page as a line to the end of history; its camera does the work. (4) Metro's glyph merge into the parent track at finish puts 127 stubs on two trunks; titles are printed only where they fit without colliding on a track. (5) Nobody has watched any page and no screenshot was taken, so label legibility, clutter and WOW are unverified; the pixel check shows ink is drawn (2 to 28 percent of pixels). (6) Hover, wheel, drag and overview scrub are written but not exercised by an automated pointer. (7) A software raster still janks (10, 33 and 18 of about 540 steady frames over 33 ms for lanes, metro, bands). (8) The generated stress case, kept only as the e40aa12 numbers, shows what happens at several times pasta's size on the same 120 days: metro breaks at 1,881 pages (11 steady frames over 33 ms, scrub p95 32 ms), lanes grows to 26,334 px, and layout height grows with the page count in all three. EASIER LATER: live-follow over the reloader socket, filters by type or status, a stacked status area behind the scrubber. HARDER: metro track allocation depends on release times and must be recomputed or kept stable when live events extend a page's life.

fit.note: Hover finds the nearest lane within 9 px and shows title, status at the playhead and at the cursor; written in app.js and tl.js hit() but not exercised by an automated pointer, so unproven in a browser session.
The renderer consumes only the recorded event list in the lifecycle-log vocabulary and never reads current page state; producing and serving that data is the other two directions' work.
2D Canvas with time as the x axis in all three candidates; pages are nodes along time, no force layout (sketch).
Not this direction's concern: how far back history reaches is decided by the source; the renderer plays whatever starts at t0.
Not this direction's concern: cleanup retention belongs to the history source; the renderer replays what it is given.
The view adds only GET routes under the shared read lock plus static files; nothing on it writes (pages are standalone files in the spike).
A browser page and a JSON endpoint on the FastAPI app; no MCP tool is added.
This direction adds nothing to the write path; recording cost is the lifecycle-log direction's risk.

On the static dataset every feature-brief, simple-change and bug-report is a lane or track with a created node, a finish marker one hour later, its plans for a feature, in all three layouts; archive is not in this dataset (the renderer draws it, exercised only by the generated history at e40aa12). Real events depend on the history-source directions.

Play/pause (space), speeds, arrow-key steps and a click-or-drag overview scrubber; a scrub is one binary-search fold plus one draw: on the static dataset p50 0.7 to 1.1 ms, p95 1.6 to 2.9 ms, max 4.1 ms in every layout (two runs each). Generated stress case (e40aa12): p95 4 to 24 ms at 191 and 567 pages, metro 1,881 pages p95 32.2 ms.

State at the playhead is a binary search into each page's segments (null before birth); check.js on the static dataset finds 0 pages outside their lifetime and 0 events off a real moment; the view follows the playhead; the future is a dim ghost that can be hidden (conflict on the ghost). No circles are drawn at the playhead any more.

Three candidate pages were built on the user's sparse real-title dataset for the user to judge; the design aims at WOW through a sweeping playhead and, in metro, branch and merge curves, with no glow and no animated circles, but nobody and no screenshot has viewed them, so WOW is untested.

Changed by the user's words: "remove the animated circles, they are slightly buggy in when they appear". Removed in round 3: rings that expanded and faded on status moves, ship, gate and archive; the scale-in with overshoot of a created node; the pop of a shipped node; the status rings drawn on every live page at the playhead. What remains is static: a mark appears fully drawn exactly when the playhead reaches its time and disappears when scrubbed back; the lane bar grows with the playhead, and the vertical camera and the follow pan ease. So 'a node grows in' and 'visibly departs' no longer hold; the playhead sweep is the motion.

On the static dataset (311 pages, 620 events) at device pixel ratio 1 and 2 on the GPU path the steady frame interval p99 is 16.9 to 17.5 ms with none of about 840 frames over 33 ms in all three layouts (one 1.2 s hitch in one of two lanes runs); a software raster still misses 10 to 33 frames of about 540. The generated stress case (e40aa12) is where metro breaks, at 1,881 pages.

The renderer has a mark for every kind (created, status, ship, archive, delete, rename, move, links, element activity) and the generated history at e40aa12 exercised them, but the user's sparse static dataset carries only created and status events for six page types (toc, feature-brief, simple-change, bug-report, implementation-plan, testing-plan), so that is all the candidate pages show.

Of the list (every page type, statuses, nesting and links, renames, reparents, archives, activity) the static dataset shows six page types, their two statuses each, and parent-child nesting only; links, renames, reparents, archives and element activity are narrowed out by the user's dataset and are covered only by the e40aa12 generated history.

A static dataset replaces the generator, in the user's words: one page per each of 127 real moments with the real PR title, created and finished an hour later, a feature-brief with its implementation and testing plans finished before it (91 feature-briefs, 31 simple-changes, 5 bug-reports, 182 plans, 2 toc pages, 620 events); the candidate pages load only dataset.js and no generator runs at load. It is the default the whole page measures on.

Avoided by design, not by sight: a continuous playhead sweep over nodes and, in metro, branches and merges, not a static table or jumping frames, yet lanes could still read as a Gantt chart and one-hour pages on a 3-day window are short ticks; the user's look test decides.

The static dataset has only exact events and check.js finds no page shown outside its lifetime; the fold is a binary search into the recorded segments. Dashed rings for approximate events and gap ticks exist in the renderer but this dataset has neither, so the uncertainty drawing is unexercised.

The client holds one event list and per-page records, linear in history (620 events fold with layout in 9 to 13 ms; 26k generated events in 88 to 110 ms at e40aa12); on the static dataset metro and bands stay one screen (635 and 607 px) and lanes is 4,354 px, while the generated stress case grows all three; bounding the stored history is the source's concern.

No glow, bloom, gradient, shadow or composite mode anywhere in tl.js or app.js (grep finds only Array.filter), and since round 3 no expanding rings or scaling circles either; flat fills, 1 px hairlines at half-pixel offsets, system type.

test.predicts: A hand-written Canvas2D renderer with no library and no animated circles, served from src/static with no build step, replays the static dataset of 127 real moments (311 pages, 620 events, over 119.5 days) in each of three layouts with fewer than 1 percent of steady frames over 33 ms at device pixel ratio 1 on the GPU path, restores any scrubbed moment in one draw with p95 under 30 ms, shows every page only inside its lifetime, and every event of the dataset is a created or status event on a real moment (finish one hour later, plans before their feature).
test.falsifier: On the static dataset at device pixel ratio 1 with the GPU path on, more than 1 percent of steady frames (after the first 60) over 33 ms, or a scrub-to-moment draw above 30 ms at the 95th percentile, or the fold showing a page before its creation, or any created event off a real moment, a finish not one hour later, a plan finishing after its feature, or a title that is not a real PR title or commit line (node check.js). The generated stress case at e40aa12 is reported as a stress case, not as the falsifier.

Read the initial commit 463cf4f ('Initial version cut', 2026-08-23) with get_commit: its message lists dated entries from 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-23, one line per change, and each listed line is one moment of change.

feature-brief:mwkzuows-54b6c4.title: Record every page's lifecycle in an append-only log on the write path

summary.body: Make the store write down every page lifecycle change as it happens - creations, status moves, renames, reparents, links made and removed, archives and unarchives, cleanup deletions, content edits and element activity - as one compact JSON line per event in an append-only per-workspace log (events/<ws_token>.jsonl), written in each mutation's transaction without ever failing or noticeably slowing the write, started once per workspace with the committed back-fill (when one exists) followed by a baseline of the pages present, never erased by cleanup, and readable as the replay JSON the timeline plays. Without it the wiki can only show where work stands now, not how it got there. One of three briefs of epic epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b, built exactly to its sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae: it owns the design's expected changes to src/lifecycle_log.py (new), src/model.py, src/serialize.py, src/store.py, tests/test_lifecycle_log.py (new), tests/test_store.py, tests/test_serialize.py and tests/test_cleanup.py, and the architecture pages it makes stale (Authoring & mutation, Scheduled workspace cleanup, Pasta Project Overview, Archiving, Page types & FSM implementation), and it defines the epic's shared contracts for the event line, the replay JSON, the store and model changes and the pure lifecycle-log module.

items.text: The write path this brief changes. Every persisted workspace write funnels through Store._touch_and_save (line 187: sets updated_at from _now() at line 66, then _write_file at line 175 - serialize, temp file, os.replace under the workspace read-write lock's write half). Its 12 callers, each holding _transaction_lock_for(workspace_id) and loading with load_workspace (line 205): create_page 556 (plus _create_auto_children 1001), mutate_page_batch 580 (pre-image `page` stays untouched: apply_command copies it, so `page` vs `working` is the scoped diff), cleanup_workspace 676 (classify, write_backup, expires_at stamps/clears, delete_subtree per prune root, early return without a write when nothing to do), _set_page_archive_state 715 (archive/unarchive/schedule/unschedule; cascades both flags onto pinned children via is_auto_child_type), set_page_status 766, reparent_page 811, reorder_page 847, rename_page 873, link_page 927, unlink_page 946, _set_workspace_status 965, set_workspace_guidance 985. create_workspace (230) and write_backup (191) call _write_file directly. _archived_in_ancestry (383) is the subtree rule. Effects: file I/O, clock (_now), threading locks. Logger precedent: src/cleanup.py uses logging.getLogger("uvicorn.error").

Page carries type, title, status, parent_id, child_ids, sections, archived, links [{to, role}], expires_at, delete_scheduled, status_revision_token; Page.copy() deep-copies sections. items.text: Do reparent_page and rename_page record a moved / renamed event when the parent / title does not actually change (a reparent under the same parent, a rename to the same title)?
items.answer: No. Each records its event only when the value changes, as set_page_status does ('status, when the status changes') and as diff_page does for a title. A reparent under the same parent is a reorder, which records nothing; a same-title rename changes nothing. This keeps criterion mwkyh77b-405bb4: nothing that did not change is recorded.

items.text: What does _load_for_write do when computing the baseline, or reading the back-fill file, raises - given that recording must never fail a mutation?
items.answer: Both are guarded. The baseline is built through _guarded_events, so an exception gives None; the start commit then runs as _touch_and_save(workspace, None, backfill=backfill): the back-fill (if any) is still installed, one seq is reserved and served as a gap, and the mutation goes on. Reading the back-fill file is wrapped so an OSError is logged and treated like a file that fails the check ([]). A non-empty log whose tail cannot be read is logged and the workspace is returned unchanged, so the log is never written into from _load_for_write. This follows decision mwksl2h5-6e895b (never let recording fail a mutation); the contract's 'If backfill or baseline' reads 'or the baseline build failed' for the None case so the failure is visible as a gap.

items.text: In what order does baseline list pages filed nowhere, given the contract says 'in id order' and the event-line rule says a parent's line precedes its children's?
items.answer: Unfiled pages in id order, each preceded by its own unfiled ancestors (followed through parent_id) that are not listed yet, topmost first. With no unfiled ancestry - the normal case - this is plain id order; when a child's id sorts before its unfiled parent's, the parent is pulled ahead, so both contract rules hold.

items.text: In what order does diff_page emit its events inside the contract's stated order (renamed, linked/unlinked, edited, el_*, status last)?
items.answer: Grouped by kind in the contract's order: renamed; linked for each (to, role) pair in after's links not in before's, in after's order; unlinked for each pair only in before's, in before's order; edited for each changed scalar, prose or blocks field in the type's section and field declaration order; then per list field in declaration order: el_added / el_status / el_edited walking after's elements in order, then el_removed walking before's; status last. Elements without a string id are skipped. A list with an element FSM compares element['status'] for el_status and the rest for el_edited; a list without one reports el_added with status null and any change as el_edited.

items.text: How does _load_for_write find 'the seq of the last complete line' of a non-empty log, and what does it adopt when no complete line parses?
items.answer: It reads backwards from the end of the file in fixed-size blocks, splitting complete lines (each ends in a newline; a final piece without one is ignored), and adopts the seq of the last complete line that parses as a JSON object with an integer seq. Only this one-time start reads past the last byte. If no complete line parses, event_seq stays 0 and a warning is logged; _load_for_write still never writes the file.

items.text: Which logger, clock seam and file modes does the store use for recording and reading the log?
items.answer:
Logger: logging.getLogger("uvicorn.error"), the precedent src/cleanup.py sets so store warnings land beside the server's own output. Clock: a module-level _utc_now() -> datetime in src/store.py that _now() and the commit instant both read, the seam the clock-behind test patches. Append: the file is opened in binary append mode ('ab+'), so each line ends in exactly b"
" on Windows, the last byte is checked with one seek and a one-byte read, and the bytes go out in one write. Reads: read_lifecycle_log and the back-fill read decode bytes as UTF-8 with errors='replace', so a torn multi-byte tail cannot raise (the torn piece is dropped as an unterminated line anyway); the back-fill text has '
' normalised to '
' first so a CRLF checkout still checks.

items.text: What exactly does check_backfill accept as a line that 'parses as an event of the event-line format'?
items.answer: A line is an event when it parses as a JSON object with seq an int >= 1 and ts an int (bools rejected), page a str, kind one of the written kinds of the event-line contract (created, present, status, renamed, moved, linked, unlinked, archived, unarchived, deleted, edited, el_added, el_status, el_edited, el_removed), and that kind's own keys present with their contract types (str, str-or-null for parent, from_parent, to_parent and el_added's status, bool for archived, list for links). Unknown extra keys are allowed. The file as a whole also needs seqs exactly 1..N, ts never decreasing and a final newline, so empty text, a blank line or a missing final newline returns None.

items.text: Where does the rule for the cleanup sweep's events (unlinked, then deleted in pruned order) live, given src/cleanup.py stays unchanged and the store holds the pre-image?
items.answer: In the pure module, as a helper the contract leaves to the builder: lifecycle_log.sweep_events(workspace, pruned_ids) returns unlinked for every link a page outside pruned_ids holds into pruned_ids (pages in document order, links in order), then deleted for each pruned id in the given order. The store computes pruned_ids before delete_subtree in the order the SweepReport lists them - per prune root, sorted(cleanup._descendants(workspace, root)) - keeping only ids that are pages and not yet listed. cleanup.py is untouched.

items.text: The contract declares _touch_and_save's backfill as `list[Event] = ()` - a tuple default on a list annotation, which basedpyright rejects. How is it typed without changing the call interface?
items.answer: backfill: Sequence[Event] = () (collections.abc.Sequence). Callers pass a list exactly as the contract shows; only the annotation widens so the tuple default typechecks.

items.text: The spec's append (decision on question mwl19a4g-966e5b) opens the log 'ab+' and reads its last byte on every commit. Measured on this Windows host, any read-open of a log modified since it was last read costs about 18-22 ms (a write-only 'ab' append costs 0.6-0.8 ms, even on a 10 MB log), so recording added about 17 ms per write and the 5 ms budget (anti-goal mwjq5k9s-1bc2cd, criterion mwksrcqr-beecbb) fails. How does the append keep the contract's 'if the file is non-empty and its last byte is not a newline, write one first' without reading the file on every commit?
items.answer: Remember, per store and workspace, the log's size right after this store's own last complete append (which always ends in a newline). Each append stats the file (no open); when the size is that remembered size the last byte is known to be a newline and nothing is read. Only when it differs - the first append in a process, or a file another writer or a crash changed - is the last byte read once, and a newline written first when it is missing. The append itself opens the file write-only ('ab') and writes once; the remembered size is cleared before writing and set to size + bytes written after it succeeds, so a failed append is never vouched for. Same contract behaviour, no read on the steady-state write path; measured stat + 'ab' at about 0.8 ms on a 10 MB log. Not a contract change: the contract names the behaviour, not the file mode.

inlines.text: Pure: lifecycle_log.baseline(workspace) and lifecycle_log.sweep_events(workspace, pruned_ids). Tests first with model-built workspaces (src.model Page/Workspace, type 'test-fields'): baseline is a pre-order walk from root_page_ids through child_ids including archived pages, each page once (a child_ids cycle terminates, a dangling id is skipped), then unreached pages in id order with an unreached parent whose id sorts later pulled ahead of its child; present carries archived and links. sweep_events gives unlinked for each link a surviving page holds into the pruned set (none for links between pruned pages), then deleted with last type, title and status for each pruned id in the given order.

detail.source:
def baseline(workspace: Workspace) -> list[Event]:
    order, seen = [], set()
    stack = list(reversed(workspace.root_page_ids))
    while stack:                                   # pre-order through child_ids
        pid = stack.pop()
        if pid in seen or pid not in workspace.pages: continue
        seen.add(pid); order.append(pid)
        stack.extend(reversed(workspace.pages[pid].child_ids))
    for pid in sorted(set(workspace.pages) - seen):  # unreached, id order
        chain, cur = [], pid
        while cur is not None and cur in workspace.pages and cur not in seen and cur not in chain:
            chain.append(cur); cur = workspace.pages[cur].parent_id
        for ancestor in reversed(chain): seen.add(ancestor); order.append(ancestor)
    return [present(workspace.pages[pid]) for pid in order]

def sweep_events(workspace: Workspace, pruned_ids: list[str]) -> list[Event]:
    pruned = set(pruned_ids)
    events = [unlinked(p.id, l["to"], l["role"]) for p in workspace.pages.values()
              if p.id not in pruned for l in p.links if l.get("to") in pruned]
    return events + [deleted(workspace.pages[pid]) for pid in pruned_ids if pid in workspace.pages]

def _append_to_log(self, workspace_id: str, lines: list[Event]) -> None:
    data = "".join(lifecycle_log.encode(line) for line in lines).encode("utf-8")
    path = self._events_path_for(workspace_id)
    with self._rw_lock_for(workspace_id).write():
        try:
            size = path.stat().st_size
        except FileNotFoundError:
            size = 0
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if size and self._log_sizes.get(workspace_id) != size:
            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
                _ = handle.seek(size - 1)
                if handle.read(1) != b"\n":
                    data = b"\n" + data
        _ = self._log_sizes.pop(workspace_id, None)
        with open(path, "ab") as handle:
            _ = handle.write(data)
        self._log_sizes[workspace_id] = size + len(data)

overview.body: Covers the write and read sides of the lifecycle log in the store, wave 1 of epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b, built to sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae (Part 1 and the serving half of Part 2): a new pure module src/lifecycle_log.py (event constructors, diff_page, baseline, sweep events, stamp, encode, check_backfill, serve_lines, timeline_types, timeline_payload); Workspace.event_seq in src/model.py and src/serialize.py; and in src/store.py the events folder, the backfill_dir constructor argument, _load_for_write in all 12 writers (starting each log once: a checked back-fill, then a baseline of present events), _touch_and_save(workspace, events, backfill) committing the document first and appending the stamped lines after it, and read_lifecycle_log. It restates the design's decisions for this slice rather than reopening them. It leaves out the GET routes, the server's backfill_dir wiring, the renderer and its node check (wave 3, agent-plan:mwkzvaab-928193), the back-fill file and its build script (wave 2, agent-plan:mwkzv9e2-e3c586; tests here use small fixture back-fills in temporary folders), README.md, and the architecture pages, which are reconciled at ship.

body.text: Data shapes (contracts mwkzwvpv-63fd76 and mwkzwvpx-2776ce)

One event is a dict whose keys are, in order, seq, ts, page, kind, then the kind's keys. Unstamped events (what writers build) have no seq or ts. The log lives at <root>/events/<ws_token>.jsonl, ws_token being the workspace id with ':' replaced by '_'. Every line is encode(event): json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')) + newline, UTF-8. Lines are never rewritten or removed. The kinds and their keys, exactly:

body.source:
created     type, title, parent(str|null), status
present     type, title, parent(str|null), status, archived(bool), links([{to, role}])   baseline only
status      from, to
renamed     from, title               (old title, new title)
moved       from_parent(str|null), to_parent(str|null)
linked      to, role                  (page is the link's source)
unlinked    to, role
archived    -                         (only the page whose own flag changed)
unarchived  -
deleted     type, title, status       (last values)
edited      section, field            (a scalar, prose or blocks field changed)
el_added    section, field, el, status(str|null: null when the list has no element FSM)
el_status   section, field, el, from, to
el_edited   section, field, el
el_removed  section, field, el

served only, never written:
gap         {seq: first missing seq, ts: ts of the line after the hole, page: null, kind: "gap", missing: int >= 1}

replay JSON (timeline_payload):
{"workspace": {"id", "name"}, "t0": first event ts | null, "t1": last event ts | null,
 "types": timeline_types(), "events": serve_lines(...)}

body.text: Pure core: src/lifecycle_log.py

Imports only src.model and the page-type registry (pagetypes._registry.registered_pagetypes, pagetypes.core.pagetype.initial_sections and element_fsm_sites, pagetypes.core.specs field kinds). No file, clock or network access. type Event = dict[str, Any].

def created(page: Page) -> Event        # page.id, type, title, parent_id, status
def present(page: Page) -> Event        # + archived, links as [{"to", "role"}]
def status(page_id: str, from_: str, to: str) -> Event
def renamed(page_id: str, old: str, new: str) -> Event
def moved(page_id: str, from_parent: str | None, to_parent: str | None) -> Event
def linked(page_id: str, to: str, role: str) -> Event
def unlinked(page_id: str, to: str, role: str) -> Event
def archived(page_id: str) -> Event
def unarchived(page_id: str) -> Event
def deleted(page: Page) -> Event        # type, title, status
def diff_page(before: Page, after: Page, page_type: PageType | None) -> list[Event]
def baseline(workspace: Workspace) -> list[Event]
def sweep_events(workspace: Workspace, pruned_ids: list[str]) -> list[Event]
def stamp(events: list[Event], first_seq: int, ts: int) -> list[Event]
def encode(event: Event) -> str
def check_backfill(text: str) -> list[Event] | None
def serve_lines(text: str) -> list[Event]
def timeline_types() -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
def timeline_payload(workspace_id: str, name: str, events: list[Event]) -> dict[str, Any]

body.text: diff_page(before, after, page_type): with a page_type, before's sections are first taken as initial_sections(page_type, before.sections), the normalisation apply_command gives its working copy, so a field the type gained since and a refreshed fixed field are never edits. Events, in this order: renamed when the title differs; linked for each (to, role) in after.links not in before.links (after's order); unlinked for each only in before (before's order); edited for each SCALAR, PROSE or BLOCKS field whose value differs, in section then field declaration order; then for each LIST field in declaration order, elements matched by their string 'id' (others skipped): walking after's elements, an id not in before is el_added (status = element.get('status') when the field has an element FSM, else null), an id in both is el_status when the field has an element FSM and the statuses differ, else el_edited when the element dicts differ; then walking before's elements, an id not in after is el_removed; status last when it differs. With page_type None only renamed, linked/unlinked and status are diffed, without normalisation. A list value that is not a list counts as empty.

baseline(workspace): one present event per page. First a pre-order walk from workspace.root_page_ids through child_ids, archived pages included, each page once (a seen set guards cycles; dangling ids are skipped). Then every page the walk did not reach, in id order, each preceded by its own unreached ancestors (followed through parent_id, cycle-safe) not yet listed, topmost first.

sweep_events(workspace, pruned_ids): computed on the pre-image. unlinked for every link whose 'to' is in pruned_ids held by a page not in pruned_ids (pages in workspace.pages order, links in order); then deleted(page) for each id of pruned_ids, in order, that is a page.
stamp(events, first_seq, ts): new dicts {seq, ts, page, kind, then the remaining keys in their order}, seq = first_seq, first_seq + 1, ... The inputs are not modified.

check_backfill(text): None unless text ends with a newline and every newline-terminated line (blank lines included) parses as an event: a JSON object with seq an int >= 1, ts an int (bools rejected), page a str, kind one of the written kinds above with that kind's keys present and typed as listed (str; str or null for parent, from_parent, to_parent and el_added's status; bool for archived; list for links); unknown extra keys allowed. The seqs must be exactly 1..N and ts never decrease. Returns the parsed dicts (key order kept, so encode reproduces each line). Empty text returns None.

serve_lines(text): split on newline; drop the final piece (it has no newline after it: torn or in flight, or empty); skip a line that is not a JSON object with an int seq (bools rejected); keep disk order; before a line whose seq exceeds the previous kept line's seq + 1, or the first kept line when its seq > 1, insert a gap event (seq = previous + 1, or 1; ts = that line's ts; missing = the difference). A seq not above the previous one gets no gap.

timeline_types(): for every registered page type, sorted by tag: initial = fsm.initial; finish = list(fsm.terminal_states) when declared, else [fsm.states[-1]] when that is not the initial status, else []; elements = {'<section>.<field>': spec.name} from element_fsm_sites; gates = the sorted unique [source, dest] pairs of fsm.transitions whose agency is 'human'. timeline_payload(workspace_id, name, events) = {'workspace': {'id', 'name'}, 't0': events[0]['ts'] or None, 't1': events[-1]['ts'] or None, 'types': timeline_types(), 'events': events}.
Model and serialization (contract mwkzwvq0-3ae7f5)
