# src/model.py, Workspace
event_seq: int = 0     # seq of the last lifecycle-log event this document reflects

# src/serialize.py
workspace_to_dict(ws)   -> also "event_seq": ws.event_seq
workspace_from_dict(d)  -> event_seq=int(d.get("event_seq", 0))

body.text: Effectful shell: src/store.py

_touch_and_save: (1) instant = the later of _utc_now() and workspace.updated_at as loaded (parsed with datetime.fromisoformat; a naive value is taken as UTC; an unparsable one is ignored); updated_at = instant.isoformat(); ts = instant in whole epoch milliseconds. If backfill is non-empty and its last ts is later than ts, log a warning and drop it. event_seq += len(backfill); lines = backfill + stamp(events, event_seq + 1, ts) (no stamped lines when events is None); event_seq += len(events), or 1 when events is None. (2) _write_file(the document): the commit; it may raise as today, and then nothing is appended. (3) When lines is non-empty, _append_to_log; any exception is logged as a warning and swallowed.

_append_to_log: under _rw_lock_for(workspace_id).write(), stat the log (size 0 when absent; mkdir the events folder then). The store remembers, per workspace, the log's size right after its own last successful append (self._log_sizes: dict[str, int]); that append ended in a newline, so when the stat'd size equals the remembered one nothing is read. When the size is non-zero and differs (the first append in a process, or another writer or a crash changed the file), open the file 'rb', read its last byte, and prefix the data with a newline when that byte is not one. Then forget the remembered size, open the file 'ab' (write-only) and write all lines' encoded UTF-8 bytes in one call, and remember size + bytes written. A read-open of a file modified since its last read costs about 20 ms on Windows (the host's scanner), a write-only append under 1 ms, so the steady-state write path never opens the log for reading.

_load_for_write (called with the transaction lock held, in place of load_workspace in every writer): load the document (raising exactly what load_workspace raises). When event_seq != 0, return it. Otherwise: (a) when the log file is non-empty, adopt the seq of its last complete line that parses as a JSON object with an int seq, read backwards from the end in blocks; none parses: keep 0 and warn; an OSError reading it: warn and return unchanged; never write the file. (b) when the log is absent or empty: backfill = check_backfill of backfill_dir/<ws_token>.jsonl when backfill_dir is set and the file exists (read as UTF-8 bytes, decoded with errors='replace', CRLF normalised to LF), else []; None or an OSError is logged and becomes []. baseline = _guarded_events(lambda: lifecycle_log.baseline(workspace)). When backfill is non-empty, or baseline is None (the build failed) or non-empty: _touch_and_save(workspace, baseline, backfill=backfill). Return the workspace.

read_lifecycle_log(workspace_id): under _rw_lock_for(workspace_id).read(), raise NotFoundError(f"Workspace '{workspace_id}' not found.") when the document does not exist, else read the log's bytes ('' when absent) and decode UTF-8 with errors='replace'; return lifecycle_log.serve_lines(text). It never calls _load_for_write or writes a file.
What each writer records

body.source:
Every writer: workspace = self._load_for_write(id); events built with self._guarded_events(...);
self._touch_and_save(workspace, events)

create_page                created(page), then created(child) per auto-created pinned child
mutate_page_batch          diff_page(page, working, page_type)   (page = the untouched pre-image)
reparent_page              moved(page, old parent, new parent) when the parent changes, else []
reorder_page               []
rename_page                renamed(page, old, new) when the title changes, else []
link_page / unlink_page    linked / unlinked(from_id, to_id, role)
_set_page_archive_state    archived or unarchived for the page and each cascaded pinned child whose
                           own archived flag changed; delete_scheduled alone records nothing
set_page_status            status(page, old, new) when the status changes, else []
cleanup_workspace          sweep_events(pre-image, pruned order) computed before delete_subtree;
                           pruned order = per prune root, sorted(cleanup._descendants(ws, root)),
                           pages only, each once; expires_at stamps and clears record nothing
_set_workspace_status      []
set_workspace_guidance     []
create_workspace, write_backup: unchanged, call _write_file directly, record nothing

body.text: Error paths

A rejected batch (any PastaError before _touch_and_save) writes nothing and records nothing. _write_file raising leaves the log untouched. An event build that raises reserves one seq (a gap) and the mutation commits. An append that raises is logged and swallowed; the next commit's lines follow a hole, served as a gap, and a half-written last line is ended with a newline before the next append. A back-fill that fails the check, cannot be read, or ends after the commit instant is skipped with a warning and the baseline is still written. A clock running behind the document's updated_at commits at updated_at's instant, so ts never decreases along seq.

Decision: implement contract mwkzwvq0-3ae7f5 exactly (events required) and leave tests/test_workspace_guidance.py untouched; the one-line change there is the plan's last step, run only when the controller clears it, else the agent-plan blocks naming it. Rejected: changing the file silently (outside the slice, a deviation the reporting contract forbids); a default for events (breaks the contract and the 'forgotten call site is a type error' guarantee). Why: the agent-plan's boundaries make a change outside the slice a block, not a fix.

Decision: moved and renamed are recorded only when the parent or title actually changes. Rejected: recording them on every call (a same-parent reparent is a reorder, which the design records as nothing; a no-op rename is not a change). Why: criterion mwkyh77b-405bb4 - nothing that did not change is recorded - and the same 'when it changes' rule set_page_status follows.

Decision: the baseline is built through _guarded_events, and a None result still commits (back-fill installed, one seq reserved as a gap); reading the back-fill or the log tail is wrapped so an OSError is logged, never raised. Rejected: an unguarded baseline (a mutation would fail when its history could not be computed, anti-goal mwjq5k9s-1bc2cd); skipping the commit on None (the failure would leave no gap and the start would silently never happen). Why: decision mwksl2h5-6e895b - recording never fails a mutation, and a reserved seq makes the loss visible.

Decision: unreached pages in id order, each preceded by its own unreached ancestors not yet listed (topmost first). Rejected: pure id order (a child whose id sorts first would precede its parent, breaking the event-line rule); a tree walk from every unreached page (no longer in id order). Why: both contract rules hold, and the ordinary case - no unreached ancestry - is plain id order.

Decision: renamed, linked, unlinked, edited (declaration order), el_* per list field (declaration order; added/status/edited in after's order, then removed in before's order), status last; one el_status or el_edited per element. Rejected: interleaving edited and el_* per field (the contract lists edited before the el_* group); emitting both el_status and el_edited for one element. Why: the contract's stated order, made deterministic; the design leaves order beyond it to the builder.

Decision: read backwards in blocks to the last complete line that parses with an int seq; none parses: keep 0 and warn. Rejected: reading the whole file (cost grows with the log); trusting only the very last complete line (one corrupt line would reset the seq to 0 and repeat seqs). Why: it runs once per workspace and only for a restored document, and it never writes the log.

Decision: a line is an event when it has int seq >= 1, int ts, str page, a written kind and that kind's keys with their contract types; unknown extra keys are allowed; plus seqs 1..N, non-decreasing ts and a final newline. Rejected: accepting any JSON object with a seq (a malformed back-fill would be installed and copied for ever); requiring exactly the kind's keys (contradicts 'later changes may add keys'). Why: the back-fill is copied verbatim into a log nobody may rewrite, so it is checked against the full line format once, at install.

Decision: lifecycle_log.sweep_events(workspace, pruned_ids) holds the rule; the store passes the pruned order computed with cleanup._descendants before delete_subtree. Rejected: computing the events inline in the store (a rule in the shell); changing delete_subtree to return events (the design keeps cleanup.py unchanged). Why: the rule stays pure and unit-testable, and the order matches the SweepReport's pruned list.

Decision: backfill: Sequence[Event] = (). Rejected: list[Event] = () (does not typecheck); list[Event] | None = None (a second empty value). Why: identical call interface to the contract, and basedpyright passes.

Decision: logger logging.getLogger("uvicorn.error"); clock _utc_now() in src/store.py read by _now() and the commit instant; a binary append in one write (its last-byte check is settled by question mwl2boc1-0e1f76); reads decode UTF-8 with errors='replace'; the back-fill's CRLF normalised to LF before the check. Rejected: a module logger nobody configures (warnings would vanish under uvicorn); patching datetime in tests; text-mode append (Windows would write '\r\n', breaking the line format and byte-identical back-fill copies). Why: the design leaves the logger and these mechanics to the builder; these follow repo precedent and the contract's line format.

Decision: remember per workspace the log size this store left after its own last append; stat before each append and read the last byte only when the size differs; append write-only ('ab') in one write. Rejected: 'ab+' with a one-byte read on every commit (measured +17 ms per write on Windows, failing the 5 ms budget); always prefixing a newline (writes blank lines into a one-object-per-line file); skipping the repair (a torn line would swallow the next commit's first event). Why: identical contract behaviour - a non-empty log whose last byte is not a newline gets one first - with no read on the steady-state write path; a failed append clears the remembered size, so it is never vouched for.

feature-brief:mwkzuptb-70b114.title: Back-fill pasta's own workspace log from its PR history

summary.body: Give pasta's own workspace a history from before recording ships: build, from this repo's real record, the initial back-fill of its lifecycle log - one page per pull request #1-#65 of dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev and per dated line of initial commit 463cf4f, titled with the PR title or commit line, created at its real start (decoded from the id of the feature-brief, simple-change or bug-report page that carries that PR's GitHub link in the repo's backup folder) and finished at the real merge moments, with a feature-brief's implementation and testing plans - committed as backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl in the lifecycle-log line format, so the store installs it as the start of that workspace's log and the normal timeline view plays it, with no separate test page. The user asked for exactly this so the timeline has real history to show from day one. One of three briefs of epic epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b, built exactly to its sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae: it owns the design's expected changes to scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py (new), scripts/timeline_dataset/pull-requests.json, scripts/timeline_dataset/initial-commit-463cf4f.txt and scripts/timeline_dataset/workspace-pages.json (new committed inputs), backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl (new) and tests/test_timeline_backfill.py (new), and it defines the epic's shared contract for the back-fill file.

items.name: src/lifecycle_log.py (wave 1, read only) - pure
items.text: Built by wave 1 and on this branch at 05b302b. Used here: `type Event = dict[str, Any]` (line 23); encode(event) (line 208) = json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')) plus a newline, keys in the dict's own order, so the builder must create each line dict with keys seq, ts, page, kind, then the kind's keys. stamp(events, first_seq, ts) (line 200) gives every event one shared ts, so it does not fit the back-fill, whose lines each carry their own ts. check_backfill(text) (line 261) returns the parsed lines, or None unless the text ends in a newline, every line is an event of the line format (created: type, title str, parent str or null, status str; status: from, to str; seq int >= 1, ts int, page str), seqs are exactly 1..N and ts never decreases. Imports src.model and the registry only; no I/O.

items.name: src/store.py Store._load_for_write and _read_backfill (wave 1, read only) - effectful
items.text: Store(..., backfill_dir=None) (line 201). _read_backfill (line 392) reads backfill_dir/<ws_token>.jsonl as bytes, decodes UTF-8, normalises CRLF to LF, runs check_backfill and installs nothing when it fails; _load_for_write (lines 386-389) installs it once, into an empty log of a document whose event_seq is 0, followed by the baseline; _touch_and_save drops a back-fill whose last ts is later than the installing commit's instant. src/server.py line 51 still builds STORE = Store(DATA_DIR) without backfill_dir - wave 3 adds backfill_dir=Path('backfill') (cwd-relative), so the committed file is inert until wave 3 lands.

items.name: Page-type registry statuses (src/pagetypes, read only) - pure
items.text: Confirmed with lifecycle_log.timeline_types() on this branch: toc initial active, no finish; feature-brief initial draft, finish shipped or abandoned; simple-change and bug-report initial draft, finish closed; implementation-plan and testing-plan initial draft, finish ready. These are exactly the statuses the back-fill contract hard-codes (created draft, tocs active; plans draft to ready; feature-brief draft to shipped; simple-change and bug-report draft to closed). The build script does not import the registry: the statuses are constants of the contract.

items.name: .pasta-data (gitignored data folder, read only) - input to collect
items.text: C:/Repos/pasta/.pasta-data (the main checkout's data folder; a worktree has none, so collect runs with --data-dir pointing at it). Root: ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json (live, 3.4 MB, 222 pages, rewritten by every MCP write while this brief runs) plus two other live workspaces (ws_mu596be5-a67213, ws_mujrihdx-24ebd2) whose pages link no pasta-dev PR. backups/: 17 *.json files, as backups/<ws_token>.json and backups/<ws_token>/<UTC stamp>.json. A document is {id, name, status, root_page_ids, created_at, updated_at, guidance_config, pages: {id: page}}; a page has type, title, parent_id, child_ids, sections; the link is sections.pull_request.url. Measured with a throwaway probe: 57 of PRs #1-#65 are linked (unlinked: #7 #14 #16 #18 #19 #33 #35 #59), PR #13 by two pages (bug-report:mtg93y9z-f3bee2, feature-brief:mth0ojmm-a53787), PR #66 is linked too (out of range), and one url is a branch url (.../tree/timeline-lifecycle-log) that the design's pattern rejects. Every linked feature-brief has an implementation-plan: and a testing-plan: child. Root tocs of the live document: Features toc:ms90fb2w-721ea1, Bug Reports toc:ms90fbg0-ba90c1.

items.name: src/ids.py (read only) - pure
items.text: Page ids are <type>:<base-36 epoch ms>-<random> (_base36 at line 18, encode only via divmod). Nothing in src/ decodes an id back to a time (no int(..., 36) anywhere under src/), which is what criterion mwkzgsoy-b627ca keeps: decoding lives only in scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py.

items.name: scripts/ conventions and pytest import path
items.text: scripts/ is a plain folder (no __init__.py). A script that imports src puts the repo root on sys.path first (scripts/gen_page_type_docs.py lines 19-20: _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent; sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT))) and is run as `uv run python scripts/<name>.py` (justfile). pyproject [tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ['.'] makes `import scripts.<name>` work from tests (checked: `import scripts.validate_workspace` resolves as a namespace package). scripts/validate_workspace.py is the precedent for a read-only reader of a data-folder document.

items.name: Spike precedent at 6556fb1 (.claude/worktrees/spike-timeline-node-timeline/spike/timeline, read only)
items.text: build-dates.mjs keeps the GitHub MCP list_pull_requests output for PRs #1-#65 verbatim as [number, rule, ISO time] (rule m = merged_at, c = closed_at of a PR closed unmerged: #20 #25 #33 #35 #48, o = created_at of a still-open PR: #44 #60). data/pr-titles.json holds the titles of #1-#66. data/initial-commit-463cf4f-message.txt holds the 62 dated lines of commit 463cf4f's message - byte-identical (after CR stripping) to the dated lines of `git log -1 --format=%B 463cf4f` in this repo. build-dataset.mjs is the rule precedent: moments (PR time, commit lines spread over 09:00-21:00 UTC of their day, ties bumped by 1 s), the title type rule, plans ready at +30 and +45 min, page finished at +60 min. Precedent only, never merged: it works in seconds, uses synthetic toc ids and <type>:NNNN ids.

items.name: tests/ (test mode)
items.text: tests/conftest.py puts the whole run in test mode at import: production page types do not resolve and registered_pagetypes() lists only test-* fixtures. tests/test_timeline_backfill.py needs no page type at all (check_backfill and encode do not read the registry), and must not need the gitignored .pasta-data: it reads only the committed inputs and the committed back-fill. Baseline on this branch before any change: `uv run pytest --testmon` 1048 passed.
Python floor: requires-python = ">=3.14" (pyproject.toml). No new dependency: the script and test use the stdlib only (argparse, json, re, datetime, pathlib, os, sys).

Ownership (agent-plan:mwkzv9e2-e3c586): change only scripts/timeline_dataset/pull-requests.json, scripts/timeline_dataset/initial-commit-463cf4f.txt, scripts/timeline_dataset/workspace-pages.json, scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py, backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl and tests/test_timeline_backfill.py (all new). The data folder .pasta-data is only ever read: collect writes only scripts/timeline_dataset/workspace-pages.json and build writes only backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl.

Contract mwkzwvpy-98b45a (the back-fill file), exactly as written on the epic: kinds created and status only, in the event-line format of mwkzwvpv-63fd76, seq 1..N with no hole, ts never decreasing, written with lifecycle_log.encode so a rebuild is byte-identical; real page ids (and a linked feature-brief's real plan ids) for linked PRs, <type>:bf-<NNNN> (4 digits, one counter in moment order) otherwise, the real Features and Bug Reports tocs as trunks; titles the PR title (the later PR's for a shared page) or the commit line, plans '<title> - implementation plan' and '<title> - testing plan', tocs 'Features' and 'Bug Reports'; created at c with status draft (tocs active), parent the toc (feature-brief, simple-change to Features; bug-report to Bug Reports) or the feature (plans); implementation-plan draft to ready at moment + 1_800_000, testing-plan at moment + 2_700_000, the page draft to shipped (feature-brief) or draft to closed (simple-change, bug-report) at moment + 3_600_000; tocs created at the earliest c and never changed; expected 314 pages, 626 lines.

Line endings: .gitattributes declares `* text=auto eol=lf`, so a checkout keeps the back-fill's LF endings on Windows; the script must still write bytes (or newline='') so Python on Windows does not turn each newline into CRLF, and git diff stays empty after a rebuild.
Criterion mwkzgsoy-b627ca: id timestamps are decoded only in scripts/ - no int(..., 36) anywhere under src/ (none today).

Tests run in test mode (tests/conftest.py) with `uv run pytest --testmon` (CLAUDE.md, workspace testingTool). Baseline on this branch: 1048 passed. tests/test_timeline_backfill.py must run on a clean checkout: no .pasta-data, no network, no production page type.

Types: [tool.pyright] include = ["src/**/*"] with typeCheckingMode = "recommended" (pyproject.toml), so scripts/ and tests/ are outside basedpyright's scope; the script is still written fully annotated in the house style (from __future__ import annotations, PEP 695 type aliases).

GitHub inputs: this session has no GitHub MCP tools (ToolSearch for github finds none) and no gh CLI (not on the bash PATH, not found by PowerShell Get-Command, not under Program Files). Per the agent-plan's Task the inputs therefore come from the copies fetched through the GitHub MCP and committed in the approved spike at 6556fb1 (build-dates.mjs's verbatim PR times, data/pr-titles.json, data/initial-commit-463cf4f-message.txt).
Wording (CLAUDE.md): use the word "create", not "mint", in code, comments and docs.

The fallback GitHub source (spike 6556fb1, build-dates.mjs) recorded for each PR only the one time its moment uses - merged_at for 58 PRs, closed_at for the 5 closed unmerged (#20 #25 #33 #35 #48), created_at for the 2 still open (#44 #60) - not all three. So scripts/timeline_dataset/pull-requests.json cannot hold created_at for 63 PRs, nor closed_at for the merged ones, 'as GitHub returns them', while this brief's own interface mwkso7pb-651210 types created_at as str. What has to give: the inputs file carries the recorded time in its own field and null for the times the source did not record (created_at becomes str or null); build's moment rule (merged_at, else closed_at, else created_at) reads exactly the recorded field, so the back-fill file is unaffected. Settled in the spec; a later re-fetch through the GitHub MCP can fill the nulls without changing the back-fill.

The data folder also links PR #66 (outside #1-#65) and holds a branch url (.../pasta-dev/tree/timeline-lifecycle-log, wave 1's registration; this brief's own registration will add .../tree/timeline-backfill). The design's pattern ^https://github.com/dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev/pull/(\d+)(?:[/?#]|$) rejects the branch urls, and collect keeps only PRs #1-#65 (the Expected-changes text 'per PR #1-#65'), so links made later do not churn the committed workspace-pages.json.

collect reads the live workspace file while MCP writes rewrite it (it changed during grounding). The store replaces it atomically (os.replace), so one json.load sees a whole document; the committed workspace-pages.json is a snapshot, and build reads only that snapshot, so the back-fill stays reproducible however the live file moves on.

The design says collect reads every *.json at the data-dir root and under backups/, which includes two other workspaces (ws:mu596be5-a67213, ws:mujrihdx-24ebd2). A page of another workspace can never be a page of pasta's own workspace's history; none links a pasta-dev PR today. Settled in the spec: collect still reads every file but takes pages only from documents whose id is ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6 - same output today, and no foreign id can leak into the back-fill.

lifecycle_log.stamp gives every event one shared ts (one commit), but each back-fill line keeps its own ts. The builder creates the stamped line dicts itself, in event-line key order (seq, ts, page, kind, then the kind's keys), and writes them with lifecycle_log.encode - no change to wave 1's module or to any contract.

The spike's build-dataset.mjs is precedent, not code: it works in seconds (fractional commit-line instants), creates every page at its moment, uses synthetic toc ids and <type>:NNNN ids. The design changes these (milliseconds rounded, decoded create times for linked pages, real tocs, <type>:bf-NNNN). A throwaway probe of the design's rules over the spike copies and today's data folder reproduces the design's numbers: 127 moments; 126 moment pages (56 real: 31 feature-briefs, 15 simple-changes, 10 bug-reports; 70 back-fill-only: 62, 6, 2); 23 real types differ from the title rule; longest wait PR #25 (feature-brief:mtiml5v4-6c209f) 41.24 days, median 0.23 days; no decoded time later than its first moment; earliest create 2026-07-20 09:40 UTC.

Criterion mwkzgsos-e866a1's reviewer run (dev server on a copy of .pasta-data, one write, then /ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/timeline) needs wave 3: src/server.py does not pass backfill_dir yet and the view does not exist. This brief delivers and tests the file, its counts, its contract and its byte-for-byte rebuild; the install itself is already covered by wave 1's store tests on small fixture back-fills.

architecture:mrteq39m-de7a49 (Pasta Project Overview): its data model and code references gain the repo's committed backfill/<ws_token>.jsonl (today only backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl: the initial back-fill rebuilt from PR history, copied by the store as lines 1..N into the empty log of that workspace at its first write once the server passes backfill_dir) and scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py (collect reads the data folder into scripts/timeline_dataset/workspace-pages.json; build turns the three committed inputs under scripts/timeline_dataset/ into the back-fill). Wave 1's documentation item left the backfill/ folder to this wave.
How does scripts/timeline_dataset/pull-requests.json carry the PR times the fallback source (spike 6556fb1) did not record - created_at for merged or closed PRs, closed_at for merged ones?
items.answer: pull-requests.json is a JSON array of exactly PRs #1-#65 ascending, each {number, title, created_at, merged_at, closed_at}: the title from the spike's data/pr-titles.json, and the one time build-dates.mjs recorded - the ISO string GitHub returned, verbatim - in the field its rule names (m: merged_at, c: closed_at, o: created_at). The other two are null, meaning not recorded by this source, so created_at is typed str or null. The moment rule (merged_at, else closed_at, else created_at) reads exactly the recorded field, so every moment and the back-fill are unchanged; a later re-fetch through the GitHub MCP can fill the nulls without moving a byte of the back-fill. Rejected: setting closed_at = merged_at for merged PRs (an inference about GitHub, not a recorded value), inventing created_at, and fetching through a channel the Task does not name.

items.text: Which documents does collect take PR-linked pages from - every *.json it reads (three workspaces), or only documents of ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6 - and how are pages seen in several files merged?
items.answer: collect reads, as the design says, every *.json at the data-dir root (sorted by name) and every *.json under backups/ recursively (sorted by path), root files first; linked_pages takes pages only from documents whose id is ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6 (the other two workspaces link no PR today, so the output is the same, and a foreign page can never be part of this workspace's history). It keeps pages of type feature-brief, simple-change or bug-report whose sections.pull_request.url matches the design's pattern with a PR number in 1..65; one record per page id, the first document read wins (the live file first), records sorted by id. A feature-brief's implementation_plan / testing_plan is the first child id starting with 'implementation-plan:' / 'testing-plan:' (an id carries its type, src/ids.py), else null; other types carry null for both. The live document is the file <data-dir>/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json itself, never backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json (same id). The tocs are the first root page, in the live root_page_ids order, of type toc titled exactly Features, and likewise Bug Reports.

items.text: How exactly are the 127 moments computed in integer milliseconds - rounding of the commit-line spread, tie-breaks and the +1 s bump - so they equal the spike dataset's moments the user judged?
items.answer: A PR's moment is merged_at, else closed_at, else created_at, parsed with datetime.fromisoformat (Z as UTC) to epoch ms. Commit lines are grouped by date in file order; line i (from 0) of the k lines dated d is at d 00:00 UTC + 9 h + round-half-up((2i + 1) x 12 h / 2k) ms, computed in integers ((2 x num + den) // (2 x den)) so no float rounding enters. All moments are sorted by (ms, 0 for a PR / 1 for a commit line) with a stable sort, so ties keep PR number order and file order; then, walking in order, a moment not later than the previous one becomes the previous + 1000 ms. A probe of exactly this over the spike copies gives 127 moments, each equal to round(spike dataset moment in seconds x 1000).

items.text: How is a page shared by several PRs (#20 and #21 share simple-change:mtisbfq5-9c02c8) built: where it sits in build order and in the bf counter, which moment times its plans and finish, and which title it gets?
items.answer: Pages are built walking the moments in order. A linked moment whose chosen page was already built adds no page: it sets that page's title to this PR's title and its last moment to this moment. So a shared page sits in build order at its first moment, its one created line carries the latest PR's title, it is created at min(id time, first moment), its plans (for a feature-brief) go ready at last moment + 30 and + 45 min and it finishes at last moment + 60 min. The bf counter numbers only back-fill-only pages, never a real page. Today the only shared page is simple-change:mtisbfq5-9c02c8 (#20 closed, #21 merged; both titled 'Read page types through one `registered_pagetypes()` accessor'), closed at #21's merge + 1 h.

items.text: How are the back-fill-only ids numbered, and how does the title rule's 'starting with Add' read (any 'Add...' word, or 'Add ' followed by a space)?
items.answer: One counter from 1, in moment order, over back-fill-only pages only: the page takes the next number and, for a feature-brief, its implementation-plan and testing-plan the two after it (feature-brief:bf-0001, implementation-plan:bf-0002, testing-plan:bf-0003, simple-change:bf-0004, ...); <type>:bf-NNNN zero-padded to 4 digits, 194 ids today. The title rule is the spike's (the judged dataset's) exactly: a title starting 'Add ' (with the space) is a feature-brief; else one the bug pattern finds (case-insensitive search) is a bug-report; else one whose first space-separated word is in the small-edit set, or that starts with 'PEP8 style cleanup' or 'Review guidance', is a simple-change; else a feature-brief. No title today starts with 'Add' without a space, so both readings agree on the data.

items.text: What do collect and build do on bad or incomplete inputs - a missing live document or toc, a missing input file, a malformed commit line, a PR in #1-#65 missing or with no time, a moment count other than 127, a linked feature-brief with no implementation-plan or testing-plan child - and where do those checks live?
items.answer: Every rule check is pure and raises ValueError (or returns problems); main maps any of them, and any OSError or JSON error from reading, to a message on stderr, exit 1, and nothing written. collect: the live file missing or unparsable, or either toc missing from its roots. build: any of the three inputs missing or unparsable; a commit line (every newline-separated piece except the empty one after the final newline) not matching ^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})  (.+)$; input_problems non-empty - a PR of 1..65 missing, a PR with none of its three times, or a moment count other than 127; a linked feature-brief whose implementation_plan or testing_plan is null (build_backfill raises: the contract asks for its real plan ids, and bf ids would give one feature two kinds of ids).

items.text: Where do the script's pure rules and its effects split, and how do tests reach collect and build without touching the repo's committed files or the real data folder?
items.answer: One file, scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py. Pure: id_time_ms, linked_pages, workspace_pages, parse_commit_lines, input_problems, moments, title_type, build_backfill, summary. Effectful and thin: read_documents(data_dir), collect(data_dir, out_path) -> int, build(dataset_dir, out_path) -> int, main(argv) -> int, writing bytes only to the out_path it is given. Tests import scripts.build_timeline_dataset (pytest pythonpath '.'), drive the pure functions on small in-memory fixtures, and call collect and build with tmp_path folders and output paths, so neither the committed files nor the real data folder are touched; the committed back-fill is checked by rebuilding it from the committed inputs and comparing bytes.

Spec to steps: committed GitHub inputs (step 1), id_time_ms and title_type (2), linked_pages and workspace_pages (3), parse_commit_lines, input_problems and moments (4), build_backfill (5), summary (6), read_documents/collect/main collect (7), build/main build (8), the committed back-fill and its contract checks (9), whole-suite and rebuild check (10). Every step answers a spec section or criterion mwkzgsos-e866a1 / mwkzgsoy-b627ca; none updates documentation. Pure steps 2-6 precede the shell steps 7-8; each step stays on one side.

Testing plan, title-rule case: its 'Additional docs -> feature-brief' example could not fail under either reading of 'starting with Add' (both give feature-brief), so it did not pin the decided 'Add ' with a space. Applied: the case was replaced (mwl3n4m3-21351c) with 'Addressing the error on load' -> bug-report, which fails if the rule matched 'Add' without the space, and 'Renamed pages keep links' -> feature-brief, which pins the whole-first-word verb match.

Testing plan: the spec's collect error path for an unreadable document (a JSON error in any file read maps to exit 1 with nothing written) had no case. Applied: the collect failure case was replaced (mwl3n4m5-6d65fe) to also cover a backup file holding invalid JSON.

Volume: 20 documents (about 18 MB) are parsed once by collect and 127 moments / 626 lines by build; both run in a second or two, so no streaming or caching is planned. Step 7 runs collect against the live data folder while MCP writes keep replacing ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json; the store replaces it atomically, so one read sees a whole document, and the committed snapshot is all build reads.

inlines.text: Step 1 - commit the two GitHub inputs (data, no code). Files created: scripts/timeline_dataset/pull-requests.json and scripts/timeline_dataset/initial-commit-463cf4f.txt. Source (no GitHub MCP and no gh in this session): the copies committed in the approved spike at 6556fb1, read with `git show` from that commit so a modified spike worktree cannot leak in. pull-requests.json is a JSON array of PRs #1..#65 ascending, each {number, title, created_at, merged_at, closed_at}: the title from data/pr-titles.json; the verbatim GitHub time from build-dates.mjs put in the field its rule letter names (m -> merged_at, c -> closed_at, o -> created_at); the other two null. Written as json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + newline, UTF-8 bytes. The commit file is copied byte for byte.

detail.source:
mkdir -p scripts/timeline_dataset
git show 6556fb1:spike/timeline/data/initial-commit-463cf4f-message.txt > scripts/timeline_dataset/initial-commit-463cf4f.txt
uv run python - <<'EOF'
import json, re, subprocess
show = lambda p: subprocess.run(['git', 'show', f'6556fb1:spike/timeline/{p}'], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout.decode('utf-8')
rows = json.loads(re.search(r'const prs = (\[\[.*?\]\]);', show('build-dates.mjs')).group(1).replace("'", '"'))
titles = json.loads(show('data/pr-titles.json'))
field = {'m': 'merged_at', 'c': 'closed_at', 'o': 'created_at'}
prs = []
for number, rule, time in rows:
    pr = {'number': number, 'title': titles[str(number)], 'created_at': None, 'merged_at': None, 'closed_at': None}
    pr[field[rule]] = time
    prs.append(pr)
open('scripts/timeline_dataset/pull-requests.json', 'wb').write((json.dumps(prs, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n').encode('utf-8'))
EOF

detail.source:
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))   # make `src` importable when run as a bare script

from src import lifecycle_log
from src.lifecycle_log import Event

WORKSPACE_ID = "ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6"
LIVE_FILENAME = "ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json"
DATASET_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "timeline_dataset"
BACKFILL_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "backfill" / "ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl"
PULL_REQUESTS_FILE, INITIAL_COMMIT_FILE, WORKSPACE_PAGES_FILE = "pull-requests.json", "initial-commit-463cf4f.txt", "workspace-pages.json"
PR_NUMBERS = range(1, 66)
EXPECTED_MOMENTS = 127
LINKED_TYPES = ("feature-brief", "simple-change", "bug-report")
PR_URL = re.compile(r"^https://github\.com/dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev/pull/(\d+)(?:[/?#]|$)")
HOUR_MS = 3_600_000
IMPLEMENTATION_READY_MS, TESTING_READY_MS, FINISH_MS = 1_800_000, 2_700_000, 3_600_000
DAY_START_MS, DAY_SPAN_MS, BUMP_MS = 9 * HOUR_MS, 12 * HOUR_MS, 1_000
FINISH_STATUS = {"feature-brief": "shipped", "simple-change": "closed", "bug-report": "closed"}
BUG = re.compile(r"\b(fix|crash|crashing|error)\b|against the write|rejected batch|instead of (rejecting|crashing)", re.IGNORECASE)
SMALL_EDIT_VERBS = frozenset("Rename Retire Move Clarify Drop Remove Bump Label Keep Convert Link Include Show Upgrade Write Read Resolve Match Carry Send Allow Store Replace".split())
SMALL_EDIT_PREFIXES = ("PEP8 style cleanup", "Review guidance")

class Moment(NamedTuple):
    ts: int
    title: str
    pr: int | None

def id_time_ms(page_id: str) -> int:
    token = page_id.split(":", 1)[1]
    return int(token.split("-")[0], 36)

def title_type(title: str) -> str:
    if title.startswith("Add "):
        return "feature-brief"
    if BUG.search(title):
        return "bug-report"
    if title.split(" ")[0] in SMALL_EDIT_VERBS or title.startswith(SMALL_EDIT_PREFIXES):
        return "simple-change"
    return "feature-brief"

inlines.text: Step 5 (pure) - add build_backfill(prs, commit_lines, pages) -> list[Event] to scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py, with a small mutable dataclass for a page during the walk (id, type, title, created, last, plans). Walk moments(prs, commit_lines): for a PR whose str(number) has records in pages['prs'], chosen = min by (id_time_ms(id), id); an already built chosen page only takes this moment's title and last = this ts; else a new page with the real id and type, created = min(id_time_ms(id), ts), plans = the real plan ids for a feature-brief (ValueError if either is None). Otherwise a back-fill-only page: type = title_type(title); counter += 1; id <type>:bf-NNNN; a feature-brief's plans take the next two numbers. Then lines: two toc created lines at c0 = min(created) (type toc, titles Features / Bug Reports, parent None, status active), then per page in build order: created page (parent Bug Reports toc for a bug-report, else Features toc; status draft); for a feature-brief created implementation-plan and testing-plan at created (parent the page, titles '<title> - implementation plan' / '<title> - testing plan', draft) and status draft->ready at last + 1_800_000 and last + 2_700_000; status draft->shipped (feature-brief) or draft->closed at last + 3_600_000. Stable sort by ts, then each line re-created as a new dict starting with seq (1..N) followed by its ts, page, kind and kind keys. Tests first on a fixture of 3 PRs and 2 commit lines: a linked feature-brief created at its id time with real plan ids and +30/+45/+60 min statuses; two PRs sharing one page give one created line titled with the later PR and finish at the later moment + 1 h; a PR with two linked pages takes the earlier id; a decoded time later than the moment is clamped to the moment; bf ids number page then plans (bf-0001..bf-0003, then bf-0004); tocs first; seq 1..N, ts never decreasing, key order exact, and lifecycle_log.check_backfill accepts the encoded output; a linked feature-brief without a testing_plan raises ValueError.

items.text: test_id_time_ms_decodes_the_base36_milliseconds_of_a_page_id (pure): id_time_ms('feature-brief:mtiml5v4-6c209f') == int('mtiml5v4', 36), and that instant falls on 2026-09-01 UTC; a type prefix with a dash (implementation-plan:...) decodes the same way.

test_title_type_follows_the_judged_rule_in_order (pure): 'Add a fix for X' -> feature-brief (the Add rule wins over the bug pattern); 'Addressing the error on load' -> bug-report (only 'Add ' with a space is the Add rule); 'Report the revision a rejected batch leaves behind' and 'Stop the crash on load' -> bug-report; 'Rename state to status', 'PEP8 style cleanup: spacing' and 'Review guidance for planReview' -> simple-change; 'Renamed pages keep links' -> feature-brief (the verb must be the whole first word); 'Make initial_sections idempotent' -> feature-brief.

test_linked_pages_keeps_only_pr_links_of_the_workspace_in_range (pure): on in-memory documents, urls .../pull/3, .../pull/3/files, .../pull/3?x=1 and .../pull/3#c match PR 3; .../tree/timeline-backfill, another repo's /pull/3, /pull/3abc, /pull/0 and /pull/66 do not; an epic carrying a PR url and a page of a document with another workspace id are ignored.

test_linked_pages_first_document_wins_and_plan_ids_come_from_child_prefixes (pure): a page seen in two documents with different child_ids keeps the first document's record; a feature-brief's implementation_plan and testing_plan are its first children with those id prefixes, None when absent; a simple-change and a bug-report carry None for both; each PR's records are sorted by id.

test_workspace_pages_finds_the_root_tocs_and_rejects_a_missing_one (pure): the toc ids are the first root pages of type toc titled exactly Features and Bug Reports (a non-root toc or a page titled 'Features' of another type is not taken); prs keys are the PR numbers as strings in ascending order; ValueError when either toc is missing and when the live document's id is not ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6.

test_parse_commit_lines_reads_dated_lines_and_rejects_others (pure): '2026-07-20  First pass\n2026-07-21  Second\n' -> [('2026-07-20', 'First pass'), ('2026-07-21', 'Second')]; a line with one space after the date, a missing date or an empty line inside raises ValueError naming the line.

test_input_problems_names_missing_prs_timeless_prs_and_a_wrong_count (pure): a synthetic complete input (PRs 1..65 each with merged_at, 62 commit lines) gives []; removing PR 7 names PR #7 and the count (126 moments); a PR with all three times null is named.

test_moments_take_the_recorded_pr_time_by_precedence (pure): a PR with merged_at and closed_at is at merged_at; one with only closed_at at closed_at; one with only created_at at created_at; '2026-08-25T18:48:23Z' becomes 1787683703000 ms.

test_moments_spread_a_days_commit_lines_over_nine_to_twenty_one_utc (pure): one line on a day is at 15:00 UTC; two at 12:00 and 18:00; three at 11:00, 15:00 and 19:00; the order of a day's lines follows the file.

test_moments_put_prs_first_on_a_tie_and_bump_by_a_second (pure): a PR merged at the instant a commit line lands comes first and the line moves to +1000 ms; three moments at one instant come out at +0, +1000 and +2000 ms; moments are strictly increasing.

test_build_backfill_uses_real_ids_and_decoded_create_times_for_linked_prs (pure, fixture): a PR linked to a feature-brief whose id time precedes the PR's moment gives created lines for that id, its real implementation-plan and testing-plan ids at the id time, parent the Features toc; plan ready lines at moment + 1_800_000 and + 2_700_000 and the page's draft -> shipped at moment + 3_600_000; a linked bug-report has the Bug Reports toc as parent and finishes draft -> closed; a PR with two linked pages takes the one with the earlier id time; a linked page whose id time is later than its moment is created at the moment.

overview.body: This spec covers wave 2 of epic epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b: building and committing the initial back-fill of pasta's own workspace log, backfill/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl, from this repo's real history. It owns six new files - three committed inputs under scripts/timeline_dataset/ (pull-requests.json, initial-commit-463cf4f.txt, workspace-pages.json), the build script scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py (collect reads the data folder, build turns the committed inputs into the back-fill), the back-fill file itself, and tests/test_timeline_backfill.py - and it defines the epic's shared contract mwkzwvpy-98b45a for the file. It restates the sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae for this slice (interface mwkso7pb-651210, Part 4 of the strategy, decisions mwkskobk-75d976, mwkskobp-badddc, mwkskobs-bdf634, mwksl2hd-1d23b3, mwkslpkw-a89109, mwkslpky-35789c, mwkzcf9o-e3c7c5, mwkzcf9r-aaa908, mwkzcf9u-8c158e; criteria mwkzgsos-e866a1 and mwkzgsoy-b627ca) and settles only what the design left open. It deliberately leaves out: installing the file into a log (wave 1's Store._load_for_write, already built), passing backfill_dir to the server and playing the file at /ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/timeline (wave 3), and any change to src/.

body.text: Binding design decisions (restated, not reopened)

mwkskobk-75d976: pasta's own workspace is back-filled once, as the start of its lifecycle log, from this file only; nothing else before recording is back-filled. mwkskobp-badddc: one page per each of the 127 real moments (PRs #1-#65 of dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev plus the 62 dated lines of commit 463cf4f), titled with the PR title or commit line, a feature-brief with its implementation-plan and testing-plan, the spike's change and ship times kept, create times reverse-engineered from page ids. mwkskobs-bdf634: a linked PR's page is the real page (its id, real type, real plan ids); every other moment gets <type>:bf-NNNN typed by the title rule. mwksl2hd-1d23b3: the file uses the log's own keys (seq, ts, page, kind, kind keys). mwkslpkw-a89109: two steps, collect (reads, never writes, the data folder into the committed workspace-pages.json) and build (pure over the three committed inputs). mwkslpky-35789c: earliest id wins among a PR's linked pages; PRs sharing a page are one page finished at the later PR's moment + 1 h with the later PR's title; never created later than its first moment; unlinked moments created at the moment; plans created with their page. mwkzcf9o-e3c7c5: titles are PR titles or commit lines, plans '<title> - implementation plan' / '<title> - testing plan'. mwkzcf9r-aaa908: the real Features and Bug Reports tocs are the trunks, created at the earliest create time. mwkzcf9u-8c158e: seq 1..N in ts order.
Committed inputs (scripts/timeline_dataset/)

body.text: Pure rules (scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py)

body.source:
WORKSPACE_ID = "ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6"
PR_NUMBERS = range(1, 66)
EXPECTED_MOMENTS = 127
LINKED_TYPES = ("feature-brief", "simple-change", "bug-report")
PR_URL = re.compile(r"^https://github\.com/dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev/pull/(\d+)(?:[/?#]|$)")
HOUR_MS = 3_600_000
IMPLEMENTATION_READY_MS, TESTING_READY_MS, FINISH_MS = 1_800_000, 2_700_000, 3_600_000

class Moment(NamedTuple):
    ts: int            # epoch ms
    title: str         # PR title or commit-line text
    pr: int | None     # the PR number, None for a commit line

def id_time_ms(page_id: str) -> int
    # int(token.split("-")[0], 36) for token = page_id.split(":", 1)[1]; ValueError when it does not decode

def linked_pages(documents: Iterable[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[int, list[dict[str, Any]]]
    # Only documents whose "id" is WORKSPACE_ID; only pages whose type is in LINKED_TYPES and whose
    # sections.pull_request.url matches PR_URL with a number in PR_NUMBERS. One record per page id, the first
    # document wins: {"id", "type", "implementation_plan", "testing_plan"} - for a feature-brief the first
    # child id starting "implementation-plan:" / "testing-plan:", else None; other types None. Lists sorted by id.

def workspace_pages(live: dict[str, Any], documents: Iterable[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]
    # The workspace-pages.json value: tocs = the first root page (live["root_page_ids"] order) of type toc titled
    # exactly "Features", and likewise "Bug Reports"; prs = linked_pages(documents) keyed by str(n), ascending.
    # ValueError when live is not WORKSPACE_ID's document or either toc is missing.

def parse_commit_lines(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
    # (date, text) per line; the empty piece after the final newline is ignored; a line not matching
    # ^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})  (.+)$ raises ValueError naming it.

def input_problems(prs: list[dict[str, Any]], commit_lines: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[str]
    # One message per problem: a number of PR_NUMBERS missing; a PR with none of merged_at, closed_at,
    # created_at; len(prs) + len(commit_lines) != EXPECTED_MOMENTS. [] when the inputs are complete.

def title_type(title: str) -> str
    # "feature-brief" if title.startswith("Add "); else "bug-report" if BUG.search(title); else "simple-change"
    # if title.split(" ")[0] in SMALL_EDIT_VERBS or title.startswith(("PEP8 style cleanup", "Review guidance"));
    # else "feature-brief".
    # BUG = re.compile(r"\b(fix|crash|crashing|error)\b|against the write|rejected batch|instead of (rejecting|crashing)", re.I)
    # SMALL_EDIT_VERBS = Rename Retire Move Clarify Drop Remove Bump Label Keep Convert Link Include Show Upgrade
    #                    Write Read Resolve Match Carry Send Allow Store Replace

def moments(prs: list[dict[str, Any]], commit_lines: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[Moment]
    # See Moments below.

def build_backfill(prs: list[dict[str, Any]], commit_lines: list[tuple[str, str]],
                   pages: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Event]
    # The stamped back-fill lines, seq 1..N. See Pages and Lines below. ValueError for a linked
    # feature-brief whose implementation_plan or testing_plan is None.

def summary(lines: list[Event], pages: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]
    # Printable lines: pages per type, line count, PRs mapped to a real page (len(pages["prs"])),
    # back-fill-only moment pages, and the longest wait (finish ts - FINISH_MS - created ts) with its page id, in days.

body.text: Moments

body.source:
PR moment   = epoch ms of merged_at, else closed_at, else created_at (datetime.fromisoformat, Z as UTC)
commit line = lines grouped by date in file order; line i (from 0) of the k lines dated d:
              ms(d 00:00 UTC) + 9 * HOUR_MS + (2 * num + den) // (2 * den)   with num = (2i + 1) * 12 * HOUR_MS, den = 2k
              (round half up of (i + 0.5) / k * 12 h, in integers)
order       = stable sort by (ts, 0 for a PR / 1 for a commit line): PRs in input order, commit lines in file order on a tie
bump        = walking in order, a ts not later than the previous one becomes previous + 1000
result      = 127 Moments today, each equal to round(spike dataset moment seconds * 1000)

body.text: Pages

body.source:
walk the moments in order, keeping pages in first-seen (build) order:
  linked = pages["prs"].get(str(m.pr)) when m.pr is not None
  linked non-empty:
    chosen = min(linked, key=(id_time_ms(id), id))
    chosen already built -> page.title = m.title; page.last = m.ts          (a shared page; no new page)
    else new page: id = chosen.id, type = chosen.type, title = m.title, first = last = m.ts,
                   created = min(id_time_ms(chosen.id), m.ts),
                   plans = (chosen.implementation_plan, chosen.testing_plan) for a feature-brief
                           (ValueError if either is None), else none
  otherwise (unlinked PR or commit line):
    type = title_type(m.title); n = next counter value (counter starts at 1, back-fill-only pages only)
    id = f"{type}:bf-{n:04d}"; for a feature-brief plans = (f"implementation-plan:bf-{n+1:04d}",
    f"testing-plan:bf-{n+2:04d}") and the counter moves past them; created = first = last = m.ts
parent = pages["tocs"]["Bug Reports"] for a bug-report, else pages["tocs"]["Features"]
finish status = "shipped" for a feature-brief, "closed" for a simple-change or bug-report

body.text: Lines

body.source:
c0 = min(page.created over the moment pages)
build order:
  created  toc Features      at c0  {type toc, title "Features",    parent null, status active}
  created  toc Bug Reports   at c0  {type toc, title "Bug Reports", parent null, status active}
  per page in build order:
    created  page                 at page.created  {type, title: page.title, parent, status draft}
    feature-brief only:
      created  implementation plan at page.created  {implementation-plan, "<title> - implementation plan", parent page.id, draft}
      created  testing plan        at page.created  {testing-plan, "<title> - testing plan", parent page.id, draft}
      status   implementation plan at page.last + IMPLEMENTATION_READY_MS  draft -> ready
      status   testing plan        at page.last + TESTING_READY_MS         draft -> ready
    status   page                 at page.last + FINISH_MS   draft -> shipped | closed
stable sort by ts (ties keep build order); seq = position + 1
each line a new dict with keys in event-line order:
  created: seq, ts, page, kind, type, title, parent, status
  status:  seq, ts, page, kind, from, to
file text = "".join(lifecycle_log.encode(line) for line in lines)   (UTF-8 bytes)

body.text: Effectful shell

body.source:
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent; sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT)) before `from src import lifecycle_log`
DATASET_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "timeline_dataset";  BACKFILL_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "backfill" / "ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.jsonl"

read_documents(data_dir: Path) -> list[tuple[Path, dict[str, Any]]]
    every *.json directly in data_dir (sorted by name), then every *.json under data_dir/backups recursively (sorted by
    path); each read as bytes, decoded UTF-8, json.loads. Opens nothing for writing.
collect(data_dir: Path, out_path: Path) -> int
    live = the document read from data_dir / "ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json"; value = workspace_pages(live, all documents);
    writes json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + newline as UTF-8 bytes to out_path only; prints the path,
    the number of PRs mapped and the files read; returns 0. Live file missing, any OSError/ValueError (JSON errors
    included) -> message on stderr, returns 1, writes nothing.
build(dataset_dir: Path, out_path: Path) -> int
    reads the three inputs; problems = input_problems(...); lines = build_backfill(...); mkdir out_path.parent;
    writes the file text as UTF-8 bytes to out_path only; prints summary(lines, pages); returns 0. A missing or
    unparsable input, a non-empty problems list or a ValueError -> message on stderr, returns 1, writes nothing.
main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int
    argparse subcommands: `collect [--data-dir PATH]` (default Path(os.environ.get("PASTA_DATA_DIR", ".pasta-data")),
    as src/server.py resolves its data folder) -> collect(data_dir, DATASET_DIR / "workspace-pages.json");
    `build` -> build(DATASET_DIR, BACKFILL_PATH). `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())`.
Run from the repo root: uv run python scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py collect --data-dir C:/Repos/pasta/.pasta-data
                      uv run python scripts/build_timeline_dataset.py build

body.text: Tests (tests/test_timeline_backfill.py)

Imports scripts.build_timeline_dataset and src.lifecycle_log; needs no data folder, no network and no page type. Against the committed files: lifecycle_log.check_backfill accepts the back-fill; kinds, page and line counts; titles; real ids, types and plan ids for linked PRs and bf ids with title-rule types otherwise; every create ts equals min(id_time_ms(id), first moment) or the moment and is never later than the first moment; plan-ready and finish times; build_backfill over the committed inputs reproduces the file byte for byte. body.text: pull-requests.json holds each PR's recorded time, verbatim, in the field its spike rule names and null for the two times the spike did not record; created_at is str or null. Rejected: closed_at = merged_at for merged PRs and any invented created_at (inferences presented as GitHub data), and a channel the Task does not name. Why: the moment rule reads exactly the recorded field, so the back-fill is unaffected and a later full re-fetch changes no byte of it.

collect reads every *.json the design names but takes linked pages only from ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6 documents, first document read wins (live file first), PRs 1..65 only; plan ids from child ids by type prefix; tocs the first matching roots of the live file at <data-dir>/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json. Rejected: pages from every workspace (a foreign id could enter pasta's history), keeping PR #66 and later (churns the committed file), the backup copy that shares the live id as the live document. Why: same result today and no way to pull in a page that was never in this workspace.

Moments in integer ms: PR time by precedence, commit lines spread with an integer round-half-up, stable sort with PRs first on a tie, then the +1000 ms bump. Rejected: float seconds as the spike computed (rounding drift), rounding after the bump. Why: byte-reproducible on any platform and equal to the spike moments the user judged (checked: all 127).

A shared page is placed at its first moment, takes the latest PR's title and times its plans and finish from its last moment; it never uses the bf counter. Rejected: two pages for one real id; the first PR's title; plans timed from the first moment while the page finishes at the last. Why: one real page has one life (mwkslpky-35789c) and plans finish before their page.

One counter from 1 over back-fill-only pages and their plans in moment order (page, then implementation-plan, then testing-plan), <type>:bf-NNNN; the title rule is the judged spike's, 'Add ' with a space. Rejected: separate counters per type; counting real pages; 'Add' without the space. Why: the contract says one counter in moment order, and the judged dataset's types must not move.

All rule checks are pure (ValueError or a problems list); collect and build map them, and any read or JSON error, to stderr, exit 1, nothing written. A linked feature-brief missing a plan id fails the build. Rejected: silently skipping bad inputs; falling back to bf plan ids for a real feature-brief. Why: the committed file must be exactly the contract's, or not written at all.

One script file with the pure rules on top and a thin shell (read_documents, collect, build, main) that writes only to the path it is given; tests call the shell with tmp_path. Rejected: a helper module under scripts/ (one use), shell functions with hard-coded output paths (a test would overwrite committed files). Why: smallest layout the design allows, and every rule is testable without I/O.

feature-brief:mwkzuqrd-6afdef.title: Timeline view: replay a workspace's lifecycle log as a Metro timeline

summary.body: Let a user watch how a workspace came to be: a Timeline link on the workspace tree page opens /ws:<id>/timeline, a full-viewport 2D Metro timeline of nodes that replays the workspace's lifecycle log served from /ws:<id>/timeline.json - each page branching off its parent's track when created and merging back when it finishes, every kind of change marked at its moment, a play/pause/scrub player at 0.25 days per second that speeds through empty stretches, hover with the page's title and status at that moment, flat and sharp with no glow and no animated circles - and plays pasta's own back-filled PR history through that same view. The WOW of this view is what the user cares about most. One of three briefs of epic epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b, built exactly to its sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae, with the approved spike page .claude/worktrees/spike-timeline-node-timeline/spike/timeline/metro.html at commit 6556fb1 as the look to match: it owns the design's expected changes to src/server.py, src/templates/_base.html, src/templates/tree.html, src/templates/timeline.html (new), src/static/timeline/timeline.js and timeline.css (new), tests/timeline/check_timeline.js (new), tests/test_timeline_renderer.py (new), tests/test_web.py, tests/test_server.py and README.md, and the architecture pages it makes stale (Web UI, HMR & live reload; Reads & navigation).

How exactly do the two routes read and fail - which store calls, in which order, and what does each answer for a missing workspace or another error?

items.text: How does the fold treat the edge cases the design leaves implicit: a present event moving a known page into a finish status, a created event for an id already known, the set of pages that end at the recording-start instant, a deleted page's later events, and a page whose type the table does not list?
items.answer: In array order: a created event for an id already known is ignored (one id, one life); every event for an unknown id and every unknown kind is ignored; events after a page's deleted event are ignored for it. A present event sets Model.recordingStart to its ts if not yet set; when its page is unknown it creates the record (born = ts, present = true, title/parent/status/own archived from the event, links from its links list, no created mark, and finishT = ts when its status is a finish status of its type - settled from that instant, no ship mark); when known it is a silent resync - a title, parent, status or archived segment is added at ts only where the value differs, open links not in its list end at ts and listed links not open start at ts, and if the new status is a finish status and finishT is null, finishT = ts (no mark). The pages that end at recordingStart are exactly those known when the first present event is read that no present event names; their endedAt = min(their endedAt if any, recordingStart). A page's type is the type of its first created or present event. A type missing from data.types has no initial and no finish status: it never sets finishT, and statusClass(status, undefined) can only answer warn, review or active.

items.text: On a time axis, what does 'not drawn while hidden' mean for history left of the playhead - is a page drawn by whether it is shown at the playhead, or by whether it was shown at each time position?
items.answer: By time position: on the time axis a page's lane, marks, ticks and links at time t are drawn solid only when t <= T and isShown(m, p, t) holds, and as grey ghost when t > T and the page will be shown at t (G on). So the column at the playhead is exactly the pages shown at T, history to its left is the workspace as it stood at each instant, an archived page's lane stops at its archive cross, and a page hidden for a while has a gap in its lane. The end caps are the one exception: an archive or delete cross is drawn at its own time when the page was shown just before it. The status chips and hover use the playhead T (chips) and the pointer's time (hover), each through isShown. The layout precomputes each page's shown intervals from isShown evaluated at every instant its own or any ever-ancestor's archived flag or parent changes, plus born and endedAt, so drawing binary-searches intervals instead of walking ancestors per mark; the node check verifies the intervals against isShown.

items.text: Which of the Metro layout choices the design leaves to the builder are taken: trunk row order and spacing, where a mark after finish sits when the parent itself has settled, where settled glyphs go when many settle at one instant (the baseline), when a track whose lane ended without finishing is free again, and which track a present-and-finished page has?
items.answer: Trunks: every page whose parent at born is null or a page the fold does not know is a trunk; trunk rows are 0, +24, -24, +48, -48, ... tracks in the order trunks are born (ties in array order), and no branch ever takes a trunk row. Branches: pages in born order; a page with at least one shown interval and not settled-from-birth gets lane0 = born and the free non-trunk track nearest the parent's row at born (rowAt of parentAt(p, born)), alternating sides by its index among its parent's children (the spike's rule); lane1 = finishT when it finishes, else the end of its last shown interval when that ends before t1 (archived or deleted for good, or ended at recordingStart), else t1; the track is free again 30 minutes after lane1 whenever lane1 < t1 (finished or ended), otherwise kept to the end. rowAt(p, t) = the trunk row for a trunk; the own track for t < finishT (or no finish); otherwise rowAt(parentAt(p, t), t) - so a mark after finish sits on whatever row its parent has at that time, following a parent that has itself settled up to the grandparent's track. A page present at the baseline in a finish status, or hidden for good from its first moment, gets track = null; the first sits as a settled glyph from recordingStart. Settled glyphs sit 22 px right of their finish instant on rowAt(parent, finishT); glyphs that would overlap on one row are packed rightwards 8 px apart in finish order, so the baseline's settled pages read as a row of beads after the recording-started hairline. The ship node itself is drawn at the end of the own lane, then the 22 px merge curve, then the glyph.

items.text: Which theme property colours which mark, what are the --tl-* values, and when does the canvas re-read them given _theme.js's asynchronous stylesheet swap?
items.answer: Stage background --background-body; overview strip background --background; axis text, rename ticks, edit ticks, labels and the recording-started hairline --text-muted; hovered label and hover outline --text-main; grid lines and branch/merge connectors --border (grid at a fixed 0.5 alpha); ghost future --text-muted at a fixed 0.35 alpha; status bars, dots, ship nodes and settled glyphs the --tl-<class> of their status; archive cross --tl-archived; delete cross --tl-warn; gate ring --tl-gate; link brackets --tl-link; playhead, its handle and the overview playhead --tl-accent with the handle text in --background-body; activity ticks: question asked or answered --tl-review, step done --tl-active, case passed --tl-done, edit --text-muted. Values are the approved spike's palette: body.light idle #8b95a7, active #2b6df0, review #e0961a, done #1c9a60, warn #d84343, archived #9aa1ad, gate #8a4fd6, link #7a5af8, accent #e5484d; body.dark idle #7d889c, active #5b8cff, review #f2b53f, done #3fcf8e, warn #ff6b6b, archived #5d6676, gate #b08cf5, link #9a86ff, accent #ff5d62. The canvas reads them with getComputedStyle(document.body) at mount, whenever a MutationObserver sees the body's class attribute change, and again on #js-stylesheet's load event (when the swapped water.css sheet has applied); each re-read redraws and drops the cached overview. All alphas are constants, never a function of time.

items.text: How do the player's controls behave at their edges: which speed each key 1-4 selects, what Play does at t1, whether seeking pauses, when the hover adds the from PR history note, and where the empty-log line is shown?
items.answer: Keys 1, 2, 3, 4 select the buttons in their order 0.25, 1, 4, 16 days per second (0.25 selected on load). Play at t1 seeks t0 and plays. Seeking (overview click or drag, arrow keys) keeps the play state; dragging the stage pans and turns Follow off; F and G toggle Follow and Future, Space plays and pauses (its default scroll prevented). The playhead stops at t1 and play pauses there. The hover title and status are at the playhead (title at the pointer's time when the page is not yet born at T); the from PR history note is added when the playhead or the pointer's time is before recordingStart. An empty log (t0 null) or a failed fetch draws one centred line on the stage canvas - No history recorded yet for this workspace., or Could not load the timeline (<status>). - and the controls stay inert.

items.text: How are the renderer's checks organised - where the node check gets the page-type table, how its brute-force replay is kept independent of the fold, which moments it samples - and how are the STORE construction and the MCP non-goal checked?
items.answer: tests/timeline/check_timeline.js embeds the production types table for the types it uses and takes `--types <file>` to replace it; tests/test_timeline_renderer.py (production_mode fixture) writes lifecycle_log.timeline_types() to a tmp file and runs `node tests/timeline/check_timeline.js --types <file>` with subprocess when shutil.which('node') finds node, else skips, asserting exit 0 and printing the output on failure. The check's brute-force replay walks the events in order keeping only each page's current born/title/parent/status/archived/ended state and evaluates the ancestor rule from that state, sharing no code with the fold; it compares isShown, statusAt and titleAt for every page at 500 seeded-random moments plus every distinct event ts and ts - 1, over (a) the committed back-fill followed by a synthetic baseline and recorded tail and (b) an all-kinds fixture. The same Python file greps timeline.js and timeline.css for the forbidden glow constructs and colour literals. The MCP non-goal goes in tests/test_server.py: list the tools through fastmcp's Client and assert no name or description mentions timeline or lifecycle. The STORE construction is pinned by a test that the source of src/server.py builds STORE = Store(DATA_DIR, backfill_dir=Path("backfill")) (the fixtures replace server.STORE, so the module object cannot be inspected reliably), and is exercised end to end in the reviewer run on a copy of .pasta-data.

detail.source:
fold(data): pages in first-seen order; segments pushed in event order (so ascending t); segAt = last seg with t <= T
  (binary search), null before born. created (unknown id only) -> mark created; present -> recordingStart ??= ts,
  snapshot of known ids at the first present, unknown -> born=ts present=true finishT=ts when finish status, known ->
  resync where different (+ finishT if now finish and null); status -> ship (first finish move) or status mark with
  gate = [from,to] in types[type].gates; renamed/moved/archived/unarchived/deleted -> segments + marks; linked/unlinked
  -> links; edited/el_* -> acts asked|answered|step|case|edit by types[type].elements[section.field]; gap -> gaps.
  After: snapshot ids not named by any present -> endedAt = min(endedAt ?? Infinity, recordingStart); drop links with
  an unknown end; eventTs = every event's ts ascending.
isShown(m, p, T): born <= T, not (endedAt !== null && endedAt <= T), and walking q = p, then byId(parentAt(q, T))
  ... no q has archived segment value true at T; unknown parent id ends the walk; at most 64 steps.

overview.body: This spec covers the web half of the timeline replay: two read-only GET routes in src/server.py (the HTML view /ws:<id>/timeline and its replay JSON /ws:<id>/timeline.json), the STORE built with the committed back-fill folder, the Timeline link on the tree page, the reloader opt-out in _base.html, and the hand-written Canvas2D Metro renderer and player (src/static/timeline/timeline.js and timeline.css) with its node check and tests. It restates the sealed design solution-design:mwjq54qk-38aaae for this slice and settles only what the design left to the builder. It leaves out everything on the write path, the replay JSON's construction (lifecycle_log.timeline_payload, wave 1) and the back-fill file (wave 2), which it uses exactly as the epic's contracts define them; it adds no MCP tool and no control that changes anything.

body.text: Server: two GET routes and the store (effectful shell, src/server.py)

body.source:
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, JSONResponse, PlainTextResponse
from . import cleanup, lifecycle_log
from .errors import NotFoundError, PastaError

STORE = Store(DATA_DIR, backfill_dir=Path("backfill"))   # cwd-relative, like src/static and src/templates

@app.get("/ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def route_timeline(request: Request, workspaceIdPart: str):
    with _guard_http():
        workspace_id = f"ws:{workspaceIdPart}"
        workspace = STORE.load_workspace(workspace_id)          # missing -> NotFoundError -> 500 page, as route_tree
        return templates.TemplateResponse(request=request, name="timeline.html", context={
            "workspace_id": workspace_id, "workspace_name": workspace.name,
            "data_url": f"/ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline.json"})

@app.get("/ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline.json")
async def route_timeline_json(workspaceIdPart: str):
    with _guard_http():
        workspace_id = f"ws:{workspaceIdPart}"
        try:
            workspace = STORE.load_workspace(workspace_id)
            events = STORE.read_lifecycle_log(workspace_id)
        except NotFoundError as exc:
            return JSONResponse({"detail": str(exc)}, status_code=404)   # "Workspace 'ws:<id>' not found."
        return JSONResponse(lifecycle_log.timeline_payload(workspace_id, workspace.name, events))

body.text: Both routes sit beside route_tree, take only the read half of the workspace rw-lock (inside load_workspace and read_lifecycle_log), write no file, never call _load_for_write and therefore never start a log. No other path or method mentions the timeline, and no @mcp.tool is added.
Templates
Stylesheet (src/static/timeline/timeline.css)

Scoped to body.timeline so no other view changes: the body fills the viewport (height 100vh, margin 0, padding 0, max-width none, overflow hidden) as a flex column; #content grows and holds a compact h1 and the #timeline grid (rows: controls auto, stage 1fr, overview 56px); #to-top and the hr are hidden; the theme toggle stays top right. Buttons and the tooltip take every colour from water.css properties (--background, --text-main, --text-muted, --border); the .on state is a --text-main border. It defines --tl-idle, --tl-active, --tl-review, --tl-done, --tl-warn, --tl-archived, --tl-gate, --tl-link and --tl-accent for body.light and body.dark (values in decision on colours). It contains no box-shadow, text-shadow, filter: or backdrop-filter.
Renderer API (src/static/timeline/timeline.js) - pure part

body.source:
// Classic script; (function (root) { ... })(globalThis). Defines root.PastaTimeline; module.exports = it when module exists.
// No DOM access at load. All times epoch ms. DAY = 86_400_000, HOUR = 3_600_000.
statusClass(status, typeInfo) -> 'warn'|'done'|'review'|'idle'|'active'
  warn   status in [blocked, drifted, superseded, abandoned, failed]
  done   typeInfo && typeInfo.finish.includes(status)
  review /review/i.test(status) || status in [judging, checking, shipping, verified]
  idle   typeInfo && status === typeInfo.initial
  active otherwise

fold(data) -> Model
  Model { pages: PageRec[] (first-seen order), byId: Map, t0, t1, types, recordingStart: number|null,
          links: Link[], gaps: [{t, missing, seq}], eventTs: number[] (ascending ts of every served event) }
  PageRec { id, type, born, present: bool, finishT: number|null, endedAt: number|null, deleted: bool,
            titles: Seg[], parents: Seg[], statuses: Seg[], archived: Seg[],   // Seg = {t, v}, ascending t
            marks: [{t, k, s?, gate?}],  // k: created|status|ship|rename|move|archive|unarchive|delete
            acts: [{t, w}],              // w: asked|answered|step|case|edit
            kidIndex: number,            // its index among the children of its first parent
            // set by layoutMetro:
            trunk: bool, track: number|null, y: number|null, lane0, lane1, shown: [[from, to), ...] }
  Link { a, b, role, t, until (Infinity while open) }

isShown(m, p, T)   born <= T && !(endedAt !== null && endedAt <= T) && no page on the chain p, parentAt(p,T), ...
                   has archivedAt(q, T); a parent id not in m.byId ends the walk; chain depth capped at 64
statusAt(p, T) / titleAt(p, T) / parentAt(p, T)   null before born; else the last segment with t <= T (binary search)
layoutMetro(m) -> { height }   // assigns trunk, track, y, lane0, lane1, shown; marks/acts/links get y
playheadStep(T, dtSeconds, speed, nextEventTs) = T + dtSeconds * speed * DAY * (nextEventTs !== null && nextEventTs - T > 6 * HOUR ? 6 : 1)
mount(root)   // effectful, below

body.text: Fold rules, per event in array order

body.source:
gap          gaps.push({t: ts, missing, seq})
created      unknown id: new PageRec born=ts, segments from the event (archived false), mark created(s=status)
             known id: ignored
present      recordingStart ??= ts; the first present event snapshots the ids known so far
             unknown id: new PageRec born=ts, present=true, segments from the event, links from event.links (start ts),
                         finishT=ts when status is a finish status (no mark)
             known id:   silent resync - add a title/parent/status/archived segment at ts only where the value differs;
                         end open links not listed, start listed links not open; finishT=ts if now in a finish status
                         and finishT is null; no mark
status       statuses.push({t, v: to}); gate = [from,to] in types[type].gates;
             to in finish && finishT === null -> finishT=ts, mark ship(s=to, gate); else mark status(s=to, gate)
renamed      titles.push({t, v: title}); mark rename
moved        parents.push({t, v: to_parent}); mark move
linked       links.push({a: page, b: to, role, t: ts, until: Infinity})
unlinked     the latest open link with that a, b and role: until = ts
archived     archived.push({t, v: true}); mark archive        unarchived  archived.push({t, v: false}); mark unarchive
deleted      endedAt = ts, deleted = true; mark delete; later events for the page are ignored
edited, el_edited, el_removed          act edit
el_added     elements[section.field] === 'Question' ? act asked : act edit
el_status    Question & to answered -> answered; Step & to done -> step; Case & to passed -> case; else edit
other kinds, events for unknown ids    ignored
after the loop: every id in the snapshot that no present event named: endedAt = min(endedAt ?? Infinity, recordingStart);
links whose a or b is unknown are dropped.

body.text: Metro layout rules

body.source:
shown intervals  for each page: candidate instants = born, endedAt, and every archived/parent segment instant of the page
                 and of every page that is ever its ancestor; shown = merged [c_i, c_i+1) where isShown(m, p, c_i)
trunks           parent at born is null or unknown -> trunk; rows 0, +24, -24, +48, -48, ... in born order;
                 lane0 = born, lane1 = end of last shown interval (t1 when open)
rowAt(p, t)      trunk -> its row; track !== null && (finishT === null || t < finishT) -> track;
                 else rowAt(parentAt(p, t), t) (null when there is none); recursion capped at 64
branches         in born order, pages that are not trunks, have a shown interval, and are not settled from birth
                 (present with finishT === born): pr = rowAt(parentAt(p, born), born) ?? 0;
                 candidates pr+1*s, pr-1*s, pr+2*s, pr-2*s, ... with s = kidIndex % 2 ? -1 : 1, skipping trunk rows,
                 first with free[c] === undefined || free[c] <= born; track = c
                 lane0 = born; lane1 = finishT ?? (last shown end < t1 ? last shown end : t1)
                 free[c] = lane1 < t1 ? lane1 + 30 min : Infinity
no track         present-and-finished pages and pages with no shown interval: track = null
y                y(row) = (row - minRow) * 17 + 20 px; height = (maxRow - minRow) * 17 + 40
mark/act y       y(rowAt(p, t)) at its own time; the ship mark uses the own track; a link stores ya, yb at link.t
settled glyph    pages with finishT !== null: at finishT on y(rowAt(parentAt(p, finishT), finishT)), drawn 22 px right
