body.text: mount(root) - the effectful shell

mount reads root.dataset.src, fetches it (cache no-store), and on success runs fold then layoutMetro once; it holds no rules of its own beyond pixel placement. It wires the controls, sizes both canvases at devicePixelRatio through a ResizeObserver (the body is hidden until _theme.js runs, so sizing waits for layout), reads the colours, seeks t0 and starts playing in a requestAnimationFrame loop. A failed fetch or a non-200 answer draws one centred line 'Could not load the timeline (<status>).' and an empty log (t0 null) draws 'No history recorded yet for this workspace.'; the controls then do nothing.

body.source:
state        T, playing, speed (0.25 on load), follow (on), ghost (on), span (ms across the stage: 3 days on load,
             clamped to [1.5, 400] days), x0 (time at the left edge), y0/yTarget (vertical camera), hover, dirty
frame(now)   dt = min(0.1, (now - last) / 1000); if playing: T = playheadStep(T, dt, speed, next event ts > T);
             T >= t1 -> T = t1, playing = false; follow -> x0 = T - 0.62 * W * span / W and the vertical camera eases
             (k = 1 - exp(-3 dt)) towards the mean y of marks and ticks in [T - 3 days, T]; draw when playing,
             following or dirty; chips every 6th drawn frame and on every non-playing draw
controls     #tl-play toggles (at t1 it seeks t0 first); [data-speed] buttons and keys 1-4 set speed (.on marks the
             selected one); #tl-follow / F, #tl-future / G toggle (.on when active); Space plays/pauses (preventDefault);
             ArrowLeft/Right seek -/+1 day (Shift: 7); wheel zooms span by 1.15 per notch about the playhead while
             following, else about the pointer; dragging the stage (> 3 px) pans x0 and y0 and turns Follow off;
             pointerdown/move on the overview seeks t0 + x / width * (t1 - t0); seek clamps to [t0, t1] and keeps
             the play state
colours      read() at mount, on a MutationObserver of document.body's class attribute and on #js-stylesheet's load
             event; each read marks dirty and drops the overview cache

TOP = 26 px axis band; X(t) = (t - x0) * W / span; Y(y) = y - y0 + TOP; draw only what intersects the viewport

body.text: Decision: timeline.json loads the workspace (for its name) and reads the log, answering a NotFoundError from either with JSONResponse({'detail': str(exc)}, 404) and everything else through _guard_http; the HTML route mirrors route_tree and never reads the log. Rejected: reading the log first and the name second (same answer, but the name read is the cheaper existence check); a separate existence probe (a third lock round-trip); a JSON 404 for the HTML route (route_tree, which the design names as the model, answers a missing workspace with the error page). Why: the contract's 404 body is exactly the store's NotFoundError message, so passing str(exc) through keeps one source of the text, and both calls are read-half only, so the route cannot start a log.

Decision: one id, one life (a duplicate created is ignored, nothing after deleted counts); present resyncs only what differs, may set finishT silently, and the pages ending at recordingStart are exactly those known when the first present arrives and not named by any present. A type missing from the table never finishes. Rejected: treating a duplicate created as a resync (a log never produces one; ignoring is the cheapest honest reading); ending every page not named (would end pages recorded after the baseline); updating a page's type from a present event (an id carries its type). Why: it is the design's fold (decision mwkzcf9l-3fac61) made total, and it is what the brute-force check replays independently.

Decision: draw by time position - an element at time t is drawn when its page is shown at t, solid for t <= T and ghost beyond; end caps are drawn when the page was shown just before; chips use T and hover the pointer's time; shown intervals are precomputed once in the layout. Rejected: drawing a page's whole history only while it is shown at T (an archive would erase the history to the left of the playhead, so the picture would jump frame to frame, the anti-goal mwjq5k9p-afcb54); walking ancestors for every mark every frame (the same answer at a per-frame cost). Why: it is the only reading in which the left of the playhead is the workspace as it stood at each instant (mwjq5k97-712194) and an archived page's lane 'stops being drawn at its archive time' as the design says.

Decision: trunks for every root (and unknown-parent) page at rows 0, +24, -24, ... in born order; branches as the spike (nearest free non-trunk track, alternating sides); lane1 = finish, else the end of the last shown interval, else t1; a track frees 30 min after a lane that ends before t1; rowAt follows the parent the page has at each time, through settled parents; present-and-finished and never-shown pages have no track; settled glyphs 22 px after their finish, packed 8 px apart per row. Rejected: the spike's title-keyed trunk table (only fits pasta's four toc titles); keeping an ended lane's track for ever (wastes a track per archived page); stacking settled glyphs on one point (the ~100 pages settled at the baseline would draw as one dot). Why: these are the layout choices the design leaves to the builder, picked to keep the approved look on any workspace and to keep the no-overlap check strict.

Decision: every colour from water.css's properties and nine --tl-* properties with the approved spike's palette values per body.light / body.dark; re-read on the body class change and on #js-stylesheet's load; alphas are constants. Rejected: hard-coded palettes in the script (breaks the colours-follow-the-theme invariant and the test); re-reading every frame (a getComputedStyle per frame for a change that happens on a click); changing _theme.js to signal the swap (outside this slice). Why: the class change and the sheet's load are the two moments the properties can change, and the spike's values are the look the user approved.

Decision: keys 1-4 follow the button order 0.25, 1, 4, 16; Play at t1 restarts from t0; seeking keeps the play state; the hover title is at the playhead; the from PR history note shows when the playhead or pointer is before recordingStart; empty and failed loads draw one line on the stage. Rejected: the spike's 1, 4, 16, 0.25 order (0.25 is the default now, so it comes first); pausing on seek (the spike kept playing and the user approved it); a separate DOM element for the empty line (the interface fixes the template's elements). Why: smallest behaviour matching the design's player paragraph and the approved spike.

Decision: the node check embeds a types table and takes --types; pytest feeds it the production table from timeline_types(); the brute force shares no code with the fold and samples 500 seeded moments plus every event boundary; glow, colour-literal and property checks are greps in tests/test_timeline_renderer.py; the MCP non-goal is a tool-list check in tests/test_server.py; the STORE line is pinned in source and exercised by the reviewer run. Rejected: porting the fold to Python (two implementations to keep in step); random moments only (misses the boundaries where an off-by-one hides); importing a second copy of src.server to inspect its STORE (heavy, and the fixtures overwrite the module global). Why: it checks the anti-goal mwjq5k9r-d69675 by brute force on the real back-fill and the real registry without any npm package.

feature-brief:mwm17fkc-c09d13.title: Metro timeline replay of a workspace's page events from a jsonl log

summary.body:
A minimal, clear Metro-style timeline in the web UI that replays how a workspace's pages came and went - created, moved through their statuses, archived and unarchived, shipped, closed or dropped - and can be played, paused and scrubbed. It is meant as an attraction: a demo of how pasta drives work, playing at 0.25 day per second and speeding up through stretches with no activity.

It is fed by an append-only event log in jsonl format stored next to each workspace's document, recording page creation, status transitions and archive/unarchive as they happen. For pasta's own workspace the log starts with a one-off back-fill: every feature-brief, simple-change and bug-report found across the backup json files, created at the time encoded in its page id, and shipped/closed/dropped at the merge or close date of the GitHub PR it links to; pages with no PR fall back to a short (hour or two) lifetime, and the dated feature list in the repo's first commit adds the history from before pasta tracked itself.

Note: an earlier epic (epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b) explored the same goal with a much richer event log and three subagent-built briefs on the unmerged timeline-replay branch; this brief is a fresh, leaner take built directly from origin/main, reusing its settled decisions (Metro layout, 0.25 day/s, speed-up through quiet stretches) but not its code.

feature-brief:mwm1gfl9-bbfc5d.title: Metro-style replayable timeline of workspace events in the web UI

summary.body:
Give a workspace a showcase: a minimal, metro-map style timeline in the web UI where each feature-brief, bug-report and simple-change is a coloured line that starts at its creation, passes through its status stations and ends delivered (shipped/closed) or dropped (abandoned, archived or shelved), and where the whole history plays, pauses and scrubs like a video - 0.25 day of workspace time per second, with idle stretches compressed to at most a second each, so pasta's four months replay in about two minutes.

The timeline reads a new append-only event log, ws_<token>.events.jsonl beside each workspace file, which the store now writes on every page creation, status transition, archive and unarchive. Because the log only starts now, a one-off backfill writes pasta's own history into it: every feature-brief, simple-change and bug-report found across the workspace backups, created at the instant encoded in its page id, and moved to its latest status at the date of its linked pasta-dev PR (merged/closed), else of the matching line in the first commit's dated feature list, else an hour or two after creation as bounded by the backups.

items.name: src/store.py - Store write transactions (effects)
items.text: The four transactions that change a page's existence, status or archived flag: create_page (L556, also creates pinned children via _create_auto_children), mutate_page_batch (L580, detects a transition as working.status != status_before), set_page_status (L766, the web admin override) and _set_page_archive_state (L715, behind archive_page / unarchive_page / schedule_page_deletion / unschedule_page_deletion; cascades the flag onto pinned children). Each ends in _touch_and_save (L187), which stamps updated_at with _now() and swaps the file atomically via _write_file, all under _transaction_lock_for(workspace_id). _path_for (L143) maps ws:<token> to <root>/ws_<token>.json. cleanup_workspace (L676) prunes pages. Effects: file I/O, clock. This is where the log append hooks in.

items.name: src/model.py - Page / Workspace (pure)
items.text: Plain dataclasses. Page carries id, type, title, status, parent_id, archived - exactly the fields a lifecycle event needs to read. Workspace.pages maps id to Page; root_page_ids and child_ids hold the tree, which decides whether a page is hidden under an archived ancestor.

items.name: src/ids.py - id tokens (impure creation, pure decode possible)
items.text: new_token() builds '<base36 epoch-millis>-<6 hex>', so every page id ('feature-brief:mwm1gfl9-bbfc5d') encodes its creation instant to the millisecond. There is no decoder today; adding one beside the encoder is pure. Confirmed: ws:mrteq0c5 decodes to 2026-07-20T15:56:20Z, the workspace's first day.

items.name: src/server.py - FastAPI web routes (effects)
items.text: STORE = Store(DATA_DIR) with DATA_DIR = PASTA_DATA_DIR or '.pasta-data'. Read-only HTML routes: route_index '/', route_tree '/ws:{id}' (tree.html), route_page '/ws:{id}/page/{pageId}', each wrapped in _guard_http and rendered through Jinja2Templates('src/templates'). The archive/unarchive/schedule/status POST routes call the Store methods above. A new '/ws:{id}/timeline' route belongs beside route_tree.

items.name: src/templates/_base.html, tree.html, _nav.html - page shell (presentation)
items.text: _base.html is the shell every view extends: water.css light/dark sheets, styles.css, the theme switcher (_theme.js) and - unconditionally in <head>, outside any block - the _reloader.js WebSocket that calls location.reload() on every refresh push (any MCP write or source edit). tree.html renders the workspace tree with a Show/Hide archived link: the natural place for a Timeline link. Scripts are included inline from the templates dir (_view_toggle.js pattern).

items.name: src/static/styles.css - theme tokens (presentation)
items.text: Water.css overrides. Extra theme colours are declared per theme on body.light / body.dark (--text-error, --text-on-error); everything else reads water.css custom properties (--text-main, --text-muted, --background, --background-alt, --border, --links). The metro line colours per page type follow the same pattern.

items.name: .pasta-data/ - workspace files and backups (data)
items.text: ws_<token>.json per workspace (pasta's is 3.6 MB, 2 other workspaces). backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6/ holds 12 timestamped snapshots 20260821T190516Z..20260927T120519Z, plus backups/ws_mrteq0c5-238cf6.json (an 11-10 copy). list_workspaces globs '*.json' non-recursively, so a sibling 'ws_<token>.events.jsonl' is not listed as a workspace. Across all 14 files there are 190 feature-brief / simple-change / bug-report pages; 58 link a PR in pull_request.url.

items.name: History inputs: first commit 463cf4f and pasta-dev PRs #1-#66 (data)
items.text: The root commit 463cf4f 'Initial version cut' (2026-08-23 +0200) carries ~70 lines '<YYYY-MM-DD>  <feature>' from 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-23 - the pre-PR era. Every PR link in the pages points at github.com/dsschneidermann-org/pasta-dev; its 66 PRs (2026-08-25..2026-11-16) were read through the GitHub MCP with created_at / merged_at / closed_at. No gh CLI is installed, so the backfill cannot fetch at runtime and needs a committed snapshot.

items.name: Page-type FSMs (pure, src/pagetypes)
items.text: feature-brief: draft..building, review, done, then shipped (human) or abandoned (human, from any pre-done status). simple-change and bug-report: draft, open, review, done, closed - and closed can reopen to open. So a line ends at shipped/closed (delivered) or abandoned (dropped), and a closed line can resume. In test mode (tests/conftest.py) these production types do not resolve, so the timeline must name its tracked types and end statuses as constants rather than ask the registry.

items.name: tests/test_web.py, tests/test_store.py, tests/conftest.py (tests)
items.text: test_web repoints server.STORE at Store(tmp_path) and drives routes through FastAPI TestClient; test_store drives transactions on fixture page types (test-*). conftest puts the run in test mode and disables the guidance event cache. pyproject: pythonpath '.', testpaths 'tests'; basedpyright include 'src/**/*' only.

Python 'requires-python = ">=3.14"', managed with uv; tests via pytest run with --testmon (CLAUDE.md: 'Run pytest with --testmon to speed up red-green testing'); types via basedpyright, typeCheckingMode 'recommended', include ['src/**/*'].
Copy rule from CLAUDE.md: 'Use the word "create" instead of "mint" when creating something.'

Layering (Project Overview invariant): the pure core does no I/O and never mutates its inputs; only the stateful shell (store, server) does I/O, creates ids or reads the clock. Event derivation, timeline layout and backfill inference belong on the pure side; file appends, reads and git/network on the shell.
The web UI is strictly read-only (Web UI invariant): its routes project store data into HTML and change nothing, taking only the shared read lock. The timeline route must stay a read.

Theming (Web UI invariant): every colour reads correctly in both light and dark - either a water.css custom property or a token defined for both body.light and body.dark in src/static/styles.css. No literal colour that only works in one theme.

Playback rate 0.25 day of workspace time per second of playback, accelerating through stretches with no activity (user requirement, verbatim: 'playback to be at 0.25 day/second, and ... speed up when there was no activity').

Writes are serialized per workspace by an in-process transaction lock only; a second OS process writing the same data dir is unguarded (Overview + Authoring invariants). Inferred consequence: an out-of-process backfill must not race the server's appends.

All web assets are served locally (water.css vendored under src/static, scripts inlined from src/templates); no CDN dependency exists today. Inferred from the templates, not a written rule: the timeline adds no third-party library.

A prior attempt exists and is being dropped at the user's direction (/cook: reset old state, do not inspect the previous worktree): archived epic:mwjq54qk-49a07b 'Timeline replay of a workspace...' with feature-briefs mwkzuows / mwkzuptb / mwkzuqrd (status done), the archived brief feature-brief:mwm17fkc-c09d13 from earlier today, and unmerged branches timeline-*, spike/timeline-*, worktree-metro-timeline. None of it is on main. This brief builds fresh from main, reuses none of those branches, and leaves those pages untouched.

src/templates/_base.html includes _reloader.js for every view, outside any block, and it calls location.reload() on every refresh push - which every MCP write fires. A timeline left playing would restart on each agent write. _base.html has to give a view a way to leave the reloader out.

Name collision: src/event_cache.py already exists (an in-memory, reload-surviving cache of guidance deliveries, imported in server.py as page_events). The on-disk lifecycle log needs distinct names so the two are not confused.

Archiving hides a whole subtree but flags only the target page (and its pinned children): many tracked pages, e.g. the W1-W10 feature-briefs under an archived epic, carry archived=false yet are hidden. Archive events alone cannot tell the timeline a line was shelved; it has to read 'hidden' off the current workspace too.

scripts/feature_brief_probe.py ('just brief-probe') creates '[probe] feature-brief lifecycle walk' pages - about 25 sit in the backups. They are test runs, not work, and would clutter both the backfill and any live replay.

Review round 2026-11-19, one deviation from spec section 7 made while building: a finished line now dims ('past') 1.5 playback s after its end instead of 0.6 s, so the status label announced at its last station is not greyed out halfway through being shown. Nothing else in the dimming changed.

Second review round, deviation from spec section 8 made while building: the stage captures the pointer when a press becomes a drag (past 4 px), not on pointerdown. Capturing on press retargets the closing click to the stage, so a plain click on a line would stop opening its page; capturing late keeps the spec's own rule that a press without movement follows the link. A pending click-swallow is also cleared on the next press, so a drag released outside the stage cannot eat a later click.

Second review round supersedes part of the first round's renderer case (testing-plan): its 'scrubbed into a squeezed gap the readout reads days per second' assertion no longer applies because the rate readout is gone. Re-run after this round, every other assertion of that case still passes; the gap-rate one is the only failure, by design.

Pasta Project Overview (architecture:mrteq39m-de7a49), Data model: 'One JSON document per workspace under PASTA_DATA_DIR...' - add the append-only ws_<token>.events.jsonl beside each workspace file, why the *.json glob does not list it, and that backups do not copy it.

Authoring & mutation (architecture:mrtqsspj-0a2ae4), invariant 'Every write is copy -> edit -> atomic overwrite under a per-workspace lock' and Data model - createPage, a transitioning mutatePageBatch and the web status override now also append lifecycle events after the save, inside the same lock; a failed append does not fail the write.

Archiving (architecture:mrtqsu5j-4643c4), Data model - archive/unarchive (and schedule-delete, which archives) append archived/unarchived events for every page whose flag moved, the pinned-child cascade included.

Web UI, HMR & live reload (architecture:mrw6s6q6-fb2ff5), Usage: the route list ('/ lists workspaces, /ws:<id> shows a workspace's page tree...') gains /ws:<id>/timeline, and 'Every served page opens a WebSocket to /ws/reloader' is no longer true for the timeline view.

GitHub README (document:mtiodadq-2fb6a6) and README.md: the web UI paragraph (line 52 'the read-only web UI at /') and the storage paragraph (line 64 'Workspaces are plain JSON files under ./.pasta-data') - mention the timeline view and the events log file.
Where does the event log live and what is it called - 'next to the workspace' read as a sibling file of ws_<token>.json in the data dir, or a folder per workspace?
items.answer: A sibling file in the data dir: <PASTA_DATA_DIR>/ws_<token>.events.jsonl beside ws_<token>.json. The non-recursive '*.json' workspace glob does not match '.jsonl', so it is never listed as a workspace, and a single file per workspace is what 'next to the workspace' says.

items.text: Which events does the log record: only the asked-for page transitions and archive/unarchive, or also creation, renames, reparents and the cleanup sweep's deletions?
items.answer: created, status (with from/to), archived and unarchived - for every page type. Creation is added to the ask because a line has to start somewhere and pinned children are created without a transition. Renames, reparents, content edits and sweep deletions are not logged: the timeline takes a page's current title from the workspace, and nothing it draws depends on the others.

items.text: Which page types become lines on the timeline: just feature-brief, simple-change and bug-report, or every page type the log records?
items.answer: feature-brief, simple-change and bug-report only - the three the user named, which are the units of work. The log stays generic (all types); the timeline filters.

items.text: How is the first commit's dated feature list used: only as a ship-date source for pages whose title matches a line, or also drawn as milestones of its own for lines with no page?
items.answer: Only as a date source: a no-PR page whose title matches a line (similarity >= 0.55, dated on or after the page's creation day) takes that line's date for its latest status. Lines with no page are not drawn - the timeline is a history of pages, and a synthetic milestone track would be a second kind of line nobody asked for.

items.text: When a page has neither a PR nor a matching first-commit line, what time does the backfill give its latest status?
items.answer: The page's creation time plus a typical lifetime of 60-120 minutes (fixed per page from a hash of its id, so lines differ but reruns agree), clamped into the snapshot interval in which the backups show the status changed: no earlier than the last backup showing an older status, no later than the first backup showing the new one.

items.text: Does the backfill infer intermediate stations and archive times, or only the creation and the latest status?
items.answer: Only creation and the latest status. The backups are days apart, so intermediate times would be invented; archive times are left out for the same reason (a shelved line ends by the hidden-page rule instead). Live logging supplies every station from now on.

items.text: How does the one-off backfill coexist with live events already in the log, and can it be re-run safely?
items.answer: Backfill lines carry "source": "backfill". A run drops earlier backfill lines, skips every page that already has a live event, and rewrites the file as backfill + live events sorted by time - so a re-run is idempotent. It is a separate process, so it is run while the server is not writing (stated in its usage text).

items.text: Where does a line end when its page never reached shipped/closed/abandoned but is now hidden (archived itself or under an archived ancestor) or deleted?
items.answer: At its last logged event, drawn with a 'dropped' end cap. A page counts as hidden if it, or any ancestor, is archived now, or it no longer exists. Archive events end a non-terminal line the same way at the archive time; an unarchive resumes it.

items.text: What exactly is 'speed up when there is no activity': which stretches count as idle, and how fast does an idle stretch play?
items.answer: Time within 3 hours of any event is active and plays at 0.25 day/s. Every stretch outside those windows (an idle gap) plays in 1 second, or at the base rate if that would be slower. On pasta's history that is ~2 minutes instead of 8. The readout shows the current rate, e.g. '6 days/s' through a gap.

items.text: Does the horizontal axis show real time (a scroll that races through idle gaps) or playback time (constant scroll, idle gaps compressed)?
items.answer: Playback time. The camera scrolls at a constant speed, active periods get the space, and idle gaps are compressed with a small gap marker - the metro-map distortion. Real time would leave whole screens empty and make 1-2 hour lines invisible next to month-long gaps.

items.text: Should the timeline view keep the live-reload socket every other view has, given it reloads the page on every agent write?
items.answer: No. _base.html wraps the reloader include in a block and timeline.html empties it, so a replay is never restarted by an agent's write. The view shows the log as of page load; reloading the tab picks up new events.

items.text: Are the '[probe] feature-brief lifecycle walk' test pages part of the backfilled history?
items.answer: No - pages titled '[probe]...' are excluded from the backfill: they are runs of scripts/feature_brief_probe.py, not work. Live logging records them like any page; no title rule is added to the timeline itself.

items.text: Review 2026-11-19: 'Remove the text 1/4 days per second' - does the rate readout go entirely, or only its base-rate text?
items.answer: Only the base-rate text goes: at 0.25 day/s the readout is empty. Through a squeezed idle gap it still reads e.g. '6 days per second »', because that is the visible sign of the speed-up the user asked for.

items.text: Review 2026-11-19: how are future elements (right of the playhead) shown greyed out - a grey copy under the coloured drawing, or recolouring each element as the playhead passes?
items.answer: A grey copy: each line is drawn twice, a ghost copy in --text-muted at 35% opacity that is never clipped, and the coloured copy on top, clipped at the playhead as before. The playhead therefore colours the map in as it passes, and the 30% of the stage ahead of it shows what is coming in grey.

items.text: Review 2026-11-19: which station labels appear as text, when, and how do they avoid colliding when stations sit 10-30 px apart?
items.answer: Each station carries its status as text ('draft', 'grounding', 'shipped'; 'archived' / 'unarchived' for archive stations), set at -40 degrees above the station like a metro map's station names so neighbours do not overprint, with a page-background halo. All of a line's labels show while the line is hovered (the existing tooltip stays). During playback a transition's label - every station except the first, creation one - shows for 1.5 s of playback after the playhead passes it, then fades.

items.text: Review 2026-11-19: what does the 'full circle with a non-color checkmark' for shipped/closed look like?
items.answer: A solid circle of radius 6 in the line's colour with a checkmark stroked inside it in the page background colour - the check carries the meaning without relying on colour. The legend shows the same mark.

items.text: Review 2026-11-19 (2nd): dropping the play icon - does the end-of-replay '↺ Replay' lose its icon too?
items.answer: No - only the play icon goes: the button reads 'Play', '❚❚ Pause' while playing, and '↺ Replay' at the end, whose icon says something 'Play' does not (it starts over).

items.text: Review 2026-11-19 (2nd): dragging the main chart - which way does time move, what happens to playback during a drag, and how does a drag avoid opening the page of the line it started on?
items.answer: The chart moves with the pointer, like dragging a map: dragging left goes forward in time by dx / 120 playback seconds, dragging right goes back, clamped to [0, duration]. While the pointer is down the playhead does not advance; if the replay was playing it carries on from the new position on release. A press only becomes a drag after 4 px of movement, and a drag swallows the click that ends it, so a press-and-release without movement still opens the line's page. Vertical touch scrolling of the stage keeps working (touch-action: pan-y).

items.text: Review 2026-11-19 (3rd): should dragging the chart or the minimap scrubber keep a playing replay running?
items.answer: No - the user directed that any drag pauses the player: a drag on the chart (once past the 4 px threshold) and any input on the minimap scrubber pause the replay, and it stays paused until Play is pressed. This replaces the earlier hold-and-resume behaviour.

items.text: Review 2026-11-19 (4th): the renderer's Node smoke checks lived in a scratch directory - how are they kept in scripts/tests/timeline so they can be rerun, and what do they check now that the rate readout and hold-while-dragging are gone?
items.answer: As three Node check scripts sharing one stub-DOM module, plus a Python runner and a README, all in scripts/tests/timeline/. The runner builds the timeline payload from a real data dir (default .pasta-data, pasta's workspace) or takes a saved payload, runs each check against src/templates/_timeline.js, and exits non-zero if any fails. The checks keep only what still holds: the replay runs to the end and its counters match the payload (check_replay.js); grey/coloured copies, checked delivered ends, one label per station, transition labels speak and creation labels never do (check_marks.js); drag direction, clamping, threshold, single swallowed click, and pausing on chart and scrubber drags (check_drag.js). The rate-readout and hold-and-resume assertions are dropped with the features they tested.

items.text: Review 2026-11-19 (5th): the backfill (src/backfill.py, its tests, id_time and its tests, the PR snapshot) is throwaway and moves to a storage-only scripts/backfill_events - what happens to the timeline's use of id_time for a line's start, and to scripts/backfill_timeline.py, which imports src.backfill?
items.answer: A line now starts at its first logged event instead of at min(id time, first event). The visible replay does not change for pasta: its backfill already wrote a 'created' event at every page's id time, and a page created since logging began has a 'created' event at its creation. Only a page that predates the log with no backfill starts at its first logged transition. scripts/backfill_timeline.py imports src.backfill, so it moves to the dump with the rest; nothing in the dump is wired up to run (the user asked for storage only). scripts/tests/timeline/README.md stops pointing at the backfill script.

findings.issue: Step 4 (build_timeline) said 'every later event (and the created event when its time is after start) appends a stop'. A live created event lands a few ms after the page's id time, so every live line would get a duplicate 'created' stop on top of its start. Applied: the step now says the created event is consumed by the first stop and never adds one of its own, matching the spec's 'first stop ... every later event adds a stop'.

Step 11 (backfill script) left 'counted via a returned summary or by recomputing' in its code comment while its own next paragraph settles on the 'anchor' key - two answers to one question. Applied: the comment now counts Counter(e['anchor']) over the status lines. The 'anchor' key itself was added to the spec (sealed addendum) during planning, so plan and spec agree.

Coverage check, no change needed: every spec section has a delivering step (ids 1, event_log 2, timeline 3-4, backfill 5-6, store 7, shell/tokens 8, route 9, JS 10, script 11, real run 12, gate 13), no step updates documentation, pure modules precede the store/route/script that call them, and each testing case asserts behaviour that can fail, including the torn-line, failed-append, aborted-batch, empty-log and unknown-workspace paths.

Review-round coverage check, no change needed: spec section 7's five items map onto step 14 (time background, ghost/check/label styles, legend) and step 15 (rate blanking, ghost copy, check path, labels, speaking window); neither step touches Python, matching the section's 'payload unchanged'; both new cases assert observable output that would differ if the item were missing (CSS rule and legend path in the served page; ghost/check/label/speaking state in the renderer run).

Step 17 sketches release() as a comment rather than code. Not blocking: spec section 8 states its behaviour exactly (end the press, drop the dragging class, swallow the next click only if the press dragged), and test case 2 of this round checks each part, so an implementer is not left deciding anything.

def id_time(identifier: str) -> float | None:
    """Epoch seconds encoded in an id or token made by `new_id` / `new_token`, or None when the
    token does not start with base-36 millis."""
    token = identifier.rsplit(":", 1)[-1]
    millis = token.split("-", 1)[0]
    if not millis or any(ch not in _ALPHABET for ch in millis):
        return None
    return int(millis, 36) / 1000

def is_hidden(workspace: Workspace, page_id: str) -> bool:
    page = workspace.pages.get(page_id)
    while page is not None:
        if page.archived:
            return True
        page = workspace.pages.get(page.parent_id) if page.parent_id else None
    return page_id not in workspace.pages

# build_timeline(events, workspace, now) -> dict, in this order:
# 1. group events whose 'type' is in LINE_TYPES by pageId; stable-sort each group by time.
# 2. per page: start = min(id_time(pageId) if not None, first event time).
#    The first stop sits at start, kind 'created', with the created event's status if the page
#    has a created event, else the first status event's 'from', else the first event's status.
#    The created event is consumed by that first stop and never adds a stop of its own; every
#    other event appends a stop {at, kind=its event, status=the page's status after it}.
# 3. end: final status == DELIVERED[type] -> ('delivered', time of the last status event);
#    final status == DROPPED.get(type) -> ('dropped', that time); archived after the last
#    archive event -> ('dropped', that event's time); is_hidden(workspace, pageId) ->
#    ('dropped', last event time); else ('open', now).
# 4. title = workspace.pages[pageId].title if present else the last event's title.
# 5. start_time = min(line starts); end_time = max(now, last event time);
#    segments = playback_segments(all stop times + line starts, start_time, end_time).
# 6. p0/p1 and every stop's p via to_playback; lanes packed in (p0, pageId) order: lowest lane
#    with lane_end + LANE_GAP <= p0, occupying max(p1, p0 + MIN_LINE).
# 7. feed = every (line, stop) sorted by (p, line index).
# 8. payload as in the spec, numbers rounded to 3 decimals; no lines -> duration 0, segments [],
#    lanes 0, lines [], feed [].

def status_time(page_id, status, history, prs, numbers, listed, now) -> tuple[datetime, str]:
    created = datetime.fromtimestamp(id_time(page_id), timezone.utc)
    typical = created + typical_lifetime(page_id)
    known = [prs[n] for n in numbers if n in prs]
    anchor = (max((p.merged for p in known if p.merged), default=None)
              or max((p.closed for p in known if p.closed), default=None)
              or min((p.created for p in known), default=None))
    if anchor is not None and anchor >= created:
        when, kind = anchor, "pr"
    elif listed is not None:
        local = typical.astimezone(LIST_TZ)
        when, kind = max(typical, datetime.combine(listed.day, local.timetz())), "list"
    else:
        # history: (taken, status) of this page in snapshot order
        first = next((i for i, (_, s) in enumerate(history) if s == status), None)
        upper = history[first][0] if first is not None else now
        lower = max((t for t, s in history[:first or 0] if s != status), default=created)
        when, kind = min(max(typical, lower), upper), "estimate"
    return min(max(when, created), now), kind

def backfill_events(snapshots, prs, features, skip_page_ids, now) -> list[Event]:
    # latest stored page per id across snapshots sorted by taken; keep LINE_TYPES, drop
    # PROBE_PREFIX titles, skip_page_ids and ids with no id_time; emit 'created' (status 'draft')
    # and, when the latest status != 'draft', one 'status' from 'draft' at status_time; both carry
    # the latest title and source 'backfill'; 'at' is datetime.isoformat() in UTC; sort by time.

def merge_log(existing, backfill) -> list[Event]:
    live = [e for e in existing if e.get("source") != "backfill"]
    return sorted([*backfill, *live], key=lambda e: datetime.fromisoformat(e["at"]))

items.text: id_time decodes ids and tokens (tests/test_ids.py): 'ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6' and the bare 'mrteq0c5-238cf6' both give 1784562980.405; a freshly created new_id is within 5 s of time.time(); 'page:NOT-base36' and 'x:' give None.

lifecycle_events derives exactly the changed marks (tests/test_event_log.py): a page absent from before gives one 'created' with its current status; a status move gives 'status' with 'from'; an archived flip gives 'archived' and the reverse 'unarchived'; a page with both changes lists status before archive; an unchanged workspace gives []; a page present in before but deleted from the workspace gives nothing; every event carries at/pageId/type/title/status.

The JSONL round trip survives real-world text and torn writes (tests/test_event_log.py): to_jsonl then parse_jsonl returns the same events for a title with 'é' and an en dash, written unescaped; parse_jsonl skips a blank line, a half-written line, a JSON array line and an object without pageId, keeping the good lines in order.

playback_segments plays activity at 0.25 day/s and squeezes idle time (tests/test_timeline.py): one event mid-way in a 10-day span gives three contiguous segments starting at p 0 - idle (1 s), active (6 h of time over 1 s, since 0.25 day/s is 6 h per second), idle (1 s); two events 1 h apart give a single active window; a 4 h idle gap plays at the base rate (0.667 s) rather than being stretched to 1 s; no times or end <= start give [].

to_playback maps time monotonically onto playback (tests/test_timeline.py): returns 0 for [], clamps a time before start to 0 and after end to the total, interpolates linearly inside a segment, and is non-decreasing across a sorted range of times spanning idle and active segments.

build_timeline ends each line by the spec's rules (tests/test_timeline.py): feature-brief shipped -> 'delivered' at the ship time; abandoned -> 'dropped'; bug-report closed then reopened -> 'open' ending at now; a non-terminal page archived -> 'dropped' at the archive time, and archived-then-unarchived -> 'open'; a page under an archived parent and a page missing from the workspace -> 'dropped' at their last event; an open live page -> 'open' at now.

build_timeline starts, titles and filters lines correctly (tests/test_timeline.py): a page whose only events are status changes starts at its id time with the first event's 'from' status as its first stop; the workspace's current title replaces the event title, and a deleted page keeps its last event title; events of type 'architecture' and 'implementation-plan' make no line; feed lists every stop ordered by p.

Lanes are packed without overlap and reused (tests/test_timeline.py): two lines overlapping in time get lanes 0 and 1; a third starting after the first ended plus LANE_GAP reuses lane 0; payload 'lanes' equals the number of lanes used; no events gives duration 0, segments [], lanes 0, lines [], feed []; json.dumps of a full payload succeeds.

Backfill parsers read the real input shapes (tests/test_backfill.py): parse_feature_list keeps only 'YYYY-MM-DD  text' lines of a commit message; parse_pull_requests accepts GitHub rows with merged_at null or missing; pr_numbers reads 'https://github.com/o/r/pull/21' and returns [] for a missing section or a null url; typical_lifetime is stable per id and within 60-120 minutes.

match_listed pairs pages with the first commit's features (tests/test_backfill.py): 'Anchored relocate & positioned insert (stale-read-safe)' created 2026-07-22 matches '2026-07-22 Anchored reorder and positioned insert (stale-read-safe)'; a feature dated before the page's creation day (+0200) is never returned; an unrelated title returns None.

status_time picks the right anchor (tests/test_backfill.py): a merged PR gives its merge time with kind 'pr'; a closed-unmerged PR gives its close time; an open PR gives its creation time; a PR older than the page is ignored; a later-day listed feature gives that day at the typical time-of-day with kind 'list'; with no anchor, created + typical clamped to the first snapshot showing the status (upper) and the last snapshot showing another status (lower) with kind 'estimate'; the result never precedes creation nor exceeds now.

backfill_events and merge_log build a re-runnable log (tests/test_backfill.py): the latest title and status across snapshots win; '[probe]' pages, skipped ids and architecture pages are left out; a draft page gets only 'created'; every line carries source 'backfill' and status lines an anchor; merge_log drops earlier backfill lines, keeps live lines in order, sorts by time, and is idempotent when re-run with the same backfill.

The store appends exactly the lifecycle events of its writes (tests/test_store_events.py): create of a test-lifecycle page logs 'created' for it and its pinned test-child; a test-flow 'open' batch logs one 'status' draft->open; a content-only setBody logs nothing; a stale-token batch raises and logs nothing; set_page_status logs 'status'; archive then unarchive log 'archived'/'unarchived' for the page and its pinned child; rename and reparent log nothing; the event 'at' equals workspace.updated_at.

The log never breaks storage (tests/test_store_events.py): list_workspaces still returns exactly one workspace when its .events.jsonl sits beside it; with the log path occupied by a directory, a create_page still succeeds, the page is saved, and read_events returns [] for a workspace with no log.

The timeline route serves the replay read-only (tests/test_web.py): with a log holding a feature-brief created and shipped, GET /ws:<part>/timeline is 200, embeds #timeline-data whose JSON has one 'delivered' line, and contains no '/ws/reloader'; with no log it is 200 with the empty-state sentence; the workspace tree page links to /<ws id>/timeline; an unknown workspace answers 500 via the error page; the other views still include the reloader.

The front-end script parses and the real history replays at demo length (manual, run commands): 'node --check src/templates/_timeline.js' succeeds; after running the backfill on pasta's data dir, build_timeline over it gives ~160 lines, fewer than 40 lanes and a duration between 60 and 180 s; GET /ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6/timeline against that data dir through TestClient is 200.
Nothing that worked before broke (whole suite + types): 'uv run pytest --testmon' over the full suite and 'uv run basedpyright' both pass.

Review 2026-11-19, timeline page styling (tests/test_web.py): the timeline page sets '.timeline time { background: var(--background-body); }' so <time> drops water.css's grey pill, and its legend's delivered entry carries the tl-check checkmark path.

Review 2026-11-19, renderer behaviour (node smoke run of _timeline.js on pasta's real payload, stub DOM): while the clock is at 0.25 day/s the rate readout is empty, and scrubbed into a squeezed gap it reads 'days per second'; every line has a tl-ghost group and a clipped coloured group; every delivered line has a tl-check path in both; every stop has a tl-label; mid-replay at least one transition label is 'speaking' and no creation label ever is; the replay still runs to the end without error.

2nd review, timeline page markup (tests/test_web.py): the timeline page has no tl-rate element, no '▶' glyph (the button starts as 'Play'), and separates feed rows with a '.tl-feed li + li' border-top instead of a bottom border on every row.

2nd review, dragging the stage (node smoke run of _timeline.js on pasta's real payload, stub DOM): pressing on the stage and moving 240 px left advances the playhead by 2 playback seconds, moving right goes back, both clamped to [0, duration]; a move under 4 px changes nothing and its click is not swallowed; a drag's closing click is swallowed exactly once; while the pointer is down playing frames do not advance the playhead, and after release a playing replay advances again; the button reads 'Play' when paused and no rate text is ever written.

3rd review, dragging pauses (node smoke run of _timeline.js on pasta's real payload, stub DOM): with the replay playing, a chart press that moves under 4 px leaves it playing; once the press passes 4 px the button reads 'Play' and later frames - during and after the drag - do not move the playhead; with the replay playing, a minimap scrubber input pauses it the same way and leaves the playhead where the scrubber put it; pressing Play afterwards resumes from there. The second round's drag checks (direction, clamping, threshold, single swallowed click) still pass.

4th review, kept renderer checks (scripts/tests/timeline/run_checks.py): run against pasta's data dir, all three checks pass and the runner exits 0; run with --script pointing at the renderer as of 36e8b4c (before drags paused), check_drag.js fails and the runner exits 1 while the other two still pass; a --data-dir that does not exist exits with an error and creates nothing.

5th review, backfill archived: nothing under src/ or tests/ imports src.backfill or id_time any more and src/ids.py no longer defines id_time; test_timeline's 'first seen at a transition' case expects the line to start at that transition (first stop at its time, status = its 'from'); the full pytest run (testmon) and basedpyright pass; the renderer checks still pass 3 of 3 on pasta's live data, whose lines all begin with a backfilled or live 'created' event.

overview.body: Covers one vertical slice: an append-only lifecycle log per workspace (ws_<token>.events.jsonl beside the workspace file) written by the store on page creation, status transition, archive and unarchive; a read-only web view at /ws:<id>/timeline that replays that log as a metro-style map of feature-brief, simple-change and bug-report lines, with play, pause and scrub at 0.25 day/s, compressing idle stretches; and a one-off backfill that writes pasta's own history into its log from the workspace backups, the pasta-dev pull requests and the first commit's dated feature list. Deliberately out: no MCP tool reads or writes the log, no live refresh of the timeline view, no events for renames, reparents, content edits or sweep deletions, no synthetic milestones for features without a page, no zoom or filtering controls, and no backfill for any workspace other than pasta's.

body.text: 1. Event log format - src/event_log.py (pure)

One JSON object per line, UTF-8, keys in this order. 'at' is a UTC ISO-8601 string in the store's own _now() format. 'from' appears only on status events; 'source' appears only on lines the backfill wrote. Live and backfill lines share the shape, so every reader treats them alike.

body.source:
{"at": "2026-11-18T11:29:03.412904+00:00", "event": "status", "pageId": "feature-brief:mwm1gfl9-bbfc5d", "type": "feature-brief", "title": "Metro-style replayable timeline...", "status": "grounding", "from": "draft"}
{"at": "2026-07-22T16:23:00+00:00", "event": "created", "pageId": "feature-brief:mrw7chrt-def44a", "type": "feature-brief", "title": "Anchored relocate...", "status": "draft", "source": "backfill"}

body.text: 2. Writing the log - src/store.py (effects)

Exactly four transactions pass before = page_marks(workspace), taken immediately after load_workspace inside the transaction lock: create_page, mutate_page_batch, set_page_status and _set_page_archive_state (which serves archive, unarchive, schedule-delete and unschedule-delete). Every other transaction calls _touch_and_save as today and appends nothing. Because the append happens after the save and inside the same lock, the log order matches the commit order, and a rejected or aborted write - which raises before saving - logs nothing.
3. Id timestamps - src/ids.py (pure)

body.source:
def id_time(identifier: str) -> float | None:
    """Epoch seconds encoded in an id or token made by new_id/new_token: the base-36 millis before
    the first '-' of the part after the last ':'. None when that part is not base-36.
    id_time('ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6') == 1784562980.405"""

body.text: 4. Timeline model - src/timeline.py (pure)

body.source:
LINE_TYPES = ("feature-brief", "bug-report", "simple-change")   # also the colour slot order
DELIVERED = {"feature-brief": "shipped", "bug-report": "closed", "simple-change": "closed"}
DROPPED = {"feature-brief": "abandoned"}
BASE_RATE = 21_600.0          # workspace seconds per playback second: 0.25 day/s
ACTIVE_WINDOW = 3 * 3600.0    # seconds either side of an event that count as activity
IDLE_PLAYBACK = 1.0           # most playback seconds an idle gap takes
LANE_GAP = 0.4                # playback seconds kept clear between lines sharing a lane
MIN_LINE = 0.15               # playback length a zero-length line occupies when packing

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Segment:
    t0: float; t1: float   # epoch seconds
    p0: float; p1: float   # playback seconds; linear between the two

def playback_segments(times: Sequence[float], start: float, end: float) -> list[Segment]
def to_playback(t: float, segments: Sequence[Segment]) -> float
def is_hidden(workspace: Workspace, page_id: str) -> bool
def build_timeline(events: Sequence[Event], workspace: Workspace, now: float) -> dict[str, Any]

body.text: playback_segments: each event time t marks [t - ACTIVE_WINDOW, t + ACTIVE_WINDOW] active, clipped to [start, end]; overlapping or touching windows merge. Walking start to end, an active stretch of length d becomes a segment of playback length d / BASE_RATE, and an idle stretch of length g one of min(g / BASE_RATE, IDLE_PLAYBACK) - so an idle gap never plays slower than the base rate and never takes more than a second. Segments are contiguous (each p0 is the previous p1, the first p0 is 0) and cover [start, end]; start == end, or no times, gives []. to_playback clamps outside the covered range and interpolates linearly inside, finding the segment by bisection; with [] it returns 0.
is_hidden: true when the page is missing from the workspace, or it or any ancestor (walking parent_id) has archived = True.

build_timeline groups events whose 'type' is in LINE_TYPES by pageId, each group stably sorted by 'at'. For one page: start = min(id_time(pageId), first event time), skipping id_time when it is None. The first stop sits at start with kind 'created' and the status of the created event if there is one, else the first status event's 'from', else the first event's 'status'. Every later event adds a stop (kind = its event, status = the page's status after it). Walking the events tracks status and archived; the end is decided in this order: final status == DELIVERED[type] -> 'delivered' at that status event; final status == DROPPED.get(type) -> 'dropped' at that status event; archived at the end -> 'dropped' at the last archive event; is_hidden now -> 'dropped' at the last event; otherwise 'open', ending at now. A closed page that reopened is judged by its final status like any other. The title is the workspace page's title when it exists, else the last event's title. start_time = min over all line starts, end_time = max(now, latest event); the segments are built from every stop time and line start.

Lanes are packed in playback space: lines sorted by (p0, pageId); each takes the lowest lane whose last occupied end + LANE_GAP <= its p0, else a new lane, where a line occupies up to max(p1, p0 + MIN_LINE). The payload is plain JSON, numbers rounded to 3 decimals:

body.source:
{
  "start": 1784562980.4, "end": 1795003200.0, "duration": 124.8, "baseRate": 21600.0,
  "segments": [[t0, t1, p0, p1], ...],
  "lanes": 14,
  "lines": [{"id": "feature-brief:...", "type": "feature-brief", "title": "...", "lane": 0,
             "p0": 0.0, "p1": 0.27, "end": "delivered" | "dropped" | "open",
             "stops": [{"p": 0.0, "at": 1784562980.4, "kind": "created", "status": "draft"}, ...]}],
  "feed": [{"p": 0.0, "line": 0, "stop": 0}, ...]
}

body.text: feed lists every stop as (line index, stop index), sorted by p then line index - the order the replay narrates them. With no line events the payload has duration 0, segments [], lanes 0, lines [] and feed [].
5. Timeline view - src/server.py, templates, styles (effects + presentation)

route_timeline serves GET /ws:{workspaceIdPart}/timeline inside _guard_http, read-only: load_workspace, read_events, build_timeline(events, workspace, time.time()), then timeline.html with workspace_id, workspace_name and payload. tree.html gains a 'Timeline' link to it beside Show/Hide archived. _base.html wraps its reloader <script> in {% block reloader %}; timeline.html overrides that block empty, so no live refresh reaches the replay.

timeline.html extends _base.html (title 'Timeline - <workspace name>', a link back to the workspace) and embeds the payload as <script type="application/json" id="timeline-data">{{ payload | tojson }}</script>, then includes _timeline.js inline like _view_toggle.js. All styling sits in the template's style block scoped under .timeline; every colour is a water.css custom property or one of three line tokens declared in src/static/styles.css for both body.light and body.dark (dataviz reference palette slots 1-3, validated all-pairs against #ffffff and #202b38):

body.source:
body.light { --line-feature-brief: #2a78d6; --line-bug-report: #eb6834; --line-simple-change: #1baf7a; }
body.dark  { --line-feature-brief: #3987e5; --line-bug-report: #d95926; --line-simple-change: #199e70; }

body.text: Layout, top to bottom: a control row (play/pause button, the clock as weekday-date-time in the browser's local zone, the current rate as '1/4 day/s' or e.g. '6 days/s' through a gap, and counters: in flight / delivered / dropped at the playhead); the stage, an SVG 100% wide and lanes x 18 px + 28 px tall whose world group is drawn once at 120 px per playback second; a minimap of every line scaled to the full width with a window marking the visible range, overlaid by a native <input type=range> (0..duration, step 0.01) that is the scrubber; a legend naming the three types and the three station marks; and a feed of the six latest stops before the playhead (time, type dot, status, title linking to the page with ?archived=true). With no lines, the stage is replaced by one sentence saying the log starts with the next page created, transitioned or archived.

Drawing: a line is a 4 px round-capped stroke in its type's token from p0 to p1 at its lane; each stop a 3.5 px circle filled with --background-body and stroked in the line's token; a 'delivered' end a solid 5 px dot in the token; a 'dropped' end a short perpendicular bar; an 'open' line simply runs on. Each line is wrapped in a link to its page with a <title> holding the page title, which is the hover tooltip. Day ticks sit at local midnights mapped through the segments, skipping any closer than 72 px to the previous; an idle segment longer than a day gets a muted gap label such as '5 d' on the axis.

Playback (_timeline.js, rendering only - every layout number arrives in the payload): playhead p advances by elapsed seconds while playing and stops at duration; play at the end restarts from 0. Each frame sets a clip rect hiding the world beyond p, translates the world so p sits at 70% of the stage width (never scrolling past the start), moves the playhead, and updates clock, rate (from the segment under p: (t1 - t0) / (p1 - p0) / 86400 days/s), counters, the minimap window, the slider value, a 'past' class on lines whose p1 < p (drawn at 45% opacity) and a 'fresh' class on stops passed within the last 0.6 s (a ring that fades). The feed is rebuilt only when the index of the latest passed stop changes. Space toggles play/pause; the slider's input event sets p. Playback starts on load unless prefers-reduced-motion is set.
6. Backfill - src/backfill.py (pure), scripts/backfill_timeline.py (effects), scripts/timeline_backfill/pull_requests.json (data)

body.source:
TYPICAL_MINUTES = (60, 120)
MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.55
LIST_TZ = timezone(timedelta(hours=2))   # the first commit's dates are +0200 local days
PROBE_PREFIX = "[probe]"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Snapshot:
    taken: datetime
    pages: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]   # page dicts as stored in the workspace file

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PullRequest:
    number: int
    created: datetime
    merged: datetime | None
    closed: datetime | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ListedFeature:
    day: date
    text: str

def parse_feature_list(message: str) -> list[ListedFeature]        # lines 'YYYY-MM-DD  text'
def parse_pull_requests(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> dict[int, PullRequest]
def pr_numbers(page: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[int]                # 'pull/<n>' in sections.pull_request.url
def typical_lifetime(page_id: str) -> timedelta                     # 60 + zlib.crc32(page_id) % 61 minutes
def match_listed(title: str, created: datetime, features: Sequence[ListedFeature]) -> ListedFeature | None
def status_time(page_id: str, status: str, history: Sequence[tuple[datetime, str]],
                prs: Mapping[int, PullRequest], numbers: Sequence[int],
                listed: ListedFeature | None, now: datetime) -> tuple[datetime, str]
def backfill_events(snapshots: Sequence[Snapshot], prs: Mapping[int, PullRequest],
                    features: Sequence[ListedFeature], skip_page_ids: Set[str], now: datetime) -> list[Event]
def merge_log(existing: Sequence[Event], backfill: Sequence[Event]) -> list[Event]

body.text: backfill_events takes each page's latest stored form across the snapshots (sorted by taken; a later snapshot overwrites), keeps type in LINE_TYPES, drops titles starting with PROBE_PREFIX and page ids in skip_page_ids, and emits per page a 'created' event at id_time(pageId) with status 'draft' (the initial status of all three types), plus - when the latest status is not 'draft' - one 'status' event from 'draft' to it at status_time. Both carry the latest title and 'source': 'backfill'; the result is sorted by time. Pages whose id has no timestamp are skipped.

status_time returns the time and the anchor it used, in this order. 'pr': among the page's PRs present in prs, the latest merged time, else the latest closed time, else the earliest created time - accepted only when not before the page's creation. 'list': match_listed found a feature - the later of created + typical and the listed day at the time-of-day of created + typical in LIST_TZ. 'estimate': created + typical, clamped into the snapshot bounds - no later than the first snapshot showing the status, no earlier than the last snapshot before that one showing another status. Every result is finally clamped to [created, now]. match_listed lowercases both sides, scores difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio, considers only features dated on or after the creation day in LIST_TZ, and returns the best one scoring >= MATCH_THRESHOLD (ties go to the earliest).

merge_log drops every existing line carrying 'source': 'backfill', adds the new backfill lines, and sorts the lot stably by parsed 'at' - live lines keep their relative order. The script takes --data-dir (default PASTA_DATA_DIR or .pasta-data), --workspace (default ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6) and --dry-run; reads snapshots from backups/<token>/<stamp>.json (taken from the stamp), backups/<token>.json (taken from its mtime) and the live <token>.json (taken = now); reads the PR rows from scripts/timeline_backfill/pull_requests.json and the feature list from 'git show -s --format=%B' of the repository's root commit; skips the pageIds of existing non-backfill lines; writes the merged log to a temp file and os.replace-s it; and prints the counts of pages and of each anchor kind. Its usage text says to run it while the server is not writing.

Addendum to sections 1 and 6: a backfill 'status' line also carries 'anchor': 'pr' | 'list' | 'estimate' - which source dated it - after 'source'. It is provenance for anyone reading the log and lets the script print its anchor counts without recomputing; every reader ignores keys it does not use, and live lines never carry it.
7. Review changes (2026-11-19) - timeline.html and _timeline.js only (presentation)

These supersede the matching sentences of section 5; the payload and every Python module are unchanged, since everything below is drawn from data the payload already carries (each stop's p, kind and status, each line's end).
Time elements: water.css paints every <time> with the grey --background pill; inside .timeline a <time> takes background: var(--background-body), the page background.
Rate readout: empty while the playback clock runs at the base rate (within 1% of 0.25 day/s); through a squeezed segment it reads '<n> day(s) per second »' as before.

Future in grey: each line's shapes (track, stations, end mark) are drawn twice inside its link - first a ghost group (class tl-ghost: --c overridden to var(--text-muted), opacity 0.35, never clipped), then the coloured group clipped at the playhead as before. Ahead of the playhead the map is visible in grey; behind it, in colour.

Delivered mark: a solid circle r = 6 in --c with a checkmark path inside it stroked in --background-body (stroke-width 1.6, round caps), drawn in both the ghost and coloured copies; the legend's delivered entry uses the same mark.

Station labels: every stop gets a <text> label - its status for 'created' and 'status' stops, 'archived' / 'unarchived' for archive stops - at (x + 3, y - 7) rotated -40 degrees about that point, 10 px, fill --text-main with a 3 px --background-body stroke halo (paint-order: stroke), pointer-events none, opacity 0 by default. Labels sit in an unclipped group last in the line's link, so a label reaching right of the playhead is not cut. A label shows (opacity 1, 0.2 s transition) while its line's link is hovered or focused, and during playback while 'speaking': for every stop except the first, from when the playhead passes it until 1.5 playback seconds later. The frame loop toggles the speaking class only when it changes, like fresh.
8. Second review (2026-11-19) - timeline.html and _timeline.js only (presentation)
Supersedes the rate readout of sections 5 and 7: there is no rate readout at all - the #tl-rate element and its text are removed; the clock stands alone.
Play button: reads 'Play' (no icon) when paused, '❚❚ Pause' while playing, '↺ Replay' at the end.
Feed: rows are separated by a 1 px --border line between consecutive rows only (li + li border-top), so the list has neither a top nor a bottom border.

Dragging the stage: pointerdown (primary button) on #tl-stage records the pointer x and the playhead p and captures the pointer. Once the pointer has moved 4 px horizontally the press becomes a drag: p = clamp(p at press - dx / 120, 0, duration), redrawn each move; while the pointer is down the playhead does not advance, and on release a playing replay carries on from there. A drag suppresses the click that ends it (a capture-phase click listener on the stage calls preventDefault once), so a press without movement still follows a line's link. The stage gets cursor: grab (grabbing while dragging), user-select: none and touch-action: pan-y, keeping vertical touch scrolling of a tall stage.
9. Third review (2026-11-19) - _timeline.js only

Supersedes the playback-during-drag rule of section 8: dragging pauses the player. A press on the chart that becomes a drag (past 4 px) pauses the replay at that moment, and every input event of the minimap scrubber pauses it before moving the playhead. The replay stays paused until Play is pressed (or Space); nothing resumes it on release. The rest of section 8 - map-direction movement, clamping, the 4 px threshold, capture on drag, click swallowing - is unchanged.
10. Renderer checks kept in the repository - scripts/tests/timeline/
The Node checks that exercised _timeline.js against a stub DOM move from a scratch directory into scripts/tests/timeline/, outside pytest's testpaths, run by hand:

body.source:
scripts/tests/timeline/
  README.md          what the checks cover, what they need (uv, Node), how to run them
  run_checks.py      builds the payload (or takes --payload FILE), runs every check, exits 1 on any failure
  stub_dom.js        the minimal DOM the renderer needs, and a loader that runs it on a payload
  check_replay.js    plays to the end: Replay button, final counters match the payload, six-item feed, scrub moves the clock
  check_marks.js     grey + clipped coloured copy per line, check in both copies of each delivered end,
                     one label per station, transition labels speak during playback, creation labels never
  check_drag.js      drag direction / clamp / 4 px threshold / one swallowed click; chart and scrubber drags pause; Play resumes

body.text: run_checks.py: --data-dir (default PASTA_DATA_DIR or .pasta-data) and --workspace (default ws:mrteq0c5-238cf6) build the payload with Store.read_events / load_workspace / build_timeline into a temp file; --payload FILE uses a saved payload instead; --script FILE checks another copy of the renderer (default src/templates/_timeline.js). A data dir that does not exist is an error, never created. Each check is run as 'node <check> <payload> <script>'; the runner prints PASS or FAIL with the check's output per check, and exits 1 if any failed or Node is missing.
11. Backfill archived (2026-11-19)

The one-off backfill has done its job (pasta's log holds its history) and leaves the product. Supersedes sections 3 and 6: id_time is removed from src/ids.py, and src/backfill.py, tests/test_backfill.py, tests/test_ids.py, scripts/backfill_timeline.py and scripts/timeline_backfill/pull_requests.json move to scripts/backfill_events/ as stored files only - id_time goes there as id_time.py. Nothing there is made runnable: imports stay as they were written, the folder is outside pytest's testpaths and basedpyright's include, and a short README.md says what the files are.

Supersedes the line-start rule of section 4: a line starts at its first logged event (the first stop sits there, with the same status rule as before). A page whose log begins with a 'created' event - every backfilled page, and every page created while logging - starts exactly where it did.
scripts/tests/timeline/README.md no longer tells the reader to run the backfill; it says the checks need a workspace whose event log has timeline events.

Log file: <data dir>/ws_<token>.events.jsonl. Rejected: a folder per workspace (a second layout to learn for one file) and a file inside backups/ (backups are snapshots, the log is live). The '.jsonl' extension keeps it out of list_workspaces' '*.json' glob without touching the glob.

Log created, status, archived, unarchived for all page types. Rejected: transitions + archive only (a line would have no start for pages whose first event is a later transition, and pinned children would never appear), and logging renames/reparents/content/deletions (nothing the timeline draws reads them; current titles come from the workspace).

Lines for feature-brief, bug-report, simple-change only, in that colour order. Rejected: every type (plans, specs and docs would triple the lines and bury the work). The log stays type-agnostic so the filter can change later without a migration.

First-commit list = date source for matching no-PR pages only. Rejected: drawing unmatched list items as milestones (a second kind of line with no page to link to, and no creation time), and using the list for pages that have a PR (the PR date is exact; the list is day-precise).

No anchor: created + 60-120 min (crc32 of the id), clamped into the backups' interval for the status change. Rejected: a fixed 90 min (every line identical), the backup time itself (would stretch most lines to the next backup, days later), and random jitter (reruns would disagree).
Backfill only creation and the latest status. Rejected: interpolating intermediate stations or archive times between backups days apart - invented precision that the replay would present as fact.

Backfill lines are marked source=backfill and replaced on every run; pages with any live event are skipped; the file is rewritten sorted by time. Rejected: append-only backfill (re-runs duplicate), and a cutoff-time rule (a page created before the cutoff but transitioned live after would get two conflicting histories). It runs out of process, so its usage text tells the operator to run it while the server is not writing - cross-process locking is out of scope per the existing concurrency model.

A never-finished line that is hidden now (self or ancestor archived) or deleted ends 'dropped' at its last event; an archive event ends it at the archive time. Rejected: running such lines to now (dozens of shelved drafts would hold lanes forever), and logging cascade events for descendants (the archive flag does not change on them, so the log would claim something the workspace does not).

Active = within 3 h of an event, played at 0.25 day/s; an idle gap plays in min(gap/base, 1 s). Prototyped on pasta's real history: ~125 s total versus 480 s unaccelerated, with ACTIVE_WINDOW 2 h giving 113 s and 4 h 136 s. Rejected: a fixed idle multiplier (a month-long gap would still take 15 s at 8x) and easing inside gaps (nothing is drawn there to ease).
x = playback time at 120 px/s, idle gaps compressed and labelled. Rejected: x = real time, where a 1.5 h line is ~2 px next to a 30-day gap and the camera would race across empty screens.

The timeline view opts out of the reloader via a new {% block reloader %} in _base.html. Rejected: keeping it and restoring the playhead from sessionStorage (each agent write would still flash a full reload mid-replay), and a timeline-specific socket (live streaming was not asked for).
The backfill drops '[probe]' titles. Rejected: a title filter in the timeline itself (a naming convention baked into a view) and changing the probe script (out of scope).

Blank the readout at the base rate, keep it through gaps. Rejected: removing the readout entirely - then nothing on screen says the replay is fast-forwarding, which is the behaviour the user asked to see.

Ghost copy under a clipped coloured copy. Rejected: per-frame recolouring of elements as the playhead crosses them (hundreds of style writes per frame, and a long line would be one colour or the other instead of colouring in as the head moves along it).

Rotated station labels, shown on hover and for 1.5 playback s after each transition. Rejected: horizontal labels (stations 10-30 px apart would overprint), labels on creation stops during playback (every new page would flash 'draft', drowning the transitions), and the 0.6 s highlight window (too short to read).
Solid coloured circle with a background-coloured check. Rejected: a check in a text colour (fails on dark lines in one theme or the other) and a ring-only mark (reads as an ordinary station).
Keep '↺ Replay'; drop only the play icon. Rejected: stripping every glyph (the user asked to keep the pause icon, and Replay's icon distinguishes restarting from resuming).

Map-style drag that holds the playhead while pressed and resumes a playing replay on release, with a 4 px threshold and click suppression. Rejected: dragging right to go forward (the content would move against the pointer), pausing for good on drag (an attraction should keep running after someone pokes it), and moving the camera without the playhead (the view would drift from what the clock, counters and feed describe).

Any drag pauses, on the chart and on the minimap, and the replay stays paused. Directed by the user. Rejected: section 8's hold-while-pressed-then-resume (the replay ran on from a spot the viewer chose to look at), and pausing only on the chart (the two scrubbing gestures would behave differently).

Three focused checks over one shared stub, run by a Python runner, documented in a README beside them. Rejected: running them from pytest (needs Node on every machine that runs the suite, and the real-data payload is local), a committed synthetic payload (the checks are meant to replay real history; a saved payload can still be passed with --payload), and keeping the four scratch scripts as they were (each copied the stub, and two asserted behaviour that has since been removed).

Lines start at their first logged event, and the backfill runner goes to the dump with the module it imports. Directed by the user (the backfill and id_time are throwaway). Rejected: keeping id_time in src for the timeline alone (the user named it throwaway, and for every page with a 'created' event it changes nothing), and leaving scripts/backfill_timeline.py in place (it would import a module that no longer exists).

summary.body: Replays a workspace's lifecycle log as a metro-style map in the web UI: each feature-brief, bug-report and simple-change is a coloured line from its first logged event, with a station for every later one, ending delivered, dropped or still open - played, paused and scrubbed like a video.

purpose.body: Make a workspace's history visible and watchable: when each unit of work started, which stages it passed through, and when it was delivered or dropped. The workspace file only knows where pages are now; the lifecycle log the store appends to knows how they got there, and this is the view that reads it. It doubles as a demonstration of the workflow pasta drives.

usage.body: Open /ws:<id>/timeline, linked from the workspace tree. The replay starts on load - or, for a viewer who prefers reduced motion, shows the finished map at rest - and plays at a quarter of a day of workspace time per second, squeezing each stretch with no activity into at most a second. Play/Pause (or Space) toggles it. Dragging the chart moves time the way dragging a map does (left is forward), and dragging the minimap scrubber below it jumps anywhere; either drag pauses the replay. Ahead of the playhead the map shows in grey and colours in as the playhead passes; each status change's name is shown above its station as it is passed, and hovering a line shows its title and every station's status. Clicking a line opens its page. A feed under the map lists the six latest stations, and counters give the work in flight, delivered and dropped at the playhead. The view is read-only and offers no MCP tool.

dataModel.body:
Input: the workspace's lifecycle log, ws_<token>.events.jsonl beside its workspace file - one JSON object per line with at (UTC ISO-8601), event (created | status | archived | unarchived), pageId, type, title, status (the page's status after the event) and, on a status event, from - plus the current workspace, for titles and for which pages are hidden. Lines that are not JSON objects with string at / event / pageId are skipped, and keys a reader does not use are ignored.

Output: a payload built per request, embedded in the page as JSON: start, end and duration (playback seconds); baseRate; segments as [t0, t1, p0, p1], mapping epoch seconds linearly to playback seconds; lanes; lines as {id, type, title, lane, p0, p1, end: delivered | dropped | open, stops: [{p, at, kind, status}]}; and feed as {p, line, stop}, every station in the order it is narrated. Every position is decided in the payload; the browser draws and animates it.

inlines.text: Where the pure line runs

inlines: is pure:
is a function of its arguments, and
is the thin shell that reads the log (
), loads the workspace, reads the clock and renders
is presentation only: it makes no layout decision, so every rule about lines, lanes and the playback clock is tested in Python.

inlines.text: How a line is built

inlines: - events whose type is feature-brief, bug-report or simple-change are grouped by page in time order. A line starts at its first event, whose first station carries the created event's status (or the

of a first status event); every later event adds a station. It ends delivered at the status event that reached shipped or closed, dropped at the one that reached abandoned, dropped at its last archive event if it is still archived, dropped at its last event if the page is now hidden (it or an ancestor archived, or deleted), and otherwise runs open to now. A closed page that reopened is judged by its final status. The title is the page's current title, else the last one logged.

inlines.text: The playback clock

inlines: marks the time within 3 hours of any event as active and plays it at 0.25 day per playback second (21,600 workspace seconds per second); every idle stretch between plays in the lesser of its time at that rate and 1 second. The horizontal axis is playback time at 120 px per second, so active periods get the space and the camera scrolls at a constant speed while the clock races through gaps. Lanes are packed in playback space, lowest free lane first, with 0.4 s kept clear between lines sharing one.

inlines.text: How the browser draws it

inlines: - the map is drawn once. Each line is drawn twice: a grey copy at 35% opacity that is never clipped, under a coloured copy clipped at the playhead, which is what greys the future and colours it in as the playhead passes. A delivered end is a solid circle with a checkmark in the page background colour, a dropped end a short bar. Station names are rotated labels in an unclipped group, so one reaching past the playhead is not cut. Each frame only moves the clip, the camera and the playhead and toggles classes when they change, so scrubbing costs no more than playing. Line colours are the theme tokens
and
, defined for both themes in src/static/styles.css.

inlines: empties the reloader block of

items.statement: The timeline is a read: route_timeline reads the log and the workspace and changes nothing, and no MCP tool exposes it. Violated, viewing a replay could alter the history it shows.

Every layout decision - lines, ends, lanes, the playback clock, feed order - is made by the pure build_timeline; the browser script only draws the payload and moves the playhead. Violated, layout rules live in untested script and drift from what the Python tests pin.

An idle stretch never plays slower than the base rate or longer than one second, and time within 3 hours of an event always plays at 0.25 day per second. Violated, a month-long gap stalls the replay, or a burst of work flashes past too fast to follow.

Any drag - on the chart past its 4 px threshold, or on the minimap scrubber - pauses the replay, and a press without a drag still follows the line's link. Violated, the replay runs away from the moment the viewer chose, or clicking a line stops opening its page.
